diego-suarez-colony.t: A small French colony around the great natural harbour of northern Madagascar, gained in 1885 and kept as a naval base.
diego-suarez-colony.o: The treaty ending the [[e:franco-hova-war|Franco-Hova War]] in 1885 gave [[e:france|France]] the bay of Diego-Suarez, now [[e:antsiranana|Antsiranana]], at the northern tip of [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]], one of the finest natural harbours in the [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]]. France organised it as a separate colony.
diego-suarez-colony.r: The colony was essentially a naval base and coaling station with a garrison town around it, with salt works and a meat-canning plant. It attracted Comoran, Indian, Arab and [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] migrants alongside Malagasy workers, and its harbour was fortified as a key point of French naval power in the [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]].
diego-suarez-colony.e: After [[e:france|France]] annexed [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]], Diego-Suarez was merged into the colony of [[s:french-madagascar|French Madagascar]] in 1896. It remained a major naval base, captured by British forces in 1942 during the [[e:battle-of-madagascar|Battle of Madagascar]].

duchy-of-pannonian-croatia.t: Slavic duchy between the Drava and Sava, centred on Sisak, whose duke Ljudevit led a great revolt against the Franks.
duchy-of-pannonian-croatia.o: After [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] destroyed the [[s:avar-khaganate|Avar Khaganate]] in the 790s, the [[e:slavs|Slavs]] of the [[e:sava|Sava]] valley came under Frankish overlordship as part of the march of [[e:friuli|Friuli]]. A duchy appears in Frankish sources by 818, with its seat at [[e:sisak|Sisak]], the Roman Siscia.
duchy-of-pannonian-croatia.r: Its dukes governed a Slavic population as Frankish [[e:vassal|vassals]]. Between 819 and 823 Duke [[e:ljudevit-posavski|Ljudevit Posavski]] rebelled against harsh Frankish rule, drawing in the [[s:timocani|Timočani]] and others, and fought the [[s:duchy-of-croatia|Duchy of Croatia]], before fleeing and being killed. Later, Duke [[e:braslav-duke-of-lower-pannonia|Braslav]] held lands between the [[e:drava|Drava]] and [[e:sava|Sava]] and aided the East Frankish king [[e:arnulf-of-carinthia|Arnulf]] against [[s:great-moravia|Great Moravia]] in the 880s and 890s.
duchy-of-pannonian-croatia.e: [[e:hungarian-invasions-of-europe|Hungarian raids]] from the 890s weakened Frankish control. Around 925 the region was united with [[e:duchy-of-croatia|Dalmatian Croatia]] under [[e:tomislav-of-croatia|Tomislav]], forming the [[s:kingdom-of-croatia-925-1102|Kingdom of Croatia]] (925-1102); the area later became [[e:slavonia|Slavonia]].

duchy-of-cantabria.t: A Visigothic frontier duchy in northern Spain whose last duke, Peter, was father of King Alfonso I of Asturias.
duchy-of-cantabria.o: The Visigothic king [[e:liuvigild|Leovigild]] conquered [[e:cantabria|Cantabria]] in 574, taking its stronghold of [[e:pena-amaya|Amaya]]. A frontier duchy was then set up to watch the mountain peoples and the [[e:basques|Basques]], though its extent and organisation are poorly documented.
duchy-of-cantabria.r: The duchy was ruled by a dux appointed by the Visigothic kings, with its centre probably at [[e:pena-amaya|Amaya]] in the north of modern [[e:burgos|Burgos]]. Its population lived from herding and farming in the valleys of the Cantabrian range, and Visigothic control seems to have been loose.
duchy-of-cantabria.e: After the Muslim conquest of 711, Duke [[e:peter-of-cantabria|Peter of Cantabria]], known only from the Asturian chronicles, probably kept some independence. His son Alfonso married the daughter of [[e:pelagius-of-asturias|Pelagius]] and became Alfonso I of [[e:asturias|Asturias]] in 739, uniting the duchy with the [[s:kingdom-of-asturias|Kingdom of Asturias]].

duchy-of-upper-bavaria.t: Wittelsbach duchy ruled from Munich, created in the first partition of Bavaria in 1255 and home of Emperor Louis IV the Bavarian.
duchy-of-upper-bavaria.o: In 1255 Duke [[e:otto-ii-duke-of-bavaria|Otto II]]'s sons divided the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria|Duchy of Bavaria]], the first of many [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] partitions. [[e:louis-ii-duke-of-bavaria|Louis II the Strict]] received [[e:upper-bavaria|Upper Bavaria]], with [[e:munich|Munich]] as residence, together with the [[e:palatinate-region|Rhenish Palatinate]], while his brother [[e:henry-xiii-duke-of-bavaria|Henry XIII]] took the [[s:duchy-of-lower-bavaria|Duchy of Lower Bavaria]].
duchy-of-upper-bavaria.r: [[e:louis-ii-duke-of-bavaria|Louis II]] made [[e:munich|Munich]] a ducal capital and acquired [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] lands after [[e:conradin|Conradin's]] execution in 1268. His sons Rudolf I and [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Louis IV]] ruled jointly, then fought each other. Louis IV was elected King of the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] in 1314, defeated [[e:frederick-the-fair|Frederick the Fair]] at [[e:battle-of-muhldorf|Mühldorf]] in 1322 and was crowned emperor in [[e:rome|Rome]] in 1328. By the Treaty of [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]] in 1329 the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] went to Rudolf's heirs.
duchy-of-upper-bavaria.e: When the Lower Bavarian line died out in 1340, [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Louis IV]] reunited Upper and [[e:lower-bavaria|Lower Bavaria]]. After his death in 1347 his sons divided the lands again, but [[e:munich|Munich]] remained the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] capital until 1918.

duchy-of-limburg-1839-1867.t: The Dutch half of Limburg, made a duchy of the German Confederation in 1839 to compensate the Confederation for losing part of Luxembourg.
duchy-of-limburg-1839-1867.o: The [[e:treaty-of-london-1839|Treaty of London]] of 1839 divided [[s:duchy-of-limburg|Limburg]] between [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]]. Because the [[s:grand-duchy-of-luxembourg|Grand Duchy of Luxembourg]] lost its western half to [[e:belgium|Belgium]], the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] part of Limburg was made a duchy and joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]], held by the Dutch king, though [[e:maastricht|Maastricht]] and [[e:venlo|Venlo]] were left outside the Confederation.
duchy-of-limburg-1839-1867.r: The duchy was governed as a [[e:dutch|Dutch]] province while its estates sent representatives to the Confederation's diet in [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]]. In 1848 some Limburgers sought separation from the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] to join [[e:germany|Germany]], and deputies sat in the [[e:frankfurt-parliament|Frankfurt Parliament]]. Mining and [[e:maastricht|Maastricht's]] pottery and glass industries developed.
duchy-of-limburg-1839-1867.e: The [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] dissolved after the war of 1866, and the [[e:treaty-of-london-1839|Treaty of London]] of 1867 confirmed that [[s:duchy-of-limburg|Limburg]] was fully part of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Kingdom of the Netherlands]]. The title 'Duchy of Limburg' lingered in official use until 1906.

diauehi.t: A tribal union in the highlands of north-eastern Anatolia, known from Assyrian and Urartian war records and often linked with the later Georgian region of Tao.
diauehi.o: Known almost entirely from the inscriptions of its enemies. The Assyrian king [[e:tiglath-pileser-i|Tiglath-Pileser I]] names the lands of Daiaeni among the [[s:nairi|Nairi]] peoples he fought around 1112 BCE and captured its king Sien, and [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] defeated its king Asia in 845 BCE. The union seems to have centred on the upper [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] and Chorokhi valleys.
diauehi.r: Its rulers commanded fortified settlements and a mixed economy of herding, farming and metalworking in rich ore country. Urartian annals record large tributes of gold, [[e:silver|silver]], [[e:copper|copper]] and [[e:cattle|cattle]], which suggests a wealthy, organised society, though nothing survives in its own words. Many scholars regard its people as early Kartvelian speakers.
diauehi.e: Diauehi was worn down by repeated campaigns of the [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Kingdom of Urartu]] under [[e:menua|Menua]] and [[e:argishti-i|Argishti I]], and its king Utupurshi was forced into tribute. By about 760 BCE it was absorbed, and its northern lands passed into the orbit of the rising [[s:kingdom-of-colchis|Kingdom of Colchis]].

duchy-of-trakai.t: The western half of medieval Lithuania, ruled by Kestutis and Vytautas from the island castle of Trakai.
duchy-of-trakai.o: [[e:trakai|Trakai]], west of [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] among lakes, became the seat of [[e:kestutis|Kestutis]], son of [[e:gediminas|Gediminas]], in the late 1330s. After 1345 [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] was effectively shared between [[e:algirdas|Algirdas]] in Vilnius and Kestutis in Trakai, who governed the western lands including [[e:samogitia|Samogitia]] and led the defence against the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]].
duchy-of-trakai.r: The duchy bore the brunt of the crusaders' raids from [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], and [[e:kestutis|Kestutis]] fought them for almost fifty years. [[e:trakai|Trakai's]] castles became seats of power and residence. [[e:vytautas-the-great|Vytautas]] brought Karaite and [[e:tatars|Tatar]] settlers to the town, whose Karaite community still lives there. The duchy had its own court and nobility, closely tied to the grand duke.
duchy-of-trakai.e: After [[e:algirdas|Algirdas]] died, his son [[e:w-adys-aw-ii-jagie-o|Jogaila]] fought [[e:kestutis|Kestutis]], who was killed in captivity at [[e:kreva|Kreva]] in 1382. Kestutis's son [[e:vytautas-the-great|Vytautas]] regained [[e:trakai|Trakai]] and later became grand duke. In 1413 the [[e:union-of-horodlo|Union of Horodlo]] turned the duchy into the [[e:trakai-voivodeship|Trakai Voivodeship]] of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]].

dahae.t: A confederation of Iranian nomads east of the Caspian whose Parni tribe founded the Parthian dynasty that would rule Iran for nearly five centuries.
dahae.o: The Dahae appear in a daiva inscription of [[e:xerxes-i|Xerxes I]] and in Greek accounts of the Achaemenid army, living on the steppes south-east of the [[e:caspian-sea|Caspian Sea]], in what is now [[s:turkmenistan|Turkmenistan]]. They comprised three main tribes, the [[e:parni|Parni]], Xanthii and Pissuri, and are often counted among the [[s:saka|Saka]] peoples.
dahae.r: They were horse-riding pastoralists famed as [[e:mounted-archer|mounted archers]], serving as cavalry for [[e:darius-iii|Darius III]] at [[e:battle-of-gaugamela|Gaugamela]] and later for [[e:alexander-the-great|Alexander the Great]] and his successors. Their territory, later called Dahistan, bordered the farming lands of [[e:hyrcania|Hyrcania]] and [[e:margiana|Margiana]], and they traded and raided along this edge.
dahae.e: Around 238 BCE [[e:arsaces-i|Arsaces]], leader of the [[e:parni|Parni]], seized the [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] province of [[e:parthia|Parthia]], founding the [[e:arsacid-dynasty|Arsacid dynasty]] of the [[s:parthian-empire|Parthian Empire]], whose era was later reckoned from 247 BCE. The remaining Dahae were absorbed into Parthian and later steppe populations, though the name Dahistan survived for the region into Islamic times.

duchy-of-cieszyn.t: Silesian duchy on the Olza ruled by Piasts until 1653 and then by the Habsburgs, whose divided land now lies in both Poland and the Czech Republic.
duchy-of-cieszyn.o: In the partition of [[e:upper-silesia|Upper Silesia]] after 1281, Mieszko received [[e:cieszyn|Cieszyn]], and by 1290 it was a separate duchy. He and his heirs accepted Bohemian overlordship in 1327. Cieszyn lay on the route from [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] to [[e:krakow|Kraków]] and [[e:hungary|Hungary]], through the [[e:moravian-gate|Moravian Gate]] and the [[e:jablunkov-pass|Jablunkov Pass]].
duchy-of-cieszyn.r: The [[e:cieszyn|Cieszyn]] [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]] ruled for over three centuries. Duke [[e:wenceslaus-iii-adam-duke-of-cieszyn|Wenceslaus III Adam]] introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in the 16th century, and the duchy kept a strong Protestant community even after the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]]. Polish, Czech and German were spoken. The duchy prospered from farming, cloth and later [[e:coal|coal]] and iron.
duchy-of-cieszyn.e: The last [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]], [[e:elizabeth-lucretia-duchess-of-teschen|Elizabeth Lucretia]], died in 1653, and the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] took the duchy; [[e:prince-albert-duke-of-teschen|Albert of Saxe-Teschen]] later held the title. It remained part of [[s:duchy-of-upper-and-lower-silesia|Austrian Silesia]] until 1918. After a brief [[e:polish-czechoslovak-war|Polish-Czechoslovak war]], it was divided along the [[e:olza|Olza]] in 1920, splitting [[e:cieszyn|Cieszyn]] itself in two.

duchy-of-massa-and-carrara.t: The marble-quarrying state of the Malaspina and Cybo families on the Tuscan coast, whose white stone supplied Michelangelo and Europe's sculptors.
duchy-of-massa-and-carrara.o: The [[e:malaspina|Malaspina]], a feudal family of [[e:lunigiana|Lunigiana]], ruled [[e:massa-tuscany|Massa]], and in 1473 [[e:jacopo-malaspina|Jacopo Malaspina]] bought [[e:carrara|Carrara]] with its marble quarries. Through the marriage of [[e:ricciarda-malaspina|Ricciarda Malaspina]], the state passed to the [[e:house-of-cybo-malaspina|Cybo]] family, and [[e:alberico-i-cybo-malaspina|Alberico I Cybo-Malaspina]] was made prince in 1568; it became a duchy in 1664.
duchy-of-massa-and-carrara.r: The rulers governed a narrow strip between the [[e:apuan-alps|Apuan Alps]] and the sea. [[e:carrara|Carrara's]] marble, quarried since Roman times, was the state's wealth; [[e:michelangelo|Michelangelo]] chose blocks there. [[e:alberico-i-cybo-malaspina|Alberico I]] laid out a new town centre at [[e:massa-tuscany|Massa]]. The state survived as an imperial fief protected by [[e:spain|Spain]] and its neighbours.
duchy-of-massa-and-carrara.e: The heiress [[e:maria-beatrice-d-este-duchess-of-massa|Maria Beatrice Cybo d'Este]] married [[e:archduke-ferdinand-karl-of-austria|Ferdinand of Austria-Este]]. After Napoleonic rule under [[e:elisa-bonaparte|Elisa Bonaparte]], she was restored in 1814, and on her death in 1829 the duchy passed to her son [[e:francis-iv-duke-of-modena|Francis IV]], joining the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]].

duchy-of-aquitaine.t: The great duchy of south-western France, home of troubadour courts and Eleanor of Aquitaine, fought over by the kings of England and France for three centuries.
duchy-of-aquitaine.o: The [[e:frankish-kingdom|Frankish kingdom]] of Aquitaine dissolved in the late 9th century, and in 893 [[e:william-i-duke-of-aquitaine|William the Pious]], count of [[s:county-of-auvergne|Auvergne]], took the ducal title; he founded the abbey of [[e:cluny-abbey|Cluny]] in 910. From the mid-10th century the counts of [[s:county-of-poitou|Poitou]], the [[e:ramnulfids|Ramnulfids]], held the duchy and ruled from [[e:poitiers|Poitiers]].
duchy-of-aquitaine.r: The dukes ruled loosely over powerful [[e:vassal|vassals]] in [[e:gascony|Gascony]], the [[s:viscounty-of-limoges|Limousin]] and [[s:county-of-auvergne|Auvergne]]. Their court was a centre of Occitan culture: [[e:william-ix-duke-of-aquitaine|Duke William IX]] is the earliest known troubadour. [[e:bordeaux|Bordeaux]] grew rich on wine exports to [[e:england|England]]. [[e:eleanor-of-aquitaine|Eleanor of Aquitaine]] brought the duchy first to [[e:louis-vii-of-france|Louis VII of France]] and then, in 1152, to [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]], joining it to the [[s:angevin-empire|Angevin Empire]].
duchy-of-aquitaine.e: English kings held the duchy as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of [[e:france|France]], reduced after 1204 to [[e:gascony|Gascony]], or Guyenne, and confirmed by the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1259|Treaty of Paris]] of 1259. Disputes over it helped spark the [[e:hundred-years-war|Hundred Years' War]], which ended with the French victory at [[e:battle-of-castillon|Castillon]] in 1453 and the annexation of Guyenne to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

duchy-of-castro.t: A Farnese duchy in northern Lazio created by Pope Paul III for his son, whose capital was razed by a later pope in 1649.
duchy-of-castro.o: In 1537 [[e:pope-paul-iii|Pope Paul III]], born Alessandro Farnese, carved the Duchy of Castro out of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] for his son [[e:pier-luigi-farnese|Pier Luigi Farnese]]. It covered the old Farnese estates between [[e:lake-bolsena|Lake Bolsena]] and the Tyrrhenian coast.
duchy-of-castro.r: Castro was rebuilt as a small [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] capital, with buildings by [[e:antonio-da-sangallo-the-younger|Antonio da Sangallo the Younger]]. After 1545 its dukes were also dukes of the [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Duchy of Parma and Piacenza]], and they ran Castro from afar, borrowing heavily against it. A quarrel over these debts and the Farnese's power led [[e:pope-urban-viii|Pope Urban VIII]] to fight the [[e:first-war-of-castro|First War of Castro]] in 1641–1644, which ended in a papal setback.
duchy-of-castro.e: In 1649, after the murder of the new [[e:bishop|bishop]] of Castro was blamed on the Farnese, [[e:pope-innocent-x|Pope Innocent X's]] troops took the town and razed it to the ground. The duchy was absorbed into the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].

duchy-of-westphalia.t: Ducal territory in the Sauerland held for six centuries by the archbishops of Cologne after the fall of Henry the Lion.
duchy-of-westphalia.o: When [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] was deposed, the [[e:gelnhausen-charter|Gelnhausen Charter]] of 1180 split his [[s:duchy-of-saxony|Duchy of Saxony]]. The western part, with the title Duke of [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]] and [[e:angria|Engern]], went to Archbishop [[e:philip-i-archbishop-of-cologne|Philip of Heinsberg]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]]. The archbishops turned this title into real rule over the [[e:sauerland|Sauerland]], buying the [[e:county-of-arnsberg|County of Arnsberg]] in 1368.
duchy-of-westphalia.r: Ruled by the [[s:electorate-of-cologne|Electorate of Cologne]] as a separate territory, the duchy had its own estates and diet meeting at [[e:arnsberg|Arnsberg]], with an electoral governor there. The land was hilly and rural, known for iron working and forestry. [[e:cologne|Cologne's]] ambitions in the region were checked by its defeat at [[e:battle-of-worringen|Worringen]] in 1288 and by the [[e:soest-feud|Soest Feud]], in which [[e:soest|Soest]] broke away to [[e:kleve|Cleves]]. The duchy stayed Catholic throughout.
duchy-of-westphalia.e: In 1803 the duchy was secularised and given to [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]]. The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] transferred it to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1816, and it became part of the [[e:province-of-westphalia|Prussian Province of Westphalia]]; it now lies in [[e:north-rhine-westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]].

duchy-of-lotharingia.t: The duchy that held together the old middle kingdom of Lothair II, between France and Germany, before it was split into Upper and Lower Lorraine in 959.
duchy-of-lotharingia.o: [[s:kingdom-of-lotharingia|Lotharingia]] was the kingdom created for [[e:lothair-ii|Lothair II]] in 855, stretching from [[e:frisia|Frisia]] to the [[e:vosges|Vosges]]. After the Carolingian lines weakened, the East Frankish king [[e:louis-the-child|Louis the Child]] appointed [[e:gebhard-duke-of-lotharingia|Gebhard]] as duke in 903. Local nobles, led by the [[e:reginarids|Reginarids]], repeatedly switched allegiance between East and [[s:west-francia|West Francia]].
duchy-of-lotharingia.r: The duchy held the old Carolingian heartland around [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]], [[e:trier|Trier]], [[e:metz|Metz]] and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]], rich in bishoprics and royal abbeys. Duke [[e:humphrey-gilbert|Gilbert]] went over to the West Frankish king before [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler]] recovered the region in 925; Gilbert drowned at [[e:andernach|Andernach]] in 939 while rebelling against Otto I. Otto's son-in-law [[e:conrad-the-red|Conrad the Red]] rebelled in 953.
duchy-of-lotharingia.e: Otto I then gave the duchy to his brother [[e:bruno-the-great|Bruno]], archbishop of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]], who divided it in 959 into the [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Duchy of Upper Lorraine]] and the [[s:duchy-of-lower-lorraine|Duchy of Lower Lorraine]]. Upper [[e:lorraine|Lorraine]] became the later Duchy of Lorraine; the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]] principalities grew out of [[e:duchy-of-lower-lorraine|Lower Lorraine]].
duchy-of-lotharingia.la: Old French and Old High German

duchy-of-limburg.t: A small duchy in the hills east of the Meuse whose succession war ended at the battle of Worringen in 1288, binding it to Brabant for five centuries.
duchy-of-limburg.o: The castle of [[e:limbourg|Limbourg]] on the [[e:vesdre|Vesdre]] was built in the early 11th century, and around 1065 Walram Udo of the house of [[e:arlon|Arlon]] became count of Limburg. His son Henry I claimed the duchy of [[e:duchy-of-lower-lorraine|Lower Lorraine]], and later rulers kept the ducal title for their own lands.
duchy-of-limburg.r: Limburg was a land of pasture, woods and later cloth and lead mining around [[e:verviers|Verviers]] and the [[e:vesdre|Vesdre]] valley. Its dukes, among them [[e:waleran-iii-duke-of-limburg|Waleran III]], intermarried with [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]] and the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]] nobility. When the line ended in 1283, [[e:john-i-duke-of-brabant|John I of Brabant]] fought for the inheritance and won at [[e:battle-of-worringen|Worringen]] in 1288.
duchy-of-limburg.e: Limburg was then ruled with the [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Duchy of Brabant]], passing to the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]], the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]] and the [[s:spanish-netherlands|Spanish Netherlands]]. In 1661 the [[e:lands-of-overmaas|Overmaas]] lands were divided with the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]]. [[e:france|France]] annexed the rest in 1795.

duchy-of-brzeg.t: A Silesian Piast duchy on the Oder whose Lutheran dukes and Renaissance castle outlasted almost every other branch of the dynasty.
duchy-of-brzeg.o: In 1311 the sons of Duke [[e:henry-v-the-fat|Henry V of Legnica]] divided their inheritance, and [[e:boleslaw-iii-the-generous|Bolesław III the Generous]] took [[e:brzeg|Brzeg]] (Brieg) on the Oder as his duchy, separating it from the [[s:duchy-of-legnica|Duchy of Legnica]]. In 1329 Bolesław did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|King John of Bohemia]], placing Brzeg under the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-brzeg.r: [[e:brzeg|Brzeg]] was often held together with [[e:legnica|Legnica]] under one duke, and its rulers were among the leading Silesian princes. [[e:frederick-ii-of-legnica|Duke Frederick II]] introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]] in the 1520s and in 1537 made an inheritance treaty with [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]]. Under [[e:george-ii-of-brieg|George II]] the castle was rebuilt in [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] style, with a gatehouse adorned with statues of the [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]], and a [[e:gymnasium|gymnasium]] was founded in 1569.
duchy-of-brzeg.e: When [[e:george-william-duke-of-legnica|George William]], the last Silesian [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]], died in 1675, the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] as kings of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] took the duchy, ignoring [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg's]] claim. [[e:frederick-the-great|Frederick II of Prussia]] later used that claim to justify his invasion of [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], which [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] won in 1742. [[e:brzeg|Brzeg]] became part of [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

danta-state.t: A Parmar Rajput state in the hills of northern Gujarat whose rulers were hereditary guardians of the Ambaji temple, one of India's major goddess shrines.
danta-state.o: The ruling [[e:parmar-rajputs|Parmar Rajputs]] claimed descent from the [[s:paramara-dynasty|Paramara dynasty]] of [[e:malwa|Malwa]]; tradition dates their rule at Danta to 1068. Little is reliably known about the state's early centuries.
danta-state.r: Danta was a small, hilly state on the border of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]]. Its importance came from the Ambaji temple within its territory, whose management and offerings were controlled by the [[e:maharana|Maharana]]. Under British rule it belonged to the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|Mahi Kantha]] and later the [[e:banas-kantha-agency|Banas Kantha Agency]].
danta-state.e: Danta acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947 and merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948; it is now in [[e:banaskantha-district|Banaskantha district]], [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]. The Ambaji temple remains a major pilgrimage site.

duchy-of-holstein-gottorp.t: The ducal branch of the Danish royal house that shared Schleswig and Holstein with the kings and later produced the tsars of Russia.
duchy-of-holstein-gottorp.o: In 1544 King [[e:christian-iii-of-denmark|Christian III of Denmark]] divided [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] and [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] with his half-brothers. Adolf received the Gottorp share, ruled from Gottorp castle at Schleswig, founding the house of Holstein-Gottorp; its lands lay intermingled with the royal parts of the [[s:duchy-of-schleswig|Duchy of Schleswig]] and the [[s:duchy-of-holstein|Duchy of Holstein]].
duchy-of-holstein-gottorp.r: The dukes kept a splendid Lutheran court at Gottorp, where Duke [[e:frederick-iii-duke-of-holstein-gottorp|Frederick III]] founded [[e:friedrichstadt|Friedrichstadt]] for [[e:dutch|Dutch]] [[e:remonstrants|Remonstrants]] and sponsored [[e:adam-olearius|Adam Olearius's]] embassy to [[e:persia|Persia]] and the great Gottorp globe. Allied with the [[s:swedish-empire|Swedish Empire]] against [[e:denmark|Denmark]], they won full [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] over their part of [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] in 1658, only to lose it in the Great Northern War.
duchy-of-holstein-gottorp.e: [[e:denmark|Denmark]] seized the Gottorp lands in [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] in 1713, a loss confirmed in 1720. Duke [[e:charles-frederick-duke-of-holstein-gottorp|Charles Frederick]]'s son became [[e:tsar|Tsar]] [[e:peter-iii-of-russia|Peter III of Russia]], and in 1773 Peter's son Paul exchanged the Gottorp part of [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] with Denmark for [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]], ending the duchy.

dendi-kingdom.t: The rump Songhai kingdom that held out on the Niger after the Moroccan conquest of 1591, under a continuing line of askias.
dendi-kingdom.o: After the defeat of the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]] at [[e:battle-of-tondibi|Tondibi]] in 1591, [[e:askia-nuh|Askia Nuh]] led the survivors south down the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] into the province of [[e:dendi|Dendi]], in present-day south-western Niger and northern [[e:benin-empire|Benin]]. From there he waged a [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] war against the Moroccan forces and kept the Songhai dynasty alive.
dendi-kingdom.r: The askias of [[e:dendi|Dendi]] ruled from Lulami and other river towns over [[e:songhai-people|Songhay]] farmers and fishermen, keeping court titles from the old empire. The kingdom later split into several small Songhay chiefdoms. They fought the [[e:arma-people|Arma]] of the [[s:pashalik-of-timbuktu|Pashalik of Timbuktu]], the [[e:tuareg|Tuareg]] and the [[e:fula|Fulani]].
dendi-kingdom.e: The [[e:dendi|Dendi]] states came under French control at the turn of the 20th century and became part of the [[s:colony-of-niger|Colony of Niger]]. The Dendi people and language of northern [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] preserve the name.

dregovichs.t: An East Slavic tribe of the Pripyat marshes, whose lands around Turov later formed one of the principalities of Rus'.
dregovichs.o: The Dregovichs settled the wet, forested lands between the [[e:pripyat-river|Pripyat]] and the [[e:western-dvina|Western Dvina]] in the 7th and 8th centuries. Their name is usually derived from a Slavic word for bog. [[e:constantine-vii|Constantine VII]] mentions them as [[s:drougoubitai|Drougoubitai]], paying tribute to the Rus', in the 10th century.
dregovichs.r: They lived in small villages and [[e:hill-fort|hill forts]] and farmed the drier ground, supplementing this with hunting, fishing and beekeeping. The river [[e:pripyat-river|Pripyat]] linked them to the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]] and to [[e:kyiv|Kiev]], which made them early tributaries of the Kievan princes. The chronicle records that they had their own princely rule before Rus' control, but no names survive.
dregovichs.e: By the 10th century the Dregovichs had been absorbed into [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']]. [[e:turov|Turov]] became the seat of a princely line, and the territory developed into the [[s:principality-of-turov-and-pinsk|Principality of Turov and Pinsk]]. Their land is now southern [[e:belarus|Belarus]].

duchy-of-scinawa.t: Small Silesian Piast duchy on the Oder, split off from Głogów in the late 13th century and repeatedly passed between related princes.
duchy-of-scinawa.o: After the death of [[e:konrad-i-of-glogow|Konrad I of Głogów]] in 1274, his lands were divided among his sons, and [[e:scinawa|Ścinawa]] on the [[e:oder-river|Oder]], with its surrounding district, became the seat of a small separate duchy. Its first rulers included [[e:przemko-of-scinawa|Przemko of Ścinawa]], who died fighting in 1289.
duchy-of-scinawa.r: Little is known of its internal history. The duchy was a modest territory of farmland and small towns between [[e:glogow|Głogów]] and [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]], ruled by [[e:piast-dynasty|Silesian Piasts]] who often held other lands as well, and it passed back and forth within the Głogów branch. Its dukes accepted Bohemian overlordship in the 1320s and 1330s.
duchy-of-scinawa.e: The duchy was absorbed back into the lands of the [[e:glogow|Głogów]] and [[e:piast-dynasty|Żagań Piasts]] in the mid 14th century, by 1365, and later followed them under the Bohemian crown. [[e:scinawa|Ścinawa]] is now a small town in [[e:poland|Poland]].

dewas-junior.t: The junior of the two Maratha Puar states that shared the town of Dewas in Malwa, descended from Jivaji Rao Puar.
dewas-junior.o: [[e:dewas|Dewas]] Junior shares its origin with [[s:dewas-senior|Dewas Senior]]: the brothers [[e:tukoji-rao-i-puar|Tukoji Rao]] and [[e:jivaji-rao-puar|Jivaji Rao Puar]] received Dewas around 1728 after campaigning in [[e:malwa|Malwa]] with [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]] [[e:baji-rao-i|Baji Rao I]]. The Junior Branch descends from Jivaji Rao, and the two lines became separate states holding interlocking villages.
dewas-junior.r: The two branches kept separate palaces and administrations in the same town and even shared the main street, an arrangement that puzzled British officials of the [[e:central-india-agency|Central India Agency]]. [[e:dewas|Dewas]] Junior was a [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] state with a Raja, later [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]], and a modest revenue.
dewas-junior.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]], [[e:dewas|Dewas]] Junior merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948, which became part of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. The twin palaces still stand in Dewas.

dobunni.t: Cotswold kingdom whose coins name a string of rulers, and whose Roman town at Cirencester became the second largest in Britain.
dobunni.o: The Dobunni held [[e:gloucestershire|Gloucestershire]], north [[e:somerset|Somerset]], [[e:worcestershire|Worcestershire]] and parts of [[e:oxfordshire|Oxfordshire]] and [[e:wiltshire|Wiltshire]] in the late [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. By the 1st century BCE they were minting coins, and a large oppidum developed at [[e:bagendon|Bagendon]] near [[e:cirencester|Cirencester]], with Roman imports reaching it before the conquest.
dobunni.r: Their gold and [[e:silver|silver]] coins carry the names of rulers such as Corio, Bodvoc, Anted and Eisu, sometimes thought to mark a divided kingdom with northern and southern halves. The economy rested on sheep and cereal farming in the [[e:cotswolds|Cotswolds]] and on the salt springs of [[e:droitwich-spa|Droitwich]]. [[e:cassius-dio|Cassius Dio]] records that part of the Bodunni, probably the Dobunni, had been subject to the [[s:catuvellauni|Catuvellauni]].
dobunni.e: In 43 part of the Dobunni surrendered to [[e:aulus-plautius|Aulus Plautius]], and the region came under Roman control without major recorded conflict. A fort was built at [[e:cirencester|Cirencester]], and the town of [[e:corinium-dobunnorum|Corinium Dobunnorum]] grew into the civitas capital and second largest town of [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

duchy-of-naples.t: Byzantine duchy that became an independent city-state, resisting Lombards and Arabs for nearly five centuries until the Normans took it in 1137.
duchy-of-naples.o: [[e:naples|Naples]] remained in Byzantine hands after the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] conquest. In 661 [[e:constans-ii|Emperor Constans II]] appointed Basil as its first duke, subject to the [[e:strategos|strategos]] of [[e:sicily|Sicily]]. Over the next century the dukes came from local families, and [[e:stephen-ii-of-naples|Duke Stephen II]], who also became [[e:bishop|bishop]], ruled with little reference to [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]].
duchy-of-naples.r: [[e:naples|Naples]] was a Greek-[[e:latin|Latin]] city of merchants and landowners, governed by dukes who also controlled [[s:cumae|Cumae]], [[e:sorrento|Sorrento]] and [[s:republic-of-amalfi|Amalfi]] for a time. [[e:sergius-i-of-naples|Sergius I]] founded a hereditary dynasty in 840. The duchy fought the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombards]] of [[e:benevento|Benevento]], but sometimes allied with Arab raiders, earning papal condemnation. Greek liturgy and learning survived alongside Latin, and Naples kept a strong civic identity.
duchy-of-naples.e: The Normans conquered the surrounding lands in the 11th and 12th centuries. After resisting a long siege in 1135–37, Duke [[e:sergius-vii-of-naples|Sergius VII]] made peace with [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]] and was killed fighting for him at [[e:battle-of-rignano|Rignano]] in 1137; after a brief interlude of self-rule, [[e:naples|Naples]] submitted to Roger in 1139 and joined the [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]]. It later became capital of the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]].

duchy-of-wroclaw.t: Lower Silesian Piast duchy centred on Wrocław, whose duke Henry IV Probus sought the Polish crown before the duchy passed to Bohemia.
duchy-of-wroclaw.o: In 1248 the sons of [[e:henry-ii-the-pious|Henry II the Pious]] divided the [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Duchy of Silesia]]. [[e:henry-iii-the-white|Henry III the White]] received [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]], the richest city of the region, and its surrounding lands, while his brother [[e:boleslaw-ii-the-bald|Bolesław II]] took [[e:legnica|Legnica]]. Wrocław had been rebuilt after the Mongol attack of 1241 and refounded under German town law.
duchy-of-wroclaw.r: The dukes ruled a prosperous land of grain, cloth and trade, encouraging German settlers alongside the Polish population. [[e:henry-iv-probus|Henry IV Probus]], also remembered as a minnesinger, won [[e:krakow|Kraków]] and tried to unite [[e:poland|Poland]] before his death in 1290. [[e:henry-v-the-fat|Henry V the Fat]] and [[e:henry-vi-the-good|Henry VI the Good]] lost lands to their relatives and had to balance [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] against Poland.
duchy-of-wroclaw.e: [[e:henry-vi-the-good|Henry VI the Good]] recognised the overlordship of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]] in 1327. On his death in 1335 the duchy passed directly to the Bohemian crown. [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]] remained Bohemian and [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] until [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] took [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] in 1742, and it has been Polish since 1945.

duchy-of-volhynia.t: The Lithuanian-ruled duchy of Volhynia, held by Lubart and later Svidrigaila from the great castle at Lutsk.
duchy-of-volhynia.o: When the [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-volhynia|Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia]] collapsed after 1340, [[e:lubart|Lubart]], a son of [[e:gediminas|Gediminas]] who had married into the local dynasty, took control of [[e:volhynia|Volhynia]]. For decades he fought [[e:casimir-iii-the-great|Casimir III]] of [[e:poland|Poland]] for the whole inheritance of Galicia-Volhynia, holding Volhynia while Poland kept [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]].
duchy-of-volhynia.r: [[e:lubart|Lubart]] built the brick castle at [[e:lutsk|Lutsk]] that still bears his name, and his rule mixed Lithuanian princes with [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] Ruthenian nobles and church. The duchy had its own court and was one of the most valuable lands of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]]. Later [[e:svitrigaila|Svidrigaila]], a son of [[e:algirdas|Algirdas]], ruled it from the 1430s after losing the struggle for the grand ducal throne.
duchy-of-volhynia.e: After [[e:svitrigaila|Svidrigaila]] died in 1452, [[e:volhynia|Volhynia]] lost its status as a separate duchy and became a voivodeship of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]]. In 1569 the [[e:union-of-lublin|Union of Lublin]] transferred it to the Polish Crown.

duchy-of-the-archipelago.t: Latin duchy of the Cyclades centred on Naxos, founded by the Venetian Marco Sanudo, which outlived most crusader states in Greece by more than a century.
duchy-of-the-archipelago.o: Around 1207 [[e:marco-sanudo|Marco Sanudo]], nephew of the doge [[e:enrico-dandolo|Enrico Dandolo]], led a private Venetian expedition that conquered [[s:naxos|Naxos]] and other Cycladic islands, sharing some with fellow adventurers. He took the title Duke of the Archipelago under the suzerainty of the [[s:latin-empire|Latin Empire]] and later of the [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]].
duchy-of-the-archipelago.r: The dukes ruled from the Kastro of [[s:naxos|Naxos]], granting fiefs to [[e:latin|Latin]] lords on islands such as [[s:andros|Andros]], [[s:paros|Paros]] and [[s:melos|Milos]]. A Catholic minority lived alongside a Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] majority, which kept its church. Revenues came from agriculture, emery and trade. In 1383 Francesco I [[e:crispo-family|Crispo]] seized the duchy and founded a new dynasty.
duchy-of-the-archipelago.e: [[e:hayreddin-barbarossa|Barbarossa]]'s raids of 1537 made the duchy an Ottoman tributary. In 1566 the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] deposed [[e:giacomo-iv-crispo|Giacomo IV Crispo]] and gave the duchy to the Jewish financier [[e:joseph-nasi|Joseph Nasi]], who ruled through a deputy. After his death in 1579 it was annexed to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]].

duchy-of-saxe-eisenach.t: Ernestine Saxon duchy around the Wartburg, birthplace of Johann Sebastian Bach, later merged with Weimar.
duchy-of-saxe-eisenach.o: After the 1662 division of Saxe-[[e:weimar|Weimar]], [[e:eisenach|Eisenach]] was briefly held by [[e:adolf-william-duke-of-saxe-eisenach|Adolf William]], whose line ended in 1671. In 1672 [[e:john-george-i-duke-of-saxe-eisenach|John George I]], previously lord of Marksuhl, received Eisenach as a separate Duchy of Saxe-Eisenach, founding the line that ruled it until 1741.
duchy-of-saxe-eisenach.r: The duchy took in parts of Saxe-[[e:jena|Jena]] in 1690. It was Lutheran, with the [[e:wartburg|Wartburg]] castle, where [[e:martin-luther|Luther]] had translated the [[e:new-testament|New Testament]], as its landmark. [[e:johann-sebastian-bach|Johann Sebastian Bach]] was born in [[e:eisenach|Eisenach]] in 1685, the son of a town musician, and [[e:georg-philipp-telemann|Georg Philipp Telemann]] served as [[e:kapellmeister|Kapellmeister]] at the Eisenach court. [[e:johann-wilhelm-duke-of-saxe-eisenach|Johann Wilhelm]] ruled from 1698 to 1729.
duchy-of-saxe-eisenach.e: Duke [[e:william-henry-duke-of-saxe-eisenach|William Henry]] died without heirs in 1741, and the duchy passed to [[e:ernest-augustus-i-duke-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|Ernest Augustus I of Saxe-Weimar]], creating the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|Duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach]], which lasted until 1918.

duchy-of-normandy.t: The Viking settlement on the lower Seine that became one of Europe's best-run principalities and launched the Norman conquest of England.
duchy-of-normandy.o: In 911, by the [[e:treaty-of-saint-clair-sur-epte|Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte]], [[e:charles-the-simple|King Charles the Simple]] granted lands around [[e:rouen|Rouen]] to the [[e:vikings|Viking]] leader [[e:rollo|Rollo]] in return for defending the [[e:seine|Seine]]. Rollo's descendants expanded westwards to the Cotentin, adopted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and the [[e:french-language|French language]], and were styled dukes by the early 11th century.
duchy-of-normandy.r: The dukes built unusually firm control over their barons, castles and the Church. Monasteries such as [[e:jumieges-abbey|Jumièges]], [[e:fecamp-abbey|Fécamp]], [[e:bec-abbey|Bec]] and [[e:mont-saint-michel|Mont-Saint-Michel]] flourished, and Bec produced the scholars [[e:lanfranc|Lanfranc]] and [[e:anselm-of-canterbury|Anselm]]. Normans also carved out lands in southern [[e:italy|Italy]] and [[e:sicily|Sicily]]. In 1066 [[e:william-the-conqueror|Duke William]] won the battle of [[e:battle-of-hastings|Hastings]] and became king of [[e:england|England]].
duchy-of-normandy.e: Normandy passed to the [[e:house-of-plantagenet|Plantagenets]] and formed a pillar of the [[s:angevin-empire|Angevin Empire]]. [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II of France]] took [[e:chateau-gaillard|Château Gaillard]] and [[e:rouen|Rouen]] in 1204, annexing the duchy to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]. The [[e:channel-islands|Channel Islands]] remained with the English crown.

duchy-of-thuringia.t: A Frankish frontier duchy in central Germany, set up against the Slavs, whose dukes briefly ruled almost independently before Carolingian absorption.
duchy-of-thuringia.o: After the [[s:franks|Franks]] destroyed the [[s:kingdom-of-the-thuringians|Kingdom of the Thuringians]] in 531, the area was ruled by Frankish officials. Around 633 [[e:dagobert-i|King Dagobert I]] appointed Radulf duke to defend the eastern frontier against the [[e:slavs|Slavs]] of [[s:samos-empire|Samo's Empire]], then raiding [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]]. Radulf later defeated Dagobert's son [[e:sigebert-iii|Sigebert III]] in 641 and ruled as a near-independent king.
duchy-of-thuringia.r: Later [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] was held by the Hedenid dukes, based at [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] on the Main. Duke [[e:heden-ii|Heden II]] supported the [[e:anglo-saxons|Anglo-Saxon]] missionary [[e:willibrord|Willibrord]], who received estates at [[e:arnstadt|Arnstadt]] in 704, and a church was founded on the [[e:marienberg-fortress|Marienberg]] at Würzburg. The duchy guarded the border with the [[s:saxons|Saxons]] and the [[s:sorbs|Sorbs]].
duchy-of-thuringia.e: [[e:heden-ii|Heden II]] disappears around 717 to 719, perhaps after the [[e:battle-of-vincy|Battle of Vincy]], and [[e:charles-martel|Charles Martel]] brought [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] under direct Frankish control. [[e:saint-boniface|Saint Boniface]] reorganised its church, founding the bishopric of [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] in 742. The region later formed part of the [[s:duchy-of-saxony|Duchy of Saxony]] and the [[s:landgraviate-of-thuringia|Landgraviate of Thuringia]].

duchy-of-saxe-zeitz.t: Short-lived Albertine Saxon duchy based on the old bishopric of Naumburg-Zeitz, created by an elector's will.
duchy-of-saxe-zeitz.o: In his will, [[e:john-george-i-elector-of-saxony|Elector John George]] I of [[e:saxony|Saxony]] created three secondary duchies for his younger sons. After his death in 1656, [[e:maurice-duke-of-saxe-zeitz|Maurice]] received [[e:zeitz|Zeitz]] with the secularised bishopric of [[e:naumburg|Naumburg]] and lands in the [[s:lordship-of-plauen|Vogtland]] and around Neustadt an der Orla, founding the Duchy of Saxe-Zeitz.
duchy-of-saxe-zeitz.r: [[e:maurice-duke-of-saxe-zeitz|Maurice]] built [[e:moritzburg-zeitz|Moritzburg]] palace in [[e:zeitz|Zeitz]] as his residence and kept a Lutheran court. The duchy remained under the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]'s [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] in foreign and military affairs. His son [[e:maurice-william-duke-of-saxe-zeitz|Maurice William]] converted to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] in 1715, a shock to his Lutheran subjects, and his relative [[e:christian-august-of-saxe-zeitz|Christian August]] became a Catholic cardinal and archbishop of [[e:esztergom|Esztergom]].
duchy-of-saxe-zeitz.e: [[e:maurice-william-duke-of-saxe-zeitz|Maurice William]] died without surviving male heirs in 1718, and the duchy reverted to the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]. [[e:zeitz|Zeitz]] passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815 and lies today in [[e:saxony-anhalt|Saxony-Anhalt]].

duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia.t: Baltic duchy of the Kettler dynasty under Polish overlordship, famous for Duke Jacob's colonies in Africa and the Caribbean.
duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia.o: When the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] dissolved in 1561, its last master, [[e:gotthard-kettler|Gotthard Kettler]], secularised the Order's lands south of the [[e:western-dvina|Daugava]] and became hereditary Duke of [[e:courland|Courland]] and [[s:semigallians|Semigallia]], a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]]. The duchy's capital was [[e:jelgava|Mitau]] (Jelgava).
duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia.r: The Lutheran Baltic German nobility dominated the duchy, holding Latvian peasants in [[e:serfdom|serfdom]], and the dukes often clashed with them. [[e:jacob-kettler|Duke Jacob Kettler]] (1642-1682) built ironworks, shipyards and a merchant fleet, and founded colonies at [[s:courland-gambia|Courland Gambia]] and [[s:courland-tobago|Courland Tobago]]. In the 18th century Russian influence grew; [[e:ernst-johann-von-biron|Ernst Johann von Biron]], favourite of [[e:anna-of-russia|Empress Anna]], became duke in 1737 and built [[e:rundale-palace|Rundāle Palace]].
duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia.e: Wars, especially the [[e:great-northern-war|Great Northern War]], ruined the duchy's prosperity. After the [[e:third-partition-of-poland|Third Partition of Poland]] in 1795, the [[e:courland|Courland]] nobility submitted to [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine the Great]], and the duchy was annexed by [[e:russia|Russia]], becoming the [[s:governorate-of-courland|Governorate of Courland]].

dutch-brazil.t: The Dutch West India Company's colony in northeastern Brazil, which under Johan Maurits briefly made Recife a centre of art, science and religious tolerance.
dutch-brazil.o: During the Eighty Years' War against [[e:spain|Spain]], which then ruled Portugal, the [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] attacked [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] coast. After a failed occupation of [[e:salvador|Salvador]] in 1624 and 1625, a [[e:dutch|Dutch]] fleet captured [[e:olinda|Olinda]] and [[e:recife|Recife]] in [[s:captaincy-of-pernambuco|Pernambuco]] in 1630 and gradually extended control along the coast from [[e:sergipe|Sergipe]] to [[e:maranhao|Maranhão]].
dutch-brazil.r: Count [[e:johan-maurits-of-nassau-siegen|Johan Maurits of Nassau-Siegen]] governed from 1637 to 1644. He built [[e:mauritsstad|Mauritsstad]] beside [[e:recife|Recife]], restored [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] production and seized Portuguese slave-trading posts in [[e:africa|Africa]]. He brought the painters [[e:frans-post|Frans Post]] and [[e:albert-eckhout|Albert Eckhout]] and the naturalists [[e:georg-marcgraf|Georg Marcgraf]] and [[e:willem-piso|Willem Piso]], whose work was the first scientific study of [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. Catholics and [[e:jews|Jews]] enjoyed toleration, and Recife's [[e:kahal-zur-israel-synagogue|Kahal Zur Israel]] was the first synagogue in the [[e:americas|Americas]].
dutch-brazil.e: After [[e:johan-maurits-of-nassau-siegen|Johan Maurits]] left, Portuguese planters rose in 1645 and defeated the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] at the [[e:battles-of-guararapes|Battles of Guararapes]] in 1648 and 1649. [[e:recife|Recife]] surrendered in 1654, and by the [[e:treaty-of-the-hague-1661|Treaty of The Hague]] in 1661 the Dutch renounced [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] for a payment. Many [[e:jews|Jews]] from Recife later settled in [[e:new-amsterdam|New Amsterdam]].
dutch-brazil.re: Dutch Reformed Church, Roman Catholicism, Judaism

duchy-of-bavaria-ingolstadt.t: A short-lived Bavarian duchy ruled from Ingolstadt, best known for its brilliant and quarrelsome duke Louis the Bearded.
duchy-of-bavaria-ingolstadt.o: In the Bavarian partition of 1392 [[e:stephen-iii-duke-of-bavaria|Stephen III]] received the lands around [[e:ingolstadt|Ingolstadt]], scattered across [[e:upper-bavaria|Upper Bavaria]]. His daughter [[e:isabeau-of-bavaria|Isabeau]] married King [[e:charles-vi-of-france|Charles VI of France]], giving the house close ties with the French court.
duchy-of-bavaria-ingolstadt.r: Stephen's son [[e:louis-vii-duke-of-bavaria|Louis VII the Bearded]] spent years at the French court and returned with great wealth, building the New Castle and the [[e:liebfrauenmunster-ingolstadt|Church of Our Lady]] in [[e:ingolstadt|Ingolstadt]]. He was constantly at war with his cousins in [[e:landshut|Landshut]] and [[e:munich|Munich]] and was placed under the imperial ban. In 1443 he was captured in a conflict that involved his own son, [[e:louis-viii-duke-of-bavaria|Louis the Hunchback]].
duchy-of-bavaria-ingolstadt.e: [[e:louis-viii-duke-of-bavaria|Louis the Hunchback]] died in 1445 and his father in 1447 as a prisoner at [[e:burghausen|Burghausen]], ending the line. The duchy passed to [[e:henry-xvi-duke-of-bavaria|Henry XVI]] of the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-landshut|Duchy of Bavaria-Landshut]]. [[e:ingolstadt|Ingolstadt]] later became the seat of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria's]] first university, founded in 1472.

duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach.t: Thuringian duchy whose court at Weimar drew Goethe, Schiller, Herder and Wieland and became the heart of German classicism.
duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach.o: Saxe-[[e:weimar|Weimar]] and Saxe-[[e:eisenach|Eisenach]] were united in 1741 when [[e:ernest-augustus-i-duke-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|Duke Ernest Augustus]] I of Saxe-Weimar inherited Eisenach on the extinction of its ducal line, creating Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach.
duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach.r: Duchess [[e:anna-amalia-of-brunswick-wolfenbuttel|Anna Amalia]], regent from 1758, invited [[e:christoph-martin-wieland|Christoph Martin Wieland]] as tutor; her son [[e:charles-augustus-grand-duke-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|Charles Augustus]] brought [[e:johann-wolfgang-von-goethe|Goethe]] to [[e:weimar|Weimar]] in 1775, later followed by [[e:johann-gottfried-herder|Herder]] and [[e:friedrich-schiller|Schiller]], while the [[e:university-of-jena|University of Jena]] flourished. Raised to a grand duchy in 1815, it adopted one of the first German constitutions in 1816. Later grand dukes hosted [[e:franz-liszt|Franz Liszt]] and founded the Weimar art school.
duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach.e: The grand duchy joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871. Grand Duke [[e:william-ernest-grand-duke-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|William Ernest]] abdicated in November 1918, and in 1920 the territory joined the [[s:free-state-of-thuringia|Free State of Thuringia]], with [[e:weimar|Weimar]] as capital.

district-of-brankovic.t: Lordship of Vuk Branković in Kosovo and northern Macedonia, rich in silver mines, which later merged into the Serbian Despotate.
district-of-brankovic.o: [[e:vuk-brankovic|Vuk Branković]], son-in-law of [[e:lazar-of-serbia|Prince Lazar]], built up lands in [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] after the collapse of the [[s:serbian-empire|Serbian Empire]]. From about 1371 he held [[e:pristina|Priština]], Peć and the mining districts, and later took [[e:skopje|Skopje]], ruling as Lazar's ally.
district-of-brankovic.r: [[e:vuk-brankovic|Vuk]] ruled from [[e:pristina|Priština]] and [[e:vucitrn|Vučitrn]], drawing income from the [[e:silver|silver]] mines of [[e:trepca|Trepča]] and [[e:novo-brdo|Novo Brdo]] and protecting the [[e:serbian-patriarchate-of-pec|Patriarchate of Peć]]. He fought at [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] in 1389 and survived; later legend unjustly made him the traitor of the battle. Afterwards he resisted Ottoman [[e:vassal|vassalage]] longer than other Serbian lords, seeking help from [[e:hungary|Hungary]].
district-of-brankovic.e: The [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] captured [[e:vuk-brankovic|Vuk]] and he died in captivity in 1397. His sons, including [[e:durad-brankovic|Đurađ Branković]], held part of his lands as Ottoman [[e:vassal|vassals]] and in 1412 made peace with [[e:stefan-lazarevic|Stefan Lazarević]]; the district merged into the [[s:serbian-despotate|Serbian Despotate]], which Đurađ inherited in 1427.

dar-tama.t: A small sultanate of the Tama people in the hills of eastern Chad, long fought over by its powerful neighbours Wadai and Darfur.
dar-tama.o: The [[e:tama-people|Tama]], who speak a language of the Taman group, formed a sultanate in the hills around [[e:guereda|Guéréda]] in eastern [[e:chad|Chad]] by the 17th century. It lay on the frontier between the [[s:wadai-empire|Wadai Empire]] and the [[s:darfur-sultanate|Darfur Sultanate]].
dar-tama.r: The sultans ruled a farming and herding population from hilltop villages, relying on rough terrain for defence. Dar [[e:tama-people|Tama]] paid tribute to [[e:wadai-empire|Wadai]] for most of its history, while sometimes turning to [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]] for support. [[e:islam|Islam]] was adopted by the ruling house, and little else is known in detail.
dar-tama.e: French forces occupied eastern [[e:chad|Chad]] after defeating [[e:wadai-empire|Wadai]] in 1909, and Dar [[e:tama-people|Tama]] came under French control around 1912. Its sultan became a traditional chief within the colony of [[s:chad-french-colony|Chad (French colony)]].

daorsi.t: Hellenised Illyrian people of the lower Neretva, whose walled hill town of Daorson near Stolac minted its own coins.
daorsi.o: The Daorsi emerged in the [[e:neretva|Neretva]] valley of [[e:herzegovina|Herzegovina]], in contact with Greek traders at [[e:narona|Narona]] and the island colonies of the Adriatic. By the 3rd century BCE they had a fortified centre at [[e:daorson|Daorson]], on a hill near modern [[e:stolac|Stolac]], enclosed by massive Cyclopean walls.
daorsi.r: Greek influence was strong: the Daorsi struck bronze coins with Greek legends, used Greek-style buildings and traded wine, oil and pottery through the [[e:neretva|Neretva]]. They broke with the Illyrian king [[e:gentius|Gentius]] and sided with [[e:rome|Rome]] in 168 BCE, which rewarded them with exemption from tribute. Their wealthier neighbours, the [[s:delmatae|Delmatae]], repeatedly attacked them.
daorsi.e: [[e:daorson|Daorson]] was destroyed in the mid-1st century BCE, probably by the [[s:delmatae|Delmatae]]. The Daorsi were absorbed into [[e:illyricum-roman-province|Roman Illyricum]] by the end of the 1st century BCE, and their region later belonged to the province of [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]].

duchy-of-carniola.t: The Habsburg duchy at the heart of modern Slovenia, centred on Ljubljana, a borderland between the German, Slovene and Italian worlds.
duchy-of-carniola.o: [[e:carniola|Carniola]] appears as a march of the Empire around 1040, a frontier zone against [[e:hungary|Hungary]]. Over the next two centuries it was held by various families, including the Weimar-Orlamünde counts, the patriarchs of [[e:aquileia|Aquileia]] and the [[e:house-of-andechs|Andechs]]. The [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] acquired it in 1335 with [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]], and [[e:rudolf-iv-duke-of-austria|Rudolf IV]] called himself Duke of Carniola in 1364.
duchy-of-carniola.r: [[e:carniola|Carniola's]] population was mainly Slovene peasants under German-speaking nobility. [[e:ljubljana|Ljubljana]] (Laibach) was the capital. Ottoman raids struck repeatedly from the 15th century. [[e:primoz-trubar|Primož Trubar]] printed the first books in Slovene in 1550, and the polymath [[e:johann-weikhard-von-valvasor|Johann Weikhard von Valvasor]] described the land in [[e:the-glory-of-the-duchy-of-carniola|The Glory of the Duchy of Carniola]] in 1689.
duchy-of-carniola.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] included [[e:carniola|Carniola]] in the [[s:illyrian-provinces|Illyrian Provinces]] from 1809 to 1813, then it returned to [[e:austria|Austria]]. It was a crown land of [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] until 1918, when it joined the [[s:state-of-slovenes-croats-and-serbs|State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs]] and later [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]]. Its core is part of modern [[e:slovenia|Slovenia]].

duchy-of-brunswick.t: North German duchy of the House of Welf, ruled by the 'Black Duke' and later the subject of a long succession dispute.
duchy-of-brunswick.o: [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel]] had been absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] in 1807. [[e:frederick-william-duke-of-brunswick-wolfenbuttel|Duke Frederick William]], the Black Duke, who had fought [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] with his [[e:black-brunswickers|Black Brunswickers]], recovered his lands in 1813, and in 1815 the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] recognised them as the sovereign Duchy of [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]]. He was killed at [[e:battle-of-quatre-bras|Quatre Bras]] that June.
duchy-of-brunswick.r: His son [[e:charles-ii-duke-of-brunswick|Charles II]] was driven out by a rising in 1830 and replaced by his brother William, who granted a constitution in 1832. The duchy was Lutheran and had industry around [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]], with [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] beet and canning. When William died in 1884, [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] blocked the Hanoverian heir, and regents ruled until [[e:ernest-augustus-duke-of-brunswick|Ernest Augustus]] married the [[e:kaiser|Kaiser's]] daughter [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]] Louise in 1913 and became duke.
duchy-of-brunswick.e: [[e:ernest-augustus-duke-of-brunswick|Ernest Augustus]] abdicated in November 1918, and the duchy became the [[s:free-state-of-brunswick|Free State of Brunswick]]. In 1946 its territory was merged into the new state of [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]], though the city of [[e:brunswick|Braunschweig]] keeps the ducal palace, rebuilt in 2007.

deogarh-kingdom.t: A Gond kingdom of the Satpura hills whose rulers founded Nagpur and were eventually displaced by the Bhonsle Marathas.
deogarh-kingdom.o: The [[e:gond-people|Gond]] kingdom of Deogarh emerged in the [[e:chhindwara-district|Chhindwara]] region of the [[e:satpura-range|Satpura]] hills in the late 16th century. Its first well-attested ruler, Jatba, is mentioned in Mughal sources and acknowledged [[e:akbar|Akbar's]] suzerainty, as recorded in the [[e:ain-i-akbari|Ain-i-Akbari]].
deogarh-kingdom.r: Deogarh ruled [[e:gond-people|Gond]] farming and forest communities and grew under [[e:bakht-buland-shah|Bakht Buland Shah]], who served [[e:aurangzeb|Aurangzeb]], converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] and encouraged [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and Muslim settlers to clear land. He founded the city of [[e:nagpur|Nagpur]] around 1702, which became the capital under his son [[e:chand-sultan|Chand Sultan]].
deogarh-kingdom.e: After [[e:chand-sultan|Chand Sultan's]] death in 1739 a succession dispute invited [[e:raghuji-i-bhonsle|Raghoji Bhonsle]] of the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] to intervene, and by 1743 he had taken effective control, making [[e:nagpur|Nagpur]] the seat of the Bhonsle Maratha state. The [[e:gond-people|Gond]] family survived as pensioners.

duchy-of-saxe-meiningen.t: Ernestine duchy in the Werra valley whose 'theatre duke' George II made its court troupe the most influential in Europe.
duchy-of-saxe-meiningen.o: [[e:bernhard-i-duke-of-saxe-meiningen|Bernhard I]], third son of [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-gotha|Ernest the Pious]], received [[e:meiningen|Meiningen]] in the 1680 partition of the Saxe-[[e:gotha|Gotha]] inheritance and made the small town his residence, building [[e:elisabethenburg-palace|Elisabethenburg Palace]]. The duchy later gained parts of Saxe-[[e:romhild|Römhild]] and, in the 1826 redistribution, [[e:hildburghausen|Hildburghausen]] and [[e:saalfeld|Saalfeld]].
duchy-of-saxe-meiningen.r: The duchy was Lutheran and largely rural, with forestry and small industries. [[e:george-ii-duke-of-saxe-meiningen|George II]], who reigned from 1866, personally directed the court [[e:theatre|theatre]]; the [[e:meiningen-ensemble|Meininger]] company toured [[e:europe|Europe]] from 1874 with historically accurate staging and disciplined ensemble acting, influencing [[e:konstantin-stanislavski|Stanislavski]]. The court orchestra under [[e:hans-von-bulow|Hans von Bülow]] and [[e:fritz-steinbach|Fritz Steinbach]] was associated with [[e:johannes-brahms|Johannes Brahms]].
duchy-of-saxe-meiningen.e: Saxe-[[e:meiningen|Meiningen]] sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866, forcing Duke [[e:bernhard-ii-duke-of-saxe-meiningen|Bernhard II]] to abdicate in favour of [[e:george-ii-duke-of-saxe-meiningen|George II]]. It joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871. [[e:bernhard-iii-duke-of-saxe-meiningen|Bernhard III]] abdicated in November 1918, and in 1920 the state merged into the [[s:free-state-of-thuringia|Free State of Thuringia]].

duchy-of-legnica.t: The longest-lived Silesian Piast duchy, ruled from Legnica until 1675 and home to the first Protestant university project in Europe.
duchy-of-legnica.o: In the 1248 partition of the [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Duchy of Silesia]], [[e:boleslaw-ii-the-bald|Bolesław II the Bald]], son of [[e:henry-ii-the-pious|Henry II the Pious]] who died fighting the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] near [[e:legnica|Legnica]] in 1241, received the duchy around Legnica. His successors also gained [[e:brzeg|Brzeg]] and at times [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]].
duchy-of-legnica.r: The [[e:legnica|Legnica]] [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]] accepted Bohemian overlordship in 1329 while keeping their ducal rule. The duchy prospered from agriculture, mining and cloth. [[e:frederick-ii-of-legnica|Frederick II of Legnica]] introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]] in the 1520s and founded a university in 1526, the first Protestant one, though it soon closed. The dukes later adopted the Reformed faith and maintained a cultivated court at Legnica and [[e:brzeg|Brzeg]].
duchy-of-legnica.e: The last [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] duke, [[e:george-william-duke-of-legnica|George William]], died in 1675, ending the dynasty that had ruled since the 10th century. The duchy passed to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and in 1742 to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]. [[e:legnica|Legnica]] has been part of [[e:poland|Poland]] since 1945.
duchy-of-legnica.re: Catholicism, then Lutheranism and Reformed Protestantism

duchy-of-ksani.t: A Georgian highland duchy in the Ksani valley whose hereditary eristavis guarded the routes north of Kartli for four centuries.
duchy-of-ksani.o: The Ksani valley north of [[e:mtskheta|Mtskheta]] was organised as a saeristavo, or duchy, of the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]], and from the late 14th century the office became hereditary in a local family known as the Ksani eristavis. After 1490 they served the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli|Kingdom of Kartli]], with their seat at Akhalgori.
duchy-of-ksani.r: The dukes ruled mountain communities of farmers and herders, raising troops for the kings and guarding passes towards [[e:ossetia|Ossetia]]. They often acted independently, intriguing with Persian governors and rival nobles. Two of their dukes, Shalva and Elizbar, rose with [[e:bidzina-cholokashvili|Bidzina Cholokashvili]] against Persian rule in 1659 and were executed by the shah, and the Georgian church venerates them as martyrs.
duchy-of-ksani.e: After repeated disloyalty, King [[e:erekle-ii|Erekle II]] abolished the duchy in 1777 and incorporated its lands into the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti|Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti]]. The family palace at Akhalgori survives, and the valley later became part of the Russian province of [[e:tbilisi|Tiflis]] after 1801.

duchy-of-swidnica.t: Piast duchy below the Sudetes whose duke Bolko II was the last Silesian prince independent of Bohemia, until his lands passed to the Bohemian crown in 1392.
duchy-of-swidnica.o: [[e:bolko-i-the-strict|Bolko I the Strict]], already Duke of [[e:jawor|Jawor]], acquired [[e:swidnica|Świdnica]] around 1291 and built a strong duchy along the Bohemian border. On his death in 1301 his son Bernard received Świdnica, which became a separate duchy. Bernard married a daughter of the Polish king [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Władysław I the Elbow-high]].
duchy-of-swidnica.r: [[e:swidnica|Świdnica]] was a prosperous town of cloth, beer and trade on the routes to [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]]. [[e:bolko-ii-the-small|Bolko II the Small]], Bernard's son, refused to accept Bohemian overlordship, ruling as an independent prince and uniting Świdnica with [[e:jawor|Jawor]] in 1346. Without sons, he arranged the marriage of his niece Anne to [[e:charles-iv|Charles IV]], making the Bohemian crown his heir.
duchy-of-swidnica.e: After [[e:bolko-ii-the-small|Bolko II]] died in 1368, his widow Agnes ruled until her death in 1392, when the duchy passed to the Bohemian crown. It later went to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], and has been Polish since 1945; its Peace Church is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

district-of-pilten.t: Small Baltic territory around Piltene, the remnant of the Bishopric of Courland, governed by its own nobles under the Polish crown until 1795.
district-of-pilten.o: After [[e:magnus-duke-of-holstein|Magnus of Holstein]] died in 1583, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] sold its rights to the former [[s:bishopric-of-courland|Bishopric of Courland]] to Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]] in 1585. The district, scattered around [[e:piltene|Pilten]] (Piltene) and [[e:aizpute|Hasenpoth]] in western [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]], was not merged into the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]] but held directly by the [[e:kingdom-of-poland|Polish crown]].
district-of-pilten.r: The local German nobility governed through their own diet and kept wide privileges, with a Lutheran church. The dukes of [[e:courland|Courland]] repeatedly claimed the district and controlled it for periods, while the nobles resisted, preferring the distant Polish king. Latvian peasants worked the estates as serfs.
district-of-pilten.e: With the [[e:third-partition-of-poland|Third Partition of Poland]] in 1795, [[e:piltene|Pilten]] was annexed by [[e:russia|Russia]] together with [[e:courland|Courland]] and absorbed into the [[s:governorate-of-courland|Governorate of Courland]]. Its separate status disappeared, though its nobility kept privileges as part of the Courland knighthood.

duchy-of-siewierz.t: A small Silesian duchy owned for almost 350 years by the bishops of Krakow, who styled themselves dukes of Siewierz.
duchy-of-siewierz.o: Siewierz, on the border of [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] and [[e:lesser-poland|Lesser Poland]], belonged to the Silesian duchies under Bohemian overlordship. In 1443 [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:zbigniew-olesnicki|Zbigniew Olesnicki]] of [[e:krakow|Krakow]] bought it from Duke Wenceslaus I of [[e:cieszyn|Cieszyn]], and from then on the bishops of Krakow ruled it as secular princes.
duchy-of-siewierz.r: The duchy was a small territory with its own laws, courts and officials, ruled from a castle at Siewierz. Its position between [[e:poland|Poland]] and [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] led to disputes about whether it belonged to the Polish Crown or the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]]. Its iron and lead workings brought income to the [[e:bishop|bishops]], who added the ducal title to their own.
duchy-of-siewierz.e: In 1790 the Great [[e:sejm|Sejm]] incorporated Siewierz into the Polish Crown, ending the [[e:bishop|bishops]]' secular rule. After the [[e:third-partition-of-poland|Third Partition]] in 1795 it passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-prussia|Kingdom of Prussia]], and later to the [[s:duchy-of-warsaw|Duchy of Warsaw]] and [[s:congress-poland|Congress Poland]].

duchy-of-montferrat.t: A Piedmontese duchy of the Gonzaga, whose fortress of Casale was one of the most contested strongholds in 17th-century Europe.
duchy-of-montferrat.o: The [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] of the [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Duchy of Mantua]] had inherited the [[s:march-of-montferrat|March of Montferrat]] in 1536. In 1574 [[e:maximilian-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Maximilian II]] raised it to a duchy for Duke [[e:guglielmo-gonzaga-duke-of-mantua|Guglielmo Gonzaga]], who governed it from Mantua through a council at [[e:casale-monferrato|Casale]].
duchy-of-montferrat.r: [[e:montferrat|Montferrat]] was a hilly wine-growing region split into two parts and surrounded by the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]] and the [[s:duchy-of-milan|Duchy of Milan]]. Its local nobles resented Mantuan rule. [[e:vincenzo-i-gonzaga|Vincenzo I Gonzaga]] built the great citadel of [[e:casale-monferrato|Casale]] around 1590. When the main [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] line died out in 1627, the [[e:war-of-the-mantuan-succession|War of the Mantuan Succession]] brought sieges of Casale by [[e:spain|Spain]] and Savoy against [[e:france|France]]. The [[e:treaty-of-cherasco|Peace of Cherasco]] in 1631 gave parts to Savoy and the rest to Charles I [[e:house-of-gonzaga-nevers|Gonzaga-Nevers]].
duchy-of-montferrat.e: The last duke, [[e:ferdinando-carlo-gonzaga|Ferdinando Carlo]], sided with [[e:france|France]] and was deposed in 1708. [[e:montferrat|Montferrat]] was given to the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]], a transfer confirmed by the [[e:treaty-of-utrecht|Treaty of Utrecht]] in 1713.

duchy-of-trent.t: Lombard frontier duchy in the Adige valley guarding the Brenner route into Italy against Franks and Bavarians.
duchy-of-trent.o: Soon after the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] invasion of 568, a duchy was set up at [[e:trento|Tridentum]] ([[s:prince-bishopric-of-trent|Trento]]) to control the [[e:adige|Adige]] valley, the main route from the [[e:brenner-pass|Brenner Pass]] into the Po plain. [[e:paul-the-deacon|Paul the Deacon]] names [[e:euin-of-trent|Euin]] as its first duke, who repelled Frankish invasions in the 570s and 580s and married a Bavarian princess.
duchy-of-trent.r: The dukes of [[e:trento|Trent]] were military lords on a sensitive frontier, dealing by war and marriage with the [[s:franks|Franks]] and the [[e:bavarians|Bavarians]] to the north. Their territory covered much of modern [[e:trentino|Trentino]] and the upper [[e:adige|Adige]]. Duke [[e:alahis|Alahis]] rebelled against King [[e:cunipert|Cunipert]], seized [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]] and was killed at the [[e:battle-of-coronate|battle of Coronate]] around 689. Otherwise little is recorded of their government.
duchy-of-trent.e: After [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] conquest of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard Kingdom]] in 774, [[e:trento|Trent]] was placed under Frankish counts as part of the [[s:carolingian-kingdom-of-italy|Carolingian Kingdom of Italy]]. In 1027 [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Conrad II]] gave the county to the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of Trent, founding the prince-bishopric.

dos-pilas.t: A Maya kingdom founded in the Petexbatún region by a breakaway branch of Tikal's dynasty that sided with Calakmul and fought its own kin.
dos-pilas.o: Dos Pilas was founded around 629 as an outpost of [[s:tikal|Tikal]], and [[e:bajlaj-chan-kawiil|B'ajlaj Chan K'awiil]], a member of the Tikal royal family, was installed there as its ruler, using the same emblem glyph. Defeated by the [[s:kingdom-of-kaan|Kingdom of Kaan]], he became its ally and fought a long civil war against Tikal, defeating it in 679.
dos-pilas.r: His successors expanded the kingdom across the [[e:petexbatun|Petexbatún]] and [[e:pasion-river|Pasión]] region, conquering [[s:ceibal|Ceibal]] in 735 and building hieroglyphic stairways recording their wars. Royal marriage linked the dynasty to [[s:naranjo|Naranjo]] through [[e:lady-six-sky|Lady Six Sky]]. Under [[e:kawiil-chan-kinich|K'awiil Chan K'inich]] the kingdom overreached and in 761 it was defeated; the capital was ringed with hastily built walls.
dos-pilas.e: After 761 the royal family moved to the fortified twin capital of Aguateca, which was burnt and abandoned around 810. The [[e:petexbatun|Petexbatún]] wars are a key example of the warfare that accompanied the [[e:classic-maya-collapse|Classic Maya collapse]].

duchy-of-sieradz.t: A Piast duchy in central Poland, a stepping stone for Leszek the Black and Wladyslaw the Elbow-high on their way to Krakow.
duchy-of-sieradz.o: Sieradz, on the [[e:warta|Warta]], was part of the lands of [[e:casimir-i-of-kuyavia|Casimir I of Kuyavia]]. In the early 1260s his eldest son [[e:leszek-the-black|Leszek the Black]] received it as his own duchy, which he kept after his father's death in 1267.
duchy-of-sieradz.r: It was a farming land on the borders of [[s:duchy-of-greater-poland|Greater Poland]] and [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]]. [[e:leszek-the-black|Leszek the Black]] used it as a base to become duke of [[e:krakow|Krakow]] in 1279, and later his half-brother [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high]] held Sieradz as he fought for the reunification of [[e:poland|Poland]]. Its towns were developed under German law in the 13th century.
duchy-of-sieradz.e: After 1320 Sieradz remained a duchy within the reunited kingdom, held by Przemysl, a nephew of the king. When he died in 1339 it was incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385) and later became the [[e:sieradz-voivodeship|Sieradz Voivodeship]].

dabuyid-dynasty.t: The last Zoroastrian rulers of Tabaristan, who kept a Sasanian-style principality alive on the Caspian coast for over a century after the Arab conquest.
dabuyid-dynasty.o: According to later tradition, [[e:gil-gavbara|Gil Gavbara]], a prince from [[e:gilan|Gilan]] claiming Sasanian descent, took control of [[e:tabaristan|Tabaristan]] around 642, as the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]] collapsed under Arab attack. His descendants, named after his son [[e:dabuya|Dabuya]], became the ispahbads of Tabaristan, ruling from [[e:sari-iran|Sari]] and the coastal lowlands.
dabuyid-dynasty.r: The Dabuyids kept Sasanian forms of rule and Zoroastrian religion and minted [[e:silver|silver]] coins in [[e:middle-persian|Pahlavi]] script on the Sasanian model, still dated by their own era. Protected by the [[e:alborz|Alborz]] and dense forests, they resisted repeated Umayyad attacks. [[e:farrukhan-the-great|Farrukhan the Great]] defeated the Arab general [[e:yazid-ibn-al-muhallab|Yazid ibn al-Muhallab]] in 717, and the dynasty paid tribute only when forced.
dabuyid-dynasty.e: The last ispahbad, [[e:khurshid-of-tabaristan|Khurshid]], rebelled against the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]], and in 759 to 760 Abbasid armies overran [[e:tabaristan|Tabaristan]]. Khurshid took poison, and Tabaristan became a caliphal province, though the [[s:bavand-dynasty|Bavand dynasty]] and [[s:qarinvand-dynasty|Qarinvand dynasty]] survived in the mountains.

domain-of-soissons.t: Last Roman-ruled territory in northern Gaul, held by the generals Aegidius and Syagrius until Clovis conquered it in 486.
domain-of-soissons.o: Around 457 the emperor Majorian appointed [[e:aegidius|Aegidius]] as commander of the Roman army in [[e:gaul|Gaul]]. When Majorian was murdered in 461, Aegidius refused to recognise his successors and kept control of the region between the Somme and the [[e:loire|Loire]], cut off from [[e:italy|Italy]].
domain-of-soissons.r: [[e:aegidius|Aegidius]] ruled as a Roman general rather than a king, allying with the [[s:franks|Franks]] and fighting the [[e:visigoths|Visigoths]] at [[e:orleans|Orléans]] in 463. After his death in 464 his son [[e:syagrius|Syagrius]] held the region from [[e:soissons|Soissons]]; [[e:gregory-of-tours|Gregory of Tours]] calls him king of the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]], though he probably never used the title.
domain-of-soissons.e: In 486 [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]] of the [[s:salian-franks|Salian Franks]] defeated [[e:syagrius|Syagrius]] near [[e:soissons|Soissons]]. Syagrius fled to the [[s:visigothic-kingdom|Visigothic Kingdom]], but [[e:alaric-ii|Alaric II]] handed him over, and Clovis had him killed. The domain became the core of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]].

demerara.t: A Dutch plantation colony on the Demerara river, settled largely by British planters, whose capital Stabroek became Georgetown, Guyana's capital.
demerara.o: In 1745 [[e:laurens-storm-van-s-gravesande|Laurens Storm van 's Gravesande]], commander of [[s:essequibo|Essequibo]], opened the Demerara river to settlement, and the [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] granted land to planters. Many settlers came from [[s:barbados|Barbados]] and other British islands, attracted by fertile soil. Demerara soon outgrew Essequibo.
demerara.r: Demerara's plantations produced [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]] worked by a large enslaved African population. A separate commander was appointed in 1750. The British seized the colony in 1781, and the French took it in 1782 and founded a new town at the river mouth, which the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] renamed [[e:georgetown-guyana|Stabroek]] in 1784. A [[e:court-of-policy|Court of Policy]] of officials and planters governed with the commander.
demerara.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] occupied Demerara again from 1796. In 1812 it was united with [[s:essequibo|Essequibo]] as [[s:demerara-essequibo|Demerara-Essequibo]], and [[e:georgetown-guyana|Stabroek]] was renamed Georgetown. The colony was ceded to [[e:britain|Britain]] in 1814 and merged into [[s:british-guiana|British Guiana]] in 1831, whose [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] economy it dominated.

duchy-of-livonia.t: Polish-Lithuanian Livonia, created when the crusader state dissolved in 1561, and fought over by Sweden and Poland for six decades.
duchy-of-livonia.o: By the [[e:treaty-of-vilnius-1561|Treaty of Vilnius]] in 1561, the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] and the [[s:archbishopric-of-riga|Archbishopric of Riga]] submitted to [[e:sigismund-ii-augustus|Sigismund II Augustus]]. The lands north of the [[e:western-dvina|Daugava]] became the Duchy of [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]], with the last master, [[e:gotthard-kettler|Gotthard Kettler]], as administrator. After the [[e:union-of-lublin|Union of Lublin]] in 1569 it was held jointly by [[e:poland|Poland]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]].
duchy-of-livonia.r: The [[e:livonian-war|Livonian War]] and later conflicts devastated the country. [[e:stephen-bathory|Stephen Báthory]] drove out the Russians by 1582 and reorganised [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]] into districts, promoting the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]] through the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] at Riga and [[e:tartu|Dorpat]], which offended the Lutheran German nobility and towns. Riga, a free city until 1581, was the chief port.
