duchy-of-livonia.e: From 1600 [[e:sweden|Sweden]] and Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]] fought over [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]]; the Polish victory at [[e:battle-of-kircholm|Kircholm]] in 1605 delayed Swedish conquest, but [[e:gustavus-adolphus|Gustav II Adolf]] took Riga in 1621. The [[e:truce-of-altmark|Truce of Altmark]] in 1629 left most of the duchy as [[s:swedish-livonia|Swedish Livonia]], while the south-east, [[e:latgale|Latgale]], remained Polish as the [[e:inflanty-voivodeship|Inflanty Voivodeship]].

cr.a: Der Eberswalder, some modification by Lexicon

diyodar-state.t: A small Vaghela Rajput state of the Banas Kantha country in northern Gujarat.
diyodar-state.o: Diyodar, also spelled Deodar, was held by a [[e:baghel|Vaghela]] [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] family in the plains north of the [[e:west-banas-river|Banas]] river. The register dates it to around 1700, though its founding is known mainly from tradition.
diyodar-state.r: The Thakor ruled a dry territory of [[e:millet|millet]] and grazing land. In the British period Diyodar was a minor state under the [[s:palanpur-state|Palanpur]] and later the [[e:banas-kantha-agency|Banas Kantha Agency]]. Little else is recorded.
diyodar-state.e: Diyodar merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in [[e:banaskantha-district|Banaskantha district]].

don-cossack-host.t: The self-governing Cossack community of the Don, frontier warriors and rebels who became the elite cavalry of the Russian Empire.
don-cossack-host.o: Free men and runaways from [[s:tsardom-of-russia|Muscovy]] and [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]] settled along the lower Don in the 16th century, living by fishing, hunting and raiding the [[e:tatars|Tatars]] and Turks. The Host traditionally dates its foundation to 1570, when [[e:ivan-iv-of-russia|Ivan IV]] sent a charter to the Don [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]]. Their capital was [[e:starocherkasskaya|Cherkassk]], on an island in the Don.
don-cossack-host.r: The Host was run by a general assembly, the krug, which elected the ataman, and it kept its own laws in return for military service to [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. In 1637 the [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]] took [[e:azov|Azov]] from the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and held it for five years. The Don also bred great rebellions, led by [[e:stepan-razin|Stepan Razin]] in 1670 and [[e:kondraty-bulavin|Kondraty Bulavin]] in 1707, which Moscow crushed.
don-cossack-host.e: Over the 18th century the Host lost its self-government and became a privileged military estate of the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]], with its capital moved to [[e:novocherkassk|Novocherkassk]] in 1805. Ataman [[e:matvei-platov|Matvei Platov]] led Don [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]] against [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]]. After 1917 they formed the anti-Bolshevik [[s:don-republic|Don Republic]], and Soviet rule dissolved the Host.

dazhou-zhang-shicheng.t: The state of the salt-boatman rebel Zhang Shicheng, who ruled the rich Yangtze delta from Suzhou and was Zhu Yuanzhang's last great rival in the east.
dazhou-zhang-shicheng.o: [[e:zhang-shicheng|Zhang Shicheng]], a salt boatman from [[e:taizhou-jiangsu|Taizhou]] in [[e:jiangsu|Jiangsu]], led salt workers in revolt against [[s:yuan-dynasty|Yuan Dynasty]] officials in 1353 and in 1354 proclaimed himself King of [[s:zhou-wu-sangui|Great Zhou]] at [[e:gaoyou|Gaoyou]]. A huge Yuan army under the chancellor [[e:toghto|Toghto]] besieged Gaoyou, but dissolved when Toghto was dismissed.
dazhou-zhang-shicheng.r: Zhang moved to [[e:suzhou|Pingjiang]] (Suzhou) in 1356 and held the wealthy delta, with its [[e:silk|silk]] and [[e:rice|rice]]. In 1357 he nominally submitted to the Yuan and shipped grain north by sea to the capital, but kept his own administration and in 1363 took the title King of Wu. His court attracted scholars and poets, and he taxed lightly.
dazhou-zhang-shicheng.e: [[e:hongwu-emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]], having defeated [[s:chen-han|Chen Han]], attacked Zhang's territories from 1365 and besieged [[e:suzhou|Suzhou]] for ten months. The city fell in 1367; Zhang was taken to [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] and hanged himself. Zhu founded the [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]] the next year and punished Suzhou with heavy taxes.

duchy-of-kuyavia.t: A Piast duchy on the lower Vistula whose ruler Casimir I fathered the dukes who later reunited Poland.
duchy-of-kuyavia.o: [[e:kuyavia|Kuyavia]], the fertile land around [[s:duchy-of-inowroclaw|Inowroclaw]] and [[e:kruszwica|Kruszwica]] west of the [[e:vistula|Vistula]], belonged to the [[s:duchy-of-masovia|Duchy of Masovia]] under [[e:konrad-i-of-masovia|Konrad I]]. In 1233 Konrad gave it to his son Casimir, who made it a separate duchy and later added [[s:duchy-of-leczyca|Leczyca]] and [[s:duchy-of-sieradz|Sieradz]] to his lands.
duchy-of-kuyavia.r: [[e:kuyavia|Kuyavia]] was rich in farmland and salt, and [[e:kruszwica|Kruszwica]] and [[e:wloclawek|Wloclawek]], seat of the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of Kuyavia, were important centres. Bordering the [[s:state-of-the-teutonic-order|State of the Teutonic Order]] across the [[e:vistula|Vistula]], the duchy faced frequent disputes over land and trade. Casimir I fought his neighbours for influence in central [[e:poland|Poland]].
duchy-of-kuyavia.e: When Casimir I died in 1267 his lands were divided among his sons: [[e:leszek-the-black|Leszek the Black]] received [[s:duchy-of-sieradz|Sieradz]], [[e:ziemomysl-of-inowroclaw|Ziemomysl]] took the [[s:duchy-of-inowroclaw|Duchy of Inowroclaw]], and [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high]] and [[e:casimir-ii-of-leczyca|Casimir II]] shared the [[s:duchy-of-brzesc-kujawski|Duchy of Brzesc Kujawski]]. Wladyslaw later reunited [[e:poland|Poland]].

duchy-of-podolia.t: A frontier duchy won from the Tatars by Lithuania, ruled by the Koriatovich princes from the cliff-top fortress of Kamianets.
duchy-of-podolia.o: [[e:podolia|Podolia]], the steppe and forest land between the [[e:southern-bug|Southern Bug]] and the [[e:dniester|Dniester]], was under the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] until [[e:algirdas|Algirdas]] of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] defeated three [[e:tatars|Tatar]] princes at the [[e:battle-of-blue-waters|Blue Waters]] around 1362. He gave the land to his nephews, the sons of [[e:karijotas|Koriat]], who made [[e:kamianets-podilskyi|Kamianets]] their capital.
duchy-of-podolia.r: The Koriatovich brothers fortified [[e:kamianets-podilskyi|Kamianets]] and other towns, invited settlers and granted town rights under German law. They issued their own coins and ruled a mixed Ruthenian, Armenian and Polish population in an exposed land on the edge of the steppe. They looked both to [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] and to [[e:poland|Poland]] for support.
duchy-of-podolia.e: Around 1393 [[e:vytautas-the-great|Vytautas]] expelled [[e:fyodor-koriatovich|Fyodor Koriatovich]] and divided the duchy, with the western part passing to [[e:poland|Poland]]. After long rivalry over the region, western [[e:podolia|Podolia]] became the [[e:podolian-voivodeship|Podolian Voivodeship]] of the Polish Crown in 1434, while the east remained with [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]].

duchy-of-estonia-1219-1346.t: Northern Estonia under the Danish crown, won by Valdemar II's crusade in 1219 and sold to the Teutonic Order after the great peasant revolt of 1343.
duchy-of-estonia-1219-1346.o: In 1219 [[e:valdemar-ii-of-denmark|Valdemar II of Denmark]] landed at Lindanise, defeated the [[e:estonians|Estonians]] and built a castle on [[e:toompea|Toompea]], the start of [[s:reval|Reval]]. [[e:denmark|Denmark]] competed with the [[s:livonian-brothers-of-the-sword|Livonian Brothers of the Sword]] for northern [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]], and the [[e:treaty-of-stensby|Treaty of Stensby]] in 1238 confirmed Danish rule over [[s:ravala|Rävala]], [[s:harjumaa|Harjumaa]] and [[s:virumaa|Virumaa]].
duchy-of-estonia-1219-1346.r: The Danish king ruled through a captain at [[s:reval|Reval]], but real power on the land lay with German [[e:vassal|vassals]] who formed the Harrien-Wierland knighthood, holding estates recorded in the [[e:liber-census-daniae|Liber Census Daniae]]. Reval received [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] law in 1248 and became a Hanseatic port. Cistercian monasteries and parish churches spread [[e:christianity|Christianity]] among the Estonian peasants.
duchy-of-estonia-1219-1346.e: In 1343 the [[e:estonians|Estonians]] of [[s:harjumaa|Harjumaa]] rose in the [[e:st-georges-night-uprising|St George's Night Uprising]], killing many Germans. The [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] crushed the revolt, and in 1346 [[e:valdemar-iv-of-denmark|Valdemar IV]] sold the duchy to the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]], which handed it to its Livonian branch. Northern [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] became part of the Livonian Order's lands.

duchy-of-guastalla.t: A small Po valley state first ruled by the Torelli and then by a branch of the Gonzaga, before joining Parma in 1748.
duchy-of-guastalla.o: In 1406 [[e:guido-torelli|Guido Torelli]], a condottiere in the service of the Visconti, received Guastalla, a town on the Po between [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Mantua]] and [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Parma]]. The Torelli ruled it as counts under the overlordship of the [[s:duchy-of-milan|Duchy of Milan]].
duchy-of-guastalla.r: In 1539 Countess [[e:ludovica-torelli|Ludovica Torelli]] sold Guastalla to [[e:ferrante-i-gonzaga|Ferrante Gonzaga]], general of [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] and governor of [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]], whose branch of the [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] ruled it from then on. [[e:ferrante-ii-gonzaga|Ferrante II]] was made duke in 1621. The duchy was a fortified town with its farmland, and its rulers were often drawn into the quarrels over the [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Duchy of Mantua]].
duchy-of-guastalla.e: The Guastalla [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] died out in 1746. By the Treaty of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aix-la-Chapelle]] in 1748 the duchy was given to [[e:philip-duke-of-parma|Philip of Bourbon]] and joined to the [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Duchy of Parma and Piacenza]].

dilmacogullari.t: A minor Turkish dynasty that ruled Bitlis and Erzen in south-eastern Anatolia in the 12th century.
dilmacogullari.o: Known mainly from brief mentions in Arabic chronicles, the dynasty descended from a Turkish commander named Dilmac who received [[e:bitlis|Bitlis]] and Erzen, south-west of [[e:lake-van|Lake Van]], after the Seljuk conquest of the region in the late 11th century.
dilmacogullari.r: Its best-documented ruler is [[e:toghan-arslan|Toghan Arslan]], nicknamed the Hunchback, who held [[e:bitlis|Bitlis]] and Erzen in the early 12th century, allied with the [[e:artuqid-dynasty|Artuqid]] [[e:ilghazi|Ilghazi]] against the [[e:georgians|Georgians]] and the [[e:crusader-states|Crusaders]], and fought his neighbours over [[e:mayyafariqin|Mayyafariqin]]. The [[e:beylik|beylik]] controlled the pass between [[e:lake-van|Lake Van]] and the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] basin and acted as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of stronger neighbours.
dilmacogullari.e: The dynasty faded under the pressure of the [[s:shah-armens|Shah-Armens]] of [[e:ahlat|Ahlat]] and later the [[e:ayyubid-empire|Ayyubids]]; its lands were absorbed around the end of the 12th century.

duchy-of-olesnica.t: A Silesian duchy that outlived its Piast founders by four centuries, passing to the Poděbrady, Württemberg and Brunswick families.
duchy-of-olesnica.o: In the division of the [[s:duchy-of-glogow|Duchy of Głogów]] among the sons of [[e:henry-iii-of-glogow|Henry III]], [[e:konrad-i-of-olesnica|Konrad I]] received [[e:olesnica|Oleśnica]] (Oels), east of [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]], and ruled it as a separate duchy by 1320. In 1329 he did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|King John of Bohemia]], placing the duchy under the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-olesnica.r: The [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] dukes of [[e:olesnica|Oleśnica]] at times also held other Silesian towns, including [[e:kozle|Koźle]] and part of [[e:bytom|Bytom]]. After their line died out in 1492, the duchy went to the Bohemian [[e:house-of-podebrady|Poděbrady]] family, who introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]], and in 1647 by marriage to [[e:silvius-i-nimrod-duke-of-wurttemberg-oels|Sylvius Nimrod of Württemberg]], whose line made Oleśnica a small centre of [[e:baroque|Baroque]] court culture and Lutheran [[e:printing-press|printing]].
duchy-of-olesnica.e: [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742. In 1792 the duchy went by marriage to the house of [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]], and when the last Brunswick duke died in 1884 it reverted to the Prussian crown, which granted it to the crown prince. [[e:olesnica|Oleśnica]] became part of [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

dzungar-khanate.t: The last great nomadic empire of the steppe, an Oirat Mongol state that fought the Qing for Central Asia until its destruction in the 1750s.
dzungar-khanate.o: The [[e:dzungars|Dzungars]] were the [[e:choros-oirats|Choros]] tribe of the [[e:oirats|Oirat]] [[e:mongols|Mongols]]. Their leader [[e:erdeni-batur|Erdeni Batur]] united Oirat tribes in the 1630s, and in 1640 helped draw up the [[e:mongol-oirat-code|Mongol-Oirat Code]]. His son [[e:galdan-boshugtu-khan|Galdan Boshugtu Khan]] conquered the [[s:yarkent-khanate|Yarkent Khanate]] in 1680 and attacked the [[e:khalkha-mongols|Khalkha Mongols]].
dzungar-khanate.r: The [[e:dzungars|Dzungars]] combined nomadic herding with farming by [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] [[e:taranchi|Taranchi]] settlers in the Ili valley and with metalworking, making firearms and [[e:field-artillery|cannon]] with the help of a captured Swedish officer, [[e:johan-gustaf-renat|Johan Gustaf Renat]]. They followed [[e:tibetan-buddhism|Tibetan Buddhism]] and intervened in [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]], sacking [[e:lhasa|Lhasa]] in 1717. Under [[e:tsewang-rabtan|Tsewang Rabtan]] they raided the [[s:kazakh-khanate|Kazakh Khanate]] in the 1720s, the 'Great Disaster'.
dzungar-khanate.e: After civil war over the succession, the [[e:qianlong-emperor|Qianlong Emperor]] sent [[e:qing-empire|Qing]] armies in 1755. Following the revolt of [[e:amursana|Amursana]], Qing forces carried out a [[e:genocide|genocide]] of the [[e:dzungars|Dzungars]] between 1755 and 1758, and [[e:smallpox|smallpox]] killed many more. [[e:dzungaria|Dzungaria]] became part of Qing [[e:xinjiang|Xinjiang]].

duchy-of-poland.t: The first Polish state, created by the Piast dukes around Gniezno, which adopted Christianity in 966 and became a kingdom in 1025.
duchy-of-poland.o: Around 960 [[e:mieszko-i|Mieszko I]] of the [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast dynasty]] ruled the [[e:polans-western|Polans]] of [[s:duchy-of-greater-poland|Greater Poland]] from strongholds at [[e:gniezno|Gniezno]] and [[e:poznan|Poznan]]. He married the Bohemian princess [[e:doubravka-of-bohemia|Dubrawka]] and was baptised in 966, bringing his realm into [[e:latin-christendom|Latin Christendom]]. By the 990s he had added [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]], [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] and [[e:lesser-poland|Lesser Poland]].
duchy-of-poland.r: The [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] dukes ruled through a network of fortified centres and a mounted retinue, and supported themselves with tribute and the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]]. Around 991 [[e:mieszko-i|Mieszko]] placed his lands under papal protection in the document known as [[e:dagome-iudex|Dagome iudex]]. His son [[e:boleslaw-i-the-brave|Boleslaw I]] welcomed [[e:otto-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Otto III]] at the [[e:congress-of-gniezno|Congress of Gniezno]] in 1000, which created an archbishopric at [[e:gniezno|Gniezno]].
duchy-of-poland.e: [[e:boleslaw-i-the-brave|Boleslaw I]] fought the emperor [[e:henry-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Henry II]] for years, gaining [[e:lusatia|Lusatia]] at the [[e:peace-of-bautzen|Peace of Bautzen]] in 1018, and the same year briefly took [[e:kyiv|Kiev]]. Shortly before his death in 1025 he was crowned king, and the duchy became the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385).

duchy-of-znojmo.t: The southern Moravian appanage of the Přemyslid dynasty, centred on Znojmo, whose Romanesque rotunda preserves rare paintings of the Bohemian dukes.
duchy-of-znojmo.o: [[e:znojmo|Znojmo]] in southern [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] was split off from the [[e:brno|Brno]] [[e:appanage|appanage]] around 1092, when Conrad I of Brno became Duke of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and his son [[e:litold-of-znojmo|Litold]] received Znojmo. It was one of three Moravian appanages, alongside [[e:olomouc|Olomouc]] and Brno, held by junior [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]] princes.
duchy-of-znojmo.r: The princes ruled from the castle of [[e:znojmo|Znojmo]] on a crag above the [[e:thaya|Dyje]] (Thaya) river, close to the Austrian border. The castle's [[e:romanesque-architecture|Romanesque]] rotunda of Saint Catherine contains wall paintings of 1134 showing the legendary and historical [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]] rulers, an important source for the dynasty's self-image. [[e:conrad-ii-of-znojmo|Conrad II of Znojmo]] was a strong contender for the Bohemian throne.
duchy-of-znojmo.e: The [[e:appanage|appanage]] system ended in the late 12th century as [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] became a margraviate; around 1197 [[e:vladislaus-iii-duke-of-bohemia|Vladislaus Henry]] united the Moravian lands. [[e:znojmo|Znojmo]] became a royal town in the 13th century under [[e:ottokar-i-of-bohemia|Ottokar I]].

duchy-of-mecklenburg-gustrow.t: North German duchy that briefly passed to Wallenstein during the Thirty Years' War, ruled from a fine Renaissance palace at Güstrow.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-gustrow.o: [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] had already been divided before, but the partition of 1621 between the brothers [[e:adolf-frederick-i-duke-of-mecklenburg|Adolf Frederick I]] and [[e:john-albert-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg|John Albert II]] created a lasting Mecklenburg-[[e:gustrow|Güstrow]] in the east of the country, with [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg-Schwerin]] in the west. [[s:lordship-of-rostock|Rostock]] and the estates remained shared between the two duchies.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-gustrow.r: Both dukes were deposed in 1628 by [[e:ferdinand-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Ferdinand II]], who gave [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] to his general [[e:albrecht-von-wallenstein|Albrecht von Wallenstein]]; Wallenstein governed from [[e:gustrow|Güstrow]] until Swedish troops restored the dukes in 1631. Government was weakened by powerful noble estates, and the countryside suffered heavily from war and depopulation. The duchy was Lutheran.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-gustrow.e: [[e:gustav-adolph-duke-of-mecklenburg-gustrow|Gustav Adolph]], the last duke, died without male heirs in 1695. A long succession dispute followed until the [[e:treaty-of-hamburg-1701|Treaty of Hamburg]] in 1701 divided [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] into the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-schwerin|Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin]] and the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz]].

duchy-of-prussia.t: The first officially Lutheran state, created in 1525 when the Teutonic Order's grand master turned duke and vassal of Poland.
duchy-of-prussia.o: After defeats by [[e:poland|Poland]], the [[s:state-of-the-teutonic-order|State of the Teutonic Order]] was reduced to [[e:east-prussia|East Prussia]]. In 1525 [[e:albert-duke-of-prussia|Grand Master Albert of Brandenburg-Ansbach]], advised by [[e:martin-luther|Luther]], secularised the order's state and, by the [[e:treaty-of-krakow|Treaty of Kraków]], did homage to his uncle [[e:sigismund-i-the-old|King Sigismund I of Poland]] as hereditary Duke of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].
duchy-of-prussia.r: [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] was the first state to adopt [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] officially. Albert founded the [[e:university-of-konigsberg|University of Königsberg]] in 1544 and supported [[e:printing-press|printing]] in German, Polish and Lithuanian. The estates were strong, and the land exported grain through [[e:konigsberg|Königsberg]]. After Duke [[e:albert-frederick-duke-of-prussia|Albert Frederick]] fell mentally ill, the [[e:prince-elector|electors]] of [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] ruled as regents and in 1618 inherited the duchy, creating [[e:brandenburg-prussia|Brandenburg-Prussia]].
duchy-of-prussia.e: Elector [[e:frederick-william-elector-of-brandenburg|Frederick William, the Great Elector]], won full [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] from [[e:poland|Poland]] by the [[e:treaty-of-wehlau|Treaty of Wehlau]] in 1657. Because [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] lay outside the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]], his son Frederick crowned himself King in Prussia at [[e:konigsberg|Königsberg]] in 1701, founding the [[s:kingdom-of-prussia|Kingdom of Prussia]].

duchy-of-krnov.t: A Silesian duchy, known in German as Jägerndorf, held successively by Přemyslids, Hohenzollerns and the princes of Liechtenstein.
duchy-of-krnov.o: [[e:krnov|Krnov]] (Jägerndorf) emerged from the [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]] lands of the [[s:duchy-of-opava|Duchy of Opava]]. After Duke [[e:nicholas-ii|Nicholas II]] died in 1365 his sons divided his possessions, and by 1377 John I held Krnov together with [[e:raciborz|Racibórz]] as his own duchy, a fief of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-krnov.r: After several changes of ruler, [[e:krnov|Krnov]] was bought in 1523 by Margrave [[e:george-the-pious|George of Brandenburg-Ansbach]], who introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] and rebuilt the castle. His [[e:house-of-hohenzollern|Hohenzollern]] heirs held it until 1621, when [[e:john-george-duke-of-jagerndorf|Johann Georg]] lost it for supporting the Bohemian revolt. [[e:ferdinand-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Ferdinand II]] then granted it to [[e:karl-i-prince-of-liechtenstein|Karl of Liechtenstein]], whose family kept the ducal title thereafter.
duchy-of-krnov.e: [[e:frederick-the-great|Frederick II of Prussia]] cited the [[e:house-of-hohenzollern|Hohenzollern]] claim to [[e:krnov|Krnov]] when he invaded [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], and in 1742 [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] annexed the northern part, while the town stayed in [[s:duchy-of-upper-and-lower-silesia|Austrian Silesia]]. The [[e:house-of-liechtenstein|Liechtensteins]] kept the title until 1918, when Krnov became part of [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]].

duchy-of-carinthia.t: The oldest duchy of the Austrian lands, heir to Slavic Carantania, which kept its unique installation rite at the Prince's Stone until 1414.
duchy-of-carinthia.o: In 976 [[e:otto-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Otto II]] separated [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]] from the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria|Duchy of Bavaria]] to weaken the rebellious Duke [[e:henry-ii-duke-of-bavaria|Henry the Quarrelsome]], creating the first new duchy of the Empire. It included [[s:carantania|Carantania]] and huge marches extending to [[s:commune-of-verona|Verona]], [[e:styria|Styria]] and [[e:carniola|Carniola]], many of which later became separate.
duchy-of-carinthia.r: Dukes were installed at the [[e:princes-stone|Prince's Stone]] near [[e:karnburg|Karnburg]] and the [[e:dukes-chair|Duke's Chair]] on the [[e:zollfeld|Zollfeld]], in a ceremony partly in Slovene. Ruling families included the [[e:house-of-eppenstein|Eppensteiners]] and the [[e:house-of-sponheim|Sponheimers]]. The population was mixed German and Slovene. Mining of lead and iron, and the rebuilding of [[e:klagenfurt|Klagenfurt]] as capital by the Carinthian estates, to whom Maximilian I gave the town in 1518, shaped later centuries.
duchy-of-carinthia.e: In 1335 the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] inherited [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]], which stayed in their hands as a crown land until 1918. The plebiscite of 1920 kept southern Carinthia in [[e:austria|Austria]], though some areas went to [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]] and [[e:italy|Italy]]. It is today an Austrian federal state.

duchy-of-glogow.t: Silesian Piast duchy on the Oder whose dukes claimed Greater Poland, later a Bohemian fief held briefly by the future King Sigismund I of Poland.
duchy-of-glogow.o: [[e:konrad-i-of-glogow|Konrad I]], a son of [[e:henry-ii-the-pious|Henry II the Pious]], received [[e:glogow|Głogów]] and the lands around it in a division of the Silesian inheritance around 1251. Głogów, a fortified town on the [[e:oder-river|Oder]], became the capital of a duchy covering much of northern [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]].
duchy-of-glogow.r: [[e:konrad-i-of-glogow|Konrad]]'s son [[e:henry-iii-of-glogow|Henry III of Głogów]] was one of the most powerful Silesian princes, holding [[s:duchy-of-greater-poland|Greater Poland]] for a time and claiming the [[e:kingdom-of-poland|Polish crown]]. After him the duchy was divided among branches, including [[e:zagan|Żagań]] and [[e:olesnica|Oleśnica]]. Half of [[e:glogow|Głogów]] passed directly to the Bohemian crown in 1331, and the remaining dukes became [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]]. German settlement and town law transformed the region.
duchy-of-glogow.e: After the [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] lines died out and disputes followed, [[e:glogow|Głogów]] was granted to the Jagiellonian [[e:sigismund-i-the-old|Sigismund]], who ruled it from 1499 until 1506 before becoming King of [[e:poland|Poland]]. It then returned to the Bohemian crown, passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742, and to Poland in 1945.

duchy-of-saint-sava.t: Domain of the Kosača family whose ruler's title, herceg, gave the region of Herzegovina its name.
duchy-of-saint-sava.o: [[e:stjepan-vukcic-kosaca|Stjepan Vukčić Kosača]] inherited the lands of Hum and the coast from his uncle [[e:sandalj-hranic-kosaca|Sandalj Hranić]] in 1435, becoming the mightiest noble of the [[s:kingdom-of-bosnia|Kingdom of Bosnia]]. In 1448 he styled himself Herceg of [[e:saint-sava|Saint Sava]], after the relics of the Serbian saint kept at the monastery of [[e:mileseva-monastery|Mileševa]] in his territory, asserting independence from the Bosnian king.
duchy-of-saint-sava.r: From his castle at [[e:blagaj|Blagaj]] near [[e:mostar|Mostar]], Stjepan controlled the [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] between the Adriatic and the interior, levying customs on trade with [[s:republic-of-ragusa|Ragusa]] and developing the port of [[e:herceg-novi|Novi]], today Herceg Novi. His lands mixed adherents of the [[e:bosnian-church|Bosnian Church]], [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] and Catholic Christians, and he quarrelled with Ragusa, [[e:venice|Venice]] and his own son Vladislav.
duchy-of-saint-sava.e: The [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] conquered [[e:bosnia|Bosnia]] in 1463 and most of Stjepan's lands by 1465; he died in 1466. His son Vlatko held a shrinking coastal remnant until [[e:herceg-novi|Herceg Novi]] fell in 1482. Another son converted and became the Ottoman grand [[e:vizier|vizier]] [[e:hersekzade-ahmed-pasha|Hersekzade Ahmed Pasha]].

duchy-of-the-franks.t: The great Robertian principality between the Seine and the Loire whose dukes overshadowed the last Carolingian kings and became the Capetian dynasty.
duchy-of-the-franks.o: The Robertian family had led the defence of [[s:neustria|Neustria]] against the [[e:vikings|Vikings]] since [[e:robert-the-strong|Robert the Strong]] in the 860s, and two of its members, [[e:odo-of-france|Odo]] and Robert I, had briefly been kings. In 936 [[e:hugh-the-great|Hugh the Great]] helped restore the Carolingian [[e:louis-iv-of-france|Louis IV]] and was recognised as 'duke of the [[e:frankish-kingdom|Franks]]', second only to the king.
duchy-of-the-franks.r: [[e:hugh-the-great|Hugh the Great]] held counties and lay abbacies around [[e:paris|Paris]], [[e:orleans|Orléans]] and [[e:tours|Tours]], including [[e:abbey-of-saint-martin-of-tours|Saint-Martin of Tours]] and [[e:basilica-of-saint-denis|Saint-Denis]], giving him more land and men than the king. He controlled royal successions and dealt as an equal with the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] and [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]]. His son [[e:hugh-capet|Hugh Capet]] inherited the title in 956.
duchy-of-the-franks.e: When the last Carolingian king, Louis V, died in 987, the [[e:magnates|magnates]] elected [[e:hugh-capet|Hugh Capet]] king. The duchy's lands became the royal domain of the new Capetian [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]], which his descendants ruled for eight centuries.

duchy-of-sabbioneta.t: The small Lombard duchy of Vespasiano Gonzaga, who built Sabbioneta from scratch as an ideal Renaissance city.
duchy-of-sabbioneta.o: [[e:vespasiano-gonzaga|Vespasiano Gonzaga]], a soldier and courtier of [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II of Spain]] from a cadet branch of the [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]], inherited Sabbioneta and the surrounding lands between [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Mantua]] and [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Parma]]. From the 1550s he rebuilt the village as a fortified ideal city, and Emperor [[e:rudolf-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Rudolf II]] made it a duchy in 1577.
duchy-of-sabbioneta.r: Sabbioneta was laid out on a regular plan with star-shaped walls, a ducal palace, a long gallery for [[e:vespasiano-gonzaga|Vespasiano]]'s art and antiquities, and the [[e:teatro-allantica|Teatro all'Antica]] by [[e:vincenzo-scamozzi|Vincenzo Scamozzi]], completed around 1590, one of the first purpose-built [[e:theatre|theatres]] in modern [[e:europe|Europe]]. The duke ran a small, tightly controlled court and drew craftsmen and Jewish printers to the town.
duchy-of-sabbioneta.e: [[e:vespasiano-gonzaga|Vespasiano]] died in 1591 without a surviving son, and the duchy passed through his daughter to the [[e:house-of-carafa|Carafa]] and then other heirs, losing its importance. It later passed to the [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] of [[s:duchy-of-guastalla|Guastalla]] and was eventually absorbed into Austrian-ruled [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] in the 18th century.

democratic-kampuchea.t: The Khmer Rouge state of Pol Pot, whose radical communist experiment killed some 1.5 to 2 million Cambodians between 1975 and 1979.
democratic-kampuchea.o: The [[e:khmer-rouge|Communist Party of Kampuchea]], known as the [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] Rouge, grew from a small insurgency in the 1960s to a large army during the civil war against the [[s:khmer-republic|Khmer Republic]]. It captured [[e:phnom-penh|Phnom Penh]] on 17 April 1975 and proclaimed Democratic [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia|Kampuchea]], with [[e:norodom-sihanouk|Sihanouk]] briefly as nominal head of state until 1976.
democratic-kampuchea.r: The regime, led by [[e:pol-pot|Pol Pot]], emptied the cities, abolished money, markets, schools and religion, and forced the population into agricultural communes. Former officials, intellectuals, ethnic minorities such as the [[e:cham|Cham]] and Vietnamese, and party members accused of treachery were executed, many after torture at the [[e:tuol-sleng|Tuol Sleng]] prison. Starvation, overwork and disease caused most of the deaths.
democratic-kampuchea.e: Border attacks on [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] provoked a Vietnamese invasion in December 1978, and [[e:phnom-penh|Phnom Penh]] fell on 7 January 1979, when the [[s:peoples-republic-of-kampuchea|People's Republic of Kampuchea]] was established. The [[e:khmer-rouge|Khmer Rouge]] fought on from the Thai border into the 1990s, and a UN-backed tribunal later convicted surviving leaders of [[e:genocide|genocide]].

da-changhe.t: The short-lived dynasty of the Zheng family that replaced Nanzhao in Yunnan in 902 and opened a period of rapid dynastic change around Lake Erhai.
da-changhe.o: [[e:zheng-maisi|Zheng Maisi]], a powerful minister descended from a [[s:later-tang|Tang]] official captured by [[s:nanzhao|Nanzhao]], killed the Meng royal family in 902 and proclaimed the kingdom of Da Changhe, keeping the capital at [[e:yangjumie|Yangjumie]] near modern Dali.
da-changhe.r: Little is known of its government, which seems to have continued [[s:nanzhao|Nanzhao]] institutions; sources are sparse. Three [[s:zheng-wang-shichong|Zheng]] rulers reigned, and the court was weakened by rivalry among the great families of the [[e:lake-erhai|Erhai]] region.
da-changhe.e: In 928 the official [[e:yang-ganzhen|Yang Ganzhen]] had [[e:zheng-longdan|Zheng Longdan]], the last ruler, killed and placed [[e:zhao-shanzheng|Zhao Shanzheng]] on the throne as ruler of [[s:da-tianxing|Da Tianxing]]. Within a decade the Duan family founded the more durable [[s:dali-kingdom|Dali Kingdom]].

dharampur-state.t: A Sisodia Rajput state in the hills of southern Gujarat, whose 20th-century ruler was a noted patron and scholar of Indian music.
dharampur-state.o: The ruling family claimed descent from the [[e:sisodia|Sisodias]] of [[s:udaipur-state|Mewar]], and tradition dates their arrival in the hills inland from [[e:valsad|Valsad]] to 1262. The capital was moved to the new town of Dharampur in the 18th century.
dharampur-state.r: Dharampur was a largely forested state with many [[e:kokna-people|Kokna]] and [[e:warli|Warli people]]. It paid [[e:chauth|chauth]] to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and later came under British supervision through the [[e:surat-agency|Surat Agency]]. [[e:maharana|Maharana]] Vijayadevji, who ruled in the first half of the 20th century, wrote on music and supported musicians.
dharampur-state.e: Dharampur merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and is now in [[e:valsad|Valsad]] district, [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]].

danish-gold-coast.t: Denmark's forts on the coast of modern Ghana, centred on Christiansborg at Osu, a hub of the Danish slave trade until the colony was sold in 1850.
danish-gold-coast.o: Danish traders, led by [[e:hendrik-carloff|Hendrik Carloff]], arrived on the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast]] in 1658 and seized the Swedish forts. [[e:denmark|Denmark]] built Fort Frederiksborg near [[e:cape-coast|Cape Coast]] and in 1661 bought the site of [[e:osu-castle|Christiansborg]] at Osu, near modern [[e:accra|Accra]], from the king of Accra.
danish-gold-coast.r: The [[e:danish-west-india-and-guinea-company|Danish West India and Guinea Company]] and later the crown ran a string of forts east of [[e:accra|Accra]], exchanging textiles, guns and alcohol for gold and enslaved Africans, who were shipped to the [[s:danish-west-indies|Danish West Indies]]. In 1792 [[e:denmark|Denmark]] became the first European state to ban the transatlantic [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]], effective from 1803, after which the [[e:danes|Danes]] tried plantation farming inland.
danish-gold-coast.e: Unprofitable after the end of the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]], the forts were sold to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1850 and joined the [[s:gold-coast-colony|British Gold Coast]] colony. [[e:osu-castle|Christiansborg]], also known as Osu Castle, later served as the seat of [[e:ghana|Ghana's]] government.
danish-gold-coast.re: Lutheran Christianity, Akan and Ga religion

dhar-state.t: A Maratha Puar state in Malwa centred on Dhar, the old Paramara capital of King Bhoja.
dhar-state.o: Udaji Rao and [[e:anand-rao-puar|Anand Rao Puar]] were [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] commanders active in the conquest of [[e:malwa|Malwa]]. Around 1728–32 the [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]] [[e:baji-rao-i|Baji Rao I]] confirmed Anand Rao in Dhar, a city with a long royal past as the 11th-century capital of the Paramara king [[e:bhoja-paramara|Bhoja]]. The Puars of Dhar were related to the Puars of [[s:dewas-senior|Dewas Senior]] and [[s:dewas-junior|Dewas Junior]].
dhar-state.r: Dhar was badly weakened by the wars of [[e:scindias|Scindia]] and [[e:holkars|Holkar]] around 1800 and recovered under British protection after the treaty of 1819. Its ruler was briefly deprived of the state after the revolt of 1857, which was restored in 1860 minus the Bairasia district. A [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] governed a mainly [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] population; the [[e:bhojshala|Bhoj Shala]] and the Dhar fort are its main monuments.
dhar-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]], Dhar merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956.

cr.a: The original uploader was Nataraja at French Wikipedia.

derg.t: The military committee that overthrew Haile Selassie in 1974 and ruled Ethiopia as a Marxist-Leninist dictatorship under Mengistu Haile Mariam.
derg.o: Amid famine, [[e:inflation|inflation]] and protest, a committee (derg) of junior officers formed in mid-1974 and gradually stripped Emperor [[e:haile-selassie|Haile Selassie]] of power, deposing him on 12 September 1974 and ending the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]]. In November it executed some 60 former officials. Leadership passed from [[e:aman-andom|Aman Andom]] and [[e:tafari-benti|Tafari Benti]] to [[e:mengistu-haile-mariam|Mengistu Haile Mariam]] by 1977.
derg.r: The Derg nationalised all rural and urban land in 1975, abolished the monarchy and allied with the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]]. The [[e:ethiopian-red-terror|Red Terror]] of 1977 to 1978 killed tens of thousands of suspected opponents. With Soviet and Cuban help it repelled [[e:somalia|Somalia's]] invasion of the [[e:ogaden|Ogaden]] in 1978, but fought long wars against Eritrean and Tigrayan rebels. The famine of 1983 to 1985 killed hundreds of thousands.
derg.e: In 1984 the [[e:workers-party-of-ethiopia|Workers' Party of Ethiopia]] was founded, and a new constitution in 1987 turned the military government into the civilian-styled [[s:peoples-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia]], with [[e:mengistu-haile-mariam|Mengistu]] as president.

duchy-of-racha.t: A highland duchy in the upper Rioni valley of western Georgia whose hereditary dukes, or eristavis, held power for over seven centuries.
duchy-of-racha.o: Racha, the mountain basin of the upper Rioni, became a saeristavo, or duchy, of the united [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] in the 11th century. Its hereditary eristavis governed on behalf of the crown and guarded the passes to the [[e:north-caucasus|North Caucasus]], while the church of [[e:nikortsminda-cathedral|Nikortsminda]], built under [[e:bagrat-iii-of-georgia|Bagrat III]], marked royal interest in the region.
duchy-of-racha.r: The dukes ruled from Oni and mountain castles over villages of farmers, herders and vineyard owners. Under the Kakhaberidze family in the 12th and 13th centuries Racha was rich and influential at the royal court. After [[s:georgia|Georgia]] split in 1490, Racha became a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-imereti|Kingdom of Imereti]] under the Chkheidze family, whose dukes often rebelled.
duchy-of-racha.e: Repeated rebellions and intervention in Imereti's civil wars brought the dukes into conflict with their kings. The duchy was abolished in 1789 and incorporated directly into the [[s:kingdom-of-imereti|Kingdom of Imereti]], which [[e:russia|Russia]] annexed in 1810.

dutch-malabar.t: The Dutch East India Company's commandment on the Malabar Coast, centred on Fort Cochin and its pepper trade.
dutch-malabar.o: Seeking to break the Portuguese hold on [[e:pepper|pepper]], the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) allied with the [[s:kingdom-of-calicut|Zamorins of Calicut]] and took [[e:kollam|Quilon]] in 1661 and [[e:kochi|Cochin]] in 1663 from [[s:portuguese-india|Portuguese India]]. The [[e:malabar-coast|Malabar]] posts were organised as a commandment governed from Fort [[s:kingdom-of-cochin|Kochi]], with factories at [[e:kannur|Cannanore]], [[e:kodungallur|Cranganore]] and Quilon.
dutch-malabar.r: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] made treaties with the Raja of [[e:kochi|Cochin]], making him effectively a dependent ally, and bought [[e:pepper|pepper]] under monopoly contracts. The commander [[e:hendrik-van-rheede|Hendrik van Rheede]] sponsored the [[e:hortus-malabaricus|Hortus Malabaricus]], a pioneering twelve-volume study of the plants of [[e:malabar-coast|Malabar]]. Dutch power was checked when [[e:marthanda-varma|Marthanda Varma]] of [[s:travancore|Travancore]] defeated them at [[e:battle-of-colachel|Colachel]] in 1741.
dutch-malabar.e: After [[e:battle-of-colachel|Colachel]] the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] lost influence, selling [[e:kannur|Cannanore]] to the [[s:arakkal-kingdom|Arakkal kingdom]] and later posts to [[s:travancore|Travancore]]. British forces occupied [[e:kochi|Cochin]] in 1795 during the [[e:french-revolutionary-wars|French Revolutionary Wars]], and the territory was formally ceded in 1814.

duchy-of-mecklenburg-stargard.t: A junior Mecklenburg duchy around Neubrandenburg and Stargard that lasted just over a century before reuniting with the main line.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-stargard.o: In 1352 the brothers [[e:albert-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg|Albert II]] and [[e:john-i-duke-of-mecklenburg-stargard|John I]], raised to dukes of [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] in 1348, divided their lands. John received the [[e:lordship-of-stargard|Lordship of Stargard]] in the east, with [[e:neubrandenburg|Neubrandenburg]] and [[e:strelitz|Strelitz]], which Mecklenburg had acquired from [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] in the 13th century.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-stargard.r: The duchy was an agrarian land of [[e:knighthood|knightly]] estates and small towns such as [[e:neubrandenburg|Neubrandenburg]], with its brick Gothic gates, [[e:friedland-mecklenburg|Friedland]] and Woldegk. Its dukes remained junior partners of their cousins in the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg|Duchy of Mecklenburg]] and joined in their wars with [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] and [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]]. Few details of its administration survive.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-stargard.e: When Duke [[e:ulrich-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg-stargard|Ulrich II]] died without sons in 1471, [[e:lordship-of-stargard|Stargard]] reverted to the main [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] line. The region re-emerged in 1701 as the core of the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz]].

duchy-of-croatia.t: Early medieval Croatian duchy on the Dalmatian coast, ruled by the Trpimirović line, which became the Kingdom of Croatia under Tomislav.
duchy-of-croatia.o: [[e:croats|Croats]] settled the Dalmatian hinterland in the 7th century. Around 800 a duchy emerged under Frankish overlordship, confirmed by the Peace of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]] of 812 between the [[s:franks|Franks]] and [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]. Duke [[e:borna-duke-of-croatia|Borna]] is the first well-attested ruler.
duchy-of-croatia.r: Dukes ruled from seats at Nin, [[e:klis-fortress|Klis]] and Bijaći, with a Latin-influenced Christian elite and Byzantine Dalmatian towns such as [[e:zadar|Zadar]] and Split nearby. [[e:trpimir-i|Trpimir I]] issued a charter in 852 calling himself duke of the [[e:croats|Croats]]. In 879 [[e:branimir-of-croatia|Branimir]] won papal recognition, and [[e:croatia|Croatia]] turned firmly to [[e:rome|Rome]]. Stone churches with interlace decoration and [[e:latin|Latin]] inscriptions survive.
duchy-of-croatia.e: Around 925 [[e:tomislav-of-croatia|Tomislav]] united it with the [[s:duchy-of-pannonian-croatia|Duchy of Pannonian Croatia]] and is recognised as the first king, creating the [[s:kingdom-of-croatia-925-1102|Kingdom of Croatia]] (925-1102).

despotate-of-dobruja.t: Bulgarian principality on the Black Sea coast ruled from Kaliakra, a naval power that fought Byzantium and Genoa before falling to the Ottomans.
despotate-of-dobruja.o: In the breakup of the [[s:second-bulgarian-empire|Second Bulgarian Empire]]'s authority, a local realm emerged in the coastal region of Karvuna, later called [[e:dobruja|Dobruja]]. Its first known ruler, [[e:balik|Balik]], appears in 1346 sending troops to aid the Byzantine empress [[e:anna-of-savoy|Anna of Savoy]] in the civil war.
despotate-of-dobruja.r: [[e:balik|Balik's]] brother [[e:dobrotitsa|Dobrotitsa]] (c. 1347–1386), styled despot by [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], ruled from [[e:kaliakra|Kaliakra]] and [[s:odessos|Varna]]. He built a fleet that fought Genoese traders and backed claimants to the [[s:empire-of-trebizond|Empire of Trebizond]]. The despotate controlled [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] ports and the grain trade, and remained [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] and broadly Bulgarian, while also dealing with the [[s:tsardom-of-vidin|Tsardom of Vidin]] and [[s:principality-of-wallachia|Wallachia]].
despotate-of-dobruja.e: [[e:dobrotitsa|Dobrotitsa's]] son [[e:ivanko-of-dobruja|Ivanko]] made peace with the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], but the Ottomans conquered the despotate around 1388. [[e:mircea-the-elder|Mircea the Elder of Wallachia]] held part of [[e:dobruja|Dobruja]] briefly before it passed fully to the Ottomans.

duchy-of-zator.t: A tiny Silesian Piast duchy on the upper Vistula, sold to the Polish king in 1494.
duchy-of-zator.o: Zator, east of [[e:oswiecim|Oswiecim]], was created in 1445 when the [[s:duchy-of-oswiecim|Duchy of Oswiecim]] was divided among the sons of Duke Casimir I, and Wenceslaus I took the Zator lands. Like Oswiecim, it was formally a fief of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-zator.r: The duchy was a small agricultural land in the [[e:vistula|Vistula]] valley, known for its fish ponds, where the breeding of carp later became a local speciality. Its dukes were minor [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]] with limited resources, and the duchy was further divided among Wenceslaus's sons.
duchy-of-zator.e: In 1494 Duke Jan V sold Zator to [[e:john-i-albert|King John I Albert]] of [[e:poland|Poland]]. It was incorporated, together with [[e:oswiecim|Oswiecim]], into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569) in 1564.

dhrangadhra-state.t: The senior Jhala Rajput state of Kathiawar, which moved its capital from Halvad to Dhrangadhra in the 18th century.
dhrangadhra-state.o: The [[e:jhala|Jhala Rajputs]] had ruled in the [[e:jhalawad|Jhalawad]] region of northern [[e:kathiawar|Saurashtra]] since medieval times, with their seat at [[e:halvad|Halvad]]. Around 1742 the ruler moved the capital to Dhrangadhra, giving the state its later name; [[s:wankaner-state|Wankaner]], [[s:limbdi-state|Limbdi]] and [[s:wadhwan-state|Wadhwan]] were branches of the same clan.
dhrangadhra-state.r: Dhrangadhra was a 13-gun salute state of the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]] ruled by a [[e:british-raj|Raj]] Saheb. Its economy relied on [[e:cotton|cotton]], salt from the [[e:little-rann-of-kutch|Little Rann]] and the local sandstone, still sold as Dhrangadhra stone. The rulers were reformers in education and administration in the early 20th century.
dhrangadhra-state.e: [[e:mayurdhwajsinhji-meghrajji-iii|Mayurdhwajsinhji Meghrajji III]] acceded to [[e:india|India]] and Dhrangadhra was merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948. He later sat in the Indian parliament; the town is in [[e:surendranagar-district|Surendranagar district]] of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]].

durotriges.t: Dorset confederation of hillfort dwellers whose resistance ended when Vespasian's legion stormed strongholds such as Maiden Castle and Hod Hill.
durotriges.o: The Durotriges took shape in the late [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] across [[e:dorset|Dorset]] and neighbouring parts of [[e:somerset|Somerset]], [[e:wiltshire|Wiltshire]] and [[e:hampshire|Hampshire]], a landscape dominated by great multivallate hillforts. Their harbour at [[e:hengistbury-head|Hengistbury Head]] traded with [[e:armorica|Armorica]] in the 1st century BCE, bringing in Italian wine [[e:amphora|amphorae]] and Gaulish pottery in exchange for metals, grain and [[e:cattle|cattle]].
durotriges.r: Power seems to have been spread among several centres rather than held by one king, and no ruler's name appears on their coins, which became crude cast and debased [[e:silver|silver]] issues. Hillforts such as Maiden Castle were heavily refortified and stocked with [[e:sling|sling]] stones. The Durotriges buried their dead in crouched inhumations, unlike the cremation rites of the south-east, and [[e:kimmeridge|Kimmeridge]] shale was worked into bracelets.
durotriges.e: In 43 and 44 the future emperor Vespasian, leading the legio [[e:legio-ii-augusta|II Augusta]], took more than twenty strongholds in the south-west according to [[e:suetonius|Suetonius]]; a Roman fort was built inside [[e:hod-hill|Hod Hill]]. The territory became the civitas of the Durotriges with its centre at [[e:dorchester-dorset|Durnovaria]], modern Dorchester, within [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

duchy-of-jawor.t: Lower Silesian Piast duchy at the foot of the Sudetes, later joined with Świdnica, which kept its independence from Bohemia longer than any other.
duchy-of-jawor.o: In 1274 the [[s:duchy-of-legnica|Duchy of Legnica]] was divided among the sons of [[e:boleslaw-ii-the-bald|Bolesław II the Bald]], and [[e:bolko-i-the-strict|Bolko I the Strict]] received [[e:jawor|Jawor]] with its lands. He soon added [[e:swidnica|Świdnica]] and built a strong duchy on the Bohemian border, protected by castles such as [[e:bolkow-castle|Bolków]] and [[e:grodziec-castle|Grodziec]].
duchy-of-jawor.r: Bolko I founded [[e:krzeszow-abbey|Krzeszów Abbey]] and fortified the mountain passes. After his death the lands were divided, with Henry I ruling [[e:jawor|Jawor]] until 1346. They were then reunited under [[e:bolko-ii-the-small|Bolko II the Small]], who resisted Bohemian overlordship, ruling as an independent [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] prince while other Silesian dukes became Bohemian [[e:vassal|vassals]]. German settlers and town law shaped the economy of farming and cloth.
duchy-of-jawor.e: [[e:bolko-ii-the-small|Bolko II]] married his niece Anne to Charles IV, so on the death of his widow Agnes in 1392 the duchy passed to the Bohemian crown. [[e:jawor|Jawor]] later passed to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], and has been Polish since 1945; its Lutheran Peace Church is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

duchy-of-athens.t: Crusader state of Athens and Thebes ruled in turn by Burgundian, Catalan and Florentine lords for two and a half centuries.
duchy-of-athens.o: In 1205 [[e:boniface-i-marquis-of-montferrat|Boniface of Montferrat]] granted [[s:athens|Athens]] and [[s:thebes|Thebes]] to the Burgundian knight [[e:otho-de-la-roche|Otho de la Roche]], who took the title Lord of [[e:athens|Athens]]. His nephew [[e:guy-i-de-la-roche|Guy I]] was styled Duke of Athens by the mid-13th century. The duchy covered [[e:attica|Attica]], [[e:boeotia|Boeotia]] and parts of [[e:locris|Locris]], and was nominally subject to the [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]].
duchy-of-athens.r: Under the de la [[e:hoffmann-la-roche|Roche]] family the duchy prospered, with its court at [[s:thebes|Thebes]], a [[e:silk|silk]] industry and a [[e:latin|Latin]] church that turned the [[e:parthenon|Parthenon]] into a Catholic cathedral of Our Lady. Greek peasants remained [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]]. In 1311 the [[e:catalan-company|Catalan Company]] killed Duke [[e:walter-v-of-brienne|Walter of Brienne]] at [[e:battle-of-halmyros|Halmyros]] and ruled the duchy for the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]] and [[e:sicily|Sicily]].
duchy-of-athens.e: [[e:nerio-i-acciaioli|Nerio I Acciaioli]], a Florentine banker's son, took [[s:athens|Athens]] in 1388 and founded a new ducal line. The [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], who already exacted tribute, captured [[e:athens|Athens]] in 1456 and the Acropolis in 1458, annexing the duchy.
duchy-of-athens.la: Old French, Catalan, Italian, Medieval Greek

dal-riata.t: A Gaelic kingdom spanning north-east Ireland and Argyll whose kings, settling Scotland's west coast, helped make Gaelic the language of medieval Scotland.
dal-riata.o: Dal Riata originated in [[e:county-antrim|County Antrim]], and by about 500 its rulers held lands across the [[e:north-channel|North Channel]] in [[e:argyll|Argyll]]. Tradition credits [[e:fergus-mor|Fergus Mor mac Eirc]] with moving the dynasty to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], though the story was shaped by later writers. The Scottish part grew into a federation of kindreds centred on the hillfort of [[e:dunadd|Dunadd]].
dal-riata.r: Power was shared among kindreds such as [[s:cenel-ngabrain|Cenel nGabrain]], [[s:cenel-loairn|Cenel Loairn]] and Cenel nOengusa, recorded in the [[e:senchus-fer-n-alban|Senchus fer nAlban]], a [[e:census|census]] of houses and naval levies. [[e:columba|Columba's]] monastery on [[e:iona|Iona]], founded in 563 with royal favour, made the kingdom a centre of Irish [[e:christianity|Christianity]], scholarship and missionary work reaching [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]].
dal-riata.e: Defeat at [[e:battle-of-moira|Mag Rath]] in 637 weakened its hold on its Irish lands. In the 8th century it fell under the [[e:picts|Picts]], and [[e:vikings|Viking]] raids from the 790s shattered its sea power. By the mid 9th century its territory and Gaelic culture merged with [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]] into the kingdom later known as Alba, the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]].

duchy-of-florence.t: The first Medici duchy, created by Charles V in 1532, under which Cosimo I conquered Siena and turned Florence into a princely state.
duchy-of-florence.o: After the siege of 1529–1530 ended the last [[s:republic-of-florence|Republic of Florence]], [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Charles V]] made [[e:alessandro-de-medici|Alessandro de' Medici]] hereditary duke in 1532. Alessandro ruled with the support of imperial troops and built the [[e:fortezza-da-basso|Fortezza da Basso]] to control the city.
duchy-of-florence.r: [[e:alessandro-de-medici|Alessandro]] was murdered by his cousin [[e:lorenzino-de-medici|Lorenzino]] in 1537, and the 17-year-old [[e:cosimo-i-de-medici|Cosimo I de' Medici]] was chosen to succeed him. Cosimo crushed the republican exiles at [[e:battle-of-montemurlo|Montemurlo]] that year and built an efficient absolutist state. He founded the Uffizi offices, designed by [[e:giorgio-vasari|Giorgio Vasari]] from 1560, created a navy and the [[e:order-of-saint-stephen-tuscany|Order of Saint Stephen]], and conquered the [[s:republic-of-siena|Republic of Siena]] in 1555.
duchy-of-florence.e: In 1569 [[e:pope-pius-v|Pope Pius V]] raised [[e:cosimo-i-de-medici|Cosimo]] to [[e:grand-duke-of-tuscany|Grand Duke of Tuscany]], and the duchy became the [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Grand Duchy of Tuscany]].

duchy-of-pomerania.t: A Baltic duchy ruled by the native Griffin dynasty for five centuries, from its Christianisation in the 1120s to its partition after the Thirty Years' War.
duchy-of-pomerania.o: [[e:wartislaw-i-duke-of-pomerania|Wartislaw I]] united Slavic tribes around the lower [[e:oder-river|Oder]] and [[e:szczecin|Szczecin]] in the early 12th century under Polish overlordship. In 1124 and 1128 [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:otto-of-bamberg|Otto of Bamberg]] converted the [[e:pomeranians-slavic-tribe|Pomeranians]] to [[e:christianity|Christianity]]. In 1181 Bogislaw I became a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]], making [[e:pomerania|Pomerania]] part of the Empire.
duchy-of-pomerania.r: The [[e:house-of-griffins|Griffin]] dukes encouraged German settlement and founded towns, many of which joined the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]], including [[e:stralsund|Stralsund]], [[e:greifswald|Greifswald]] and [[e:szczecin|Szczecin]]. The duchy was frequently divided into [[e:pomerania-wolgast|Pomerania-Wolgast]] and [[e:pomerania-stettin|Pomerania-Stettin]]. [[e:bogislaw-x|Bogislaw X]] reunited it in 1478, and [[e:johannes-bugenhagen|Johannes Bugenhagen]] introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1534. [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] long claimed overlordship.
duchy-of-pomerania.e: The last duke, [[e:bogislaw-xiv|Bogislaw XIV]], died in 1637 during the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]], with [[e:sweden|Sweden]] occupying the land. The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 split the duchy: Sweden took western [[e:pomerania|Pomerania]] and [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] the east. Most of the region became Polish in 1945.

dhrol-state.t: A Jadeja Rajput state of Kathiawar founded by a kinsman of the Jams of Nawanagar, one of the salute states of the peninsula.
dhrol-state.o: Dhrol was founded in 1595 by Hardholji, a brother of [[e:jam-rawal|Jam Rawal]], the founder of Nawanagar, who took the town and its surrounding villages from earlier holders. It belonged to the wider family of [[e:jadeja|Jadeja]] states that spread from [[s:cutch-state|Kutch]] into northern [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]].
dhrol-state.r: The Thakor Sahib ruled a compact territory of [[e:cotton|cotton]] and grain villages in the [[s:nawanagar-state|Halar]] region. Like other [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] states it paid tribute to the Mughal governors of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and later to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]], before coming under British protection after the settlement of 1807. It was a nine-gun salute state.
dhrol-state.e: Dhrol merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948, which became part of [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1956 and of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. The town now lies in [[s:nawanagar-state|Jamnagar]] district.

duchy-of-savoy.t: The Alpine duchy of the house of Savoy that straddled France and Italy and grew into the Kingdom of Sardinia, the core of united Italy.
duchy-of-savoy.o: In 1416 [[e:sigismund-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Sigismund]] raised Count [[e:amadeus-viii-duke-of-savoy|Amadeus VIII]] of the [[s:county-of-savoy|County of Savoy]] to the rank of duke. Amadeus later retired and was elected antipope Felix V in 1439. The duchy then included Savoy, [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]], [[e:nice|Nice]], [[e:bresse|Bresse]] and the [[e:vaud|Vaud]].
duchy-of-savoy.r: The dukes ruled an Alpine state of pass tolls, farming and soldiers. French occupation from 1536 ended when [[e:emmanuel-philibert-duke-of-savoy|Emmanuel Philibert]] recovered his lands at [[e:peace-of-cateau-cambresis|Cateau-Cambrésis]] in 1559 and moved the capital from [[e:chambery|Chambéry]] to [[e:turin|Turin]] in 1563. [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]] lost [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] and the [[e:vaud|Vaud]] but built a centralised military state. [[e:victor-amadeus-ii|Victor Amadeus II]] gained [[e:sicily|Sicily]] in 1713, exchanged for [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] in 1720.
duchy-of-savoy.e: From 1720 the dukes were kings of [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]]. [[e:france|France]] annexed [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]] in 1792–1815. In 1847 the 'perfect fusion' merged the mainland states with Sardinia, ending the duchy as a separate state; Savoy itself passed to France in 1860.

demetae.t: People of south-west Wales whose name survives in Dyfed, and who accepted Roman rule with little recorded fighting.
demetae.o: The Demetae lived in what is now [[e:pembrokeshire|Pembrokeshire]] and western [[e:carmarthenshire|Carmarthenshire]], a region of small defended farmsteads, known as raths, and coastal promontory forts. Ptolemy recorded them in the 2nd century, but no earlier writer describes them, and they were probably a grouping of local communities with long roots in the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]].
demetae.r: Unlike their neighbours the [[s:silures|Silures]] and [[s:ordovices|Ordovices]], the Demetae are not recorded as resisting [[e:rome|Rome]], and their territory needed few garrisons. Farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-rearing sustained a dispersed population, and the region looked west across the [[e:irish-sea|Irish Sea]]. The [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] mined gold at [[e:dolaucothi-gold-mines|Dolaucothi]] on the eastern edge of their land.
demetae.e: After the conquest of [[e:wales|Wales]] in the 70s the Demetae formed a civitas centred on [[e:carmarthen|Moridunum]], modern Carmarthen, one of the westernmost towns of [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]]. The name passed to the post-[[s:roman-kingdom|Roman Kingdom]] of [[s:kingdom-of-dyfed|Dyfed]], ruled by a dynasty of Irish descent, and survives in the modern county of Dyfed.

darkoti-state.t: One of the tiniest princely states in India, a Rajput chiefship of a few villages in the Shimla hills.
darkoti-state.o: Tradition dates the ruling family to around 1500, but little is reliably known of its origins.
darkoti-state.r: Darkoti covered only a handful of villages east of [[e:shimla|Shimla]] and had a very small population and revenue. It was restored under British protection after the [[e:anglo-nepalese-war|Anglo-Nepalese War]] as one of the [[e:simla-hill-states|Simla Hill States]]. Its history is poorly recorded.
darkoti-state.e: Darkoti merged into [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]] in April 1948 and is now part of [[e:shimla|Shimla]] district.

danish-kingdom-of-east-anglia.t: The Viking kingdom founded by Guthrum in East Anglia after his defeat by Alfred, the first Danish state in England to accept Christianity.
danish-kingdom-of-east-anglia.o: After Alfred defeated [[e:guthrum|Guthrum]] at [[e:battle-of-edington|Edington]] in 878, the Danish leader accepted baptism with the name Aethelstan. In 879 his army settled [[s:kingdom-of-east-anglia|East Anglia]], the former [[e:kingdom-of-east-anglia|Kingdom of East Anglia]], and a treaty with Alfred around 886 fixed the boundary along the [[e:river-lea|Lea]], the [[e:river-great-ouse|Ouse]] and [[e:watling-street|Watling Street]].
danish-kingdom-of-east-anglia.r: [[e:guthrum|Guthrum]] ruled as a Christian king and minted coins under his baptismal name. Danish settlers took land across [[e:norfolk|Norfolk]] and [[e:suffolk|Suffolk]], and soon after his death coins honouring the martyred [[e:edmund-the-martyr|King Edmund]] were issued, showing rapid integration. Later rulers, such as [[e:eohric|Eohric]], are poorly documented.
danish-kingdom-of-east-anglia.e: The kingdom joined attacks on English territory, but [[e:edward-the-elder|Edward the Elder]] conquered it in 917 to 918, and the East Anglian [[e:danes|Danes]] submitted. It became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-anglo-saxons|Kingdom of the Anglo-Saxons]] and later an earldom of [[e:england|England]].

dutch-formosa.t: The Dutch East India Company's colony in south-western Taiwan, which brought the first large-scale Chinese settlement to the island before Koxinga expelled it in 1662.
dutch-formosa.o: Seeking a base for the [[e:china|China]] trade, the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] failed to take [[e:macau|Macau]] in 1622 and occupied the [[e:penghu|Penghu]] islands, but a [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] fleet forced them out in 1624. By agreement they moved to Tayouan on the coast of [[s:republic-of-china|Taiwan]], where they built [[e:fort-zeelandia-taiwan|Fort Zeelandia]], within the sphere of [[e:dutch-east-india-company|Dutch East India Company]] territories in [[e:asia|Asia]].
dutch-formosa.r: The Company ruled through a governor and council, subdued indigenous villages by force and treaty, and expelled the Spanish from the north in 1642. It recruited Chinese settlers to grow [[e:rice|rice]] and [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], taxing them heavily, and exported deer skins to [[e:japan|Japan]]. Reformed missionaries such as [[e:georgius-candidius|Georgius Candidius]] wrote the [[e:siraya-people|Siraya]] language in [[e:latin|Latin]] letters. Chinese discontent erupted in the [[e:guo-huaiyi-rebellion|Guo Huaiyi revolt]] of 1652.
dutch-formosa.e: In 1661 the [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] loyalist [[e:koxinga|Koxinga]] landed with a large fleet and besieged [[e:fort-zeelandia-taiwan|Fort Zeelandia]] for nine months. Governor [[e:frederick-coyett|Frederick Coyett]] surrendered in February 1662, and the colony became the [[s:kingdom-of-tungning|Kingdom of Tungning]].
dutch-formosa.re: Indigenous religions, Chinese folk religion, Reformed Christianity

duala-kingdoms.t: Trading chiefdoms of the Duala people on the Wouri estuary, whose kings Bell and Akwa controlled commerce with Europeans and signed the treaty that created German Kamerun.
duala-kingdoms.o: The [[e:duala-people|Duala]] settled on the Wouri estuary, probably in the 17th century, and by the late 1600s were dealing with European ships that called at the river. Their settlements grew into rival lineage chiefdoms, chief among them Bell (Bonanjo) and Akwa, with Deido and Bonaberi as smaller units. Leaders styled themselves kings in dealings with European traders.
duala-kingdoms.r: Power rested on middleman trade: the [[e:duala-people|Duala]] bought slaves, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and later [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] and palm kernels from inland peoples and sold them to British, [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and German merchants, refusing outsiders direct access to the interior. Kings ruled with lineage heads and the ngondo assembly. British missionaries, notably [[e:alfred-saker|Alfred Saker]] from 1845, introduced [[e:baptists|Baptist]] [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and a written Duala language.
duala-kingdoms.e: On 12 July 1884 King Bell and King Akwa signed a treaty with German agents, and the estuary became the core of [[s:kamerun|Kamerun]]. [[e:douala|Douala]] grew into [[e:cameroon|Cameroon's]] main port, and Bell and Akwa families remained prominent; [[e:rudolf-duala-manga-bell|Rudolf Duala Manga Bell]] was executed by the Germans in 1914.

dynasty-of-e.t: The mixed series of Babylonian kings who ruled from about 979 to 732 BCE, through Aramean upheaval and growing Assyrian domination.
dynasty-of-e.o: The Dynasty of E is the conventional name for the kings who followed the Elamite ruler [[e:mar-biti-apla-usur|Mar-biti-apla-usur]] on the throne of [[e:babylon|Babylon]] from around 979 BCE; the king lists use an abbreviation of uncertain meaning. They were not a single family. The first, [[e:nabu-mukin-apli|Nabu-mukin-apli]], ruled at a time when [[e:aramaeans|Arameans]] cut Babylon off and the New Year festival could not be held.
dynasty-of-e.r: [[e:nabu-apla-iddina|Nabu-apla-iddina]] restored the cult of [[e:utu|Shamash]] at [[e:sippar|Sippar]], commemorated on the [[e:tablet-of-shamash|Sun-god Tablet]]. [[e:marduk-zakir-shumi-i|Marduk-zakir-shumi I]] relied on [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] to put down his brother's revolt, a sign of growing dependence. [[e:chaldean-tribes|Chaldean tribes]] such as [[s:bit-yakin|Bit-Yakin]] and [[s:bit-amukani|Bit-Amukani]] grew powerful in the south. Under [[e:nabonassar|Nabonassar]] (747 to 734 BCE) systematic astronomical observations and the [[e:babylonian-chronicles|Babylonian Chronicles]] began, later used by Ptolemy.
dynasty-of-e.e: After [[e:nabonassar|Nabonassar]], [[e:nabu-mukin-zeri|Nabu-mukin-zeri of Bit-Amukani]] seized the throne in 732 BCE, and Tiglath-Pileser III of [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] took [[e:babylon|Babylon]] in 729 BCE, beginning direct Assyrian kingship there.

dominion-of-ceylon.t: Sri Lanka's first independent state, a Commonwealth dominion that won freedom peacefully and later became a republic.
dominion-of-ceylon.o: [[s:british-ceylon|British Ceylon]] gained independence on 4 February 1948 under the [[e:ceylon-independence-act-1947|Ceylon Independence Act]], with the British monarch remaining head of state and a Governor-General. [[e:d-s-senanayake|D. S. Senanayake]] of the [[e:united-national-party|United National Party]] became the first prime minister, and the [[e:soulbury-constitution|Soulbury Constitution]] provided a [[e:westminster-system|Westminster-style]] parliament.
dominion-of-ceylon.r: The new state disenfranchised most plantation [[e:tamils|Tamils]] of Indian origin through the citizenship laws of 1948 and 1949. [[e:s-w-r-d-bandaranaike|S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike]] won the 1956 election and passed the [[e:sinhala-only-act|Sinhala Only Act]], deepening tension with Tamils. After his assassination in 1959, his widow [[e:sirimavo-bandaranaike|Sirimavo Bandaranaike]] became the world's first woman prime minister in 1960. A youth insurrection by the [[e:janatha-vimukthi-peramuna|JVP]] was suppressed in 1971.
dominion-of-ceylon.e: A new constitution adopted on 22 May 1972 ended dominion status and renamed the country [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]], with [[e:william-gopallawa|William Gopallawa]], the last Governor-General, becoming its first president and [[e:sirimavo-bandaranaike|Sirimavo Bandaranaike]] remaining prime minister.

denkyira.t: Akan kingdom that dominated the gold-rich central forest in the 17th century before being overthrown by the rising Asante.
denkyira.o: Denkyira emerged in the early 17th century in the forest south-west of present-day [[e:kumasi|Kumasi]], among [[e:akan|Akan]] clans that had moved from the area of [[s:kingdom-of-adansi|Adansi]]. Controlling rich goldfields and routes to the coastal forts, it conquered neighbouring states, including Adansi, and grew into the leading power of the central Akan forest.
denkyira.r: Under [[e:boa-amponsem|Boa Amponsem]] in the late 17th century, Denkyira took tribute from many [[e:akan|Akan]] states, including the young [[e:ashanti-empire|Asante]] chiefdoms, and held the [[e:elmina-note|Elmina Note]], a rent paid by the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] at [[e:elmina|Elmina]]. Its wealth came from gold mining and trade in gold and slaves with the [[s:dutch-gold-coast|Dutch Gold Coast]].
denkyira.e: Denkyira's demands provoked revolt. In 1701 [[e:osei-tutu-i|Osei Tutu]] of [[e:ashanti-empire|Asante]] defeated and killed King [[e:ntim-gyakari|Ntim Gyakari]] at [[e:battle-of-feyiase|Feyiase]], and Denkyira became tributary to the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]]. It survives as a traditional area in [[e:ghana|Ghana's]] Central Region.

dar-sila.t: A Daju sultanate in south-eastern Chad, heir to the old Daju kings of Darfur, that kept its autonomy between Wadai and Darfur until 1916.
dar-sila.o: The Daju had ruled in [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]] before the [[s:tunjur-kingdom|Tunjur]], as the [[s:daju-kingdom|Daju kingdom]]. Their royal line later moved south-west to the [[e:sila-region|Sila]] region, in present-day south-eastern [[e:chad|Chad]], where by the mid-17th century they had established a sultanate, eventually based at [[e:goz-beida|Goz Beida]].
dar-sila.r: Dar [[e:sila-region|Sila]]'s sultans ruled a farming population in a well-watered savanna region and controlled hunting and slave-raiding zones to the south. The sultanate paid tribute at times to the [[s:wadai-empire|Wadai Empire]] or the [[s:darfur-sultanate|Darfur Sultanate]] but retained its own dynasty. Few details of its government are recorded.
dar-sila.e: After the French conquest of [[e:wadai-empire|Wadai]], the sultan of Dar [[e:sila-region|Sila]] resisted, and French forces occupied [[e:goz-beida|Goz Beida]] in 1916. The sultanate became part of [[s:chad-french-colony|Chad (French colony)]], and its sultans continued as traditional rulers.

duchy-of-franconia.t: The short-lived stem duchy of the Franks in central Germany whose duke Conrad I became king of East Francia in 911.
duchy-of-franconia.o: In the early 10th century the Conradine family won a bloody feud with the [[e:house-of-babenberg|Babenbergs]] for dominance in [[e:franconia|Franconia]], the Frankish heartland along the Main and the middle [[e:rhine|Rhine]]. After [[e:adalbert-of-babenberg|Adalbert of Babenberg]] was executed in 906, [[e:conrad-i-of-germany|Conrad the Younger]] became the leading [[e:magnates|magnate]], recognised as duke of the [[s:franks|Franks]].
duchy-of-franconia.r: In 911 Conrad was elected king of [[s:east-francia|East Francia]] as [[e:conrad-i-of-germany|Conrad I]], the first non-Carolingian ruler, while his brother [[e:eberhard-of-franconia|Eberhard]] governed [[e:franconia|Franconia]]. Conrad struggled against the [[e:saxons|Saxon]], Bavarian and Swabian dukes and the [[e:magyars|Magyars]]. Dying in 918, he reportedly sent the royal insignia to [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler of Saxony]], his former enemy.
duchy-of-franconia.e: [[e:eberhard-of-franconia|Eberhard]] accepted [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry I]]'s kingship but rebelled against Otto I and was killed at the [[e:battle-of-andernach|Battle of Andernach]] in 939. Otto did not appoint a new duke; [[e:franconia|Franconia]] passed directly to the crown and fragmented into bishoprics such as [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] and [[e:bamberg|Bamberg]] and later secular lordships.

dutch-east-indies.t: The Dutch colonial state in the Indonesian archipelago from 1800 to 1949, forerunner of the borders of modern Indonesia.
dutch-east-indies.o: When the charter of the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] expired at the end of 1799, its Asian possessions passed to the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] state. Governor-General [[e:herman-willem-daendels|Herman Willem Daendels]] reorganised [[e:java|Java]] from 1808, and after the interlude of [[s:british-java|British Java]] the Dutch returned in 1816, then fought the [[e:java-war|Java War]] of 1825 to 1830 against [[e:diponegoro|Prince Diponegoro]].
dutch-east-indies.r: Under the [[e:cultivation-system|Cultivation System]] introduced by [[e:johannes-van-den-bosch|Johannes van den Bosch]] in 1830, Javanese villages had to grow export crops such as [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and [[e:indigo|indigo]], making the colony hugely profitable. Conquest of the outer islands followed, including the long [[e:aceh-war|Aceh War]] from 1873. The [[e:ethical-policy|Ethical Policy]] after 1901 expanded schooling, and nationalist movements such as [[e:sarekat-islam|Sarekat Islam]] and [[e:sukarno|Sukarno's]] party grew.
dutch-east-indies.e: [[e:japan|Japan]] conquered the colony in 1942. [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]] proclaimed independence in August 1945, and after four years of war and diplomacy the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] transferred [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] on 27 December 1949, keeping only [[s:netherlands-new-guinea|Netherlands New Guinea]] until 1962.

duchy-of-leczyca.t: A small Piast duchy of central Poland that changed hands among the Kuyavian and Masovian dukes before rejoining the Crown.
duchy-of-leczyca.o: Leczyca, an old stronghold where Polish church synods were held in the 12th century, became a separate duchy in the age of division. In 1229 [[e:konrad-i-of-masovia|Konrad I of Masovia]] took control of it, and after Konrad's death in 1247 it passed to his son [[e:casimir-i-of-kuyavia|Casimir I of Kuyavia]], whose descendants ruled it in various combinations with [[s:duchy-of-sieradz|Sieradz]] and [[e:kuyavia|Kuyavia]].
duchy-of-leczyca.r: Leczyca was a farming land in the middle of [[e:poland|Poland]] with a fortified castle and a collegiate church at [[e:tum-collegiate-church|Tum]], one of the finest Romanesque churches in the country. Its dukes were minor [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]], among them [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high]], who held it in the 1290s while building his base for reuniting Poland. The duchy suffered raids by the [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]] and the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]].
duchy-of-leczyca.e: After [[e:poland|Poland]] was reunited in 1320, Leczyca continued as a duchy under [[e:wladyslaw-of-dobrzyn|Wladyslaw of Dobrzyn]], a nephew of the king. When he died in 1352 it was incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385) as a province, later the [[e:leczyca-voivodeship|Leczyca Voivodeship]].

duchy-of-teck.t: Swabian duchy of a Zähringen branch named after Teck castle near Kirchheim, a ducal title without a duchy that later passed to the British royal family's ancestors.
duchy-of-teck.o: Adalbert, a younger son of Duke [[e:conrad-i-duke-of-zahringen|Conrad of Zähringen]], inherited lands around the castle of Teck on the edge of the [[e:swabian-jura|Swabian Jura]] and called himself Duke of Teck from 1187. The ducal title came from his family's rank rather than any ancient duchy, and the lands were modest, centred on Kirchheim and Owen.
duchy-of-teck.r: The dukes ruled a small cluster of castles, towns and farmland and often served greater lords, including the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. The family split into lines and, under financial pressure, sold its holdings piece by piece. Most of the territory, including Kirchheim, was sold to the Counts of Württemberg in 1381 to 1386.
duchy-of-teck.e: The last duke, Ludwig, Patriarch of [[e:aquileia|Aquileia]], died in 1439. Württemberg later took the ducal title, and in 1871 it was revived for [[e:francis-duke-of-teck|Francis of Teck]], father of Queen Mary of [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Great Britain]]. Teck castle survives in part.

dominion-of-new-zealand.t: New Zealand's four decades as a British dominion, which built one of the world's first welfare states and fought in both world wars.
dominion-of-new-zealand.o: [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] declined to join the [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Commonwealth of Australia]] in 1901. At the request of Prime Minister [[e:joseph-ward|Joseph Ward]], the [[s:colony-of-new-zealand|Colony of New Zealand]] was proclaimed a dominion on 26 September 1907, signalling self-governing status within the [[s:british-empire|British Empire]]. The change was largely symbolic, as the country already ran its own affairs.
dominion-of-new-zealand.r: [[e:william-massey|William Massey's]] Reform government held office from 1912 to 1925 and sent the expeditionary force whose losses at [[e:gallipoli-campaign|Gallipoli]] in 1915 shaped national identity. Farm exports of wool, meat and butter to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] dominated the economy, and the [[e:great-depression|Depression]] hit hard. The first Labour government under [[e:michael-joseph-savage|Michael Joseph Savage]], from 1935, built state housing and the [[e:social-security-act-1938|Social Security Act]] of 1938. [[e:peter-fraser|Peter Fraser]] led the country through the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]].
dominion-of-new-zealand.e: [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] was cautious about formal independence and did not adopt the [[e:statute-of-westminster-1931|Statute of Westminster]] of 1931 until November 1947. With that act it became fully sovereign, and the term dominion fell out of use.
