dvaravati.t: A Mon Buddhist civilisation of central Thailand from the 7th to 11th centuries, the earliest Theravada culture of the Chao Phraya basin.
dvaravati.o: Dvaravati takes its name from [[e:silver|silver]] coins found at [[e:nakhon-pathom|Nakhon Pathom]] and other sites inscribed 'meritorious deeds of the king of Dvaravati', matching the Duoluobodi of Chinese pilgrims. Moated towns appear in the [[e:chao-phraya-river|Chao Phraya]] valley from around the 6th and 7th centuries, built by Mon-speaking communities.
dvaravati.r: Whether Dvaravati was a single kingdom or a cultural network of city-states, including [[e:nakhon-pathom|Nakhon Pathom]], [[e:ramathibodi-i|U Thong]], [[e:khu-bua|Khu Bua]], [[e:si-thep|Si Thep]] and [[s:lavo-kingdom|Lopburi]], is debated. Its people were early adopters of [[e:theravada-buddhism|Theravada Buddhism]], using Pali and [[e:old-mon|Old Mon]] in inscriptions, and produced distinctive Buddha images, stone [[e:dharmachakra|Wheels of the Law]] and terracotta stupa decoration. Moats, canals and [[e:rice|rice]] farming supported the towns.
dvaravati.e: From the 10th and 11th centuries the region came under the influence of the [[s:khmer-empire|Khmer Empire]], and Lavo became a [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] centre. Dvaravati's Mon Buddhist traditions passed to [[s:hariphunchai|Hariphunchai]] in the north and fed into the later Thai kingdoms of [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]] and [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]].

domain-of-matthew-csak.t: Vast private domain of the magnate Matthew Csák in north-western Hungary, ruled like an independent state during the struggle for the crown.
domain-of-matthew-csak.o: [[e:matthew-iii-csak|Matthew III Csák]], of a leading baronial clan, built up power in the Váh valley in the 1290s as royal authority collapsed. After the death of [[e:andrew-iii-of-hungary|Andrew III]] in 1301 ended the [[e:arpad|Árpád]] line, he backed rival claimants and seized castles across north-western [[e:hungary|Hungary]], centred on [[e:trencin|Trencsén]] (Trenčín).
domain-of-matthew-csak.r: At its height he controlled some fourteen counties in modern [[e:slovakia|Slovakia]] and northern [[e:hungary|Hungary]], with around 50 castles. He kept his own court, palatine and household officials, granted lands, made treaties with [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and ran justice and taxation like a king. He refused to submit to Charles I, and the pope excommunicated him in 1311.
domain-of-matthew-csak.e: Charles I defeated his allies at [[e:battle-of-rozgony|Rozgony]] in 1312 but could not take his heartland. After Matthew died in 1321, royal armies quickly took his castles, and the domain returned to the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1301-1526|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1301-1526).

delaware-colony.t: The Lower Counties on the Delaware, a former Swedish and Dutch settlement area that shared Pennsylvania's governor but kept its own assembly and became the first state.
delaware-colony.o: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] settlement of [[e:zwaanendael|Zwaanendael]] near modern [[e:lewes-delaware|Lewes]] was destroyed in 1631, and in 1638 [[s:new-sweden|New Sweden]] built [[e:fort-christina|Fort Christina]] at what is now [[e:wilmington-delaware|Wilmington]]. [[s:new-netherland|New Netherland]] conquered the Swedish colony in 1655, and its [[e:fort-casimir|Fort Casimir]], renamed New Amstel, later became [[e:new-castle-delaware|New Castle]]. After the English conquest of 1664 the area was ruled from [[e:new-york|New York]] under [[e:james-ii-of-england|James, Duke of York]].
delaware-colony.r: In 1682 James granted the three counties of [[e:new-castle-delaware|New Castle]], Kent and [[s:kingdom-of-sussex|Sussex]] to [[e:william-penn|William Penn]], who governed them with the [[s:province-of-pennsylvania|Province of Pennsylvania]]. The Lower Counties resented domination by [[e:philadelphia|Philadelphia]] and from 1704 met in their own assembly at New Castle, while still sharing the Penn family's governor. Farmers of Swedish, Finnish, [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and English descent grew grain and tobacco, and enslaved Africans worked many farms in the south.
delaware-colony.e: On 15 June 1776 the assembly declared the Lower Counties separate from both [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:pennsylvania|Pennsylvania]], and [[e:caesar-rodney|Caesar Rodney's]] ride helped carry the vote for independence. As the state of Delaware, it was the first to ratify the [[e:constitution-of-the-united-states|United States Constitution]] in 1787.

duchy-of-bavaria.t: One of Germany's oldest territories, a duchy for more than a thousand years under the Agilolfings, Welfs and Wittelsbachs, and the core of modern Bavaria.
duchy-of-bavaria.o: The [[e:bavarians|Bavarians]] (Baiuvarii) appear in the mid 6th century between the [[e:danube|Danube]], the [[e:lech-river|Lech]] and the [[e:alps|Alps]], a people formed from Germanic groups and the Romanised population. Around 555 the Frankish kings recognised [[e:garibald-i-of-bavaria|Garibald I]] of the [[e:agilolfings|Agilolfing]] family as duke. [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] later became a stem duchy of [[s:east-francia|East Francia]] and the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
duchy-of-bavaria.r: The [[e:agilolfings|Agilolfing]] dukes ruled almost as kings, with their own law code, the [[e:lex-baiuvariorum|Lex Baiuvariorum]], and bishoprics organised by [[e:saint-boniface|Saint Boniface]] in 739 at [[e:salzburg|Salzburg]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]], [[e:freising|Freising]] and [[e:passau|Passau]]. Regensburg was the early capital. From 1180 the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] family held the duchy, ruling from [[e:munich|Munich]], [[e:landshut|Landshut]] and [[e:ingolstadt|Ingolstadt]] during long periods of division.
duchy-of-bavaria.e: [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] deposed Duke [[e:tassilo-iii-of-bavaria|Tassilo III]] in 788, but the duchy was revived. [[e:albert-iv-duke-of-bavaria|Albert IV]] reunited [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] in 1505 and imposed [[e:primogeniture|primogeniture]]. In 1623 Maximilian I received the electoral dignity during the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]], and the duchy became the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]], later the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1806.

duchy-of-bukovina.t: Habsburg crown land carved from northern Moldavia, a mosaic of Romanians, Ukrainians, Jews and Germans centred on Czernowitz.
duchy-of-bukovina.o: In 1774 Austrian troops occupied the north-western corner of [[s:principality-of-moldavia|Moldavia]], linking newly acquired [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] with [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]], and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] ceded it in 1775. Named [[e:bukovina|Bukovina]], the beech land, it was ruled by the military until 1786, then attached to [[e:galicia|Galicia]]. In 1849 it became a separate crown land with the title of duchy.
duchy-of-bukovina.r: [[e:bukovina|Bukovina]] had its own diet from 1861 and a governor at [[e:chernivtsi|Czernowitz]], which grew into a German-speaking university town after 1875. [[e:romanians|Romanians]], [[e:ukrainians|Ukrainians]], [[e:jews|Jews]], Germans and [[e:poles|Poles]] lived side by side, and in 1910 the diet adopted a compromise sharing seats among national groups. The [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] metropolitan resided in Czernowitz, and the painted monasteries of [[e:suceava|Suceava]] were preserved.
duchy-of-bukovina.e: As [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] collapsed in 1918, a congress in [[e:chernivtsi|Czernowitz]] voted for union with [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]]. In 1940 the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] annexed northern [[e:bukovina|Bukovina]], which is now part of [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]], while southern Bukovina remains in [[e:romania|Romania]]. Its Jewish community was largely destroyed in the [[e:holocaust|Holocaust]].
duchy-of-bukovina.re: Eastern Orthodox Christianity, Judaism, Catholic Christianity

duchy-of-bourbon.t: The central French duchy of a Capetian branch whose last great duke betrayed Francis I and whose cousins later became kings of France.
duchy-of-bourbon.o: The lords of [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]] had held the Bourbonnais since the 10th century. In 1272 the heiress [[e:beatrice-of-bourbon|Beatrice of Bourbon]] married [[e:robert-count-of-clermont|Robert of Clermont]], son of [[e:louis-ix-of-france|Louis IX]], and in 1327 Charles IV raised the barony to a duchy for their son Louis I, creating the Capetian house of [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbon]].
duchy-of-bourbon.r: The dukes ruled from [[e:moulins|Moulins]] and gathered [[s:county-of-forez|Forez]], [[s:lordship-of-beaujeu|Beaujolais]], [[s:county-of-auvergne|Auvergne]] and [[s:county-of-la-marche|La Marche]] through marriage and inheritance, making their lands one of [[e:france|France's]] largest princely blocs. [[e:louis-ii-duke-of-bourbon|Louis II]], called the Good Duke, was a model crusading prince. [[e:anne-of-france|Anne of France]] and her husband [[e:peter-ii-duke-of-bourbon|Peter II]] governed the kingdom during the minority of [[e:charles-viii-of-france|Charles VIII]].
duchy-of-bourbon.e: [[e:charles-iii-duke-of-bourbon|Charles III]], constable of [[e:france|France]], fell out with [[e:francis-i|Francis I]], who claimed his lands; he joined [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] in 1523 and was killed leading the sack of [[e:rome|Rome]] in 1527. His lands were confiscated and joined to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]], but a younger [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]] line gave France [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry IV]].

danube-sich.t: The refuge of Zaporozhian Cossacks in the Ottoman Danube Delta after Catherine the Great destroyed their Sich.
danube-sich.o: When the Russian army abolished the [[s:zaporozhian-sich|Zaporozhian Sich]] in 1775, several thousand [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]] fled to Ottoman territory. After moving between several sites, they settled in the [[e:danube|Danube]] Delta, where the sultan allowed them to found a new Sich in return for military service. Its main centre from 1814 was at Dunavets, in modern [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]].
danube-sich.r: The [[e:danube|Danube]] Sich kept the old Zaporozhian institutions of an elected kish otaman, a council and kurins. The [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]] fished, farmed and fought in Ottoman campaigns, including against Serbian and Greek rebels. They clashed repeatedly with the [[e:nekrasov-cossacks|Nekrasov Cossacks]], Russian [[e:old-believers|Old Believers]] settled nearby, over fishing grounds and Ottoman favour.
danube-sich.e: During the [[e:russo-turkish-war-1806-1812|Russo-Turkish War]] of 1828, the kish otaman [[e:osyp-hladky|Osyp Hladky]] defected to [[e:russia|Russia]] with part of the Host. In response the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] destroyed the Sich. The defectors formed the [[e:azov|Azov]] [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] Host in Russia, while the others dispersed within Ottoman lands.

duchy-of-finland.t: Short-lived Finnish duchy granted to the future John III of Sweden, whose independent policy led his brother Eric XIV to crush it in 1563.
duchy-of-finland.o: In 1556 [[e:gustav-i-of-sweden|Gustav Vasa]] granted his second son John the Duchy of [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]], covering south-western [[e:finland|Finland]], as an [[e:appanage|appanage]]. John set up his court at [[e:turku-castle|Turku Castle]], which he enlarged in [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] style, and governed with considerable independence.
duchy-of-finland.r: Duke John ran his own administration, collected taxes and pursued a foreign policy of his own, which brought him into conflict with his half-brother, King [[e:eric-xiv-of-sweden|Eric XIV]]. In 1562 he married [[e:catherine-jagiellon|Catherine Jagiellon]], sister of King [[e:sigismund-ii-augustus|Sigismund II Augustus]] of [[e:poland|Poland]], and lent money to Poland while [[e:sweden|Sweden]] and Poland competed for [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]].
duchy-of-finland.e: [[e:eric-xiv-of-sweden|Eric XIV]] regarded this as treason. In 1563 his army besieged and took [[e:turku-castle|Turku Castle]], and John and [[e:catherine-jagiellon|Catherine]] were imprisoned at [[e:gripsholm-castle|Gripsholm]]. The duchy was abolished, and [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] returned to direct rule by the [[s:kingdom-of-sweden|Kingdom of Sweden]]. John deposed Eric in 1568 and reigned as [[e:john-iii-of-sweden|John III]].

duchy-of-magdeburg.t: The secularised Archbishopric of Magdeburg as a Brandenburg-Prussian duchy, rebuilt after the Thirty Years' War's worst massacre.
duchy-of-magdeburg.o: The [[s:archbishopric-of-magdeburg|Archbishopric of Magdeburg]] was devastated in the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]], when [[e:johann-tserclaes-count-of-tilly|Tilly]]'s army sacked the city in 1631. The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 promised it to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] on the death of its administrator, [[e:augustus-duke-of-saxe-weissenfels|Augustus of Saxe-Weissenfels]]; when he died in 1680, it became the Duchy of [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]].
duchy-of-magdeburg.r: [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] made [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] one of its strongest fortresses and an administrative centre. The duchy was a rich grain region of the [[e:magdeburg-borde|Magdeburg Börde]], and [[e:huguenots|Huguenot]] and Palatine refugees settled in the city. The [[e:university-of-halle|University of Halle]], founded in 1694 in the duchy, became a centre of [[e:pietism|Pietism]] and the early [[e:age-of-enlightenment|Enlightenment]] under [[e:august-hermann-francke|August Hermann Francke]] and [[e:christian-thomasius|Christian Thomasius]].
duchy-of-magdeburg.e: [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] lost the duchy to the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] in 1807. In 1815 it returned to Prussia and formed the core of the [[e:province-of-saxony|Province of Saxony]], with [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] as provincial capital, a role it now holds in [[e:saxony-anhalt|Saxony-Anhalt]].

daura-emirate.t: The emirate established in Daura, the legendary mother city of the Hausa, after the Fulani jihad, while the old Hausa dynasty survived in exile.
daura-emirate.o: [[s:kingdom-of-daura|Daura]] is honoured in the [[e:bayajidda|Bayajidda]] legend as the oldest of the [[e:hausa|Hausa states]]. In the [[e:jihad|jihad]] of [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]], [[e:fula|Fulani]] forces under [[e:mallam-ishaku|Mallam Ishaku]] took the town around 1806, and the Hausa ruler fled north. Ishaku became the first Fulani emir, under the overall authority of [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]], while the exiled Hausa line set up rival courts at [[e:zango|Zango]] and Baure.
daura-emirate.r: The [[e:fula|Fulani]] [[e:emirate|emirate]] was small and exposed, lying on the frontier between the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]] and the unconquered [[e:hausa|Hausa states]] of [[s:sultanate-of-maradi|Maradi]] and [[s:sultanate-of-damagaram|Damagaram]] to the north. It ruled through titled officials on the [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] pattern, collected Islamic taxes and joined in the wars of the frontier. [[s:kingdom-of-daura|Daura]] remained a place of symbolic prestige for all Hausa.
daura-emirate.e: After British occupation in 1903 the old dynasty was restored: the British installed the head of the [[e:zango|Zango]] line as emir, and his descendants still reign. The Anglo-French boundary split the old [[s:kingdom-of-daura|Daura]] country between [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]] and [[e:niger-river|Niger]].

da-yining.t: The short dynasty of Yang Ganzhen in western Yunnan, overthrown in 937 by Duan Siping, founder of the Dali Kingdom.
da-yining.o: [[e:yang-ganzhen|Yang Ganzhen]], a leading official of the [[e:lake-erhai|Erhai]] region who had brought down [[s:da-changhe|Da Changhe]] in 928 and installed [[s:da-tianxing|Da Tianxing]], deposed his own puppet [[e:zhao-shanzheng|Zhao Shanzheng]] in 929 and proclaimed the kingdom of Da [[e:yining|Yining]] at [[e:yangjumie|Yangjumie]].
da-yining.r: Sources are scanty. Later accounts describe [[e:yang-ganzhen|Yang Ganzhen's]] rule as oppressive and his government as unstable, alienating both the Bai nobility and the many tribal peoples of eastern [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]].
da-yining.e: In 937 [[e:duan-siping|Duan Siping]], a military commander of the Tonghai region, allied with eastern tribes, marched on the capital and overthrew [[e:yang-ganzhen|Yang Ganzhen]]. He founded the [[s:dali-kingdom|Dali Kingdom]], which lasted until the Mongol conquest.

dutch-republic.t: The federal republic born of the revolt against Spain, which became the world's leading trading power and a centre of art, science and toleration.
dutch-republic.o: The northern provinces of the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]] rose against [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]] from 1568 under [[e:william-the-silent|William the Silent]]. They allied in the [[e:union-of-utrecht|Union of Utrecht]] in 1579 and renounced Philip by the [[e:act-of-abjuration|Act of Abjuration]] in 1581. After failing to find a new sovereign, the provinces governed themselves as a republic, recognised by [[e:spain|Spain]] in the [[e:peace-of-munster|Peace of Münster]] in 1648.
dutch-republic.r: Each province was sovereign, sending delegates to the [[e:states-general-of-the-netherlands|States General]] at [[e:the-hague|The Hague]], while Holland's [[e:grand-pensionary|Grand Pensionary]] and the [[e:house-of-orange-nassau|Orange-Nassau]] stadtholders competed for leadership. Founded in 1602, the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] built an Asian trading empire. [[e:amsterdam|Amsterdam]] became [[e:europe|Europe's]] financial centre, and [[e:rembrandt|Rembrandt]], [[e:johannes-vermeer|Vermeer]], [[e:baruch-spinoza|Spinoza]] and [[e:christiaan-huygens|Huygens]] worked in relative freedom, though the Reformed church was official.
dutch-republic.e: After the disaster year of 1672, [[e:william-iii-of-england|William III]] led resistance to [[e:france|France]] and became king of [[e:england|England]] in 1689. The 18th century brought decline and clashes between [[e:orangists|Orangists]] and Patriots. In 1795 French armies and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] revolutionaries founded the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]].

dilmun.t: The island trading power of Bahrain that linked Mesopotamia with Magan and the Indus, remembered in Sumerian myth as a pure land.
dilmun.o: Dilmun appears in Sumerian texts by the late 3rd millennium BCE as a trading partner of Ur. From around 2200 BCE the settlement at [[e:qalat-al-bahrain|Qal'at al-Bahrain]] grew into a walled town, and the [[e:barbar-temple|Barbar]] culture built temples at Barbar and [[e:saar-bahrain|Saar]] and tens of thousands of burial mounds across northern [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]], with influence reaching [[e:failaka-island|Failaka]] in [[s:sheikhdom-of-kuwait|Kuwait]] and the coast of eastern [[e:arabia|Arabia]].
dilmun.r: Dilmun was a merchant state, handling [[e:copper|copper]] from [[s:magan|Magan]], carnelian and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] from the [[e:indus|Indus]] and grain and textiles from [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]], and it set its own weight standard and stamp seals. Its gods [[e:inzak|Inzak]] and [[e:enki|Enki]] were worshipped at freshwater springs. Around 1500 BCE [[s:kassite-babylonia|Kassite Babylonia]] ruled the island through governors at [[e:qalat-al-bahrain|Qal'at al-Bahrain]], and its date trade flourished.
dilmun.e: Later kings of Dilmun paid tribute to the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]]: [[e:uperi|Uperi]] sent gifts to [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] in 709 BCE. Dilmun passed under Neo-Babylonian control and vanishes as a political entity in the 6th century BCE, the island later reappearing as [[e:tylos|Tylos]] in Greek sources. Its burial mounds are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

dauphine-of-viennois.t: The Alpine principality around Grenoble whose last ruler sold it to France on condition that the heir to the throne bear the title Dauphin.
dauphine-of-viennois.o: Around 1029 [[e:guigues-i-of-albon|Guigues the Old]], count of Albon, began gathering lands in the Viennois and the [[e:gresivaudan|Grésivaudan]] as royal power in the [[s:kingdom-of-arles|Kingdom of Arles]] weakened. His descendants made [[e:grenoble|Grenoble]] their centre, and [[e:guigues-iv-of-albon|Guigues IV]], nicknamed '[[e:dauphin-of-france|Dauphin]]', gave the family its distinctive title in the 12th century.
dauphine-of-viennois.r: The dauphins governed a mountain land of pastures, mines and passes towards [[e:italy|Italy]], and later added the [[e:brianconnais|Briançonnais]] and Gapençais. In 1339 [[e:humbert-ii-of-viennois|Humbert II]] founded a university at [[e:grenoble|Grenoble]]. The principality had its own council and courts, and its lords balanced between [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]], [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]] and the French crown.
dauphine-of-viennois.e: [[e:humbert-ii-of-viennois|Humbert II]], childless and deep in debt, sold the Dauphiné to [[e:philip-vi-of-france|Philip VI]] under the Treaty of [[e:roman-empire|Romans]], completed in 1349. It went to the king's grandson Charles, and from then on the eldest son of the French king held the title [[e:dauphin-of-france|Dauphin]], while the province joined the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia-1918.t: German client state proclaimed by Courland's Baltic German nobles in 1918, which offered its ducal crown to Kaiser Wilhelm II.
duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia-1918.o: Under German occupation, the [[e:courland|Courland]] Landesrat, a council dominated by [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] nobles, proclaimed on 8 March 1918 the restoration of the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]], covering the former [[s:governorate-of-courland|Governorate of Courland]]. It offered the ducal crown to [[e:wilhelm-ii|Wilhelm II]], and [[e:germany|Germany]] recognised the duchy on 15 March.
duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia-1918.r: The duchy had no real government of its own and depended on the German military administration that had replaced [[s:ober-ost|Ober Ost]]. Its leaders planned German settlement and close union with the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]]. [[e:latvians|Latvians]], the great majority of the population, were excluded from its councils and rejected it.
duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia-1918.e: In autumn 1918 the duchy was to join the [[s:united-baltic-duchy|United Baltic Duchy]], but [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat in November ended the scheme. The [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]], proclaimed on 18 November 1918, took over its territory after the [[e:latvian-war-of-independence|War of Independence]].

demerara-essequibo.t: A British-ruled sugar colony on the Guiana coast, formed from two Dutch colonies and shaken by the great slave rebellion of 1823.
demerara-essequibo.o: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] had occupied the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] colonies of [[s:demerara|Demerara]] and [[s:essequibo|Essequibo]] in 1796 and, after their brief return to the Dutch in 1802, again from 1803. In 1812 the British administration united them as Demerara-Essequibo, renaming the capital [[e:georgetown-guyana|Stabroek]] as Georgetown, after [[e:george-iii|George III]]. The [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1814|Convention of London]] in 1814 formally ceded the territory to [[e:britain|Britain]].
demerara-essequibo.r: The colony kept [[e:dutch|Dutch]] laws and its [[e:court-of-policy|Court of Policy]], in which planters held most power. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] dominated the economy, worked by tens of thousands of enslaved Africans. In August 1823 the [[s:demerara|Demerara]] rebellion involved some 10,000 or more enslaved people, who demanded rights they believed had been granted in [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. It was crushed with many executions. The missionary [[e:john-smith-missionary|John Smith]], accused of encouraging it, died in prison, inspiring abolitionists in [[e:britain|Britain]].
demerara-essequibo.e: In 1831 Demerara-Essequibo was merged with [[s:berbice|Berbice]] to form [[s:british-guiana|British Guiana]]. [[e:slavery|Slavery]] was abolished across the [[s:british-empire|British Empire]] in 1834. [[e:georgetown-guyana|Georgetown]] remained the capital and is today the capital of [[s:co-operative-republic-of-guyana|Guyana]], and the rebellion of 1823 is remembered as a milestone on the road to emancipation.

cr.a: Original: Acts of Union 1800 Vector: Yaddah

dir-state.t: A Pashtun principality of the mountainous north-west frontier, ruled by its Nawabs until absorption into Pakistan in 1969.
dir-state.o: The ruling family of Dir, of the Yusufzai [[e:pashtuns|Pashtun]] Painda Khel, traced their power to a religious leader, [[e:mulla-ilyas|Mulla Ilyas]], known as Akhund Baba, in the 17th century. His descendants became khans and later Nawabs of the Panjkora valley.
dir-state.r: The Nawabs ruled a rugged valley of tribal [[e:pashtuns|Pashtun]] farmers through personal authority and levies, receiving British [[e:subsidy|subsidies]] to keep the route to [[s:chitral-state|Chitral]] open after 1895. Rule was autocratic and modern education and services were very limited.
dir-state.e: Dir acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] after independence. In 1960 Nawab [[e:shah-jahan|Shah Jahan]] Khan was deposed, and in 1969 the state was abolished and became a district of the [[e:north-west-frontier-province|North-West Frontier Province]], later divided into Upper and [[e:lower-dir-district|Lower Dir]].

duchy-of-aragvi.t: A powerful Georgian duchy in the Aragvi valley, centred on the fortress of Ananuri, that controlled the main road across the Caucasus.
duchy-of-aragvi.o: The upper Aragvi valley lay on the route that later became the Georgian Military Road through the [[e:darial-pass|Darial Pass]]. From the late 14th century the eristavis of Aragvi held the region hereditarily, first under the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] and after 1490 as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli|Kingdom of Kartli]].
duchy-of-aragvi.r: The dukes commanded the mountaineers of Mtiuleti, Gudamakari and the [[e:pshavs|Pshav]] and [[e:khevsurs|Khevsur]] communities and could field large armies. Their fortress of [[e:ananuri|Ananuri]], with its 17th-century churches, overlooked the road. Ambitious dukes such as Nugzar and Zurab played major roles in Kartli's politics; Zurab helped defeat Persian forces in 1625 before being killed on the king's orders in 1629.
duchy-of-aragvi.e: Feuds with the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-ksani|Ksani]], who stormed [[e:ananuri|Ananuri]] in 1739, and rebellions against the crown weakened the house. In 1743 King [[e:teimuraz-ii-of-kakheti|Teimuraz II]] abolished the duchy and annexed it to the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli|Kingdom of Kartli]].

duchy-of-alamannia.t: The Frankish duchy that ruled the Alemanni of south-west Germany and Switzerland for two centuries, until the Carolingians abolished it at Cannstatt.
duchy-of-alamannia.o: After [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]]' victories over the [[s:alemanni|Alemanni]] around 496 and 506, the southern Alemanni stayed under Ostrogothic protection until 536, when the [[e:ostrogoths|Ostrogoth]] king [[e:witigis|Witigis]] ceded them to the [[s:franks|Franks]]. The Merovingian kings then placed the Alemanni under dukes, a region covering modern [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]], [[e:alsace|Alsace]], eastern [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]] and [[e:swabia-bavaria|Bavarian Swabia]].
duchy-of-alamannia.r: The dukes governed under Frankish overlordship but often acted independently, especially as Merovingian power weakened. Law was codified in the [[e:pactus-alamannorum|Pactus]] and the [[e:lex-alamannorum|Lex Alamannorum]] of the early 8th century. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread through bishoprics at [[e:konstanz|Constance]] and [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] and monasteries such as St Gall, founded on the hermitage of [[e:saint-gall|Gallus]], and [[e:reichenau-island|Reichenau]], founded in 724.
duchy-of-alamannia.e: Duke [[e:lantfrid|Lantfrid]] and his successor [[e:theudebald-duke-of-alamannia|Theudebald]] resisted the rising Carolingian mayors of the palace. In 746 [[e:carloman-mayor-of-the-palace|Carloman]] summoned the Alemannic nobility to [[e:blood-court-at-cannstatt|Cannstatt]] and executed many of them, ending the ducal office. Alamannia was then ruled by Frankish counts until the [[s:duchy-of-swabia|Duchy of Swabia]] emerged in the early 10th century.

duchy-of-arenberg.t: Small Eifel territory of the Arenberg family, great nobles of the Habsburg Netherlands who held ducal rank in the Empire.
duchy-of-arenberg.o: The lordship of Arenberg, named after a castle in the [[e:eifel|Eifel]], passed through heiresses to the [[e:house-of-ligne|Ligne]] family in the 16th century, which took the Arenberg name. It became a princely county in 1576, and in 1644 [[e:ferdinand-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Ferdinand III]] raised it to a duchy under Philippe-Charles d'Arenberg.
duchy-of-arenberg.r: The [[e:eifel|Eifel]] territory was tiny; the dukes' wealth and influence lay in vast estates in the Spanish and later [[s:austrian-netherlands|Austrian Netherlands]], where they served as governors, generals and courtiers in [[e:brussels|Brussels]]. The family was Catholic. After losing the left-bank lands to [[e:france|France]], the duke received the former Münster district of [[e:meppen|Meppen]] and the [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] enclave of [[e:recklinghausen|Recklinghausen]] in 1803.
duchy-of-arenberg.e: Arenberg joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] in 1806, but [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] annexed its northern lands to [[e:france|France]] in 1810. In 1815 [[e:meppen|Meppen]] came under the [[s:kingdom-of-hanover|Kingdom of Hanover]] and [[e:recklinghausen|Recklinghausen]] under [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], with the dukes as mediatised lords.

duchy-of-inowroclaw.t: A Kuyavian Piast duchy on the Teutonic border, ruled by Ziemomysl and his sons until Casimir the Great absorbed it.
duchy-of-inowroclaw.o: In the division of the [[s:duchy-of-kuyavia|Duchy of Kuyavia]] after [[e:casimir-i-of-kuyavia|Casimir I]]'s death in 1267, the northern lands around Inowroclaw went to his son [[e:ziemomysl-of-inowroclaw|Ziemomysl]]. He relied on support from the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] and the dukes of [[e:pomerelia|Pomerelia]], which caused revolts among his own nobles.
duchy-of-inowroclaw.r: Inowroclaw was a salt-producing land near the [[e:vistula|Vistula]], and its towns grew under German law. After [[e:ziemomysl-of-inowroclaw|Ziemomysl]] died in 1287 his sons Leszek, Przemysl and Casimir shared and exchanged its parts, including Gniewkowo. The duchy was devastated during the war between [[e:poland|Poland]] and the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Knights]] in the 1320s and 1330s.
duchy-of-inowroclaw.e: [[e:casimir-iii-the-great|Casimir III the Great]] gradually bought out the local dukes. The last claimant, [[e:wladyslaw-the-white|Wladyslaw the White of Gniewkowo]], gave up his rights and became a monk in the 1360s, and around 1364 Inowroclaw was incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385).

duchy-of-wurttemberg.t: The south-west German duchy, raised in 1495, that combined strong estates, a model Lutheran church and a constitution dating from 1514.
duchy-of-wurttemberg.o: The [[s:county-of-wurttemberg|County of Württemberg]], reunited by [[e:eberhard-i-duke-of-wurttemberg|Count Eberhard im Bart]] in 1482, was raised to a duchy at the [[e:diet-of-worms-1495|Diet of Worms]] in 1495; Eberhard had founded the [[e:university-of-tubingen|University of Tübingen]] in 1477. His successor [[e:ulrich-duke-of-wurttemberg|Ulrich]] proved a violent ruler, and the peasant revolt of the [[e:poor-conrad|Poor Conrad]] in 1514 forced him to accept the [[e:treaty-of-tubingen|Treaty of Tübingen]], guaranteeing the estates' rights.
duchy-of-wurttemberg.r: Expelled by the [[e:swabian-league|Swabian League]] in 1519, [[e:ulrich-duke-of-wurttemberg|Ulrich]] lost the duchy to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] until 1534, when he returned and introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]]. Duke [[e:christoph-duke-of-wurttemberg|Christoph]] built a model Lutheran church order and school system. The Landtag, dominated by town notables because the nobility had left the duchy, controlled taxation. [[e:stuttgart|Stuttgart]] was the capital, and [[e:ludwigsburg-palace|Ludwigsburg]] was built as a [[e:baroque|Baroque]] residence from 1704.
duchy-of-wurttemberg.e: [[e:frederick-i-of-wurttemberg|Duke Frederick II]] gained the rank of elector in 1803 and, allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], became king in 1806, doubling his lands; the duchy became the [[s:electorate-of-wurttemberg|Electorate of Württemberg]] and then the [[s:kingdom-of-wurttemberg|Kingdom of Württemberg]]. Its territory is now part of [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]].

dhurwai-state.t: A tiny Bundela chiefship of the Bundelkhand Agency in central India.
dhurwai-state.o: Dhurwai was recognised by the British as a separate holding in the early 19th century, one of the small [[e:bundela|Bundela]] estates confirmed after the British gained control of [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]].
dhurwai-state.r: It consisted of a few villages under a hereditary [[e:bundela|Bundela]] chief. Little else is recorded of its history.
dhurwai-state.e: After independence Dhurwai was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states and absorbed by 1950.

duchy-of-split.t: Short-lived Dalmatian duchy granted to the Bosnian magnate Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić, uniting Split and the central Dalmatian islands under one lord.
duchy-of-split.o: In the struggle for the Hungarian crown between [[e:sigismund-holy-roman-emperor|Sigismund of Luxembourg]] and [[e:ladislaus-of-naples|Ladislaus of Naples]], the powerful Bosnian noble [[e:hrvoje-vukcic-hrvatinic|Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić]] backed Ladislaus. In 1403 Ladislaus rewarded him with the title of Duke of Split, together with the islands of [[e:brac|Brač]], [[e:hvar|Hvar]] and [[e:korcula|Korčula]], carving a duchy out of royal [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]].
duchy-of-split.r: [[e:hrvoje-vukcic-hrvatinic|Hrvoje]] ruled from Split while remaining Grand Duke of [[e:bosnia|Bosnia]], so the duchy linked the inland Bosnian lands with the Adriatic trade of the city. Split kept its communal statutes and council. Hrvoje's court produced the richly illuminated [[e:hrvojes-missal|Glagolitic Missal of Hrvoje]], made in Split around 1404, one of the finest Croatian medieval [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]].
duchy-of-split.e: [[e:hrvoje-vukcic-hrvatinic|Hrvoje]] later reconciled with Sigismund, but fell from favour and was declared a traitor in 1413; Split threw off his rule and returned to the Hungarian crown. Hrvoje died in 1416, and in 1420 Split passed to [[e:venice|Venice]], which held it for nearly four centuries.

daju-kingdom.t: The earliest remembered kingdom of Darfur, centred on the Jebel Marra mountains of western Sudan.
daju-kingdom.o: The Daju kingdom is known mainly from oral tradition, a few Arabic references and archaeology, so its history is very uncertain. [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]] traditions name the Daju as the first dynasty to rule the region, from around the 12th century, based in the fertile valleys and slopes of the [[e:marrah-mountains|Jebel Marra]] massif.
daju-kingdom.r: The Daju were a Nilo-Saharan-speaking people who farmed [[e:millet|millet]] and [[e:sorghum|sorghum]] and kept [[e:cattle|cattle]], ruling over neighbouring peoples through a [[e:sacred-kingship|sacred kingship]]. Stone-built sites on [[e:marrah-mountains|Jebel Marra]] may date from their era. The state probably took part in trade routes linking the [[e:nile|Nile]] valley and Christian [[e:nubia|Nubia]] with the [[e:lake-chad|Lake Chad]] region.
daju-kingdom.e: Traditions say the Daju were displaced by the [[s:tunjur-kingdom|Tunjur]] around the 14th or 15th century, and Daju groups moved south and west, where Daju-speaking communities still live in [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]], [[e:kordofan|Kordofan]] and [[e:chad|Chad]]. The later [[s:darfur-sultanate|Darfur Sultanate]] looked back on them as its forerunners.

decapolis-levant.t: The Decapolis, a group of Greek cities east of the Jordan freed by Pompey, famous for the colonnaded streets of Gerasa.
decapolis-levant.o: The [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]] cities, among them [[e:jerash|Gerasa]], [[e:gadara|Gadara]], [[s:pella|Pella]], [[e:amman|Philadelphia]], [[e:beit-shean|Scythopolis]] and [[e:hippos|Hippos]], had grown as Greek-style towns under the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]] and the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]]. The [[s:hasmonean-kingdom|Hasmonean Kingdom]] conquered many of them, and in 63 BCE [[e:pompey|Pompey]] freed them and attached them to Roman [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
decapolis-levant.r: Each city governed itself, minted coins and dated years from [[e:pompey|Pompey's]] liberation. They were less a formal league than a regional group with shared Greek culture, temples to [[e:zeus|Zeus]] and [[e:artemis|Artemis]], and trade with the [[s:nabataean-kingdom|Nabataean Kingdom]]. The [[e:gospels|Gospels]] mention the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]] as the setting of [[e:jesus|Jesus]]' ministry.
decapolis-levant.e: In 106 CE [[e:trajan|Trajan]] created the province of [[e:arabia|Arabia]], dividing the cities between it and [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]]. [[e:jerash|Gerasa]], modern Jerash, preserves one of the best-preserved Roman cityscapes.

dholpur-state.t: A Jat-ruled state on the Chambal, created in 1806 when the British gave Dholpur to the Rana of Gohad.
dholpur-state.o: The Jat Ranas of [[e:gohad|Gohad]] had held lands near [[s:gwalior-state|Gwalior]] in the 18th century. In 1806 the British returned Gohad and Gwalior to the [[e:scindias|Scindias]] and compensated Rana [[e:kirat-singh-of-dholpur|Kirat Singh]] with Dholpur, [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]] and Rajakhera on the [[e:chambal-river|Chambal]] river.
dholpur-state.r: Dholpur was a 15-gun salute state of the [[e:rajputana-agency|Rajputana Agency]], ruled by a Maharaj Rana over a population of farmers in the ravine country of the [[e:chambal-river|Chambal]]. Its red sandstone quarries supplied building stone across northern [[e:india|India]]. [[e:udaybhan-singh|Udaybhan Singh]], who ruled from 1911, was the last Maharaj Rana.
dholpur-state.e: [[e:udaybhan-singh|Udaybhan Singh]] acceded to [[e:india|India]], and in 1948 Dholpur joined the [[s:matsya-union|Matsya Union]], which merged into the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] in 1949. It is now a district of [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]].

duchy-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.t: Twin Ernestine duchy whose dynasty placed rulers on the thrones of Belgium, Britain, Portugal and Bulgaria.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.o: In the Ernestine redistribution of 1826, Duke [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Ernest I]] of Saxe-Coburg-[[e:saalfeld|Saalfeld]] gave up Saalfeld and received [[e:gotha|Gotha]], forming Saxe-[[e:coburg|Coburg]] and Gotha. The two duchies remained legally separate, joined only in the person of the duke, with separate parliaments.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.r: [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Ernest I]]'s brother Leopold became King of the Belgians in 1831, and his son Albert married [[e:queen-victoria|Queen Victoria]] in 1840. [[e:ernest-ii-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Ernest II]] was a liberal patron of the German national movement and of music. [[e:gotha|Gotha]] was a centre of [[e:cartography|cartography]] with the [[e:justus-perthes|Justus Perthes]] firm and of insurance, while [[e:coburg|Coburg]] was a court town. Victoria's son Alfred and grandson [[e:charles-edward-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Charles Edward]] later succeeded as dukes.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.e: [[e:charles-edward-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Charles Edward]] abdicated in November 1918. The [[s:free-state-of-coburg|Free State of Coburg]] voted to join [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] in 1920, while [[e:gotha|Gotha]] joined the [[s:free-state-of-thuringia|Free State of Thuringia]].

duchy-of-swabia.t: The stem duchy of south-west Germany, home of the Hohenstaufen emperors, which collapsed with the execution of the last Staufer in 1268.
duchy-of-swabia.o: After the death of the Alemannic dukes in 746, Alamannia was governed by counts. In 915 Count [[e:erchanger-duke-of-swabia|Erchanger]] defeated King [[e:conrad-i-of-germany|Conrad I]]'s forces at Wahlwies and was proclaimed duke; Conrad executed him in 917, but [[e:burchard-ii-duke-of-swabia|Burchard II]] established the duchy, recognised by [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler]] in 919. [[e:swabia|Swabia]] covered south-west [[e:germany|Germany]], [[e:alsace|Alsace]] and eastern [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]].
duchy-of-swabia.r: Dukes were often royal relatives, and from 1079 the office went to the [[e:hohenstaufen|Staufer]] family, who became emperors with [[e:conrad-iii-of-germany|Conrad III]] and [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]]. [[e:swabia|Swabia]] was rich in monasteries, imperial cities such as Ulm and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-augsburg|Augsburg]], and lesser nobles. Its [[e:knighthood|knightly]] culture produced [[e:minnesang|Minnesang]] poets.
duchy-of-swabia.e: After the fall of the [[e:hohenstaufen|Staufer]], the last duke, [[e:conradin|Conradin]], was beheaded at [[e:naples|Naples]] in 1268. The duchy dissolved into many territories, including the [[s:county-of-wurttemberg|County of Württemberg]], the [[s:margraviate-of-baden|Margraviate of Baden]], [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] lands and [[e:free-imperial-city|free imperial cities]], which later formed the [[e:swabian-league|Swabian League]] and the [[e:swabian-circle|Swabian Circle]].

duchy-of-sandomierz.t: A Piast duchy of eastern Lesser Poland around the Vistula town of Sandomierz, usually joined to Krakow in the age of division.
duchy-of-sandomierz.o: [[e:boleslaw-iii-wrymouth|Boleslaw III]]'s testament of 1138 assigned Sandomierz and its land to his young son Henry, who took control in 1146. Henry went on [[e:crusade|crusade]] to the [[e:holy-land|Holy Land]] in 1154 and was killed fighting the pagan [[e:old-prussians|Prussians]] in 1166, after which the duchy passed to his brother [[e:casimir-ii-the-just|Casimir II the Just]].
duchy-of-sandomierz.r: Sandomierz was a prosperous trading town on the [[e:vistula|Vistula]], on the route between [[e:krakow|Krakow]] and Rus'. For most of the period it was ruled by the same dukes as Krakow, so the two duchies formed [[e:lesser-poland|Lesser Poland]]. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] sacked the town in 1241 and again in 1260, killing many of its inhabitants and the [[e:dominican-order|Dominican friars]] of Saint James.
duchy-of-sandomierz.e: Its rulers included [[e:leszek-the-white|Leszek the White]], [[e:boleslaw-v-the-chaste|Boleslaw V the Chaste]] and [[e:leszek-the-black|Leszek the Black]]. [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high]] gained Sandomierz in the early 14th century, and in 1320 it became part of the reunited [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385).

djibouti.t: A small republic at the mouth of the Red Sea whose port serves as Ethiopia's gateway to the sea and hosts military bases of several world powers.
djibouti.o: The [[s:french-territory-of-the-afars-and-the-issas|French Territory of the Afars and the Issas]] became independent on 27 June 1977 as the Republic of Djibouti, after a referendum in which voters overwhelmingly chose independence. [[e:hassan-gouled-aptidon|Hassan Gouled Aptidon]], an [[e:issa-clan|Issa Somali]] politician, became its first president.
djibouti.r: [[e:hassan-gouled-aptidon|Gouled]] made his party, the [[e:peoples-rally-for-progress|People's Rally for Progress]], the only legal party in 1981. [[e:afar|Afar]] grievances led to the [[e:front-for-the-restoration-of-unity-and-democracy|FRUD]] rebellion of 1991 to 1994, ended by power-sharing agreements. [[e:ismail-omar-guelleh|Ismail Omar Guelleh]] succeeded Gouled in 1999 and has held office since. The economy rests on the port, which handles most of [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia's]] foreign trade, and on rents from foreign bases, including French, American and Chinese.
djibouti.e: Djibouti has remained politically stable but tightly controlled, with limited opposition. New ports and the electrified railway to [[e:addis-ababa|Addis Ababa]], opened in 2016 to 2018, have strengthened its role as a regional trade hub.

daspalla-state.t: A small princely state in the hills south of the Mahanadi in Odisha, ruled from Kunjabangarh until 1948.
daspalla-state.o: Tradition holds that the ruling family was a branch of the [[e:bhanja-dynasty|Bhanja]] rulers of [[s:baudh-state|Baudh State]], founding Daspalla around 1498. Its early history is not well documented.
daspalla-state.r: Daspalla was a hilly, forested state with a large [[e:kondh|Kondh]] population. It was tributary to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and, from 1803, one of the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]] under British supervision. Little else of its history is recorded.
daspalla-state.e: Daspalla merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now in [[s:nayagarh-state|Nayagarh]] district.

duchy-of-austria.t: The Babenberg and Habsburg duchy on the Danube, created by the Privilegium Minus in 1156, which became the core of the Habsburg monarchy.
duchy-of-austria.o: In 1156 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] issued the [[e:privilegium-minus|Privilegium Minus]], raising the [[s:margraviate-of-austria|Margraviate of Austria]] to a duchy for [[e:henry-ii-duke-of-austria|Henry II Jasomirgott]], in compensation for giving up [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. The new duchy received special privileges, including inheritance through female lines. [[e:vienna|Vienna]] became the ducal capital.
duchy-of-austria.r: The [[e:house-of-babenberg|Babenbergs]] acquired [[e:styria|Styria]] in 1192 and made [[e:vienna|Vienna]] a centre of [[e:minnesang|Minnesang]]. After the line died out in 1246, [[e:ottokar-ii-of-bohemia|Ottokar II of Bohemia]] took [[e:austria|Austria]], but in 1278 Rudolf I of [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] defeated him at the [[e:battle-on-the-marchfeld|Marchfeld]]. [[e:rudolf-iv-duke-of-austria|Rudolf IV]] founded the [[e:university-of-vienna|University of Vienna]] in 1365 and forged the [[e:privilegium-maius|Privilegium Maius]] to claim higher rank.
duchy-of-austria.e: In 1453 [[e:frederick-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Frederick III]], himself a [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]], confirmed the [[e:privilegium-maius|Privilegium Maius]], raising [[e:austria|Austria]] to an archduchy. The [[s:archduchy-of-austria|Archduchy of Austria]] became the core of the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburg]] monarchy, the [[s:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire]] and, ultimately, the modern [[s:first-austrian-republic|Republic of Austria]].

delos.t: The sacred island of Apollo, independent from 314 to 167 BCE, when its sanctuary became a meeting place of kings and a hub of Aegean commerce.
delos.o: Delos, birthplace of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] and [[e:artemis|Artemis]] in Greek myth, had long been under Athenian control. In 314 BCE, with [[e:antigonus-i-monophthalmus|Antigonus]] I extending his power into the [[e:aegean|Aegean]], the Athenians were ousted and the Delians governed their island as an independent city, also hosting the [[s:nesiotic-league|Nesiotic League]].
delos.r: Independent Delos was run by an archon, council and assembly, while elected hieropoioi managed the sanctuary's lands, loans and treasures; their yearly inscribed accounts are among the richest economic records from antiquity. Kings of [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]], [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and [[e:pergamon|Pergamon]] built porticoes and dedications. Banking and trade grew, drawing merchants from [[e:italy|Italy]] and the East.
delos.e: In 167 BCE [[e:rome|Rome]] handed Delos to [[s:athens|Athens]] and made it a free port to damage [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]]; the Delians were expelled to [[e:achaea|Achaea]]. Delos then boomed as a slave and grain market until sacked in 88 BCE by the forces of [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI]] and again by [[e:piracy|pirates]] in 69 BCE. It is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

da-chu.t: A puppet state set up by the Jurchen at Kaifeng in 1127 under the former Song chancellor Zhang Bangchang, which lasted only about a month.
da-chu.o: After the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234) captured [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]] and deported the [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] emperors [[e:emperor-huizong|Huizong]] and [[e:emperor-qinzong|Qinzong]] in the [[e:jingkang-incident|Jingkang incident]] of 1127, the [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] wished to leave a friendly regime behind. They forced [[e:zhang-bangchang|Zhang Bangchang]], a Song chief minister, to accept the throne as emperor of Chu.
da-chu.r: [[e:zhang-bangchang|Zhang Bangchang]] accepted reluctantly and did not behave as a full emperor, avoiding the throne hall and imperial forms of address. His regime existed only as long as [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] troops remained in [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]].
da-chu.e: When the [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] withdrew north, Zhang stepped down after about thirty-three days, invited the deposed Empress Meng to act as regent and supported [[e:emperor-gaozong-of-song|Zhao Gou]], who became the first emperor of [[s:southern-song|Southern Song]]. Zhang was soon ordered to commit suicide for having accepted the throne.

duchy-of-saxe-eisenberg.t: Tiny Ernestine duchy in eastern Thuringia whose single duke built a celebrated baroque palace chapel.
duchy-of-saxe-eisenberg.o: In the 1680 division of the inheritance of [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-gotha|Ernest the Pious]], his fifth son Christian received Eisenberg and its district, between Gera and [[e:jena|Jena]], founding the Duchy of Saxe-Eisenberg.
duchy-of-saxe-eisenberg.r: Christian rebuilt Christiansburg Palace in Eisenberg and added a richly decorated baroque chapel, still one of the finest in [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]]. He was interested in alchemy and kept a small Lutheran court. The duchy was largely rural, with no independent policy of note.
duchy-of-saxe-eisenberg.e: Christian died in 1707 without a male heir. After a dispute among his relatives, Saxe-Eisenberg passed to [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg]]; in 1826 it went with [[e:altenburg|Altenburg]] to the new [[s:duchy-of-saxe-altenburg|Duchy of Saxe-Altenburg]].

duchy-of-bavaria-straubing.t: A Wittelsbach inheritance that joined a Lower Bavarian duchy with the rich Low Country counties of Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut.
duchy-of-bavaria-straubing.o: After the death of [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Louis the Bavarian]] his sons divided their lands, and in 1353 a further partition created Bavaria-[[e:straubing|Straubing]] for William I and [[e:albert-i-duke-of-bavaria|Albert I]], together with the counties of [[s:county-of-hainaut|Hainaut]], Holland and [[s:county-of-zeeland|Zeeland]] inherited through their mother Margaret. Albert governed the whole inheritance from 1358, after his brother became insane.
duchy-of-bavaria-straubing.r: The dukes lived mostly in [[e:the-hague|The Hague]] and governed [[e:straubing|Straubing]] through deputies, while in the [[s:county-of-holland|County of Holland]] they were drawn into the [[e:hook-and-cod-wars|Hook and Cod]] factional wars. In [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] they built the ducal castle at Straubing from 1356. The [[e:danube|Danube]] plain of the [[e:gauboden|Gäuboden]] around the town was among the most fertile farmland in Bavaria.
duchy-of-bavaria-straubing.e: After [[e:william-ii-duke-of-bavaria|William VI]] died in 1417 his daughter [[e:jacqueline-countess-of-hainaut|Jacqueline of Hainaut]] fought her uncle [[e:john-iii-duke-of-bavaria|John III]] for the inheritance. John died in 1425, the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]] passed to [[e:philip-the-good|Philip the Good]] of [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]], and in 1429 the [[e:straubing|Straubing]] lands were divided among the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-munich|Duchy of Bavaria-Munich]], the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-ingolstadt|Duchy of Bavaria-Ingolstadt]] and the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-landshut|Duchy of Bavaria-Landshut]].

despotate-of-serres.t: Realm of the despot Jovan Uglješa around Serres in eastern Macedonia, a successor of the Serbian Empire destroyed at the Maritsa in 1371.
despotate-of-serres.o: After [[e:stefan-dusan|Stefan Dušan's]] death in 1355, his widow, [[e:helena-of-bulgaria-empress-of-serbia|Empress Jelena]], ruled [[e:serres|Serres]], the city he had taken from [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] in 1345. Around 1365 she handed power to the despot [[e:jovan-uglesa|Jovan Uglješa]], brother of [[e:vukasin-mrnjavcevic|Vukašin Mrnjavčević]], who ruled eastern [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]] from Serres.
despotate-of-serres.r: [[e:jovan-uglesa|Uglješa]] governed a largely Greek population and was close to the monasteries of [[s:monastic-community-of-mount-athos|Mount Athos]], to which he made many grants. In 1368 he reconciled his church with the [[e:ecumenical-patriarch-of-constantinople|Patriarch of Constantinople]], ending the schism caused by Dušan's patriarchate. Alarmed by the Ottoman conquest of [[e:thrace|Thrace]], he sought allies against them.
despotate-of-serres.e: In 1371 [[e:jovan-uglesa|Uglješa]] and his brother [[e:vukasin-mrnjavcevic|Vukašin]] led a large army against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and were killed at the [[e:maritsa|Maritsa]]. [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] under [[e:manuel-ii-palaiologos|Manuel II]] then retook [[e:serres|Serres]], which fell to the Ottomans in 1383.

dutch-gold-coast.t: Dutch forts on the coast of present-day Ghana, run from Elmina for nearly three centuries as a base for the gold and slave trades.
dutch-gold-coast.o: [[e:dutch|Dutch]] merchants began trading on the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast]] in the 1590s, challenging the Portuguese monopoly. In 1612, at the invitation of the [[s:kingdom-of-asebu|Kingdom of Asebu]], they built [[e:fort-nassau-gold-coast|Fort Nassau]] at [[e:moree|Moree]]. The [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] captured [[e:elmina|Elmina]] from the [[s:portuguese-gold-coast|Portuguese Gold Coast]] in 1637 and [[e:axim|Axim]] in 1642, making Elmina its headquarters.
dutch-gold-coast.r: A director-general at [[e:elmina|Elmina]] governed a chain of forts and lodges along the coast, trading cloth, guns and metal goods for gold and, from the late 17th century, enslaved Africans shipped to [[e:dutch|Dutch]] colonies in the [[e:americas|Americas]]. Relations with inland powers such as [[s:denkyira|Denkyira]] and the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] were vital; [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]] held the [[e:elmina-note|Elmina Note]], a rent paid by the Dutch. In the 1830s and 1840s the Dutch recruited soldiers there for the [[e:east-indies|East Indies]] army.
dutch-gold-coast.e: In 1868 the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and British exchanged forts to consolidate their zones, and in 1872 the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] handed its remaining posts to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. They became part of the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]], and [[e:elmina|Elmina Castle]] is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

duchy-of-ziebice.t: A Lower Silesian duchy, known in German as Münsterberg, that passed from the Piasts to the Poděbrady and Auersperg families before being sold to Prussia.
duchy-of-ziebice.o: In 1322 the sons of Duke [[e:bolko-i-the-strict|Bolko I of Świdnica]] divided his lands, and [[e:bolko-ii-of-ziebice|Bolko II]] received [[e:ziebice|Ziębice]] (Münsterberg), south of [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]], as a separate duchy split from the [[s:duchy-of-swidnica|Duchy of Świdnica]]. Bolko II resisted Bohemian overlordship longer than most Silesian dukes but did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|King John of Bohemia]] in 1336.
duchy-of-ziebice.r: The duchy was a modest agrarian territory of small towns and villages. The [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] line ended in 1428, and in 1456 the duchy passed to [[e:george-of-podebrady|George of Poděbrady]], later king of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], whose sons held it as dukes of [[e:ziebice|Münsterberg]] and introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. In 1654 the emperor granted it to the [[e:house-of-auersperg|Auersperg family]], who seldom lived there.
duchy-of-ziebice.e: [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] came under [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742, though the [[e:house-of-auersperg|Auerspergs]] kept the ducal title and estates. In 1791 they sold their remaining Silesian holdings to the Prussian crown, ending the duchy. The town, now [[e:ziebice|Ziębice]], became part of [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

dardanian-kingdom.t: Kingdom of the Dardani in Kosovo and the upper Vardar, a persistent threat to Macedon that allied with Rome before being absorbed into Moesia.
dardanian-kingdom.o: The [[e:dardanians|Dardani]] lived in the plains of [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] and around [[e:scupi|Scupi]] ([[e:skopje|Skopje]]) from at least the 4th century BCE. A Dardanian monarchy appears by the mid-4th century, and some historians count [[e:bardylis|Bardylis]], the Illyrian king who fought [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]], as Dardanian.
dardanian-kingdom.r: Dardanian kings led a mixed Illyrian and Thracian population of farmers and herders. They raided [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]] repeatedly and took advantage of the Celtic invasions of 279 BCE. King [[e:longarus|Longarus]] fought [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] in the 230s BCE, and his son [[e:bato-of-dardania|Bato]] allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] against Philip V in 200 BCE, and King Monunius minted coins at [[e:durres|Dyrrhachium]]. Roman writers described the [[e:dardanians|Dardani]] as rough but musical.
dardanian-kingdom.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] fought the [[e:dardanians|Dardani]] during the 1st century BCE, and [[e:marcus-licinius-crassus|Marcus Licinius Crassus]] brought them under control in 28 BCE. Their land became part of the province of [[e:moesia|Moesia]] and later the late Roman province of Dardania, birthplace of the emperor Justinian.

danish-india.t: Denmark's trading posts in India, led by Tranquebar on the Coromandel Coast, where the first Protestant missionaries in India began work in 1706.
danish-india.o: A Danish expedition under [[e:ove-gjedde|Ove Gjedde]] reached south [[e:india|India]], and in 1620 [[e:raghunatha-nayak|Raghunatha Nayak]] of [[e:thanjavur|Thanjavur]] granted the [[e:danish-east-india-company|Danish East India Company]] the village of [[e:tharangambadi|Tranquebar]] (Tharangambadi). The [[e:danes|Danes]] built [[e:fort-dansborg|Fort Dansborg]] there, which became the centre of their Asian trade.
danish-india.r: Danish [[e:india|India]] was governed by the company and later the crown, trading in textiles, [[e:pepper|pepper]] and [[e:tea|tea]]. In 1706 the German missionaries [[e:bartholomaus-ziegenbalg|Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg]] and [[e:heinrich-plutschau|Heinrich Plütschau]], sent by the Danish king, founded the [[e:tranquebar-mission|Tranquebar Mission]] and translated the [[e:new-testament|New Testament]] into Tamil. [[e:serampore|Serampore]] near [[e:kolkata|Calcutta]], acquired in 1755, became a centre of [[e:printing-press|printing]] and of [[e:serampore-college|Serampore College]], founded by English [[e:baptists|Baptists]]. [[e:denmark|Denmark]] also claimed the [[e:nicobar-islands|Nicobar Islands]].
danish-india.e: Overshadowed by [[s:british-raj|British India]] and loss-making, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] sold [[e:tharangambadi|Tranquebar]] and [[e:serampore|Serampore]] to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1845 and gave up its claim to the [[e:nicobar-islands|Nicobar Islands]] in 1868-1869. [[e:fort-dansborg|Fort Dansborg]] and Tranquebar's churches still stand.

daegaya.t: The leading Gaya kingdom of the 5th and 6th centuries, based at Goryeong, whose court produced the gayageum zither.
daegaya.o: Daegaya grew from Banpa-guk, a [[s:byeonhan|Byeonhan]] statelet in the [[e:goryeong|Goryeong]] valley. Its founding legend names Ijinashi as first king, brother of [[e:suro-of-geumgwan-gaya|Suro of Geumgwan Gaya]]. It rose to lead the northern Gaya states after Goguryeo's campaign of 400 weakened [[e:gimhae|Gimhae]].
daegaya.r: Daegaya's kings drew wealth from iron mines and controlled routes to the [[e:seomjin-river|Seomjin river]] and the sea. In 479 King Haji sent an envoy to the [[s:southern-qi|Southern Qi]] court and received a title. Its royal cemetery at [[e:jisan-dong-tombs|Jisan-dong]] includes tombs with dozens of sacrificed attendants. Under [[e:king-gasil|King Gasil]] the musician [[e:ureuk|Ureuk]] composed twelve pieces for the newly devised gayageum.
daegaya.e: A marriage alliance with [[s:silla|Silla]] in 522 broke down, and in 562 Silla's general [[e:isabu|Isabu]], with the young hwarang [[e:sadaham|Sadaham]], conquered Daegaya, ending the last Gaya state. [[e:ureuk|Ureuk]] had already fled to Silla, preserving its music.

dongdan.t: The 'Eastern Khitan Kingdom' that the Liao set up in conquered Balhae, at first a semi-independent realm under the crown prince Yelü Bei.
dongdan.o: In 926 [[e:emperor-taizu-of-liao|Abaoji]], founder of the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]], destroyed [[s:balhae|Balhae]] after a short campaign and took its capital Huhan (Holhan). He renamed the country Dongdan and made his eldest son [[e:yelu-bei|Yelü Bei]] its king, with his own court, officials and reign title, retaining many Balhae institutions.
dongdan.r: Dongdan was intended as a separate kingdom for the former [[s:balhae|Balhae]] population, partly governed by Balhae nobles. After [[e:emperor-taizu-of-liao|Abaoji's]] death the throne of [[e:liao-dynasty|Liao]] went to [[e:yelu-bei|Yelü Bei's]] brother [[e:yelu-deguang|Yelü Deguang]], who distrusted him. Around 929 much of the population and the capital were moved west to [[e:liaoyang|Liaoyang]], and in 930 Yelü Bei fled to the [[s:later-tang|Later Tang]].
dongdan.e: Thereafter Dongdan was little more than an administrative unit within [[e:liao-dynasty|Liao]], governed by Khitan appointees. It was formally abolished around 982 under Emperor [[e:shengzong-of-liao|Shengzong]]. Many [[s:balhae|Balhae]] refugees had meanwhile fled to [[s:goryeo|Goryeo]] or founded short-lived successor states such as [[s:dingan|Dingan]].

dutch-coromandel.t: The Dutch East India Company's trading posts on India's south-east coast, centred on Pulicat, a hub of the Asian textile trade.
dutch-coromandel.o: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) opened a factory at [[e:machilipatnam|Masulipatnam]] in 1605 and in 1610 obtained permission from the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara]] ruler to settle at Pulicat, where [[e:fort-geldria|Fort Geldria]] was built in 1613. Further factories followed at [[e:nagapattinam|Negapatnam]], [[e:sadras|Sadras]] and [[e:bheemunipatnam|Bimlipatnam]], forming the governorate of [[e:coromandel-coast|Coromandel]].
dutch-coromandel.r: [[e:coromandel-coast|Coromandel]] [[e:cotton|cotton]] textiles, printed and painted chintz above all, were the [[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC's]] key goods for buying [[e:spice-trade|spices]] in [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]]. The company bought cloth from weavers through Indian merchants and also traded slaves during famines. Pulicat housed the governor and a mint. In 1690 the capital moved to [[e:nagapattinam|Negapatnam]], then back to Pulicat in 1781.
dutch-coromandel.e: British competition from [[e:chennai|Madras]] eroded [[e:dutch|Dutch]] trade, and the British occupied the posts during the French Revolutionary and [[e:napoleonic-wars|Napoleonic Wars]]. Under the [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824|Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824]] the remaining settlements were transferred to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1825.

duchy-of-nysa.t: Silesian duchy ruled by the bishops of Wrocław from Nysa, the Silesian Rome, a Catholic stronghold for over five centuries.
duchy-of-nysa.o: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]] held the castellany of [[e:nysa|Nysa]] and [[e:otmuchow|Otmuchów]] from the 12th century. In 1290 Duke [[e:henry-iv-probus|Henry IV Probus]] granted Bishop [[e:thomas-ii-zaremba|Thomas II]] full princely rights there, making the territory an episcopal duchy. Its bishops took the title Prince of Nysa and in 1342 accepted the overlordship of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-nysa.r: The [[e:bishop|bishop]]-dukes ruled from [[e:nysa|Nysa]] and [[e:otmuchow|Otmuchów]] through officials and the estates. Nysa became a wealthy town of churches and convents, called the Silesian [[e:rome|Rome]]. After the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] spread in [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], the bishops led the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]], and [[e:charles-of-austria-bishop-of-wroclaw|Archduke Charles of Austria]], bishop from 1608, founded the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] college Carolinum. The population was largely German-speaking.
duchy-of-nysa.e: In 1742 most of the duchy passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], which secularised it in 1810, while the southern part around [[e:jesenik|Jeseník]] remained Austrian under the [[e:bishop|bishops]] until 1850. [[e:nysa|Nysa]] has been Polish since 1945.

democratic-republic-of-vietnam.t: The communist-led Vietnamese state proclaimed by Ho Chi Minh in 1945, which defeated France, fought the Vietnam War and reunified the country in 1976.
democratic-republic-of-vietnam.o: During the [[e:august-revolution|August Revolution]] of 1945 the [[e:viet-minh|Viet Minh]], a front led by the [[e:indochinese-communist-party|Indochinese Communist Party]], seized power across much of [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]]. On 2 September 1945 [[e:ho-chi-minh|Ho Chi Minh]] read the declaration of independence in [[e:ba-dinh-square|Ba Dinh Square]] in [[e:hanoi|Hanoi]], proclaiming the Democratic [[s:republic-of-vietnam|Republic of Vietnam]].
democratic-republic-of-vietnam.r: The DRV fought [[e:france|France]] in the [[e:first-indochina-war|First Indochina War]] from 1946, winning at [[e:battle-of-dien-bien-phu|Dien Bien Phu]] in 1954. The [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] Accords left it in control of the north above the 17th parallel. It built a one-party socialist state with collectivised agriculture after a harsh land reform, backed by the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] and [[e:china|China]], and supported the southern insurgency through the [[e:ho-chi-minh-trail|Ho Chi Minh Trail]] against the [[s:republic-of-vietnam|Republic of Vietnam]] and the [[s:united-states|United States]].
democratic-republic-of-vietnam.e: After the [[e:paris-peace-accords|Paris Peace Accords]] of 1973 and the fall of [[e:ho-chi-minh-city|Saigon]] in April 1975, the DRV merged with the [[s:republic-of-south-vietnam|Republic of South Vietnam]]. On 2 July 1976 the united country was proclaimed the [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Socialist Republic of Vietnam]].

dal-fiatach.t: Ruling dynasty of east County Down, centred on Downpatrick, which claimed to be the true Ulaid and held the Ulster kingship until 1177.
dal-fiatach.o: The Dál Fiatach were a dynasty of the [[s:kingdom-of-ulaid|Ulaid]] in what is now east County Down. They claimed descent from the ancient Ulaid royal line, and after the Ulaid were pushed east of the [[e:river-bann|River Bann]] they became one of the two main powers in the Kingdom of Ulaid, with their stronghold at [[e:downpatrick|Dún Lethglaise]], Downpatrick, associated with St Patrick's burial.
dal-fiatach.r: Dál Fiatach kings alternated the over-kingship of the [[s:kingdom-of-ulaid|Ulaid]] with the [[s:dal-naraidi|Dal nAraidi]]. [[e:baetan-mac-cairill|Báetán mac Cairill]], who died in 581, is said to have claimed authority as far as the [[s:isle-of-man|Isle of Man]] and [[e:scotland|Scotland]]. [[e:fiachnae-mac-demmain|Fiachnae mac Demmáin]] fought for the kingship in the early 7th century. Their wealth lay in the fertile lands of [[e:lecale|Lecale]] and the [[e:ards-peninsula|Ards]], and the monasteries of [[e:bangor-abbey|Bangor]] and [[e:movilla-abbey|Movilla]] lay nearby.
dal-fiatach.e: From the 11th century their kings were the Mac Duinn Sléibe, MacDunleavy. In 1177 the [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] [[e:john-de-courcy|John de Courcy]] seized [[e:downpatrick|Downpatrick]] and defeated [[e:ruaidri-mac-duinn-sleibe|Ruaidrí Mac Duinn Sléibe]], establishing the Anglo-Norman lordship of [[s:northern-ireland|Ulster]], later an earldom, and ending Dál Fiatach rule.

dungarpur-state.t: The senior Guhila Rajput state of the Vagad region in southern Rajasthan, from which Banswara split in the 16th century, ruled by Maharawals until 1948.
dungarpur-state.o: The Maharawals of Dungarpur claimed descent from the elder line of the [[e:guhila-dynasty|Guhila dynasty]] of [[s:udaipur-state|Mewar]], said to have moved south into the [[e:vagad|Vagad]] hills in the late 12th century. The town of Dungarpur was founded in the 14th century and named after a local [[e:bhils|Bhil]] chief, Dungaria.
dungarpur-state.r: [[e:vagad|Vagad]] was a hilly, forested country with a large [[e:bhils|Bhil]] population. Rawal [[e:udai-singh-of-dungarpur|Udai Singh]] was killed fighting [[e:babur|Babur]] at [[e:battle-of-khanwa|Khanwa]] in 1527, after which his lands were divided between two sons, creating [[s:banswara-state|Banswara State]]. Dungarpur accepted Mughal and then [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] overlordship, and signed a treaty with the British in 1818. Its palaces are known for blue-grey stone and mirror work.
dungarpur-state.e: Maharawal [[e:lakshman-singh-of-dungarpur|Lakshman Singh]] joined the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] in 1948, and Dungarpur is now a district of [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]].

dulkadirids.t: A Turkmen beylik around Elbistan and Marash that served as the buffer, and the battleground, between the Mamluks and the Ottomans.
dulkadirids.o: In 1337 the [[e:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluks]] recognised the [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] chief [[e:zayn-al-din-karaja|Zayn al-Din Karaja Bey]] as ruler of [[e:elbistan|Elbistan]] and the surrounding uplands of the eastern [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]], creating a [[e:vassal|vassal]] state on their northern frontier.
dulkadirids.r: The Dulkadirids led pastoral [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] tribes, raised horses and controlled the passes between [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. Both [[e:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluks]] and [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] tried to control them through marriage and by backing rival claimants. [[e:shah-suwar|Shah Suwar]] rebelled against the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] with Ottoman encouragement and was executed in [[e:cairo|Cairo]] in 1472. [[e:ala-al-dawla-bozkurt|Ala al-Dawla Bozkurt]], a long-reigning ruler, built in [[e:kahramanmaras|Marash]] and resisted the rising [[e:safavid-empire|Safavids]].
dulkadirids.e: When Ala al-Dawla failed to support the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] against the [[e:safavid-empire|Safavids]], [[e:selim-i|Selim I's]] army defeated and killed him in 1515. His nephew [[e:ali-bey-of-dulkadir|Ali Bey]] ruled as an Ottoman [[e:vassal|vassal]] until he was executed in 1522 and the [[e:beylik|beylik]] was annexed.

derdeship-of-tibesti.t: The office of the derde, paramount chief of the Teda people of the Tibesti mountains, an elected leader of a fiercely independent Saharan society.
derdeship-of-tibesti.o: The [[e:teda-people|Teda]], a branch of the [[e:toubou-people|Tubu]] peoples, have lived in the Tibesti mountains of northern [[e:chad|Chad]] and southern [[e:libya|Libya]] for centuries. By around 1700 they recognised a derde, a paramount chief chosen in rotation from leading families of the Tomaghra clan.
derdeship-of-tibesti.r: The derde acted mainly as judge and arbitrator among largely autonomous clans of [[e:camel|camel]] herders and oasis farmers, settling feuds through compensation. His power was moral rather than coercive. [[e:teda-people|Teda]] raids reached across the [[e:sahara|Sahara]], and in the 19th century the [[s:senussi-order|Senussi Order]] gained influence through its lodges.
derdeship-of-tibesti.e: French troops occupied Tibesti in 1914, withdrew in 1916 and returned in 1929 to 1930, ending its independence. The derdeship survived as a traditional office in [[e:chad|Chad]]; the derde Oueddei Kichidemi's son [[e:goukouni-oueddei|Goukouni Oueddei]] became president of Chad in 1979.

duchy-of-brittany.t: The Celtic-speaking peninsula of western France, an independent-minded duchy for six centuries until its heiress Anne married two French kings.
duchy-of-brittany.o: After [[e:vikings|Viking]] occupation in the early 10th century, [[e:alan-ii-duke-of-brittany|Alan Twisted Beard]] returned from exile in [[e:england|England]] and drove the Norse out, completing the reconquest with the victory at [[e:battle-of-trans|Trans]] in 939. He took the title of duke and made [[e:nantes|Nantes]] his base. The duchy's frontier with [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]] and [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] remained contested for generations.
duchy-of-brittany.r: Brittany kept its own customs, coinage, Estates and courts, with Breton spoken in the west and [[e:gallo-language|Gallo]] and French in the east. The [[s:county-of-montfort|Montfort]] and [[s:county-of-blois|Blois]] families fought the [[e:war-of-the-breton-succession|War of the Breton Succession]] (1341–1364), won by [[e:john-iv-duke-of-brittany|John IV]] at [[e:battle-of-auray|Auray]]. Under the Montfort dukes the duchy prospered from salt, linen and shipping and was nearly sovereign.
duchy-of-brittany.e: [[e:francis-ii|Francis II's]] defeat at [[e:battle-of-saint-aubin-du-cormier|Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier]] in 1488 sealed French dominance. His daughter [[e:anne-of-brittany|Anne of Brittany]] married [[e:charles-viii-of-france|Charles VIII]] and then [[e:louis-xii-of-france|Louis XII]], and the [[e:edict-of-union|Edict of Union of 1532]] joined the duchy to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]. When the Dauphin, its last duke, became [[e:henry-ii-of-france|Henry II]] in 1547, the title merged with the crown.
