duchy-of-eastern-zhou.t: A breakaway duchy east of Luoyang, created in a family quarrel in 367 BCE, which outlasted the Zhou kings by seven years before falling to Qin.
duchy-of-eastern-zhou.o: After the death of Duke Wei of the [[s:duchy-of-western-zhou|Duchy of Western Zhou]], his younger son [[e:duke-hui-of-eastern-zhou|Gen]], backed by the [[s:state-of-zhao|State of Zhao]] and the [[s:state-of-han|State of Han]], set himself up at Gong (modern [[e:gongyi|Gongyi]], [[e:henan|Henan]]) in 367 BCE as Duke Hui of [[s:eastern-zhou|Eastern Zhou]], splitting the remaining royal domain in two.
duchy-of-eastern-zhou.r: The duchy was a cluster of towns along the [[e:luo-river-henan|Luo River]] whose rulers competed with [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] for influence over the king and survived by diplomacy with the great powers. Little is known of its internal life.
duchy-of-eastern-zhou.e: After the fall of [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] in 256 BCE, the [[s:eastern-zhou|Eastern Zhou]] ruler continued to plot with other states against the [[s:state-of-qin|State of Qin]]. In 249 BCE [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin's]] chancellor [[e:lu-buwei|Lü Buwei]] led an army that annexed the duchy, extinguishing the last political remnant of the Zhou royal house.

datia-state.t: A Bundela Rajput state of Bundelkhand, famed for the seven-storey palace built by Bir Singh Deo of Orchha.
datia-state.o: Datia was granted in 1626 to [[e:bhagwan-rao-of-datia|Bhagwan Rao]], a son of [[e:vir-singh-deo|Bir Singh Deo of Orchha]], making it a branch of the [[s:orchha-state|Orchha State]]. Bir Singh Deo had already built the great palace at Datia, completed around 1614.
datia-state.r: The [[e:maharaja|Maharajas]] served the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] as mansabdars and later contended with the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]]. In 1804 Datia made a treaty with the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] and became a salute state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]]. Its economy rested on agriculture, and the town grew around the palace and the [[e:pitambara-peeth|Pitambara Peeth]] temple.
datia-state.e: Datia joined [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] in 1948 and [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. The [[e:datia-palace|Datia Palace]], a landmark of [[e:bundelas|Bundela]] architecture, survives in the town.

duchy-of-lower-lorraine.t: The northern half of old Lotharingia, a duchy over the Low Countries whose title was carried by Godfrey of Bouillon and survived in Brabant.
duchy-of-lower-lorraine.o: In 959 Archbishop [[e:bruno-the-great|Bruno]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] divided the [[s:duchy-of-lotharingia|Duchy of Lotharingia]], creating a separate duchy for the lands of the lower [[e:meuse|Meuse]], [[e:scheldt|Scheldt]] and [[e:rhine|Rhine]]. The German kings appointed its dukes, including the [[e:charles-duke-of-lower-lorraine|Carolingian Charles]], brother of the West Frankish king [[e:lothair-i|Lothair]], from 977 to 991.
duchy-of-lower-lorraine.r: Ducal power was always limited, since counts such as those of [[e:leuven|Louvain]], [[s:county-of-hainaut|Hainaut]], [[s:county-of-namur|Namur]], Holland and [[s:duchy-of-limburg|Limburg]] and the prince-[[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]] and [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]] built their own principalities. The emperors used the office to reward loyal families: [[e:godfrey-i-of-louvain|Godfrey the Bearded's]] house held it, and [[e:godfrey-of-bouillon|Godfrey of Bouillon]] was duke before leading the First Crusade in 1096.
duchy-of-lower-lorraine.e: From 1106 the title was disputed between the counts of [[e:leuven|Louvain]] and [[s:duchy-of-limburg|Limburg]]. At the [[e:diet-of-schwabisch-hall|Diet of Schwäbisch Hall]] in 1190 [[e:henry-vi-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry VI]] limited the duke's authority to his own lands, and the Louvain dukes thereafter ruled as dukes of [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Brabant]], keeping the title duke of Lothier.

duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg.t: A small north German duchy on the lower Elbe that kept the Saxon ducal title for centuries but lost the electoral vote to its Wittenberg cousins.
duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg.o: When the Ascanian dukes of [[e:saxony|Saxony]] divided their lands, the younger line received the scattered northern territories around Lauenburg on the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and [[e:ratzeburg|Ratzeburg]], formally separated from the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg|Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg]] in 1296. The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] gave the [[e:saxons|Saxon]] electoral vote to [[e:wittenberg|Wittenberg]] rather than Lauenburg, leaving Lauenburg a minor duchy.
duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg.r: The dukes were often in debt and pledged lands, including the [[e:vierlande|Vierlande]] and [[e:bergedorf|Bergedorf]], to [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] and [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-hamburg|Hamburg]]. The estates of the duchy held real power, and the old salt road from [[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]] to [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] crossed its territory. The duchy turned Lutheran in the 16th century. When the Ascanian line died out in 1689, the dukes of Brunswick-Lüneburg seized it.
duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg.e: Lauenburg passed with the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] and in 1815 to [[e:denmark|Denmark]]. After the war of 1864 it went to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], whose king ruled it in personal union until it was incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-prussia|Kingdom of Prussia]] in 1876. Bismarck later received the honorary title Duke of Lauenburg in 1890.

duchy-of-benevento.t: Southern Lombard duchy and later principality that outlived the Lombard Kingdom by three centuries, a centre of southern Italian culture.
duchy-of-benevento.o: [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] warriors under [[e:zotto|Zotto]] established themselves at [[e:benevento|Beneventum]] in [[e:campania|Campania]] around 571, perhaps first as soldiers in Byzantine pay. Under [[e:arechis-i-of-benevento|Arechis I]] the duchy expanded across most of southern [[e:italy|Italy]], apart from the Byzantine coastal cities, [[e:calabria|Calabria]] and [[e:apulia|Apulia's]] heel.
duchy-of-benevento.r: [[e:benevento|Benevento]] was effectively independent of [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]]; Duke [[e:grimoald-i-of-benevento|Grimoald I]] even became [[e:king-of-the-lombards|King of the Lombards]] in 662. When [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] took the north in 774, [[e:arechis-ii-of-benevento|Arechis II]] took the title of prince and claimed the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] heritage, building the church of [[e:santa-sofia-benevento|Santa Sofia]]. The duchy developed the Beneventan script and was a cultural centre linked to [[e:monte-cassino|Monte Cassino]]. Civil war in 849 split it into Benevento and [[s:principality-of-salerno|Salerno]], and [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]] later broke away.
duchy-of-benevento.e: Weakened by Arab raids, [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] and Normans, the principality shrank. In 1051 the city placed itself under [[e:pope-leo-ix|Pope Leo IX]], and when the last prince, Landulf VI, died in 1077, [[e:benevento|Benevento]] became a papal enclave, while its lands passed to the Normans.

cr.a: The original map was reconstructed by Alfredo Zazo and sculpted by Michelangelo Parlato.

daunians.t: Iapygian people of northern Apulia, known for their carved stone stelae and painted pottery, who allied with Rome against the Samnites.
daunians.o: The Daunians were the northernmost of the Iapygian peoples of [[e:apulia|Apulia]], settled in the [[e:tavoliere-delle-puglie|Tavoliere]] plain and the [[e:gargano|Gargano]] from the early 1st millennium BCE. Greek legend made the hero [[e:diomedes|Diomedes]], returning from [[e:troy|Troy]], the founder of Arpi and other towns, a story the Daunians themselves seem to have adopted.
daunians.r: Daunian society was organised in large settlements such as Arpi, [[e:canusium|Canusium]], [[e:salapia|Salapia]] and [[e:sipontum|Sipontum]], with chieftains whose wealth appears in their tombs. Between the 7th and 6th centuries BCE they set up hundreds of anthropomorphic stone stelae near Sipontum, carved with weapons, ornaments and scenes of daily life. Their matt-painted pottery is distinctive. They farmed the plain, raised horses and traded across the Adriatic.
daunians.e: During the [[e:samnite-wars|Samnite Wars]] the Daunian towns sided with [[e:rome|Rome]]; [[e:livy|Livy]] records alliances in 318 BCE, and Rome founded [[e:lucera|Luceria]] in 314 BCE. Arpi went over to [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] after [[e:battle-of-cannae|Cannae]] in 216 BCE and was punished when retaken. The towns became Roman municipia after the [[e:social-war-91-87-bce|Social War]], and Daunian identity faded into Roman [[e:apulia|Apulia]].

dian-kingdom.t: A bronze-working kingdom around Lake Dian in Yunnan, whose tombs at Shizhaishan show lively scenes of ritual, war and daily life cast on cowrie containers.
dian-kingdom.o: Dian grew among the farming and fishing peoples around [[e:lake-dian|Lake Dian]], near [[e:kunming|Kunming]]. Tradition holds that the Chu general [[e:zhuang-qiao|Zhuang Qiao]] reached the lake around 279 BCE and, cut off by the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] conquest of Chu's western lands, made himself king of Dian, but the kingdom's culture was overwhelmingly local.
dian-kingdom.r: Dian's elite were buried at [[e:shizhaishan|Shizhaishan]] and [[e:lijiashan|Lijiashan]] with bronze drums, weapons and [[e:cowrie-shell|cowrie]]-shell containers topped with miniature figures showing sacrifices, weaving, markets and battles. These reveal a stratified society of farmers, herders and craftsmen, with women prominent in ritual. Dian controlled routes south towards South-[[e:east-asia|East Asia]] and west to [[s:myanmar|Burma]].
dian-kingdom.e: In 109 BCE the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] sent an army, and the king of Dian surrendered. Han created [[e:yizhou-commandery|Yizhou Commandery]] but let the king keep his title, granting him a gold seal that was found at [[e:shizhaishan|Shizhaishan]] in 1956. Dian culture faded into Han provincial life during the 1st century CE.

dinh-dynasty.t: The dynasty that reunited Vietnam after the anarchy of the Twelve Warlords and named the country Dai Co Viet, with its capital at Hoa Lu.
dinh-dynasty.o: [[e:dinh-tien-hoang|Dinh Bo Linh]], a local leader from [[e:hoa-lu|Hoa Lu]] in present-day [[e:ninh-binh-province|Ninh Binh]], defeated the rival warlords one by one and in 968 proclaimed himself emperor, Dinh Tien Hoang. He named the state [[s:early-le-dynasty|Dai Co Viet]] and built a fortified capital among the limestone hills at Hoa Lu.
dinh-dynasty.r: [[e:dinh-tien-hoang|Dinh Tien Hoang]] ruled with harsh punishments to restore order, organised the army into units, and gave Buddhist monks official ranks. He sent tribute to the [[e:song-dynasty|Song dynasty]], which granted titles to his son [[e:dinh-lien|Dinh Lien]] in the 970s, while using the title of emperor at home. Coins called Thai Binh were issued, among the first Vietnamese coinage.
dinh-dynasty.e: In 979 [[e:dinh-tien-hoang|Dinh Tien Hoang]] and his eldest son were assassinated, leaving the child [[e:dinh-phe-de|Dinh Phe De]] on the throne. With a [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] invasion looming, the commander [[e:le-dai-hanh|Le Hoan]] took power in 980 with the support of the queen mother, founding the [[s:early-le-dynasty|Early Le dynasty]]. Temples to the Dinh kings stand at [[e:hoa-lu|Hoa Lu]].

duchy-of-kozle.t: A minor Upper Silesian Piast duchy around the Oder town of Koźle, carved from the lands of the dukes of Bytom in the early 14th century.
duchy-of-kozle.o: [[e:kozle|Koźle]] belonged to the Upper Silesian lands of the [[s:duchy-of-bytom|Duchy of Bytom]], ruled by a branch of the [[e:piast-dynasty|Silesian Piasts]]. Around 1303 it was set apart for a junior member of the dynasty, beginning a short history as a separate duchy, though for much of the period it was held together with [[e:bytom|Bytom]] itself.
duchy-of-kozle.r: Like other small Silesian duchies, [[e:kozle|Koźle]] was a fortified market town on the [[e:oder-river|Oder]] with surrounding villages, settled partly by German colonists under German town law. In 1327 its duke did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|King John of Bohemia]], making the duchy a fief of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]]. Little else is recorded of its government.
duchy-of-kozle.e: The Bytom-[[e:kozle|Koźle]] line ended in 1355, and after a dispute Koźle passed to the dukes of the [[s:duchy-of-olesnica|Duchy of Oleśnica]], who held it until the late 15th century. It later reverted to the Bohemian crown, followed [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742 and became part of [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

duchy-of-lucca.t: A small Tuscan duchy created in 1815 for the former queen of Etruria, Maria Luisa of Bourbon, and absorbed by Tuscany in 1847.
duchy-of-lucca.o: The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] gave [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]] to [[e:maria-luisa-duchess-of-lucca|Maria Luisa of Spain]], former regent of the [[s:kingdom-of-etruria|Kingdom of Etruria]], as compensation for losing [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Parma]], which went to [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] widow [[e:marie-louise-duchess-of-parma|Marie Louise]]. Maria Luisa took possession in 1817 and ruled until her death in 1824.
duchy-of-lucca.r: [[e:maria-luisa-duchess-of-lucca|Maria Luisa]] revived court life, built roads and the aqueduct of [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]] and encouraged the arts. Her son [[e:charles-ii-duke-of-parma|Charles Louis]], Duke Charles I, ruled from 1824, an extravagant and unpredictable prince who spent much time abroad and left government to ministers. The duchy was small, conservative and dependent on [[e:austria|Austria]].
duchy-of-lucca.e: Under the [[e:vienna|Vienna]] settlement, the [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbons]] were to return to [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Parma]] when [[e:marie-louise-duchess-of-parma|Marie Louise]] died. In October 1847, shortly before her death, [[e:charles-ii-duke-of-parma|Charles Louis]] handed [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]] to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Grand Duchy of Tuscany]] and later became Duke of Parma.

dhami-state.t: A small Rajput hill state near Shimla, remembered for the Dhami firing of 1939, when its ruler's forces fired on protesters of the Praja Mandal.
dhami-state.o: Tradition dates the ruling family to around 1500, but little is reliably known of its origins. Its seat was at Halog.
dhami-state.r: Dhami was a small hill state, occupied by the [[e:gurkhas|Gurkhas]] in the early 19th century and restored under British protection after 1815. In July 1939 a march by the Dhami Prem Pracharini [[e:sabha-libya|Sabha]] and [[e:praja-mandal|Praja Mandal]] activists demanding reforms was fired on near Halog, killing protesters, an event remembered in the movement for democratic rule in the hill states.
dhami-state.e: Dhami merged into [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]] in April 1948 and is now part of [[e:shimla|Shimla]] district.

dompu-sultanate.t: A small sultanate in eastern Sumbawa, conquered by Majapahit in the 14th century and lasting into independent Indonesia.
dompu-sultanate.o: Dompo is listed in the Javanese [[e:nagarakretagama|Nagarakretagama]] among the dependencies of [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]], and an expedition to it is recorded in the mid-14th century. The register dates the sultanate from 1545, when its rulers are said to have adopted [[e:islam|Islam]], influenced by [[s:gowa-sultanate|Makassar]] and Bima.
dompu-sultanate.r: Dompu was an agricultural state of [[e:rice|rice]] and horses, whose people spoke the Bima language. It lived in the shadow of its larger neighbour Bima and of Gowa, and from the 17th century of the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]], which made treaties with the [[e:sumbawa|Sumbawa]] rulers. The eruption of [[e:mount-tambora|Mount Tambora]] in 1815 devastated the region, destroying the neighbouring kingdoms of [[s:kingdom-of-tambora|Tambora]] and Pekat.
dompu-sultanate.e: Dompu remained a self-governing state under [[e:dutch|Dutch]] rule into the 20th century. After [[e:indonesian-independence|Indonesian independence]] the sultanates of [[e:sumbawa|Sumbawa]] were dissolved, Dompu becoming a regency of [[e:west-nusa-tenggara|West Nusa Tenggara]] in 1958.

duklja.t: Medieval Serbian principality and kingdom on the Montenegrin coast, the first South Slav state whose ruler received a crown from the pope.
duklja.o: Duklja, named after the Roman town of [[e:doclea|Doclea]], emerged among [[e:serbs|Serbs]] of the southern Adriatic hinterland. It appears in the 10th century under Byzantine overlordship; Prince [[e:jovan-vladimir|Jovan Vladimir]] ruled it until his murder in 1016, and is venerated as a saint.
duklja.r: Around 1040 [[e:stefan-vojislav|Stefan Vojislav]] threw off Byzantine control and defeated a Byzantine army near [[e:bar-montenegro|Bar]] in 1042. His son [[e:mihailo-i-of-duklja|Mihailo I]] extended rule over [[s:grand-principality-of-serbia|Raška]], [[s:travunia|Travunia]] and [[s:zachlumia|Zachlumia]] and received a royal crown from [[e:pope-gregory-vii|Pope Gregory VII]] in 1077. His son [[e:constantine-bodin|Constantine Bodin]] briefly ruled a wide realm, and under him Bar became an archbishopric in 1089. The state lay on the Catholic-[[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] divide, with [[e:latin|Latin]] coastal towns such as [[s:commune-of-kotor|Kotor]] and Bar.
duklja.e: Dynastic strife after [[e:constantine-bodin|Bodin]]'s death around 1101 let [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] and [[s:grand-principality-of-serbia|Raška]] intervene. [[e:stefan-nemanja|Stefan Nemanja]] of the Grand [[s:principality-of-serbia|Principality of Serbia]] annexed it around 1186, and the region, later called [[e:zeta-region|Zeta]], became a [[e:nemanjic-dynasty|Nemanjić]] [[e:appanage|appanage]].

dyme.t: Westernmost city of Achaea and one of the four cities that refounded the Achaean League in 280 BCE.
dyme.o: Dyme lay on the coastal plain of western [[e:achaea|Achaea]], near [[e:cape-araxos|Cape Araxos]], facing the [[e:ionian-sea|Ionian Sea]]. It was one of the twelve cities of Achaea, formed in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] from local villages.
dyme.r: Little is known of its government before the Hellenistic age. In 280 BCE Dyme, [[s:patrae|Patrae]], [[e:tritaea|Tritaea]] and [[e:pharae-achaea|Pharae]] revived the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]], which grew into a major power. Exposed to the west, Dyme was sacked in 208 BCE by a Roman force during the [[e:first-macedonian-war|First Macedonian War]], its people enslaved and later ransomed by Philip V of the [[s:antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia|Antigonid Kingdom of Macedonia]].
dyme.e: Dyme passed under Roman control in 146 BCE. In 67 BCE [[e:pompey|Pompey]] resettled defeated Cilician [[e:piracy|pirates]] there, and it received a Roman colony c. 44 BCE before Augustus placed it under [[s:patrae|Patrae]].

despotate-of-the-morea.t: Late Byzantine principality based at Mistras in the Peloponnese, a last flowering of Byzantine culture and the home of the philosopher Plethon.
despotate-of-the-morea.o: [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] regained [[e:mystras|Mistras]], [[e:monemvasia|Monemvasia]] and the [[e:mani|Mani]] in 1262 from the [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]] and slowly expanded from there. In 1349 [[e:john-vi-kantakouzenos|John VI Kantakouzenos]] made his son [[e:manuel-kantakouzenos|Manuel Kantakouzenos]] despot of the province, giving it a permanent ruler. From 1383 it passed to members of the [[e:palaiologos-dynasty|Palaiologos]] family, beginning with Theodore I.
despotate-of-the-morea.r: Despots, usually younger sons of the emperor, ruled from [[e:mystras|Mistras]], whose churches with their frescoes survive. They gradually conquered the Frankish principality, completing it in 1432. Greek, Albanian and Slavic farmers formed the population. The philosopher [[e:gemistos-plethon|Gemistos Plethon]] proposed radical reforms there. The [[e:hexamilion-wall|Hexamilion wall]] across the Isthmus was rebuilt in 1415 against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].
despotate-of-the-morea.e: After the fall of [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 1453, the despots Thomas and [[e:demetrios-palaiologos|Demetrios Palaiologos]] quarrelled and faced Albanian revolts. [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] conquered the [[e:peloponnese|Morea]] in 1460, the last Greek fortresses falling in 1461.

despotate-of-melnik.t: Rhodope principality of Alexius Slav, a relative of the Asen tsars, who ruled from Melnik as an ally of the Latin crusaders.
despotate-of-melnik.o: After the death of [[e:tsar|Tsar]] [[e:kaloyan-of-bulgaria|Kaloyan]] in 1207, his relative [[e:alexius-slav|Alexius Slav]] refused to recognise the new tsar [[e:boril-of-bulgaria|Boril]] and seized the [[e:rhodope-mountains|Rhodope]] region. He made [[e:melnik|Melnik]], in the [[e:struma|Struma]] valley, his capital and held Tsepina and other fortresses.
despotate-of-melnik.r: [[e:alexius-slav|Alexius Slav]] allied with the [[s:latin-empire|Latin Empire of Constantinople]], marrying a daughter of Emperor [[e:henry-of-flanders|Henry of Flanders]], and bore the title of despot. He built churches and a residence at [[e:melnik|Melnik]], whose monastery of the Mother of God Spileotissa has a charter from him, and he fought [[e:boril-of-bulgaria|Boril]] and the Epirotes.
despotate-of-melnik.e: After 1228 he disappears from the record. The Bulgarian tsar [[e:ivan-asen-ii|Ivan Asen II]] absorbed his lands around 1230, after defeating [[e:epirus|Epirus]] at [[e:battle-of-klokotnitsa|Klokotnitsa]], into the [[s:second-bulgarian-empire|Second Bulgarian Empire]].

datarpur-state.t: A small Rajput hill principality in the Shivalik foothills of the Punjab, swallowed by Ranjit Singh's Sikh Empire in 1818.
datarpur-state.o: Datarpur was one of the petty [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] states of the outer Himalayan hills between the [[e:beas|Beas]] and [[e:sutlej-river|Sutlej]], in what is now [[e:hoshiarpur-district|Hoshiarpur district]]. Its ruling family belonged to the Dadwal clan and traced kinship to neighbouring hill houses such as those of [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] and [[s:guler-state|Guler]].
datarpur-state.r: Little is recorded of its internal history. Like its neighbours it was a small chieftaincy of hill villages and forts, paying tribute in turn to the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]], to Raja [[e:sansar-chand-katoch|Sansar Chand]] of [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] and then to the [[e:sikhs|Sikhs]] as their power grew in the late 18th century.
datarpur-state.e: In 1818 [[e:ranjit-singh|Maharaja Ranjit Singh]] annexed Datarpur to the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]], leaving the family a [[e:jagir|jagir]]. The area passed to the British with the [[e:bist-doab|Jalandhar Doab]] in 1846.

duchy-of-neopatras.t: Catalan duchy in southern Thessaly, created on the ruins of the Greek Principality of Thessaly and ruled with Athens by the kings of Sicily and Aragon.
duchy-of-neopatras.o: After the [[e:catalan-company|Catalan Company]] conquered the [[s:duchy-of-athens|Duchy of Athens]] in 1311, it pushed north into [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]]. When [[e:john-ii-doukas|John II Doukas]] of the [[s:principality-of-thessaly|Principality of Thessaly]] died without heirs in 1318, the Catalans occupied the south of the region with its capital [[e:ypati|Neopatras]] (modern Ypati) and organised it as a duchy in 1319.
duchy-of-neopatras.r: [[e:ypati|Neopatras]] was held together with [[s:athens|Athens]] by the Aragonese kings of [[e:sicily|Sicily]], who appointed vicars-general such as [[e:alfonso-fadrique|Alfonso Fadrique]] to govern it. A small Catalan military class ruled over [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and [[e:vlachs|Vlachs]], following the customs of [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]]. In 1379-1380 the duchies passed to [[e:peter-iv-of-aragon|Peter IV of Aragon]], who called the Acropolis the most beautiful jewel in the world.
duchy-of-neopatras.e: Attacks by the [[e:navarrese-company|Navarrese Company]], the Florentine [[e:nerio-i-acciaioli|Nerio Acciaioli]] and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] broke the Catalan hold. [[e:ypati|Neopatras]] fell around 1390, and the Ottomans took [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]] in the 1390s.

duchy-of-niemodlin.t: A small Upper Silesian Piast duchy around the castle of Niemodlin, split from the Duchy of Opole in 1313 and reabsorbed in 1382.
duchy-of-niemodlin.o: On the death of Duke [[e:bolko-i-of-opole|Bolko I of Opole]] in 1313, his lands were divided among his sons. [[e:boleslaw-the-elder-of-niemodlin|Bolesław the Elder]] received [[e:niemodlin|Niemodlin]] (Falkenberg), a castle town west of [[e:opole|Opole]], as his own duchy. He was close to the Bohemian court and in 1327 did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|King John of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-niemodlin.r: The duchy consisted of [[e:niemodlin|Niemodlin]] and its surrounding villages, settled partly under German law, with the castle as the ducal residence. Its dukes depended on Bohemian patronage and on their cousins in the [[s:duchy-of-opole|Duchy of Opole]]. Little is recorded of its internal government.
duchy-of-niemodlin.e: The [[e:niemodlin|Niemodlin]] line died out with Duke Henry in 1382, and the duchy returned to the [[s:duchy-of-opole|Duchy of Opole]]. Niemodlin later passed through various Silesian lords, went to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742 and became part of [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

diocese-of-hispania.t: The late Roman administrative unit that grouped the provinces of Iberia and north-west Africa under a single vicar based at Mérida.
diocese-of-hispania.o: The diocese was created in [[e:diocletian|Diocletian's]] reforms around 297 to 314, grouping the provinces of [[s:hispania-baetica|Baetica]], [[s:lusitania|Lusitania]], [[s:carthaginiensis|Carthaginiensis]], [[s:gallaecia|Gallaecia]] and [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Tarraconensis]] with [[s:mauretania-tingitana|Mauretania Tingitana]] across the Strait. The [[s:balearica|Balearica]] province was added around 369. It formed part of the Praetorian Prefecture of the [[e:gaul|Gauls]].
diocese-of-hispania.r: A vicarius at [[e:emerita-augusta|Emerita Augusta]] oversaw the provincial governors, mainly in justice and taxation, while separate officers commanded the army. [[e:hispania|Hispania]] was largely peaceful in the 4th century, a land of rich villas and cities. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] grew strong, as the [[e:council-of-elvira|Council of Elvira]] shows, and the emperor [[e:theodosius-i|Theodosius I]] came from [[e:coca-spain|Cauca]] in the north.
diocese-of-hispania.e: In 409 [[e:vandals|Vandals]], [[s:alans|Alans]] and [[s:suebi|Suebi]] crossed the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] during the usurpation of [[e:constantine-iii-western-roman-emperor|Constantine III]] and his general [[e:gerontius-general|Gerontius]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] partly restored control with Visigothic help, but the diocese effectively broke up as barbarian kingdoms took over.

duchy-of-brno.t: One of the Moravian appanage duchies held by junior Přemyslid princes, centred on Brno, until Moravia was reunited as a margraviate.
duchy-of-brno.o: Duke [[e:bretislaus-i-duke-of-bohemia|Bretislaus I]] of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] arranged [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] as a domain for junior members of the [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid dynasty]]. After his death in 1055, his sons divided it; Conrad I received the [[e:brno|Brno]] portion, centred on the castle of Brno (Brünn) in southern [[e:moravia|Moravia]], while [[e:olomouc|Olomouc]] and later [[e:znojmo|Znojmo]] formed separate [[e:appanage|appanages]].
duchy-of-brno.r: The princes of [[e:brno|Brno]] owed allegiance to the senior duke in [[e:prague|Prague]] but frequently joined in the dynasty's feuds; Conrad I himself briefly became Duke of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] in 1092. Brno grew as a castle and market centre. Little is known in detail of its administration, which followed the Bohemian castle system.
duchy-of-brno.e: In the late 12th century the Moravian [[e:appanage|appanages]] were absorbed. Around 1182 [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] was declared a margraviate directly subject to the emperor, and by about 1197 [[e:vladislaus-iii-duke-of-bohemia|Vladislaus Henry]] united the Moravian lands under his rule. [[e:brno|Brno]] later became the capital of the Margraviate of [[e:moravia|Moravia]].

dara-sultanate.t: One of the seven Muslim states of medieval Abyssinia named by Arab writers, a small principality tributary to the Ethiopian emperors.
dara-sultanate.o: Dara is known only from brief mentions, chiefly by the 14th-century Arab writer [[e:al-umari|al-Umari]], who listed it among the seven Muslim kingdoms of [[e:ethiopia|Abyssinia]] alongside [[e:ifat-sultanate|Ifat]], [[s:sultanate-of-dawaro|Dawaro]], [[s:arababni|Arababni]], [[s:hadiya-sultanate|Hadiya]], [[s:sharkha-sultanate|Sharkha]] and [[e:bale|Bale]]. It lay in the south-eastern [[e:ethiopian-highlands|Ethiopian highlands]], probably near Bale.
dara-sultanate.r: [[e:al-umari|Al-Umari's]] brief notice suggests a small state with a modest army and an economy of farming and herding. Like its neighbours it paid tribute to the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]] after the campaigns of [[e:amda-seyon-i|Amda Seyon]] in the 1330s.
dara-sultanate.e: Dara disappears from the record in the 15th century, absorbed into neighbouring provinces and later overrun during the wars of [[e:adal-sultanate|Adal]] and the [[e:oromo-migrations|Oromo migrations]].

duchy-of-glad.t: Duchy in the Banat described in the Gesta Hungarorum as resisting the conquering Hungarians around 900; its existence is debated.
duchy-of-glad.o: The main source is the [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta Hungarorum]], written by an anonymous notary around 1200. It says [[e:glad|Glad]], who came from [[e:vidin|Vidin]], ruled the land between the [[e:mures-river|Mureș]], the [[e:tisza|Tisza]] and the [[e:danube|Danube]], with [[e:cumans|Cumans]], [[e:bulgarians|Bulgarians]] and [[e:vlachs|Vlachs]], from the fortress of [[e:kovin|Keve]] (Kovin).
duchy-of-glad.r: Nothing is known of its government beyond the [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta]], which claims [[e:glad|Glad]] fought the [[e:magyars|Hungarians]] with Cuman, Bulgarian and [[e:vlachs|Vlach]] forces before being defeated and submitting. Historians disagree on whether he was a real ruler, perhaps a Bulgarian governor, or a figure invented from later place-names.
duchy-of-glad.e: The [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta]] says the [[e:magyars|Hungarians]] took his lands, which then passed to the [[s:principality-of-hungary|Principality of Hungary]]. The same source makes [[e:ahtum|Ahtum]], of the [[s:duchy-of-ahtum|Duchy of Ahtum]], his descendant.

duchy-of-slutsk.t: A Ruthenian duchy in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, ruled by the Olelkovich princes and famous for resisting Tatar raids.
duchy-of-slutsk.o: In 1395 [[e:vytautas-the-great|Vytautas]] removed [[e:volodymyr-olgerdovich|Volodymyr Olgerdovich]] from the [[s:principality-of-kiev|Principality of Kiev]] and gave him [[e:slutsk|Slutsk]] and [[e:kapyl|Kapyl]] in compensation. Volodymyr's descendants, the [[e:olelkovich|Olelkovich]] princes, held Slutsk as a hereditary duchy within the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] for two centuries.
duchy-of-slutsk.r: The [[e:olelkovich|Olelkovich]] princes were among the greatest [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] [[e:magnates|magnates]] of the grand duchy, with their own court, troops and towns. In 1506 the regent [[e:anastasia-of-slutsk|Anastasia of Slutsk]] defended the town against a [[e:tatars|Tatar]] siege. The princes built churches and monasteries, and [[e:slutsk|Slutsk]] became a centre of Orthodox learning and crafts.
duchy-of-slutsk.e: The male line of the [[e:olelkovich|Olelkovich]] princes died out in 1592. Through the marriage of the heiress [[e:sophia-olelkovich|Sophia Olelkovich]] to [[e:janusz-radziwill-1579-1620|Janusz Radziwill]], the duchy passed to the [[e:radziwill-family|Radziwill]] family, who held it as a private estate. [[e:slutsk|Slutsk]] later became famous for its woven [[e:silk|silk]] sashes.

donetsk-krivoy-rog-soviet-republic.t: A Bolshevik republic of the Donbas and Kryvyi Rih industrial regions, proclaimed in 1918 as part of Soviet Russia rather than Ukraine.
donetsk-krivoy-rog-soviet-republic.o: In February 1918 a regional congress of soviets in [[e:kharkiv|Kharkiv]] proclaimed the Donetsk-Krivoy Rog Soviet Republic over the [[e:coal|coal]] and iron districts of eastern and southern [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]]. Its leader, [[e:fyodor-sergeyev|Fyodor Sergeyev]], known as Artyom, argued that the industrial region belonged economically with [[e:russia|Russia]] rather than with the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]].
donetsk-krivoy-rog-soviet-republic.r: The republic had a council of people's commissars in [[e:kharkiv|Kharkiv]] and tried to nationalise mines and factories, but it existed for only a few weeks. Its separate status was opposed by Bolsheviks who backed a single [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic-of-soviets|Soviet Ukraine]], and [[e:moscow|Moscow]] did not formally recognise it as distinct from [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]].
donetsk-krivoy-rog-soviet-republic.e: After the [[e:treaty-of-brest-litovsk|Treaty of Brest-Litovsk]], German and Austro-Hungarian forces advanced into the [[e:donbas|Donbas]]. The government retreated to [[e:luhansk|Luhansk]] and beyond, and by spring 1918 the republic was dissolved into [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic-of-soviets|Soviet Ukraine]]'s structures, with its territory occupied by the [[e:central-powers|Central Powers]].

dal-naraidi.t: Leading kingdom of the Cruthin in south Antrim, whose king Congal Cáech fought for the high kingship and fell at Mag Rath in 637.
dal-naraidi.o: The Dál nAraidi were the leading dynasty of the Cruthin, a people of east [[s:northern-ireland|Ulster]] distinguished in early Irish sources from the [[s:kingdom-of-ulaid|Ulaid]] proper. By the 6th century they held south and central [[e:county-antrim|County Antrim]], with their royal centre in Mag Line near the town of Antrim, and they competed with the [[s:dal-fiatach|Dal Fiatach]] for the kingship of the Kingdom of Ulaid.
dal-naraidi.r: [[e:fiachnae-mac-baetain|Fiachnae mac Báetáin]], who died in 626, became king of the [[s:kingdom-of-ulaid|Ulaid]] and is said to have campaigned in [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. [[e:congal-caech|Congal Cáech]], king of the Ulaid and briefly claimant to the kingship of [[e:hill-of-tara|Tara]], allied with [[s:dal-riata|Dál Riata]] but was defeated and killed by [[e:domnall-mac-aedo|Domnall mac Áedo]] at [[e:battle-of-moira|Mag Rath]] in 637. St [[e:saint-comgall|Comgall]], founder of the monastery of [[e:bangor-abbey|Bangor]], belonged to this people.
dal-naraidi.e: After [[e:battle-of-moira|Mag Rath]] their power declined, though their kings still held the [[s:kingdom-of-ulaid|Ulaid]] kingship at times until the 10th century. Pressure from [[e:vikings|Viking]] raiders, the [[e:ui-neill|Uí Néill]] and the [[s:dal-fiatach|Dal Fiatach]] reduced them, and by the 12th century their lands passed under [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] and [[e:o-neill-dynasty|Ua Néill]] rule.

danish-greenland.t: Greenland as a Danish colony, from the missionary Hans Egede's arrival in 1721 to its integration into the Danish realm in 1953.
danish-greenland.o: Hoping to find the lost Norse colonists, the Norwegian priest [[e:hans-egede|Hans Egede]] sailed to [[e:greenland|Greenland]] in 1721 with the support of [[s:denmark-norway|Denmark-Norway]] and founded a mission and trading post, moving it to [[e:nuuk|Godthåb]] (Nuuk) in 1728. Danish trading stations then spread along the west coast.
danish-greenland.r: From 1776 the [[e:royal-greenland-trading-department|Royal Greenland Trade Department]] held a monopoly on trade, keeping the island closed to outsiders. The [[e:inuit|Inuit]] population lived by seal hunting, while the [[e:danes|Danes]] bought skins, blubber and later cod. Lutheran and Moravian missions converted most Greenlanders. When [[e:norway|Norway]] was ceded to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in 1814, [[e:greenland|Greenland]] stayed Danish, and in 1933 the Permanent Court of International Justice rejected Norway's claim to East Greenland.
danish-greenland.e: During the German occupation of [[e:denmark|Denmark]] the [[s:united-states|United States]] protected [[e:greenland|Greenland]] and built bases there. In 1953 a new Danish constitution ended colonial status and made Greenland an integral part of the [[s:kingdom-of-denmark|Kingdom of Denmark]]. Home rule followed in 1979 and self-government in 2009.

duchy-of-tuscia.t: Lombard duchy of Tuscany, centred on Lucca, whose duke Desiderius rose to become the last king of the Lombards.
duchy-of-tuscia.o: After the [[e:lombards|Lombards]] occupied most of [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]] in the 570s, the region was organised under dukes, with [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]] as the chief seat. Smaller duchies existed at [[s:clusium|Chiusi]] and elsewhere, but Lucca, on the route to [[e:rome|Rome]] later called the [[e:via-francigena|Via Francigena]], emerged as the dominant centre.
duchy-of-tuscia.r: Little is known of the early dukes. Documents from [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]], unusually rich for the 8th century, show a society of [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] landowners, churches and notaries, and Duke Walpert appears in the early 8th century. The Lombard nobleman [[e:desiderius|Desiderius]] held authority in [[s:march-of-tuscany|Tuscia]] before becoming king in 756. Lucca minted gold coins and was the main town of Lombard [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]].
duchy-of-tuscia.e: After [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] conquest of 774, [[s:march-of-tuscany|Tuscia]] passed to Frankish counts and dukes based at [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]]. By the 9th century these governors were styled margraves, and the region became the March of [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]].

duchy-of-gelou.t: Transylvanian duchy of Gelou, called a Vlach by the Gesta Hungarorum, whose defeat opened Transylvania to the Hungarians; its existence is debated.
duchy-of-gelou.o: The [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta Hungarorum]], written around 1200, is the only source. It describes [[e:gelou|Gelou]] as a [[e:vlachs|Vlach]] ruling Vlachs and [[e:slavs|Slavs]] in the [[e:somes|Someș]] valley of [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] at the time of the Hungarian conquest, with his centre usually placed at Dăbâca.
duchy-of-gelou.r: Nothing is known of the duchy beyond the chronicle, which praises the land for its salt and gold-bearing rivers and says its people were poorly armed and suffered Cuman and [[e:pechenegs|Pecheneg]] raids. An early medieval fortification at Dăbâca has been excavated, but its dating is disputed.
duchy-of-gelou.e: The [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta]] says [[e:tuhutum|Tuhutum]], a Hungarian chief, defeated [[e:gelou|Gelou's]] army at the river Almaș and had him killed by the Căpuș as he fled, and the inhabitants accepted him as lord; his descendants are linked to the [[s:realm-of-the-gyulas|Realm of the Gyulas]]. The episode is central to debates over the early history of [[e:romanians|Romanians]] in [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]].

duchy-of-gaeta.t: Small coastal state between Rome and Naples that broke free of Byzantium in the 9th century and lasted until the Normans absorbed it in 1140.
duchy-of-gaeta.o: [[e:gaeta|Gaeta]], a fortified promontory on the Tyrrhenian coast, was part of Byzantine territory loosely tied to the [[s:duchy-of-naples|Duchy of Naples]]. In the 9th century, amid Arab raids and [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] pressure, it gained autonomy under local rulers styled hypatoi (consuls). Around 867 [[e:docibilis-i-of-gaeta|Docibilis I]] founded the dynasty that made it a hereditary state.
duchy-of-gaeta.r: The rulers of [[e:gaeta|Gaeta]], who later took the title of duke, controlled a small territory around the [[e:gulf-of-gaeta|Gulf of Gaeta]] and grew rich from sea trade. They sometimes allied with Arab raiders settled at the [[e:garigliano|Garigliano]], then joined the Christian coalition that destroyed that base in 915. The duchy minted its own [[e:copper|copper]] coins, and its charters, the [[e:codex-diplomaticus-cajetanus|Codex Caietanus]], document its society.
duchy-of-gaeta.e: From 1032 [[e:gaeta|Gaeta]] fell under the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] princes of [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]] and then under Norman lords. In 1140 it submitted to [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]] and joined the [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]], keeping a degree of municipal autonomy.

deli-sultanate.t: East Sumatran Malay sultanate whose land concessions created the famous Deli tobacco industry and the city of Medan.
deli-sultanate.o: Deli was founded in 1632 by [[e:tuanku-gocah-pahlawan|Tuanku Gocah Pahlawan]], a commander sent by the [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]] under [[e:iskandar-muda|Iskandar Muda]] to secure the coast of eastern [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]]. His descendants ruled as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of [[e:aceh|Aceh]] and later of the [[s:siak-sultanate|Siak Sultanate]], before Deli declared itself an independent sultanate in the 19th century.
deli-sultanate.r: The sultans governed Malay coastal communities and held authority over neighbouring [[e:karo-batak|Karo Batak]] lands. After the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] took control in 1862, the court leased vast tracts to planters such as [[e:jacob-nienhuys|Jacob Nienhuys]], whose wrapper tobacco became world famous. Chinese and Javanese contract labourers were brought in, and [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:mamun-al-rasyid-perkasa-alam|Ma'mun Al Rasyid Perkasa Alam]] began the [[e:maimun-palace|Maimun Palace]] in Medan in 1888.
deli-sultanate.e: Deli became the wealthiest of the self-governing states of the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]], and Medan grew into a major city. The social revolution of March 1946 ended the sultanate as a political power, though the sultan remains a ceremonial figure in Medan today.

duchy-of-mecklenburg-schwerin.t: The larger Mecklenburg state on the Baltic, ruled by one of Europe's oldest dynasties and known for its archaic feudal constitution.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-schwerin.o: After the extinction of the [[e:gustrow|Güstrow]] line in 1695, a succession dispute in the [[e:house-of-mecklenburg|House of Mecklenburg]] was settled by the [[e:treaty-of-hamburg-1701|Treaty of Hamburg]] in 1701. [[e:frederick-william-duke-of-mecklenburg-schwerin|Frederick William]] received the larger western share as the Duchy of [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg-Schwerin]], with [[s:county-of-schwerin|Schwerin]], [[s:lordship-of-rostock|Rostock]] and [[e:wismar|Wismar's]] hinterland, while a smaller share became Mecklenburg-[[e:strelitz|Strelitz]].
duchy-of-mecklenburg-schwerin.r: The dynasty descended from the Obotrite prince [[e:niklot|Niklot]] of the 12th century. Under the 1755 settlement with the estates, power was shared with the knighthood, preserving large noble estates and [[e:serfdom|serfdom]] until 1820. The economy rested on grain and [[e:cattle|cattle]]. Frederick Francis I joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] and became grand duke in 1815. A liberal constitution of 1849 was annulled in 1850, and the old estates constitution remained in force until 1918.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-schwerin.e: [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg-Schwerin]] joined the [[s:north-german-confederation|North German Confederation]] and in 1871 the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]]. [[e:frederick-francis-iv-grand-duke-of-mecklenburg-schwerin|Grand Duke Frederick Francis IV]] abdicated in November 1918, and the state continued as the [[s:free-state-of-mecklenburg-schwerin|Free State of Mecklenburg-Schwerin]].

duchy-of-estonia-1561-1721.t: Northern Estonia under the Swedish crown, Sweden's first Baltic conquest, held from 1561 until Peter the Great took it in the Great Northern War.
duchy-of-estonia-1561-1721.o: As [[s:terra-mariana|Terra Mariana]] collapsed under Russian attack, the city of [[s:reval|Reval]] and the knighthoods of [[e:harju-county|Harrien]], [[s:virumaa|Wierland]] and [[e:jarva-county|Jerwen]] submitted to [[e:eric-xiv-of-sweden|Eric XIV of Sweden]] in 1561. [[e:sweden|Sweden]] held on through the long [[e:livonian-war|Livonian War]], and the [[e:treaty-of-teusina|Treaty of Teusina]] in 1595 confirmed its possession of northern [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]].
duchy-of-estonia-1561-1721.r: The duchy was ruled by a Swedish governor at [[s:reval|Reval]], but the [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] nobility kept wide self-government, their Lutheran church and control of their serfs. Swedish rule founded schools, including a [[e:gymnasium|gymnasium]] at Reval in 1631, and promoted [[e:printing-press|printing]] in Estonian; [[e:charles-xi-of-sweden|Charles XI's]] reduction of noble estates in the 1680s angered the nobles. Reval and [[e:narva|Narva]] were key ports for Baltic trade.
duchy-of-estonia-1561-1721.e: In the [[e:great-northern-war|Great Northern War]] Russian forces took [[s:reval|Reval]] in 1710, and the [[e:treaty-of-nystad|Treaty of Nystad]] in 1721 confirmed the loss. The region became the [[s:governorate-of-estonia|Governorate of Estonia]] within the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]], its nobles' privileges guaranteed by [[e:peter-the-great|Peter the Great]].

dutch-bengal.t: The Dutch East India Company's directorate in Bengal, based at Chinsurah on the Hooghly, a major source of silk, opium and saltpetre.
dutch-bengal.o: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) began trading in [[e:bengal|Bengal]] in the 1620s, opening a factory at Pipli and then establishing its main base at [[e:chinsurah|Chinsurah]] on the [[e:hooghly-river|Hooghly]] river around 1635. In 1656 it built [[e:fort-gustavus|Fort Gustavus]] there, and Bengal became a separate directorate with posts at [[e:kasimbazar|Kasimbazar]], [[e:patna|Patna]] and [[e:dhaka|Dhaka]].
dutch-bengal.r: [[e:bengal|Bengal]] supplied raw [[e:silk|silk]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth, saltpetre for [[e:gunpowder|gunpowder]] and opium for the Indonesian trade, and by the late 17th century was among the [[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC's]] most profitable regions. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] operated under the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] and later the [[s:nawabate-of-bengal|Nawabate of Bengal]], paying duties and seeking privileges by negotiation.
dutch-bengal.e: The British [[e:east-india-company|East India Company's]] victory at [[e:chinsurah|Chinsurah]] in 1759 ended [[e:dutch|Dutch]] ambitions in [[e:bengal|Bengal]]. The British occupied the posts during the [[e:napoleonic-wars|Napoleonic Wars]], and Chinsurah was ceded to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1825 under the [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824|Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824]].

deva-dynasty-of-bengal.t: A Hindu dynasty of south-eastern Bengal that ruled from the Dhaka region in the 13th century, after the Sena dynasty withdrew from the west.
deva-dynasty-of-bengal.o: The Deva dynasty is known almost entirely from a few [[e:copper|copper]]-plate inscriptions. It arose in the early 13th century in eastern [[e:bengal|Bengal]], around [[e:vikrampur|Vikrampur]] and the later [[e:sonargaon|Suvarnagrama]] (Sonargaon), as [[e:sena-dynasty|Sena]] power collapsed in western Bengal after [[e:bakhtiyar-khalji|Bakhtiyar Khalji's]] conquest of [[e:nabadwip|Nadia]].
deva-dynasty-of-bengal.r: Dasharathadeva, the best-known king, styled himself supreme ruler and held the [[e:dhaka|Dhaka]] and [[e:comilla|Comilla]] region; his inscriptions mention the capital at [[e:sonargaon|Suvarnagrama]]. The kings were [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnava]] [[e:hinduism|Hindus]] who made land grants to [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] in [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]]. Little else is known of their administration or economy.
deva-dynasty-of-bengal.e: The dynasty disappears from the record in the late 13th century, when [[e:sonargaon|Sonargaon]] came under the control of Muslim governors of [[e:gaur|Lakhnauti]] and eventually the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]]. Sonargaon later became the capital of the [[s:sonargaon-sultanate|Sonargaon Sultanate]].

duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg.t: Duchy created in 1235 for Otto the Child, grandson of Henry the Lion, which reconciled the Guelphs with the Hohenstaufen and founded the house of Brunswick.
duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg.o: After [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion's]] fall in 1180, his family kept their allodial lands around [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] and [[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]]. At the Diet of [[e:mainz|Mainz]] in 1235 his grandson [[e:otto-the-child|Otto the Child]] surrendered these lands to [[e:frederick-ii|Emperor Frederick II]] and received them back as a new imperial duchy, ending the long feud between the [[e:house-of-welf|Guelphs]] and the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]].
duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg.r: Otto ruled from [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]], where [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion's]] castle of [[e:dankwarderode-castle|Dankwarderode]] and the bronze lion stood, and from [[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]], whose salt works were the duchy's main source of wealth. The duchy lay between the [[e:weser|Weser]] and the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and included [[e:hanover|Hanover]], [[e:celle|Celle]] and [[e:gottingen|Göttingen]]. After Otto's death in 1252 his sons Albert I the Tall and John ruled jointly.
duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg.e: In 1269 Albert and John divided the duchy, creating the [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Principality of Wolfenbüttel]] and the [[s:principality-of-luneburg|Principality of Lüneburg]]. The ducal title stayed common to all [[e:house-of-welf|Guelph]] lines, from which the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] and the British royal house of [[e:hanover|Hanover]] later descended.

despotate-of-angelokastron-and-lepanto.t: Albanian principality in Aetolia under the Shpata family, holding Angelokastron and the port of Lepanto after the Serbian conquest of Epirus.
despotate-of-angelokastron-and-lepanto.o: After [[e:nikephoros-ii-orsini|Nikephoros II Orsini]] of [[e:epirus|Epirus]] was killed by Albanian clans in 1359, Albanian leaders divided southern Epirus. [[e:gjin-bua-shpata|Gjin Bua Shpata]] took [[e:angelokastron|Angelokastron]] and [[e:nafpaktos|Lepanto]] (Naupaktos) in [[e:aetolia|Aetolia]], while [[e:peter-losha|Peter Losha]] held the [[s:despotate-of-arta|Despotate of Arta]]. Both received the title of despot from the Serbian ruler [[e:simeon-uros|Simeon Uroš]].
despotate-of-angelokastron-and-lepanto.r: The [[e:shpata-family|Shpata]] ruled Albanian clans who had migrated south as herders and soldiers, alongside a Greek population. They fought the [[e:capetian-house-of-anjou|Angevins]], the [[e:tocco-family|Tocco of Kefalonia]], the [[e:navarrese-company|Navarrese Company]] and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. In 1374 [[e:gjin-bua-shpata|Gjin Bua Shpata]] also took Arta, joining the two Albanian despotates.
despotate-of-angelokastron-and-lepanto.e: After [[e:gjin-bua-shpata|Gjin]]'s death in 1399 his family held on briefly: [[e:nafpaktos|Lepanto]] was sold to [[e:venice|Venice]] in 1407, and [[e:angelokastron|Angelokastron]] fell to [[e:carlo-i-tocco|Carlo I Tocco]] around 1408.

dervish-state.t: A Somali religious and military state led by Mohammed Abdullah Hassan, which fought Britain, Italy and Ethiopia for two decades.
dervish-state.o: [[e:mohammed-abdullah-hassan|Mohammed Abdullah Hassan]], a scholar of the [[e:salihiyya|Salihiyya]] [[e:sufism|Sufi]] order, returned from [[e:arabia|Arabia]] in the mid-1890s and began preaching in [[e:berbera|Berbera]] against British rule and Christian missions. Rejected by local elites, he moved inland, won over clans in the [[e:nugaal-valley|Nugaal]] and [[e:ogaden|Ogaden]], and in 1899 declared a holy war, building a movement of followers called Dervishes (Darawiish).
dervish-state.r: The Dervish State was a militant religious community under the sayyid's authority, with a council of leaders, armed horsemen and riflemen. Hassan was also a celebrated poet. It defeated several British expeditions, including at [[e:battle-of-dul-madoba|Dul Madoba]] in 1913, and built stone forts at [[e:taleh|Taleh]]. Its raids devastated rival clans, and famine and war killed many [[e:somalis|Somalis]].
dervish-state.e: In 1920 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] combined aircraft, the [[e:camel|Camel]] Corps and local levies to destroy the forts at [[e:taleh|Taleh]]. Hassan fled to the [[e:ogaden|Ogaden]] and died there later that year. Many [[e:somalis|Somalis]] remember the Dervishes as early fighters for independence.

duchy-of-burgundy.t: The wine-rich duchy around Dijon, home of Cluny and Cîteaux, that under its Valois dukes became the seed of a great European power.
duchy-of-burgundy.o: [[e:richard-the-justiciar|Richard the Justiciar]], count of [[e:autun|Autun]], gathered the counties of western [[e:burgundy|Burgundy]] and was recognised as duke by around 918. After a century of disputes the duchy went in 1032 to Robert, younger brother of King Henry I, founding a Capetian line that ruled from [[e:dijon|Dijon]] for over 300 years.
duchy-of-burgundy.r: The dukes were great [[e:vassal|vassals]] of [[e:france|France]], governing through their council and the [[e:estates-of-burgundy|Estates of Burgundy]]. The duchy was a heartland of monastic reform: [[e:cluny-abbey|Cluny]] lay on its borders, and [[e:citeaux-abbey|Cîteaux]], founded in 1098, launched the Cistercian order. Its vineyards in the Côte d'Or were already famous in the [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]].
duchy-of-burgundy.e: When [[e:philip-i-duke-of-burgundy|Philip of Rouvres]] died in 1361, [[e:john-ii-of-france|John II of France]] took the duchy and in 1363 gave it to his son [[e:philip-the-bold|Philip the Bold]], founding the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]]. After [[e:charles-the-bold|Charles the Bold]] fell at [[e:battle-of-nancy|Nancy]] in 1477, [[e:louis-xi|Louis XI]] annexed the duchy to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

decapole.t: A league of ten imperial cities of Alsace, founded in 1354 for mutual defence, which survived until Louis XIV absorbed it.
decapole.o: In 1354 [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]] joined ten [[e:free-imperial-city|free imperial cities]] of [[e:alsace|Alsace]] in an alliance: [[s:free-imperial-city-of-haguenau|Haguenau]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-colmar|Colmar]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-wissembourg|Wissembourg]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-turckheim|Turckheim]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-obernai|Obernai]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-kaysersberg|Kaysersberg]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-rosheim|Rosheim]], [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-selestat|Sélestat]] and [[s:republic-of-mulhouse|Mulhouse]]. They were placed under the imperial bailiff at Haguenau to defend their rights against local lords.
decapole.r: The cities governed themselves but pledged mutual aid, shared costs and met in diets. [[s:republic-of-mulhouse|Mulhouse]] left in 1515 to ally with the Swiss and [[e:landau|Landau]] joined in 1521. Members were wine and market towns, and some, like [[s:free-imperial-city-of-colmar|Colmar]], adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] while others stayed Catholic. The league had no army or capital of its own.
decapole.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 transferred imperial rights in [[e:alsace|Alsace]] to [[e:france|France]] ambiguously, and [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] occupied the cities in 1673. The [[e:treaties-of-nijmegen|Treaty of Nijmegen]] of 1679 confirmed French control, ending the league.

duchy-of-warsaw.t: Napoleon's Polish client state, which revived a Polish government and army after the partitions and introduced the Napoleonic Code.
duchy-of-warsaw.o: After defeating [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1806 and 1807, [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] created the Duchy of [[e:warsaw|Warsaw]] by the [[e:treaties-of-tilsit|Treaty of Tilsit]] out of the lands Prussia had taken in the Second and [[e:third-partition-of-poland|Third Partitions]] of [[e:poland|Poland]]. He made [[e:frederick-augustus-i-of-saxony|Frederick Augustus I]], King of [[e:saxony|Saxony]], its duke, linking it to the [[s:kingdom-of-saxony|Kingdom of Saxony]].
duchy-of-warsaw.r: The constitution of 1807 abolished personal [[e:serfdom|serfdom]], declared equality before the law and introduced the [[e:napoleonic-code|Napoleonic Code]], though nobles kept their land. Real power lay with French officials and the needs of [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] wars. Prince [[e:jozef-poniatowski|Jozef Poniatowski]] built a Polish army that defeated [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1809, after which the duchy gained [[e:krakow|Krakow]] and [[e:lublin|Lublin]].
duchy-of-warsaw.e: About 100,000 soldiers from the duchy joined the invasion of [[e:russia|Russia]] in 1812, and Poniatowski died at [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]] in 1813. Russia occupied the duchy, and the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] divided it in 1815 into [[s:congress-poland|Congress Poland]], the [[s:grand-duchy-of-posen|Grand Duchy of Posen]] and the [[s:free-city-of-krakow|Free City of Krakow]].

duchy-of-saxe-altenburg.t: Ernestine duchy in eastern Thuringia, home of the card game Skat and of the dukes who exchanged Hildburghausen for Altenburg.
duchy-of-saxe-altenburg.o: When [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg]] died out in 1825, the Ernestine lands were rearranged in 1826. Duke [[e:frederick-duke-of-saxe-altenburg|Frederick]] of Saxe-[[e:hildburghausen|Hildburghausen]] gave up his old duchy and received [[e:altenburg|Altenburg]], founding the new Duchy of Saxe-Altenburg.
duchy-of-saxe-altenburg.r: The duchy was Lutheran and agriculturally rich, with prosperous peasant farms and later lignite mining. The card game [[e:skat|Skat]] was developed in [[e:altenburg|Altenburg]] around 1810-1820, and the town remains its centre, with a Skat court. A constitution was granted in 1831, and in 1848 unrest forced Duke Joseph to abdicate. [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-altenburg|Ernest I]] ruled from 1853 to 1908.
duchy-of-saxe-altenburg.e: Saxe-[[e:altenburg|Altenburg]] joined the [[s:north-german-confederation|North German Confederation]] and the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]]. Duke [[e:ernst-ii-duke-of-saxe-altenburg|Ernest II]] abdicated in November 1918, and in 1920 the state merged into the [[s:free-state-of-thuringia|Free State of Thuringia]]. [[e:altenburg-castle|Altenburg Castle]] now houses a museum of playing cards.

duchy-of-saxe-hildburghausen.t: Small Ernestine duchy in southern Thuringia whose princess's 1810 wedding in Munich gave rise to the Oktoberfest.
duchy-of-saxe-hildburghausen.o: [[e:ernest-duke-of-saxe-hildburghausen|Ernest]], the sixth son of [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-gotha|Ernest the Pious]], received [[e:hildburghausen|Hildburghausen]] in the 1680 partition of the Saxe-[[e:gotha|Gotha]] inheritance. He made the small town his residence and was given full ducal [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], later adding Eisfeld and Königsberg in [[e:franconia|Franconia]].
duchy-of-saxe-hildburghausen.r: The dukes built a palace and attracted [[e:huguenots|Huguenot]] refugees to a new town quarter. Extravagance led to bankruptcy, and in 1769 an imperial debt commission took over the finances. [[e:frederick-duke-of-saxe-altenburg|Duke Frederick]]'s daughter [[e:therese-of-saxe-hildburghausen|Therese]] married [[e:ludwig-i-of-bavaria|Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria]] in [[e:munich|Munich]] in October 1810, and the horse race held in her honour became the [[e:oktoberfest|Oktoberfest]]; the Theresienwiese still bears her name.
duchy-of-saxe-hildburghausen.e: After [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg]] died out, the Ernestine lands were redistributed in 1826. [[e:frederick-duke-of-saxe-altenburg|Duke Frederick]] exchanged [[e:hildburghausen|Hildburghausen]] for [[e:altenburg|Altenburg]], becoming Duke of Saxe-Altenburg, and Hildburghausen went to Saxe-[[e:meiningen|Meiningen]].

date-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Date of southern Mutsu, which under the one-eyed Date Masamune briefly dominated northeastern Japan.
date-clan-domain.o: The Date had long held lands in southern [[e:mutsu-province|Mutsu]]. [[e:date-tanemune|Date Tanemune]] issued the detailed [[e:jinkaishu|Jinkai-shu]] law code in 1536, and from 1542 a war with his son [[e:date-harumune|Harumune]] split the clan; Harumune won and in 1548 moved the family seat to [[e:yonezawa|Yonezawa]].
date-clan-domain.r: The Date built power through marriage alliances with neighbouring families across the [[e:tohoku-region|Tohoku]]. [[e:date-masamune|Date Masamune]], who lost an eye to [[e:smallpox|smallpox]] as a child, became head in 1584 and expanded aggressively, defeating the [[e:ashina-clan|Ashina]] at [[e:battle-of-suriagehara|Suriagehara]] in 1589 to take [[e:aizu|Aizu]], briefly controlling much of southern Tohoku.
date-clan-domain.e: [[e:date-masamune|Masamune]] submitted late to [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] in 1590, lost [[e:aizu|Aizu]] and in 1591 was moved to Iwadeyama. Siding with [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] in 1600, he founded the [[s:sendai-domain|Sendai Domain]], which the Date ruled until 1871.

duchy-of-mantua.t: The Gonzaga state of Mantua, whose court commissioned Mantegna, Giulio Romano and Monteverdi before war and plague ruined it.
duchy-of-mantua.o: In 1328 [[e:luigi-i-gonzaga|Luigi Gonzaga]] overthrew the Bonacolsi lords of Mantua and became captain of the people. The [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] ruled as imperial vicars, became marquises in 1433 under [[e:gianfrancesco-i-gonzaga|Gianfrancesco Gonzaga]] and dukes in 1530 under [[e:federico-ii-gonzaga-duke-of-mantua|Federico II]], who also acquired [[e:montferrat|Montferrat]], later the [[s:duchy-of-montferrat|Duchy of Montferrat]].
duchy-of-mantua.r: Mantua's court was among the most brilliant in [[e:italy|Italy]]. [[e:andrea-mantegna|Andrea Mantegna]] painted the [[e:camera-degli-sposi|Camera degli Sposi]] for [[e:ludovico-iii-gonzaga|Ludovico III]]; Isabella d'[[e:house-of-este|Este]] collected art; [[e:giulio-romano|Giulio Romano]] built the [[e:palazzo-te|Palazzo Te]] for [[e:federico-ii-gonzaga-duke-of-mantua|Federico II]]. Under [[e:vincenzo-i-gonzaga|Vincenzo I]], [[e:l-orfeo|Monteverdi's Orfeo]] was staged in 1607. The duchy lived from farming, textiles and the condottiere service of its lords.
duchy-of-mantua.e: The main line died out in 1627, and the [[e:war-of-the-mantuan-succession|War of the Mantuan Succession]] brought an imperial sack in 1630. The [[e:house-of-gonzaga-nevers|Gonzaga-Nevers]] line ruled until [[e:ferdinando-carlo-gonzaga|Ferdinando Carlo]] sided with [[e:france|France]] and was deposed in 1708, when [[e:austria|Austria]] annexed Mantua.

duchy-of-opava.t: Duchy carved out of northern Moravia for a son of King Ottokar II, later ruled by the Liechtensteins and capital of Austrian Silesia until 1918.
duchy-of-opava.o: Around 1269 [[e:ottokar-ii-of-bohemia|King Ottokar II of Bohemia]] gave the [[e:opava|Opava]] region of northern [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] to his illegitimate son Nicholas I. Nicholas's descendants ruled it as a separate duchy, and it gradually came to be counted among the Silesian duchies rather than [[e:moravia|Moravia]], under the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-opava.r: The [[e:opava|Opava]] [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslids]] ruled until the 15th century, after which the duchy passed to the [[e:house-of-podebrady|Poděbrady]] family, the Hungarian king [[e:matthias-corvinus|Matthias Corvinus]] and the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. In 1614 it was granted to [[e:karl-i-prince-of-liechtenstein|Karl I]] of [[s:principality-of-liechtenstein|Liechtenstein]], whose family kept the ducal title. Opava was a town of German and Czech speakers, cloth and trade, and the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]] restored [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] after 1620.
duchy-of-opava.e: In 1742 [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] took the northern part; the rest became the core of [[s:duchy-of-upper-and-lower-silesia|Austrian Silesia]], with [[e:opava|Opava]] as capital, and hosted the [[e:congress-of-troppau|Congress of Troppau]] in 1820. In 1918 it joined [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]] and is now in the [[e:czech-republic|Czech Republic]].

dulafid-dynasty.t: An Arab family of governors who ruled the Jibal region of western Iran for most of the 9th century from their own city, Karaj.
dulafid-dynasty.o: [[e:abu-dulaf|Abu Dulaf al-Qasim ibn Isa]], of the Arab [[e:banu-ijl|Banu Ijl]], was a general and poet in the service of [[e:harun-al-rashid|Harun al-Rashid]] and [[e:al-mamun|al-Ma'mun]]. Around 825 he founded or developed the town of Karaj (Karaj Abi Dulaf, near modern [[e:arak-iran|Arak]], not the city near [[e:tehran|Tehran]]) and governed much of the [[e:jibal|Jibal]] as an Abbasid official.
dulafid-dynasty.r: The Dulafids ruled hereditarily but in the name of the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]], collecting taxes in a rich agricultural and horse-raising region on the route from [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]] to [[e:khorasan|Khurasan]]. [[e:abu-dulaf|Abu Dulaf]] was celebrated as a patron and poet and appears in Arabic literature for his generosity. His descendants, notably [[e:ahmad-ibn-abd-al-aziz-ibn-abi-dulaf|Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz]], fought the [[s:saffarid-dynasty|Saffarids]] and sometimes defied Baghdad.
dulafid-dynasty.e: After internal disputes, the [[e:caliphate|caliph]] [[e:al-mutadid|al-Mu'tadid]] ended Dulafid rule in 897, reabsorbing the [[e:jibal|Jibal]] into direct caliphal administration.

deisi-muman.t: Kingdom of the Déisi in Waterford and south Tipperary, whose legendary migrations reached Wales and whose name survives in the Decies.
deisi-muman.o: The Déisi were a population group whose name means '[[e:vassal|vassals]]'. The early Irish tale The [[e:expulsion-of-the-deisi|Expulsion of the Déisi]] tells how they were driven from [[s:kingdom-of-brega|Brega]] near [[e:hill-of-tara|Tara]] and wandered south, some settling in [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]] and others crossing to [[s:kingdom-of-dyfed|Dyfed]] in [[e:wales|Wales]], where the Kingdom of Dyfed's kings later claimed Déisi descent. In Munster they settled in what is now [[e:county-waterford|County Waterford]] and south [[e:county-tipperary|Tipperary]].
deisi-muman.r: The Déisi Muman were a subject kingdom within the [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Kingdom of Munster]], paying tribute to the [[e:eoganacht-chaisil|Eóganachta of Cashel]]. The monastery of [[e:lismore-county-waterford|Lismore]], founded by St [[e:carthach-of-lismore|Mochuda]] in the 7th century, was one of the great schools of early Ireland and lay in their territory. A northern branch, the Déis Tuaiscirt, later grew into the [[e:dal-cais|Dál Cais]], the dynasty of [[e:brian-boru|Brian Bóruma]].
deisi-muman.e: The [[e:ua-faelain|Ua Fáeláin]], O'Phelan, kings ruled the Déisi in the 11th and 12th centuries. After the [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Normans]] took [[e:waterford|Waterford]] in 1170 their lands were granted to settlers, and the kingdom faded around 1200. The name survives in the baronies of Decies in Waterford.

damnonii.t: People of the Clyde valley recorded by Ptolemy, whose territory was crossed by the Antonine Wall and later formed the heart of Strathclyde.
damnonii.o: The Damnonii appear in Ptolemy's 2nd-century Geography in the region of the [[e:river-clyde|Clyde]], [[e:ayrshire|Ayrshire]] and parts of [[e:stirlingshire|Stirlingshire]], with places such as Vanduara and Alauna listed among their settlements. They derived from the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] communities of west central [[e:scotland|Scotland]], who lived in hillforts, crannogs and enclosed farms.
damnonii.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or institutions. Their land lay on the line of the [[e:antonine-wall|Antonine Wall]], built across the [[e:firth-of-forth|Forth]] and [[e:river-clyde|Clyde]] isthmus from 142, and was occupied by Roman forts during the periods of Roman advance into [[e:scotland|Scotland]]. Their society was otherwise rural and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-based, much like their neighbours.
damnonii.e: After the Roman withdrawal to [[e:hadrians-wall|Hadrian's Wall]] the Damnonii lived beyond the frontier. They are generally regarded as ancestors of the British people of the [[e:river-clyde|Clyde]], whose [[s:kingdom-of-strathclyde|Kingdom of Strathclyde]] was centred on Alt Clut, [[e:dumbarton-rock|Dumbarton Rock]].

derbent-khanate.t: A short-lived khanate based in the ancient fortress city of Derbent, the Caspian gateway between the North Caucasus and Transcaucasia.
derbent-khanate.o: After [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah's]] death in 1747, the Persian governor of [[e:derbent|Derbent]], [[e:muhammad-husayn-khan-of-derbent|Muhammad Husayn Khan]], ruled the walled city and its hinterland as an independent khan. Derbent's Sasanian walls and citadel of [[e:naryn-kala|Naryn-Kala]] still controlled the narrow coastal passage between the mountains and the [[e:caspian-sea|Caspian Sea]].
derbent-khanate.r: The khanate was small but strategically vital, drawing income from customs on the coastal route and from the trade of its port. Its population was mixed, including Azerbaijani, Persian, Tat-speaking Jewish and [[e:lezgins|Lezgin]] communities. Rivalry with neighbouring [[s:kaitag-utsmiyate|Kaitag]] and [[e:quba|Quba]] weakened it, and in 1765 [[e:fatali-khan-of-quba|Fatali Khan]] of the [[s:quba-khanate|Quba Khanate]] seized the city.
derbent-khanate.e: [[e:derbent|Derbent]] remained under [[e:quba|Quba's]] rulers until Russian troops took it in 1796, briefly, and again in 1806, when the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] annexed it permanently. The city's walls and citadel are now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

duchy-of-oldenburg.t: North German duchy, later grand duchy, created by a Danish-Russian exchange and ruled by a branch of the house that also held the Russian throne.
duchy-of-oldenburg.o: The [[s:county-of-oldenburg|County of Oldenburg]] had been ruled by the Danish kings since 1667. In the [[e:treaty-of-tsarskoye-selo-1773|Treaty of Tsarskoye Selo]] of 1773, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] exchanged it with [[e:russia|Russia]] for the [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Gottorp]] share of [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]], and Grand Duke Paul passed it to his relative [[e:frederick-augustus-i-duke-of-oldenburg|Frederick Augustus]], prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]]. In 1774 the emperor raised Oldenburg to a duchy.
duchy-of-oldenburg.r: The dukes of the [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Holstein-Gottorp]] line governed a Lutheran land of marshes, moors and [[e:cattle|cattle]] farming, with the secularised [[s:prince-bishopric-of-lubeck|Principality of Lübeck]] at [[e:eutin|Eutin]] and, from 1817, the [[s:principality-of-birkenfeld|Principality of Birkenfeld]]. [[e:peter-i-grand-duke-of-oldenburg|Peter Frederick Louis]] was a careful administrator. [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] annexed [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] to [[e:france|France]] in 1811, but it was restored in 1813 and became a grand duchy, adopting a constitution in 1849.
duchy-of-oldenburg.e: [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] joined the [[s:north-german-confederation|North German Confederation]] and the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]]. [[e:frederick-augustus-ii-grand-duke-of-oldenburg|Grand Duke Frederick Augustus II]] abdicated in November 1918, and the state became the [[s:free-state-of-oldenburg|Free State of Oldenburg]].

drevlians.t: Forest-dwelling East Slavs west of Kiev who killed Prince Igor in 945 and suffered the ferocious revenge of his widow Olga.
drevlians.o: The Drevlians, the people of the trees, lived in the forests between the [[e:pripyat-river|Pripyat]] and the middle [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]], west of the Polans. They appear in the [[e:primary-chronicle|Primary Chronicle]] as an old tribe with their own princes and their chief town at [[e:korosten|Iskorosten]], modern Korosten in [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]].
drevlians.r: They were farmers, hunters and beekeepers, and the Kievan chronicler, hostile to them, describes them as living in a bestial way. After Oleg subdued them, in 883 according to the chronicle, they paid tribute to [[e:kyiv|Kiev]]. In 945 [[e:igor-svyatoslavich|Prince Igor]] tried to collect a second tribute, and the Drevlians under their prince [[e:mal-of-the-drevlians|Mal]] killed him.
drevlians.e: [[e:igor-of-kiev|Igor]]'s widow [[e:olga-of-kiev|Olga]] took vengeance in 946, burying and burning Drevlian envoys and setting [[e:korosten|Iskorosten]] alight with birds carrying burning tinder. The Drevlian land was then ruled directly from [[e:kyiv|Kiev]], and in 970 [[e:sviatoslav-i-of-kiev|Sviatoslav I]] gave it to his son Oleg. The tribe merged into the population of [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']].

duchy-of-pomerania-stettin.t: The southern Pomeranian duchy created in 1295, centred on the Oder port of Stettin and long contested with Brandenburg.
duchy-of-pomerania-stettin.o: The partition of the [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Duchy of Pomerania]] in 1295 gave Otto I the lands around [[e:szczecin|Stettin]] (Szczecin) on the lower [[e:oder-river|Oder]], while his brother [[e:bogislaw-iv-duke-of-pomerania|Bogislaw IV]] took [[e:pomerania-wolgast|Pomerania-Wolgast]]. Otto's descendants spent much of the 14th and 15th centuries resisting the [[s:margraviate-of-brandenburg|Margraviate of Brandenburg]]'s claims to overlordship and to the succession.
duchy-of-pomerania-stettin.r: [[e:szczecin|Stettin]] was a Hanseatic port exporting grain, [[e:timber|timber]] and herring, and its [[e:burghers|burghers]] often acted independently of the dukes. [[e:bogislaw-x|Bogislaw X]], who reunited all [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]] in 1478, reformed its administration and finances. The [[e:treaty-of-grimnitz|Treaty of Grimnitz]] in 1529 freed the dukes from [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg's]] feudal claims in exchange for a promise of succession, and [[e:pomerania|Pomerania]] adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in 1534.
duchy-of-pomerania-stettin.e: After a new division in 1532, [[e:szczecin|Stettin]] was ruled by a series of dukes who died without heirs. [[e:bogislaw-xiv|Bogislaw XIV]] united both duchies in 1625, but [[e:sweden|Sweden]] occupied [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]] in 1630. On his death in 1637 the [[e:house-of-griffins|Griffin]] line ended, and in 1648 the lands were divided between [[s:swedish-pomerania|Swedish Pomerania]] and [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]].

duchy-of-upper-and-lower-silesia.t: The small part of Silesia that Austria kept after Frederick the Great's conquest, an industrial crown land of the Habsburgs.
duchy-of-upper-and-lower-silesia.o: [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] seized most of [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] in the [[e:war-of-the-austrian-succession|War of the Austrian Succession]], and under the [[e:treaty-of-breslau|Treaty of Breslau]] and the [[e:treaty-of-berlin-1742|Peace of Berlin]] in 1742 [[e:austria|Austria]] kept only a southern strip, including the duchies of [[e:opava|Troppau]], [[e:cieszyn|Teschen]] and part of [[e:krnov|Jägerndorf]]. This remnant was governed as the Duchy of Upper and [[e:lower-silesia|Lower Silesia]], usually called Austrian Silesia.
duchy-of-upper-and-lower-silesia.r: Austrian [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] was administered from [[e:opava|Troppau]] (Opava), joined to [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] from 1782 and from 1849 a separate crown land with its own diet. Its population was German, Czech and Polish, Catholic with Lutheran minorities in [[e:cieszyn|Teschen]]. [[e:coal|Coal]] mining in the [[e:ostrava-karvina-coal-basin|Ostrava-Karviná]] basin and the heavy industry around it made it one of the most industrialised parts of the monarchy.
duchy-of-upper-and-lower-silesia.e: With the collapse of [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] in 1918, the territory was claimed by [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]] and [[e:poland|Poland]]. After a brief war over [[e:cieszyn|Teschen]] in 1919, it was divided in 1920, with most going to [[e:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]].

duchy-of-schleswig.t: Duchy of southern Jutland on the Danish-German border, held by Danish royal princes and Holstein counts and fought over in the 19th-century Schleswig wars.
duchy-of-schleswig.o: [[e:schleswig|Southern Jutland]] was the frontier of the [[s:kingdom-of-denmark|Kingdom of Denmark]], guarded by the [[e:danevirke|Danevirke]] earthworks and home to the [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]] trading town of [[e:hedeby|Hedeby]]. From the 11th century it was governed as a jarldom or duchy by members of the royal family; [[e:canute-lavard|Canute Lavard]] held it from 1115, and the dukes descended from King [[e:abel-king-of-denmark|Abel]] made it a hereditary fief.
duchy-of-schleswig.r: The duchy straddled Danish and German worlds: Danish speech dominated in the north, German and Frisian in the south, and the town of [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] on the [[e:schlei|Schlei]] was its capital. From 1386 the counts of [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] held it, and in 1460 the [[e:treaty-of-ribe|Treaty of Ribe]] made Christian I its duke, promising Schleswig and Holstein would stay forever undivided. [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Gottorp]] Castle became a seat of a ducal line.
duchy-of-schleswig.e: Rising Danish and German nationalism led to the [[e:first-schleswig-war|First Schleswig War]] in 1848-1851 and the Second in 1864, after which [[e:denmark|Denmark]] ceded the duchy to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:austria|Austria]]. Prussia annexed it in 1866-1867. A 1920 plebiscite returned northern [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] to Denmark, while the south remains part of [[e:germany|Germany]].

dujana-state.t: A tiny Pathan Nawabi state in Haryana, granted by the British in 1806 to a cavalry leader who had served them against the Marathas.
dujana-state.o: [[e:abdul-samad-khan-of-dujana|Abdul Samad Khan]], a Pathan soldier, served [[e:gerard-lake-1st-viscount-lake|Lord Lake]] in the [[e:second-anglo-maratha-war|Second Anglo-Maratha War]], and in 1806 the British granted him Dujana and its villages as a hereditary state.
dujana-state.r: The Nawabs governed a very small farming territory under British supervision through the [[e:punjab|Punjab]] government. Little is recorded of its internal history.
dujana-state.e: Dujana acceded to [[e:india|India]] and in 1948 was merged into [[e:east-punjab|East Punjab]]; it lies in [[e:jhajjar|Jhajjar]] district of [[e:haryana|Haryana]].

duchy-of-julich.t: A Rhineland county turned duchy between Aachen and Cologne, whose union with Cleves and Berg created a powerful state and a famous succession crisis.
duchy-of-julich.o: A count named Gerhard appears in the Jülichgau around 1003, and his family built a county around the old Roman town of Jülich west of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]]. The counts fought the archbishops of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] for supremacy in the lower [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]], sharing the victory at [[e:battle-of-worringen|Worringen]] in 1288 with Berg and [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Brabant]].
duchy-of-julich.r: [[e:william-i-duke-of-julich|Count William V]] was made margrave in 1336 and duke in 1356. In 1423 Jülich united with the [[s:duchy-of-berg|Duchy of Berg]], and in 1521 with the [[s:duchy-of-cleves|Duchy of Cleves]] and the County of the Mark, forming the [[s:united-duchies-of-julich-cleves-berg|United Duchies]].
