Duke [[e:william-duke-of-julich-cleves-berg|William the Rich]] built Jülich into an Italian [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] fortress town with a citadel.
duchy-of-julich.e: When the last duke, [[e:john-william-duke-of-julich-cleves-berg|John William]], died in 1609, the [[e:war-of-the-julich-succession|Jülich succession crisis]] between [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] and [[s:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]] nearly sparked a European war. The [[e:treaty-of-xanten|Treaty of Xanten]] in 1614 gave Jülich and Berg to [[e:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]]. [[e:french-revolutionary-occupation-of-the-netherlands|French revolutionary armies]] took Jülich in 1794, and in 1815 it became Prussian.

duchy-of-saxe-gotha.t: Ernestine Saxon duchy in Thuringia whose founder, Ernest the Pious, made it a model of Lutheran school reform and orderly government.
duchy-of-saxe-gotha.o: Saxe-[[e:gotha|Gotha]] was created in 1640 when the Ernestine lands of Saxe-[[e:weimar|Weimar]] were divided among the brothers of the ducal house, and Ernest I received Gotha. He built [[e:friedenstein-palace|Friedenstein Palace]] as his residence. In 1672 he inherited Saxe-[[e:altenburg|Altenburg]], and the state became known as Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg.
duchy-of-saxe-gotha.r: [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-gotha|Ernest the Pious]] introduced compulsory schooling, a famous school method and detailed church and state ordinances, rebuilding a land ruined by the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]]. On his death in 1675 his lands were divided among seven sons, creating the duchies of [[e:coburg|Coburg]], [[e:meiningen|Meiningen]], [[e:romhild|Römhild]], Eisenberg, [[e:hildburghausen|Hildburghausen]] and [[e:saalfeld|Saalfeld]]. [[e:ernest-ii-duke-of-saxe-gotha-altenburg|Ernest II]], in the 18th century, was an [[e:age-of-enlightenment|Enlightenment]] patron of [[e:babylonian-astronomy|astronomy]] who founded the [[e:seeberg-observatory|Seeberg]] observatory.
duchy-of-saxe-gotha.e: The line died out with [[e:frederick-iv-duke-of-saxe-gotha-altenburg|Duke Frederick IV]] in 1825. In the redistribution of 1826 [[e:gotha|Gotha]] went to the [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Duke of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld]], forming the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha]], while [[e:altenburg|Altenburg]] became the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-altenburg|Duchy of Saxe-Altenburg]].

duchy-of-modena-and-reggio.t: The Este duchy that became the family's main state after the loss of Ferrara, lasting until Italian unification in 1859.
duchy-of-modena-and-reggio.o: In 1452 [[e:frederick-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Frederick III]] made [[e:borso-deste|Borso d'Este]] duke of [[e:modena|Modena]] and [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]], imperial fiefs held alongside the papal [[s:duchy-of-ferrara|Duchy of Ferrara]]. When [[e:ferrara|Ferrara]] passed to the [[e:papacy|papacy]] in 1598, [[e:cesare-d-este-duke-of-modena|Cesare d'Este]] moved his court to Modena, which became the capital.
duchy-of-modena-and-reggio.r: The [[e:house-of-este|Este]] rebuilt [[e:modena|Modena]] as a capital, with a ducal palace and the [[e:biblioteca-estense|Biblioteca Estense]], where the scholar [[e:ludovico-antonio-muratori|Ludovico Antonio Muratori]] worked as librarian. The duchy added [[e:mirandola|Mirandola]], [[s:principality-of-correggio|Correggio]] and [[s:county-of-novellara|Novellara]]. After French occupation from 1796, when it joined the [[s:cispadane-republic|Cispadane Republic]], the restored duchy passed in 1814 to [[e:francis-iv-duke-of-modena|Francis IV of Austria-Este]], who ruled harshly and executed the revolutionary [[e:ciro-menotti|Ciro Menotti]] in 1831.
duchy-of-modena-and-reggio.e: Francis V fled after the Austrian defeat in 1859. The duchy joined the [[s:united-provinces-of-central-italy|United Provinces of Central Italy]] and was annexed to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] in 1860.

dutch-ceylon.t: The Dutch East India Company's colony on the coasts of Sri Lanka, run for its cinnamon monopoly and leaving a lasting legal and architectural mark.
dutch-ceylon.o: [[e:rajasinha-ii-of-kandy|Rajasinha II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-kandy|Kingdom of Kandy]] invited the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) to help expel the Portuguese. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] took [[e:batticaloa|Batticaloa]] in 1638, [[e:trincomalee|Trincomalee]] in 1639 and [[e:galle|Galle]] in 1640, then [[e:colombo|Colombo]] in 1656 and [[e:jaffna|Jaffna]] in 1658, but kept the conquered coasts for themselves rather than handing them to [[e:kandy|Kandy]].
dutch-ceylon.r: A governor at [[e:colombo|Colombo]] ruled the maritime provinces, enforcing a strict monopoly on [[e:cinnamon|cinnamon]], the colony's chief product, and also trading elephants, pearls and areca. [[e:roman-dutch-law|Roman-Dutch law]], introduced in this period, still forms the basis of Sri Lankan [[e:civil-law|civil law]]. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] built forts at [[e:galle|Galle]] and [[e:jaffna|Jaffna]], Reformed churches and canals, and a [[e:burghers|Burgher]] community of European descent emerged. Relations with [[e:kandy|Kandy]] alternated between trade and war.
dutch-ceylon.e: During the [[e:french-revolutionary-wars|French Revolutionary Wars]], British forces from [[e:chennai|Madras]] occupied the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] possessions in 1795 to 1796. They were formally ceded by the [[e:treaty-of-amiens|Treaty of Amiens]] in 1802 and became [[s:british-ceylon|British Ceylon]]. [[e:galle-fort|Galle Fort]] is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

durrani-empire.t: The empire founded by Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1747, regarded as the foundation of the modern state of Afghanistan.
durrani-empire.o: After [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah's]] assassination in 1747, [[e:ahmad-shah-abdali|Ahmad Khan Abdali]], commander of his Afghan bodyguard, was chosen as king by a tribal assembly in [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]]. Taking the title Durr-i Durran, 'Pearl of Pearls', he founded the Durrani dynasty of the [[e:sadozai|Sadozai clan]].
durrani-empire.r: [[e:ahmad-shah-abdali|Ahmad Shah]] conquered [[e:herat|Herat]], [[e:kabul|Kabul]], the [[e:punjab|Punjab]], [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] and [[e:sindh|Sindh]], and in 1761 crushed the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] at the [[e:third-battle-of-panipat|Third Battle of Panipat]]. Revenue came from Indian plunder and tribute. [[e:pashtuns|Pashtun]] tribal chiefs held great power, and the state relied on their loyalty. His son [[e:timur|Timur]] Shah moved the capital from [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]] to Kabul in 1776.
durrani-empire.e: Under [[e:timur|Timur's]] sons, rivalry between [[e:zaman-shah-durrani|Shah Zaman]], Shah Mahmud and [[e:shah-shuja-durrani|Shah Shuja]], and the power of the [[e:barakzai-dynasty|Barakzai]] ministers, broke the empire. The [[e:sikhs|Sikhs]] took the [[e:punjab|Punjab]], and by 1823 the Barakzais held [[e:kabul|Kabul]], founding the [[s:emirate-of-afghanistan|Emirate of Afghanistan]], while [[e:sadozai|Sadozais]] kept the [[s:principality-of-herat|Principality of Herat]].

domnonee.t: Breton kingdom of northern Brittany, named after Dumnonia in Britain, whose king Judicael treated with Dagobert I as an equal.
domnonee.o: Migrants from [[s:kingdom-of-dumnonia|Dumnonia]] in south-west [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], the land of modern [[e:devon|Devon]] and [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]], settled the northern coast of [[e:armorica|Armorica]] in the 5th and 6th centuries and gave it the name of their [[e:bantustan|homeland]]. Its early rulers are known mainly from saints' lives, which may preserve legend.
domnonee.r: The kingdom stretched along the [[e:english-channel|Channel]] coast from the [[e:rance|Rance]] to the [[e:morlaix|Morlaix]] area. Its life centred on monastic foundations such as [[e:saint-malo|Saint-Malo]], [[e:dol-de-bretagne|Dol]] and [[e:saint-pol-de-leon|Saint-Pol-de-Léon]], linked to saints from [[e:wales|Wales]] and [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]]. The chronicle of [[e:chronicle-of-fredegar|Fredegar]] records that King [[e:judicael|Judicael]] met [[e:dagobert-i|Dagobert I]] at [[e:clichy|Clichy]] in 636 and made peace with the [[s:franks|Franks]].
domnonee.e: In the 9th century Domnonée was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-brittany|Kingdom of Brittany]] created by [[e:nominoe|Nominoe]] and [[e:erispoe|Erispoe]]. The bishopric of [[e:dol-de-bretagne|Dol]] and the later counties of [[e:penthievre|Penthièvre]] and Léon preserved parts of its territory.

duchy-of-greater-poland.t: The duchy of the Piast heartland around Poznan and Gniezno, which produced Poland's first crowned king after two centuries of division.
duchy-of-greater-poland.o: Under the testament of [[e:boleslaw-iii-wrymouth|Boleslaw III]] in 1138, his son [[e:mieszko-iii-the-old|Mieszko III the Old]] received Greater [[e:poland|Poland]], with [[e:poznan|Poznan]] and [[e:gniezno|Gniezno]], the cradle of the [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] state. For much of the next century the duchy was contested between Mieszko's descendants and was at times divided between Poznan and [[e:kalisz|Kalisz]].
duchy-of-greater-poland.r: Greater [[e:poland|Poland]] was a farming region, settled in the 13th century by German colonists and towns founded under [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] law, such as [[e:poznan|Poznan]] in 1253. Its dukes, especially [[e:wladyslaw-odonic|Wladyslaw Odonic]] and his sons, built up their power with the support of the church of [[e:gniezno|Gniezno]]. Duke [[e:przemysl-ii|Przemysl II]] gained [[e:pomerelia|Pomerelia]] in 1294 and was crowned King of Poland in Gniezno in 1295.
duchy-of-greater-poland.e: [[e:przemysl-ii|Przemysl II]] was murdered in 1296, and the duchy passed to [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high]], [[e:wenceslaus-ii-of-bohemia|Wenceslaus II of Bohemia]] and [[e:henry-iii-of-glogow|Henry of Glogow]]. Wladyslaw I took it back in 1314, and in 1320 it became part of the reunited [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385).

duchies-of-bremen-and-verden.t: Two secularised prince-bishoprics between Elbe and Weser that passed from Sweden to Hanover, controlling the approaches to Bremen and Hamburg.
duchies-of-bremen-and-verden.o: The [[s:prince-archbishopric-of-bremen|Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen]] and the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-verden|Prince-Bishopric of Verden]] had been occupied by [[e:sweden|Sweden]] during the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]]. At the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 they were secularised and granted to the Swedish crown as the duchies of [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] and [[e:verden|Verden]], with the government seated at [[e:stade|Stade]].
duchies-of-bremen-and-verden.r: The duchies kept their estates and Lutheran church while [[e:sweden|Sweden]] used them as a strategic base. The city of [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] resisted Swedish claims and remained an imperial free city. [[e:denmark|Denmark]] occupied the duchies in 1712 during the [[e:great-northern-war|Great Northern War]] and sold them to the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] in 1715, a transfer recognised by Sweden in 1719. Farming in the marshlands and moors was the mainstay.
duchies-of-bremen-and-verden.e: After Napoleonic occupation the lands returned to [[e:hanover|Hanover]] in 1813, a kingdom from 1814. In 1823 they were merged into the [[e:stade|Stade]] administrative region, ending the duchies as distinct units; the area passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1866.

duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria.t: The Norman duchy of Robert Guiscard, which drove the Byzantines out of southern Italy and laid the groundwork for the Kingdom of Sicily.
duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria.o: Norman [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] in Byzantine [[e:apulia|Apulia]] elected [[e:william-iron-arm|William Iron Arm]] as their count at [[e:melfi|Melfi]] around 1042–1043. After his brothers [[e:drogo-of-hauteville|Drogo]] and [[e:humphrey-of-hauteville|Humphrey]], their half-brother [[e:robert-guiscard|Robert Guiscard]] took over in 1057, and in 1059 Pope [[e:nicholas-ii|Nicholas II]] invested him at Melfi as duke of Apulia, [[e:calabria|Calabria]] and, in prospect, [[e:sicily|Sicily]], making the [[e:papacy|papacy]] the duchy's overlord.
duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria.r: [[e:robert-guiscard|Guiscard]] captured [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]] in 1071, ending Byzantine rule in [[e:italy|Italy]], and [[s:principality-of-salerno|Salerno]] in 1077, which became his capital. The duchy ruled Greek-speaking [[e:calabria|Calabria]] and [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] and [[e:latin|Latin]] [[e:apulia|Apulia]], keeping Byzantine officials and Greek monasteries alongside Latin [[e:bishop|bishops]]. Its army also invaded the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]] across the Adriatic in 1081, and in 1084 sacked [[e:rome|Rome]] while rescuing [[e:pope-gregory-vii|Pope Gregory VII]].
duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria.e: After [[e:robert-guiscard|Guiscard]]'s death in 1085, his son [[e:roger-borsa|Roger Borsa]] and grandson [[e:william-ii-duke-of-apulia|William II]] struggled to control rebellious barons. When William died childless in 1127, his cousin [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]] of the [[s:county-of-sicily|County of Sicily]] claimed the duchy, and in 1130 merged it into the new [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]].

despotate-of-arta.t: Albanian despotate in southern Epirus, ruled by the Losha and Shpata clans from Arta until Carlo Tocco took the city in 1416.
despotate-of-arta.o: In 1358–1359 Albanian clans defeated [[e:nikephoros-ii-orsini|Nikephoros II Orsini]], the last Orsini despot, and divided southern [[e:epirus|Epirus]]. [[e:peter-losha|Peter Losha]] took Arta and was recognised as despot by [[e:simeon-uros|Simeon Uroš]], the Serbian ruler of [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]]; [[e:gjin-bua-shpata|Gjin Bua Shpata]] held the [[s:despotate-of-angelokastron-and-lepanto|Despotate of Angelokastron and Lepanto]] to the south.
despotate-of-arta.r: The despots relied on Albanian clans who had moved into [[e:epirus|Epirus]], ruling a Greek town population around Arta. They fought the Serbian rulers of [[e:ioannina|Ioannina]], notably [[e:thomas-preljubovic|Thomas Preljubović]], and later [[e:esau-de-buondelmonti|Esau de' Buondelmonti]]. After Losha's death in 1374 [[e:gjin-bua-shpata|Gjin Bua Shpata]] ruled both despotates until 1399, followed by [[e:muriq-shpata|Muriq Shpata]] and [[e:yaqub-shpata|Yaqub Shpata]], who allied with the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].
despotate-of-arta.e: [[e:yaqub-shpata|Yaqub Shpata]] was killed in 1416, and [[e:carlo-i-tocco|Carlo I Tocco]], ruler of [[e:ioannina|Ioannina]], captured Arta. The city was taken by the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] in 1449.

democratic-republic-of-afghanistan.t: The communist state of Afghanistan, whose radical reforms and the Soviet invasion of 1979 ignited decades of war.
democratic-republic-of-afghanistan.o: The [[e:peoples-democratic-party-of-afghanistan|People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan]] seized power in the [[e:saur-revolution|Saur Revolution]] of April 1978, killing President [[e:mohammad-daoud-khan|Daoud Khan]] of the [[s:republic-of-afghanistan-1973-1978|Republic of Afghanistan]] (1973-1978). [[e:nur-muhammad-taraki|Nur Muhammad Taraki]] of the [[e:khalq|Khalq]] faction became head of state.
democratic-republic-of-afghanistan.r: Radical land reform, literacy and marriage decrees and the repression of clergy and opponents provoked uprisings. [[e:hafizullah-amin|Hafizullah Amin]] killed [[e:nur-muhammad-taraki|Taraki]] in 1979, and in December the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] invaded, killing Amin and installing [[e:babrak-karmal|Babrak Karmal]] of the [[e:parcham|Parcham]] faction. A war against the mujahideen, backed by [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]], the [[s:united-states|United States]] and [[s:saudi-arabia|Saudi Arabia]], killed perhaps a million [[e:afghans|Afghans]] and drove some five million into exile. [[e:mohammad-najibullah|Mohammad Najibullah]], leader from 1986, pursued 'national reconciliation' and renamed the state [[s:republic-of-afghanistan-1973-1978|Republic of Afghanistan]] in 1987.
democratic-republic-of-afghanistan.e: Soviet troops withdrew by February 1989, but the government survived until Soviet aid ended. In April 1992 mujahideen forces entered [[e:kabul|Kabul]], and the [[s:islamic-state-of-afghanistan|Islamic State of Afghanistan]] was proclaimed.

dutch-mauritius.t: The Dutch East India Company's settlement on Mauritius, which introduced sugar cane and saw the extinction of the dodo.
dutch-mauritius.o: [[e:dutch|Dutch]] sailors named [[e:mauritius|Mauritius]] after Prince [[e:maurice-prince-of-orange|Maurice of Nassau]] in 1598, and in 1638 the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) founded [[e:fort-frederik-hendrik|Fort Frederik Hendrik]] at [[e:grand-port|Grand Port]] to forestall French and English rivals. The first commander was [[e:cornelis-gooyer|Cornelis Gooyer]].
dutch-mauritius.r: The small settlement exported [[e:ebony|ebony]], cut from the island's forests, and served as a supply base for ships bound for the [[e:east-indies|East Indies]]. Enslaved people were brought from [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]] and the East Indies, and the colonists introduced [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] cane, deer and pigs. Hunting and introduced animals contributed to the extinction of the dodo, last reliably seen in 1662.
dutch-mauritius.e: The colony was abandoned in 1658, reoccupied in 1664 and finally abandoned in 1710 after cyclones, droughts and losses. [[e:france|France]] claimed the empty island in 1715 as [[s:isle-de-france|Isle de France]].

dominion-of-pakistan.t: Pakistan's first form as an independent state, a dominion of the British Commonwealth in two wings separated by a thousand miles of India.
dominion-of-pakistan.o: The demand for a separate [[e:bantustan|homeland]] for Muslims, adopted by the [[e:all-india-muslim-league|All-India Muslim League]] in the [[e:lahore-resolution|Lahore Resolution]] of 1940, led to the partition of the [[s:british-raj|British Raj]]. On 14 August 1947 the [[e:dominion|Dominion]] of [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] came into being, with [[e:muhammad-ali-jinnah|Muhammad Ali Jinnah]] as Governor-General and [[e:karachi|Karachi]] as capital, comprising [[e:west-pakistan|West Pakistan]] and [[s:bangladesh|East Bengal]].
dominion-of-pakistan.r: The new state faced the upheaval of partition, with millions of refugees and massacres, and war with the [[s:dominion-of-india|Dominion of India]] over [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] in 1947 to 1948. [[e:muhammad-ali-jinnah|Jinnah]] died in 1948 and prime minister [[e:liaquat-ali-khan|Liaquat Ali Khan]] was assassinated in 1951. The [[e:objectives-resolution|Objectives Resolution]] of 1949 set Islamic principles for a constitution, while the Bengali Language Movement of 1952 exposed tensions between the two wings.
dominion-of-pakistan.e: After years of constitutional deadlock and the dismissal of the Constituent Assembly in 1954, a constitution was adopted on 23 March 1956, declaring the [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Islamic Republic of Pakistan]] and ending dominion status.

duchy-of-brzesc-kujawski.t: The small Kuyavian duchy of Wladyslaw the Elbow-high, the starting point of the duke who reunited Poland in 1320.
duchy-of-brzesc-kujawski.o: When [[e:casimir-i-of-kuyavia|Casimir I of Kuyavia]] died in 1267, his sons divided the [[s:duchy-of-kuyavia|Duchy of Kuyavia]], and the southern part around Brzesc Kujawski went to the young [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw]] and his brother Casimir. Wladyslaw, nicknamed the Elbow-high for his small stature, was born nearby around 1260.
duchy-of-brzesc-kujawski.r: Brzesc was a modest farming land on the [[e:vistula|Vistula]] plain, bordered by the [[s:state-of-the-teutonic-order|State of the Teutonic Order]]. From this small base [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I]] gathered further duchies, including [[s:duchy-of-sieradz|Sieradz]] and [[s:duchy-of-leczyca|Leczyca]], and after long struggles with Bohemian and Silesian rivals he was crowned King of [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1320.
duchy-of-brzesc-kujawski.e: After 1320 the duchy merged into the reunited [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385). In 1332 the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Knights]] occupied [[e:kuyavia|Kuyavia]] during their war with [[e:poland|Poland]], and it was returned to the Polish Crown by the [[e:treaty-of-kalisz-1343|Treaty of Kalisz]] in 1343.

duchy-of-lorraine.t: The duchy between France and the Empire, ruled for seven centuries by one dynasty from Nancy before passing to France in 1766.
duchy-of-lorraine.o: [[e:lorraine|Lorraine]] grew from the Duchy of Upper Lorraine, created in 959 when the [[s:duchy-of-lotharingia|Duchy of Lotharingia]] was divided. In 1048 Emperor [[e:henry-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Henry III]] gave it to [[e:gerard-of-alsace|Gerard of Alsace]], whose descendants ruled until 1737. The dukes settled on [[e:nancy|Nancy]] as their capital and held their lands as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
duchy-of-lorraine.r: The duchy was bilingual, French in the west and German in the east, and surrounded by the bishoprics of [[e:metz|Metz]], [[e:toul|Toul]] and [[e:verdun|Verdun]]. [[e:rene-ii-duke-of-lorraine|René II]] defeated and killed [[e:charles-the-bold|Charles the Bold]] before [[e:nancy|Nancy]] in 1477. The [[e:house-of-guise|Guise]] branch led the [[e:catholic-league|Catholic League]] in [[e:france|France]], and Nancy's [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] and baroque palaces reflected a brilliant court.
duchy-of-lorraine.e: [[e:france|France]] occupied [[e:lorraine|Lorraine]] repeatedly in the 17th century; Duke Leopold recovered it in 1697. In 1737 [[e:francis-i-holy-roman-emperor|Francis Stephen]] exchanged it for [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]], and the deposed Polish king [[e:stanislaw-leszczynski|Stanisław Leszczyński]] ruled it for life. On his death in 1766 it was annexed to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

duchy-of-brabant.t: The duchy of Brussels, Leuven and Antwerp, famous for its charter of liberties, the Joyous Entry, and the economic heart of the Low Countries.
duchy-of-brabant.o: The counts of [[e:leuven|Louvain]] had held the title of duke of [[e:duchy-of-lower-lorraine|Lower Lorraine]] since 1106. Around 1183 Henry I began styling himself duke of Brabant, and after the [[e:diet-of-schwabisch-hall|Diet of Schwäbisch Hall]] in 1190 the [[s:county-of-louvain|County of Louvain]] and its neighbouring lands formed the Duchy of Brabant.
duchy-of-brabant.r: Brabant's dukes ruled with powerful towns: [[e:brussels|Brussels]], [[s:county-of-louvain|Leuven]], [[e:antwerp|Antwerp]] and [[e:s-hertogenbosch|'s-Hertogenbosch]]. John I won [[s:duchy-of-limburg|Limburg]] at [[e:battle-of-worringen|Worringen]] in 1288. The [[e:joyous-entry-of-1356|Joyous Entry of 1356]] bound Duchess [[e:joanna-duchess-of-brabant|Joanna]] to respect the estates' rights, a charter sworn by every later ruler. Cloth, then Antwerp's world trade in the 16th century, made Brabant the richest part of the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]].
duchy-of-brabant.e: Brabant passed to [[e:philip-the-good|Philip the Good]] in 1430 and joined the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]], then the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]]. The [[e:dutch-revolt|Dutch Revolt]] split it: the north went to the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]] in 1648, the south stayed in the [[s:spanish-netherlands|Spanish Netherlands]] and [[s:austrian-netherlands|Austrian Netherlands]], rose in the [[e:brabant-revolution|Brabant Revolution]] of 1789, and was annexed by [[e:france|France]] in 1795.

duchy-of-rome.t: Byzantine district around Rome in which the popes gradually took over government, the seed of the Papal States.
duchy-of-rome.o: After the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] invasion, the territory around [[e:rome|Rome]] remained in Byzantine hands, cut off from [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] by Lombard [[e:spoleto|Spoleto]]. A duke (dux) commanded its garrison under the exarch of Ravenna. From the pontificate of [[e:pope-gregory-i|Gregory the Great]] (590–604), who organised Rome's food supply and defence, the popes became the area's real leaders.
duchy-of-rome.r: The duke led the local militia while the pope administered the vast Church estates, fed the city and negotiated with the [[e:lombards|Lombards]]. A local military aristocracy grew powerful. Disputes with [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] over doctrine and taxation, especially [[e:byzantine-iconoclasm|Iconoclasm]] under [[e:leo-iii-the-isaurian|Leo III]], loosened ties to the empire. King [[e:liutprand-king-of-the-lombards|Liutprand]]'s gift of [[e:sutri|Sutri]] to the pope in 728 was its first territorial grant.
duchy-of-rome.e: When the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombards]] took [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]] in 751 and threatened [[e:rome|Rome]], [[e:pope-stephen-ii|Pope Stephen II]] crossed the [[e:alps|Alps]] and gained the protection of [[e:pepin-the-short|Pepin the Short]] in 754. Pepin's donation of 756 created the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], into which the duchy was absorbed.

duchy-of-bohemia.t: The Czech duchy of the Přemyslid dynasty, home of Saint Wenceslas, which grew from Prague into a strong state and a kingdom of the Empire.
duchy-of-bohemia.o: [[e:borivoj-i-duke-of-bohemia|Bořivoj I]], the first historically attested [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]], was baptised around 870, probably by [[e:cyril-and-methodius|Methodius]], while under Great Moravian overlordship. After [[s:great-moravia|Great Moravia]] fell, the Přemyslids of [[e:prague|Prague]] unified the Bohemian tribes. In 895 they sought East Frankish protection, and [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] became tied to the German kingdom.
duchy-of-bohemia.r: Dukes ruled from [[e:prague-castle|Prague Castle]] through a network of castle districts. [[e:wenceslaus-i-duke-of-bohemia|Wenceslas]], murdered by his brother [[e:boleslaus-i-of-bohemia|Boleslaus I]] in 935, became the country's patron saint. Boleslaus II founded the bishopric of [[e:prague|Prague]] in 973. Dukes were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the German kings, while [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]], [[e:silver|silver]] and later colonisation shaped the economy.
duchy-of-bohemia.e: [[e:vratislaus-ii-of-bohemia|Vratislaus II]] received a personal royal title in 1085 and [[e:vladislaus-ii-of-bohemia|Vladislaus II]] in 1158. In 1198 [[e:ottokar-i-of-bohemia|Ottokar I]] secured a hereditary royal crown, confirmed by the [[e:golden-bull-of-sicily|Golden Bull of Sicily]] in 1212, and the duchy became the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]], a leading state of the Empire.

duchy-of-saxe-merseburg.t: Albertine Saxon secondary duchy on the Saale, created by an elector's will and absorbed back into the Electorate after eighty years.
duchy-of-saxe-merseburg.o: [[e:john-george-i-elector-of-saxony|Elector John George]] I of [[e:saxony|Saxony]] divided parts of his lands in his will among his younger sons. After his death in 1656, [[e:christian-i-duke-of-saxe-merseburg|Christian I]] received [[e:merseburg|Merseburg]], the secularised bishopric and its district, founding the Duchy of [[e:saxe-merseburg|Saxe-Merseburg]], which also held parts of [[e:lusatia|Lusatia]].
duchy-of-saxe-merseburg.r: The dukes held their lands as secundogenitures under the [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] of the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]], with limited independence in foreign affairs. They rebuilt [[e:merseburg|Merseburg]] Castle and maintained a court with music and a library. The duchy was Lutheran and agrarian. Its later dukes were known more for extravagance than for policy; [[e:maurice-william-duke-of-saxe-merseburg|Maurice William]] was nicknamed the Fiddle Duke.
duchy-of-saxe-merseburg.e: Heinrich, the last duke, died without heirs in 1738, and the territory reverted to the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]. [[e:merseburg|Merseburg]] passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815 and is now in [[e:saxony-anhalt|Saxony-Anhalt]].

duchy-of-plock.t: The northern Masovian duchy around the old Piast city of Plock, a Polish vassal until its incorporation in 1495.
duchy-of-plock.o: In 1275 the [[s:duchy-of-masovia|Duchy of Masovia]] was split, and the part centred on Plock, an early [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] capital and bishopric on the [[e:vistula|Vistula]], went to [[e:boleslaw-ii-of-masovia|Boleslaw II of Masovia]]. For two centuries Plock was sometimes reunited with the rest of [[e:masovia|Masovia]] and sometimes ruled as a separate duchy.
duchy-of-plock.r: Plock was an old episcopal city with a Romanesque cathedral containing [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] tombs. Its dukes balanced between [[e:poland|Poland]], [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]]: [[e:wenceslaus-of-plock|Wenceslaus of Plock]] did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|John of Bohemia]] in 1329. From 1351 the Masovian dukes were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Polish Crown.
duchy-of-plock.e: The last duke of Plock, [[e:janusz-ii-of-plock|Janusz II]], died in 1495, and [[e:john-i-albert|King John I Albert]] incorporated the duchy into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569). The rest of [[e:masovia|Masovia]] followed in 1526.

demak-sultanate.t: The first Muslim sultanate of Java, founded by Raden Patah on the north coast, which replaced Majapahit as the island's leading power.
demak-sultanate.o: Demak was a port on the north coast of [[e:central-java|Central Java]]. In the late 15th century its ruler [[e:raden-patah|Raden Patah]], described in Javanese tradition as a son of the last [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]] king and a Chinese mother, threw off Majapahit's overlordship. Supported by the [[e:wali-songo|Wali Songo]], the nine saints, he made Demak the centre of a coalition of Muslim coastal states.
demak-sultanate.r: [[e:great-mosque-of-demak|Demak's Great Mosque]], whose pillars are said to have been made by the saints themselves, became the holiest site in [[e:java|Java]]. [[e:pati-unus|Pati Unus]] led fleets against [[s:portuguese-malacca|Portuguese Malacca]] in 1513. [[e:trenggana|Sultan Trenggana]] expanded inland and west, taking [[e:sunda-kelapa|Sunda Kalapa]] from the [[s:sunda-kingdom|Sunda Kingdom]] in 1527 and conquering much of [[e:east-java|East Java]].
demak-sultanate.e: [[e:trenggana|Trenggana]] died during a campaign at [[e:panarukan|Panarukan]] in 1546, and a succession war followed in which [[e:arya-penangsang|Arya Penangsang]] killed rival princes. [[e:hadiwijaya|Hadiwijaya of Pajang]] defeated him and moved power inland, founding the [[s:pajang-sultanate|Pajang Sultanate]].

duchy-of-saxe-weimar.t: An Ernestine Saxon duchy centred on Weimar, forerunner of the Goethe-era duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach.
duchy-of-saxe-weimar.o: The [[e:house-of-wettin|Ernestine Wettins]], who lost the electorate in 1547, kept lands in [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] that were repeatedly divided. The [[e:erfurt-division|Erfurt Division]] of 1572 gave [[e:frederick-william-i-duke-of-saxe-weimar|Duke Frederick William I]] the lands around [[e:weimar|Weimar]], while his cousins received [[e:coburg|Coburg]] and [[e:eisenach|Eisenach]].
duchy-of-saxe-weimar.r: [[e:weimar|Weimar's]] Lutheran dukes ruled a farming territory with the university of [[e:jena|Jena]] nearby. The duchy was repeatedly divided among brothers, and in 1640 the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Duchy of Saxe-Gotha]] split off, while [[e:bernhard-of-saxe-weimar|Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar]] became a famous Protestant general in the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]]. [[e:johann-sebastian-bach|Johann Sebastian Bach]] served as court organist and concertmaster at Weimar from 1708 to 1717.
duchy-of-saxe-weimar.e: When the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-eisenach|Duchy of Saxe-Eisenach]]'s line died out in 1741, [[e:ernest-augustus-i-duke-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|Duke Ernest Augustus]] I united the two as the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|Duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach]]. Under Duchess [[e:anna-amalia-of-brunswick-wolfenbuttel|Anna Amalia]] and [[e:charles-augustus-grand-duke-of-saxe-weimar-eisenach|Charles Augustus]] the united duchy became the home of [[e:johann-wolfgang-von-goethe|Goethe]] and [[e:friedrich-schiller|Schiller]].

ditadura-nacional.t: The military dictatorship that ended Portugal's First Republic and brought António de Oliveira Salazar to power.
ditadura-nacional.o: On 28 May 1926 a military coup launched from [[e:bracara-augusta|Braga]] by General [[e:manuel-gomes-da-costa|Manuel Gomes da Costa]] overthrew the [[s:first-portuguese-republic|First Portuguese Republic]]. Within weeks Gomes da Costa was pushed aside by General [[e:oscar-carmona|Óscar Carmona]], who became president.
ditadura-nacional.r: The military regime dissolved parliament, introduced censorship and repressed several revolts. Unable to solve the financial crisis, it appointed the [[e:coimbra|Coimbra]] economics professor [[e:antonio-de-oliveira-salazar|António de Oliveira Salazar]] as finance minister in 1928, with control over all spending. He balanced the budget and steadily accumulated power, becoming prime minister in 1932.
ditadura-nacional.e: A new constitution, approved by plebiscite in 1933, transformed the military dictatorship into [[e:antonio-de-oliveira-salazar|Salazar]]'s civilian, corporatist [[s:estado-novo-portugal|Estado Novo (Portugal)]], with [[e:oscar-carmona|Carmona]] remaining president.

cr.a: Original: Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro Vector: Vítor Luís Rodrigues, António Martins-Tuválkin

dongye.t: An early people of Korea's east coast, noted in Chinese records for clan territories, a sky-worship festival and fine bows and small horses.
dongye.o: Dongye occupied the eastern coast of the peninsula, roughly modern [[e:gangwon-province|Gangwon]] and southern [[e:hamgyong-province|Hamgyong]]. After 108 BCE it came under the Han commandery of [[e:lintun-commandery|Lintun]], later folded into [[e:lelang-commandery|Lelang]], and Chinese sources treat its people as kin of [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] in language and custom.
dongye.r: There was no king; local chiefs ruled, and each clan's hills and rivers were bounded so that trespassers paid fines in slaves or [[e:cattle|cattle]]. Marriage within the clan was forbidden. In the tenth month people held the mucheon festival, dancing in worship of heaven, and they revered the tiger. Dongye was known for its bows of sandalwood, sea-leopard skins and a breed of small horses.
dongye.e: Dongye fell under [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] control during the 2nd to 4th centuries and was fully absorbed by about 400. Its southern areas later passed to [[s:silla|Silla]].

duchy-of-spoleto.t: Powerful Lombard duchy of central Italy whose later dukes, Guy and Lambert, became kings of Italy and emperors in the 9th century.
duchy-of-spoleto.o: [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] warriors under [[e:faroald-i-of-spoleto|Faroald I]] took [[e:spoleto|Spoleto]] in the Umbrian [[e:apennines|Apennines]] around 570, cutting the Byzantine route between [[e:rome|Rome]] and [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]]. The duchy grew into a large territory covering much of [[e:umbria|Umbria]], the [[e:marche|Marche]] and [[e:abruzzo|Abruzzo]], largely independent of the kings in [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]].
duchy-of-spoleto.r: The dukes of [[e:spoleto|Spoleto]] acted like rulers in their own right, waging war on the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] and sometimes defying the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] kings; Transamund II was deposed by [[e:liutprand-king-of-the-lombards|Liutprand]]. After 774 it passed to Frankish dukes but kept its weight. [[e:guy-iii-of-spoleto|Guy of Spoleto]] was crowned King of [[e:italy|Italy]] in 889 and emperor in 891, and his son [[e:lambert-of-italy|Lambert]] also became emperor. The town's Romanesque churches reflect its medieval wealth.
duchy-of-spoleto.e: In the 10th to 12th centuries the duchy was often held with [[e:camerino|Camerino]] or [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]] by imperial appointees. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] sacked [[e:spoleto|Spoleto]] in 1155. In 1198 [[e:pope-innocent-iii|Pope Innocent III]] took the duchy into the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], where it remained until 1860.

duchy-of-milan.t: Northern Italy's richest state under the Visconti and Sforza, scene of Leonardo's Last Supper, and later a prize held by Spain and Austria.
duchy-of-milan.o: In 1395 [[e:gian-galeazzo-visconti|Gian Galeazzo Visconti]] bought the title of duke from [[e:wenceslaus-iv-of-bohemia|Emperor Wenceslas]], turning the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]] into an imperial duchy. Gian Galeazzo expanded it far into central [[e:italy|Italy]] before his sudden death in 1402.
duchy-of-milan.r: After the last Visconti, [[e:filippo-maria-visconti|Filippo Maria]], died in 1447 and the [[s:golden-ambrosian-republic|Golden Ambrosian Republic]] failed, the condottiere [[e:francesco-sforza|Francesco Sforza]] became duke in 1450. [[e:milan|Milan]] was a centre of arms making, [[e:silk|silk]] and wool, with a strong bureaucracy. [[e:ludovico-sforza|Ludovico Sforza]] employed [[e:leonardo-da-vinci|Leonardo da Vinci]], who painted the [[e:the-last-supper-leonardo|Last Supper]]. [[e:france|France]] invaded in 1499; after the last [[e:house-of-sforza|Sforza]] died in 1535 [[s:habsburg-spain|Habsburg Spain]] ruled through governors, followed by [[e:austria|Austria]] from 1714, whose reforms suited thinkers such as [[e:cesare-beccaria|Cesare Beccaria]].
duchy-of-milan.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] army entered [[e:milan|Milan]] in 1796, and the duchy was replaced by the [[s:transpadane-republic|Transpadane Republic]] and then in 1797 the [[s:cisalpine-republic|Cisalpine Republic]]. [[e:austria|Austria]] later ruled [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] as part of the [[s:kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia|Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia]].

cr.a: F l a n k e r

duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.t: The Ascanian duchy on the middle Elbe that won the Saxon electoral vote in 1356 and became the core of the Electorate of Saxony.
duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.o: After the fall of [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] in 1180, the [[e:saxons|Saxon]] ducal title passed to the [[e:bernhard-duke-of-saxony|Ascanian Bernhard]] of [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]], whose heirs held lands around [[e:wittenberg|Wittenberg]] on the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and around [[s:duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg|Lauenburg]] in the north. In 1296 the inheritance was partitioned: [[e:albert-ii-duke-of-saxony|Albert II]] kept Wittenberg, while his nephews received the Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg.
duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.r: The duchy was small, but its Ascanian dukes claimed the full dignity of the old [[s:duchy-of-saxony|Duchy of Saxony]], including the office of imperial arch-marshal and a vote in royal elections, which [[s:duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg|Lauenburg]] disputed. [[e:rudolf-i-duke-of-saxe-wittenberg|Rudolf I]] was a close ally of [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]]. The territory was agrarian, with [[e:wittenberg|Wittenberg]] a modest residence town at an important [[e:elbe|Elbe]] crossing.
duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.e: The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] settled the dispute in [[e:wittenberg|Wittenberg's]] favour, recognising [[e:rudolf-i-duke-of-saxe-wittenberg|Rudolf I]] as prince-elector and creating the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]. When the Ascanian line died out in 1422, the electorate passed to the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettin]] margraves of [[e:meissen|Meissen]].

duchy-of-masovia.t: The long-lived duchy of central Poland whose duke invited the Teutonic Knights and whose town of Warsaw became Poland's capital.
duchy-of-masovia.o: [[e:masovia|Masovia]], on the middle [[e:vistula|Vistula]] with its centre at [[s:duchy-of-plock|Plock]], was given to [[e:boleslaw-iv-the-curly|Boleslaw IV the Curly]] under the testament of [[e:boleslaw-iii-wrymouth|Boleslaw III]] in 1138. From 1199 it was held by [[e:konrad-i-of-masovia|Konrad I]] and his descendants, a branch of the [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]] that ruled it for over three centuries.
duchy-of-masovia.r: Exposed to raids by the pagan [[e:old-prussians|Prussians]] and [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]], [[e:konrad-i-of-masovia|Konrad I]] invited the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] in 1226 and gave it the land of [[e:chelmno-land|Chelmno]], a decision with lasting consequences. [[e:masovia|Masovia]] was a poor, heavily forested land with a large petty nobility. Its dukes often divided it into smaller duchies such as [[s:duchy-of-plock|Plock]] and Rawa, and from 1351 they were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Polish king.
duchy-of-masovia.e: [[e:janusz-i-of-warsaw|Janusz I]] made [[e:warsaw|Warsaw]] his main seat in the early 15th century. When the last dukes, [[e:stanislaw-of-masovia|Stanislaw]] and [[e:janusz-iii-of-masovia|Janusz III]], died young in 1524 and 1526, [[e:masovia|Masovia]] was incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569), and Warsaw became the royal capital in 1596.

danish-west-indies.t: Denmark's Caribbean sugar colony of St Thomas, St John and St Croix, built on slave labour and sold to the United States in 1917.
danish-west-indies.o: The [[e:danish-west-india-and-guinea-company|Danish West India Company]] settled [[e:saint-thomas-u-s-virgin-islands|St Thomas]] in 1672 and [[e:saint-john-u-s-virgin-islands|St John]] in 1718, and bought [[e:saint-croix|St Croix]] from [[e:france|France]] in 1733. [[e:charlotte-amalie|Charlotte Amalie]] on St Thomas, with its excellent harbour, became the capital and a busy free port.
danish-west-indies.r: [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]] plantations worked by enslaved Africans made the islands profitable; at their peak most of the population was enslaved. An uprising on [[e:saint-john-u-s-virgin-islands|St John]] in 1733 was crushed with French help. In 1848, facing a revolt on [[e:saint-croix|St Croix]], Governor-General [[e:peter-von-scholten|Peter von Scholten]] declared emancipation. [[e:charlotte-amalie|Charlotte Amalie]] thrived as a trading and coaling port where English and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] [[e:criollo-people|creole]] were widely spoken.
danish-west-indies.e: After [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] declined, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] sought to sell the islands. During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] the [[s:united-states|United States]], worried about German naval bases, bought them for 25 million dollars, and they were transferred in 1917, becoming the [[s:united-states-virgin-islands|United States Virgin Islands]].

duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.t: The richest of the late medieval Bavarian duchies, ruled from Landshut by the 'Rich Dukes' and famed for the Landshut Wedding of 1475.
duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.o: In 1392 the three sons of [[e:stephen-ii-duke-of-bavaria|Duke Stephen II]] divided [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]: Frederick took [[e:bavaria-landshut|Bavaria-Landshut]], [[e:john-ii-duke-of-bavaria|John II]] the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-munich|Duchy of Bavaria-Munich]] and [[e:stephen-iii-duke-of-bavaria|Stephen III]] the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-ingolstadt|Duchy of Bavaria-Ingolstadt]]. [[e:landshut|Landshut]], seat of the Lower Bavarian dukes since the 13th century, became capital of the wealthiest share, which gained part of the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-straubing|Duchy of Bavaria-Straubing]] in 1429 and all of [[e:ingolstadt|Ingolstadt]] in 1447.
duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.r: Three successive dukes, [[e:henry-xvi-duke-of-bavaria|Henry XVI]], [[e:louis-ix-duke-of-bavaria|Louis IX]] and George, were known as the Rich for the treasure they amassed from [[e:silver|silver]], salt tolls and strict financial administration, kept in [[e:trausnitz-castle|Trausnitz]] castle and the fortress of [[e:burghausen|Burghausen]]. Louis IX founded the [[e:university-of-ingolstadt|University of Ingolstadt]] in 1472, and the wedding of George to [[e:hedwig-jagiellon-duchess-of-bavaria|Hedwig Jagiellon]] in 1475 was among the most lavish festivals of the age.
duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.e: George died in 1503 without sons, leaving his lands to his son-in-law [[e:rupert-of-germany|Rupert of the Palatinate]] in breach of [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] house law. The [[e:war-of-the-landshut-succession|War of the Landshut Succession]] of 1503 to 1505 gave most lands to [[e:albert-iv-duke-of-bavaria|Albert IV of Bavaria-Munich]], while [[s:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]] was created for Rupert's sons.

deciates.t: Ligurian people near Antibes whose attacks on Greek colonies brought the first Roman army into southern Gaul in 154 BCE.
deciates.o: The Deciates were a Ligurian people living in the hills behind [[e:antibes|Antipolis]] (Antibes), a colony of [[s:massalia|Massalia]]. [[e:polybius|Polybius]] is the main source.
deciates.r: Like other Ligurian peoples of the coast they lived in fortified hilltop settlements and combined farming and herding with raids on the Greek coastal towns.
deciates.e: In 154 BCE the Deciates and the [[s:oxybii|Oxybii]] besieged [[e:antibes|Antipolis]] and [[e:nice|Nikaia]], and [[s:massalia|Massalia]] appealed to the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]]. The consul [[e:quintus-opimius|Quintus Opimius]] defeated them and handed part of their land to Massalia. Their territory later lay within the Roman province of [[e:gallia-narbonensis|Gallia Narbonensis]].

denmark-norway.t: The Oldenburg kings' twin realm of Denmark and Norway, a Lutheran absolute monarchy with colonies from India to the Caribbean, lasting until 1814.
denmark-norway.o: After [[e:sweden|Sweden]] left the [[s:kalmar-union|Kalmar Union]] in 1523, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] and [[e:norway|Norway]] remained under one king, Frederick I. His son [[e:christian-iii-of-denmark|Christian III]] introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]] in 1536 and declared Norway a province of the Danish crown in 1537, though it kept its own laws. The realm also included [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]], the [[e:faroe-islands|Faroes]], [[e:greenland|Greenland]], and the duchies of [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] and [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]].
denmark-norway.r: [[e:copenhagen|Copenhagen]] was the centre of government, funded by [[e:oresund|the Sound]] Toll on shipping into the Baltic. [[e:christian-iv-of-denmark|Christian IV]] built palaces and towns but lost wars with [[e:sweden|Sweden]], and in 1658 [[e:denmark|Denmark]] ceded [[e:scania|Scania]]. [[e:frederick-iii-of-denmark|Frederick III]] introduced absolute monarchy in 1660, set down in the [[e:kings-law|King's Law]] of 1665. Trading companies founded [[s:danish-india|Danish India]], the [[s:danish-gold-coast|Danish Gold Coast]] and the [[s:danish-west-indies|Danish West Indies]], and Norwegian [[e:timber|timber]] and fish fed a growing merchant fleet.
denmark-norway.e: Allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] after the British bombardment of [[e:copenhagen|Copenhagen]] in 1807, Denmark-[[e:norway|Norway]] ended on the losing side. By the [[e:treaty-of-kiel|Treaty of Kiel]] in 1814 [[e:denmark|Denmark]] ceded Norway to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] but kept [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]], the [[e:faroe-islands|Faroes]] and [[e:greenland|Greenland]]. Norway briefly declared independence as the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]] (1814) before entering [[s:sweden-norway|Sweden-Norway]].

dhenkanal-state.t: A princely state in central Odisha, remembered for the killing of the twelve-year-old boatman Baji Rout during the Praja Mandal movement of 1938.
dhenkanal-state.o: Tradition holds that [[e:hari-singh-vidyadhar|Hari Singh Vidyadhar]], a commander of the [[s:gajapati-kingdom|Gajapati Kingdom]], defeated a local chief named Dhenka and founded the state in 1529. The capital was the town of Dhenkanal.
dhenkanal-state.r: Dhenkanal was a large inland state on the [[e:brahmani-river|Brahmani]], with [[e:rice|rice]] fields, forest and Adivasi communities. It was tributary to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and from 1803 one of the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]]. In October 1938 state police fired on villagers at Bhuban, and the young ferryman [[e:baji-rout|Baji Rout]] was shot for refusing to take them across the river.
dhenkanal-state.e: Dhenkanal merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now a district of Odisha.

da-tianxing.t: A one-year dynasty in Yunnan under Zhao Shanzheng, a figurehead raised to the throne at Yangjumie after the fall of Da Changhe.
da-tianxing.o: In 928 the powerful official [[e:yang-ganzhen|Yang Ganzhen]] overthrew [[e:zheng-longdan|Zheng Longdan]], last ruler of [[s:da-changhe|Da Changhe]], and placed the minister [[e:zhao-shanzheng|Zhao Shanzheng]] on the throne at [[e:yangjumie|Yangjumie]] as ruler of Da Tianxing.
da-tianxing.r: Almost nothing is known of the regime beyond its existence; [[e:zhao-shanzheng|Zhao Shanzheng]] appears to have been a puppet of [[e:yang-ganzhen|Yang Ganzhen]] and the great families of the [[e:lake-erhai|Erhai]] region, who continued the institutions inherited from [[s:nanzhao|Nanzhao]].
da-tianxing.e: In 929 [[e:yang-ganzhen|Yang Ganzhen]] removed [[e:zhao-shanzheng|Zhao Shanzheng]] and took the throne himself, founding [[s:da-yining|Da Yining]]. The rapid succession of dynasties ended only with the [[s:dali-kingdom|Dali Kingdom]] in 937.

dutch-cape-colony.t: The Dutch East India Company's colony at the Cape of Good Hope, from which European settlement and the Afrikaans language spread across South Africa.
dutch-cape-colony.o: In 1652 [[e:jan-van-riebeeck|Jan van Riebeeck]] landed at [[e:table-bay|Table Bay]] to set up a refreshment station for [[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]] ships sailing to the [[e:east-indies|East Indies]]. From 1657 the Company released servants as free [[e:burghers|burghers]] to farm, and the settlement expanded at the expense of [[e:khoekhoe|Khoikhoi]] herders, who were defeated in wars in 1659 and 1673–77.
dutch-cape-colony.r: The colony was run by Company officials, including [[e:simon-van-der-stel|Simon van der Stel]] and his son [[e:willem-adriaan-van-der-stel|Willem Adriaan]], and its economy depended on wine, wheat and enslaved labour brought from the [[e:east-indies|East Indies]], [[e:india|India]] and [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]]. French [[e:huguenots|Huguenots]] arrived in 1688. [[e:trekboers|Trekboer]] [[e:cattle|cattle]] farmers pushed the frontier east to the [[e:great-fish-river|Fish River]], where they met the [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]], and [[e:afrikaans|Afrikaans]] developed from [[e:cape-dutch|Cape Dutch]].
dutch-cape-colony.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] seized the Cape in 1795 after the [[e:battle-of-muizenberg|Battle of Muizenberg]], returned it to the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]] in 1803 and took it again after the [[e:battle-of-blaauwberg|Battle of Blaauwberg]] in 1806. It became the British [[s:cape-colony|Cape Colony]].

dasada-state.t: A small state of the Jhalawad district of Kathiawar, on the edge of the Little Rann of Kutch, held by a Muslim chiefly family.
dasada-state.o: Dasada lay on the southern edge of the [[e:little-rann-of-kutch|Little Rann of Kutch]] in the [[e:jhalawad|Jhalawad]] region of northern [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]]. Its rulers, a Muslim family of Malik descent, held the estate from around 1600, though its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
dasada-state.r: The ruler governed a dry, thinly settled territory of grazing land and [[e:cotton|cotton]] villages bordering the salt flats. The state paid tribute to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]] and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Few further details are recorded.
dasada-state.e: Dasada merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in present [[e:surendranagar-district|Surendranagar district]].

duchy-of-western-zhou.t: The tiny duchy around Luoyang that sheltered the last Zhou kings and surrendered to Qin in 256 BCE, ending the Zhou royal line.
duchy-of-western-zhou.o: In 440 BCE [[e:king-kao-of-zhou|King Kao of Zhou]] enfeoffed his younger brother Jie, Duke Huan, at Henan (the old royal city of [[e:wangcheng|Wangcheng]], near [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]]). The duchy took over much of what remained of the shrunken royal domain.
duchy-of-western-zhou.r: The dukes of [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] were the real masters of the land around the king, who by the 4th century BCE had almost no territory of his own. After a succession dispute in 367 BCE the domain split, with the [[s:duchy-of-eastern-zhou|Duchy of Eastern Zhou]] ruling around Gong. [[e:king-nan-of-zhou|King Nan]] lived under the protection of Western Zhou, and the duchy survived by playing off the great powers.
duchy-of-western-zhou.e: In 256 BCE Duke Wu of [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] joined an alliance against the [[s:state-of-qin|State of Qin]]. [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] attacked, the duke surrendered his 36 towns, and [[e:king-nan-of-zhou|King Nan]] died that year. Qin removed the Nine Tripods, symbols of royal legitimacy, and the [[e:zhou-dynasty|Zhou dynasty]] came to an end.

duchy-of-bavaria-munich.t: The Wittelsbach duchy centred on Munich that outlasted its rival Bavarian branches and reunited the country under Albert IV in 1505.
duchy-of-bavaria-munich.o: The partition of 1392 gave [[e:john-ii-duke-of-bavaria|John II]] the lands around [[e:munich|Munich]], the smallest share of the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] inheritance in [[e:upper-bavaria|Upper Bavaria]]. His sons [[e:ernest-duke-of-bavaria|Ernest]] and [[e:william-iii-duke-of-bavaria|William III]] ruled jointly after 1397, and in 1429 they received a share of the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-straubing|Duchy of Bavaria-Straubing]].
duchy-of-bavaria-munich.r: The dukes ruled from the [[e:alter-hof|Alter Hof]] in [[e:munich|Munich]], a city grown rich on the [[e:salt-trade|salt trade]]. [[e:ernest-duke-of-bavaria|Duke Ernest]] had [[e:agnes-bernauer|Agnes Bernauer]], the commoner wife of his son [[e:albert-iii-duke-of-bavaria|Albert III]], drowned at [[e:straubing|Straubing]] in 1435. [[e:albert-iv-duke-of-bavaria|Albert IV]], duke from 1465, built a stronger, more centralised state, and Munich's [[e:frauenkirche-munich|Frauenkirche]] was completed under his rule in 1488.
duchy-of-bavaria-munich.e: [[e:albert-iv-duke-of-bavaria|Albert IV]] won the [[e:war-of-the-landshut-succession|War of the Landshut Succession]] in 1505 and reunited most of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. His [[e:primogeniture|primogeniture]] decree of 1506 forbade further divisions, so the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria|Duchy of Bavaria]], with [[e:munich|Munich]] as its capital, remained united from then on.

duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.t: Ernestine duchy in Franconia and Thuringia whose ambitious family married into the royal houses of Europe.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.o: [[e:john-ernest-iv-duke-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld|John Ernest]], seventh son of [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-gotha|Ernest the Pious]], received [[e:saalfeld|Saalfeld]] in 1680. When the [[e:duchy-of-saxe-coburg|Duchy of Saxe-Coburg]] died out in 1699, he gained most of [[e:coburg|Coburg]] after a long dispute, forming Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.r: The duchy was Lutheran and small, with debts that led to an imperial debt commission in the 18th century. Duke [[e:ernest-frederick-duke-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld|Ernest Frederick]] and Duke Francis governed modestly; Francis was a collector whose prints formed the [[e:coburg|Coburg]] collections. Duke [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Ernest I]] was restored after French occupation in 1807. Francis's children married well: Leopold later became King of the Belgians and [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]], Duchess of Kent, was mother of [[e:queen-victoria|Queen Victoria]].
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.e: After [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg]] died out, [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Ernest I]] gave up [[e:saalfeld|Saalfeld]] and received [[e:gotha|Gotha]] in 1826, forming the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha]]. Saalfeld went to Saxe-[[e:meiningen|Meiningen]], and the family's dynastic rise continued under the new name.

dingan.t: A small successor state of Balhae in the Yalu valley, which resisted the Khitan for half a century and sought alliance with Song China.
dingan.o: After the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]] destroyed [[s:balhae|Balhae]] in 926, groups of Balhae people in the middle [[e:yalu-river|Yalu]] river valley, beyond effective Khitan control, formed their own state. Its beginnings are obscure; it is first recorded in the 930s and 970s, with a royal house sometimes linked to the Yeol family.
dingan.r: Known almost entirely from Chinese and Korean chronicles, Dingan presented itself as heir to [[s:balhae|Balhae]]. In 970 its king Yeol Man-hwa (Lie Wanhua) sent envoys to the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]], and in 981 King O Hyeon-myeong (Wu Xuanming) proposed joint action against the Khitan, but no help came.
dingan.e: [[e:shengzong-of-liao|Emperor Shengzong of Liao]] sent a campaign in 985 that destroyed the kingdom by 986. Its people were deported or fled, many to [[s:goryeo|Goryeo]], which absorbed numerous [[s:balhae|Balhae]] refugees in this period.

duchy-of-cleves.t: A lower Rhine duchy, home of Anne of Cleves, whose union with Jülich and Berg and later inheritance by Brandenburg brought Prussia to the Rhine.
duchy-of-cleves.o: The counts of [[e:kleve|Cleves]] appear around 1092, with a castle on a hill above the lower [[e:rhine|Rhine]] at Kleve. Their county lay on both banks of the river near the modern [[e:dutch|Dutch]] border. In 1368 it passed to the counts of the Mark, and Adolf I was raised to duke by [[e:sigismund-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Sigismund]] in 1417.
duchy-of-cleves.r: [[e:kleve|Cleves]] was a wealthy trading land on the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], with towns such as [[e:wesel|Wesel]], [[e:emmerich-am-rhein|Emmerich]] and [[e:kalkar|Kalkar]]. In 1521 Duke [[e:john-iii-duke-of-cleves|John III]] united Cleves with Jülich and Berg, forming the [[s:united-duchies-of-julich-cleves-berg|United Duchies]]. His daughter [[e:anne-of-cleves|Anne of Cleves]] married [[e:henry-viii-of-england|Henry VIII of England]] in 1540. The dukes favoured the humanist middle way of [[e:erasmus|Erasmus]].
duchy-of-cleves.e: After the [[e:war-of-the-julich-succession|Jülich succession crisis]], the [[e:treaty-of-xanten|Treaty of Xanten]] in 1614 gave [[e:kleve|Cleves]] to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]], giving the [[e:house-of-hohenzollern|Hohenzollerns]] their first foothold in the west. [[e:france|France]] took the left bank in 1795, and after 1815 the region returned to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]; it is now part of [[e:north-rhine-westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]].
duchy-of-cleves.re: Catholic Christianity, later mixed Catholic and Protestant

duchy-of-saxe-romhild.t: Short-lived Ernestine duchy in southern Thuringia, one of the seven shares of Ernest the Pious's inheritance.
duchy-of-saxe-romhild.o: [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-gotha|Ernest the Pious]] of Saxe-[[e:gotha|Gotha]] died in 1675, and his sons ruled jointly until they divided the lands in 1680. Henry, the fourth son, received [[e:romhild|Römhild]] near the Franconian border, establishing the small Duchy of Saxe-Römhild.
duchy-of-saxe-romhild.r: Henry rebuilt Glücksburg Castle in [[e:romhild|Römhild]] and spent heavily on his court, leaving debts far greater than the tiny duchy's revenues. The territory was rural, Lutheran and administered by a handful of officials. Little else distinguishes its short history, which is known mainly from the disputes over its inheritance.
duchy-of-saxe-romhild.e: Henry died without children in 1710. His lands were divided among [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg]], Saxe-[[e:meiningen|Meiningen]] and Saxe-Coburg-[[e:saalfeld|Saalfeld]] after a long dispute, and [[e:romhild|Römhild]] later passed to Saxe-Meiningen.

duchy-of-bar.t: A Lorraine county raised to a duchy, divided between French and imperial allegiance, and united with the Duchy of Lorraine under René of Anjou's heirs.
duchy-of-bar.o: [[e:bar-le-duc|Bar-le-Duc's]] castle was built in the 10th century by Duke Frederick of [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Upper Lorraine]]. In 1033 the county passed to his descendant [[e:sophie-of-bar|Sophie of Bar]], who around 1038 married [[e:louis-of-mousson|Louis of Mousson]], count of [[s:county-of-montbeliard|Montbéliard]]; their descendants ruled the county of Bar as a separate principality between [[s:county-of-champagne|Champagne]] and [[e:lorraine|Lorraine]].
duchy-of-bar.r: The counts ruled a fertile land along the [[e:meuse|Meuse]] and [[e:ornain|Ornain]]. After a defeat by [[e:philip-iv-of-france|Philip IV]], the [[e:treaty-of-bruges-1301|Treaty of Bruges]] in 1301 made the western part, the Barrois mouvant, a fief of the French crown, while the rest stayed imperial. Robert I became the first duke in 1354. [[e:rene-of-anjou|René of Anjou]] inherited Bar in 1430 from his great-uncle, Cardinal [[e:louis-cardinal-of-bar|Louis of Bar]], and through his wife Isabella gained [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]] in 1431.
duchy-of-bar.e: René's grandson [[e:rene-ii-duke-of-lorraine|René II]] united Bar and the [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Duchy of Lorraine]] in 1480, and the two shared rulers thereafter. Like [[e:lorraine|Lorraine]], Bar passed to [[e:stanislaw-leszczynski|Stanisław Leszczyński]] in 1737 and was annexed to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] on his death in 1766.

duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.t: Albertine Saxon duchy on the Saale whose lavish court employed musicians and gave Bach an honorary title.
duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.o: After Elector [[e:john-george-i-elector-of-saxony|John George I]] of [[e:saxony|Saxony]] died in 1656, his son [[e:augustus-duke-of-saxe-weissenfels|Augustus]], already administrator of the [[s:archbishopric-of-magdeburg|Archbishopric of Magdeburg]], received [[e:weissenfels|Weissenfels]], [[e:querfurt|Querfurt]] and other lands under his father's will, founding the Duchy of [[e:saxe-weissenfels|Saxe-Weissenfels]]. Augustus built the large [[e:neu-augustusburg|Neu-Augustusburg]] palace at Weissenfels.
duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.r: The duchy was Lutheran and depended on the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]] in foreign affairs. Its court was a centre of music and opera: [[e:george-frideric-handel|Handel]]'s father was surgeon to the duke, and [[e:johann-sebastian-bach|Johann Sebastian Bach]] held the honorary title of [[e:kapellmeister|Kapellmeister]] of [[e:weissenfels|Weissenfels]] from 1729. Lavish court spending left the state deeply in debt.
duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.e: [[e:johann-adolf-ii-duke-of-saxe-weissenfels|Johann Adolf II]], the last duke and a [[e:saxons|Saxon]] field marshal, died in 1746, and the duchy reverted to the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]. [[e:weissenfels|Weissenfels]] passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815 and is now in [[e:saxony-anhalt|Saxony-Anhalt]].

dutch-angola.t: The Dutch West India Company's brief occupation of Luanda, which allied with Queen Njinga before Portugal retook the city in 1648.
dutch-angola.o: During the [[e:dutch|Dutch]]–Portuguese war, a [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] fleet under [[e:cornelis-jol|Cornelis Jol]] captured [[e:luanda|Luanda]] in August 1641, aiming to secure enslaved labour for the [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] plantations of [[s:dutch-brazil|Dutch Brazil]]. The Portuguese withdrew inland to [[s:massangano|Massangano]] on the [[e:kwanza-river|Kwanza]].
dutch-angola.r: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] held [[e:luanda|Luanda]] and [[e:benguela|Benguela]], strengthened the fort they called Aardenburgh and shipped captives to [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. They allied with [[e:njinga-of-ndongo-and-matamba|Njinga Mbande]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-matamba|Kingdom of Matamba]] and the [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kingdom of Kongo]] against the Portuguese, and their combined forces won victories in the interior, though they failed to destroy the Portuguese garrison at [[s:massangano|Massangano]].
dutch-angola.e: In August 1648 a fleet from [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] under [[e:salvador-correia-de-sa-e-benevides|Salvador Correia de Sa]] recaptured [[e:luanda|Luanda]], and the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] surrendered. The episode left [[s:portuguese-angola|Portuguese Angola]] restored and [[e:njinga-of-ndongo-and-matamba|Njinga]] and [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kongo]] exposed to Portuguese reprisals.

cr.a: Zscout370; derivative work by Fentener van Vlissingen; derivative work by Mnmazur

democratic-republic-of-georgia.t: Georgia's first modern republic, a Menshevik social democracy that won international recognition before the Red Army invaded in 1921.
democratic-republic-of-georgia.o: With the [[s:transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic|Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic]] collapsing, the Georgian National Council declared independence in [[e:tbilisi|Tiflis]] on 26 May 1918. German troops arrived to protect the new state against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], and after [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat British forces took their place until 1920.
democratic-republic-of-georgia.r: Governed by the Social Democratic ([[e:mensheviks|Menshevik]]) party under [[e:noe-zhordania|Noe Zhordania]], the republic held democratic elections, carried out land reform, founded [[e:tbilisi-state-university|Tbilisi State University]] in 1918 and adopted a constitution in 1921. It fought border wars with [[s:armenia|Armenia]] and faced risings in [[e:south-ossetia|South Ossetia]] and [[s:principality-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]]. [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] recognised its independence in the Treaty of [[e:moscow|Moscow]] of May 1920.
democratic-republic-of-georgia.e: In February 1921 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] invaded, and [[e:tbilisi|Tiflis]] fell on 25 February; the government went into exile in [[e:france|France]]. The [[s:georgian-ssr|Georgian SSR]] replaced it, and independent [[s:georgia|Georgia]] restored its flag in 1990-1991.

cr.a: Vector version: Giorgi Balakhadze. Original: Iakob Nikoladze

don-republic.t: The anti-Bolshevik state of the Don Cossacks in the Russian Civil War, led by Ataman Krasnov and later part of Denikin's White movement.
don-republic.o: After Ataman [[e:alexey-kaledin|Alexey Kaledin]] shot himself in February 1918 as Bolsheviks overran the Don, a [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] uprising in spring drove them out. In May 1918 a Cossack assembly in [[e:novocherkassk|Novocherkassk]] elected General [[e:pyotr-krasnov|Pyotr Krasnov]] ataman and proclaimed the independent Almighty Don Host, heir to the [[s:don-cossack-host|Don Cossack Host]].
don-republic.r: [[e:pyotr-krasnov|Krasnov]] allied with [[e:germany|Germany]], from which he obtained weapons, and organised a sizeable Don army that besieged [[e:volgograd|Tsaritsyn]] in 1918. The republic had a constitution, its own currency and a government based on [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] institutions. After Germany's defeat Krasnov resigned in February 1919, and under Ataman [[e:afrikan-bogaevsky|Afrikan Bogaevsky]] the Don joined [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]]'s [[e:armed-forces-of-south-russia|Armed Forces of South Russia]].
don-republic.e: The White advance on [[e:moscow|Moscow]] failed in 1919. The [[e:red-army|Red Army]] captured [[e:novocherkassk|Novocherkassk]] in January 1920, and the Don was absorbed into the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]]. The Bolsheviks' policy of decossackisation brought executions and [[e:deportation|deportations]].

deceangli.t: People of north-east Wales, the first target of Roman campaigns into Wales in 48, whose lead mines soon stamped their name on Roman ingots.
deceangli.o: The Deceangli lived in what is now [[e:flintshire|Flintshire]] and [[e:denbighshire|Denbighshire]], between the [[e:river-dee-wales|Dee]] estuary and the [[e:vale-of-clwyd|Clwyd]] valley, a region of hillforts such as [[e:moel-hiraddug|Moel Hiraddug]] and [[e:penycloddiau|Penycloddiau]]. They were probably a small [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] grouping of local communities and are first named by [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]].
deceangli.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or society beyond the archaeology of their hillforts and farms. Their territory was rich in lead and [[e:silver|silver]] ores on [[e:halkyn-mountain|Halkyn Mountain]], which the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] quickly exploited; lead pigs found near [[e:chester|Chester]] carry the inscription DECEANGL and a date of 74, showing that mining was organised under the name of the people.
deceangli.e: In 48 the governor [[e:publius-ostorius-scapula|Ostorius Scapula]] marched against the Deceangli, ravaging their land almost to the [[e:irish-sea|Irish Sea]] before trouble among the [[s:brigantes|Brigantes]] recalled him. The area was secured by the fortress of [[e:chester|Chester]] in the 70s, and the Deceangli are not known to have formed a civitas of [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

duchy-of-raciborz.t: Upper Silesian duchy on the upper Oder, ruled first by Piasts and then by a Přemyslid branch from Opava until 1521.
duchy-of-raciborz.o: In the 1281 partition of the [[s:duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz|Duchy of Opole and Racibórz]], [[e:przemyslaw-of-raciborz|Przemysław]] received [[e:raciborz|Racibórz]], the old capital of [[e:upper-silesia|Upper Silesia]]. His son [[e:leszek-of-raciborz|Leszek]] accepted Bohemian overlordship in 1327, and when Leszek died without heirs in 1336, the duchy passed to [[e:nicholas-ii-of-opava|Nicholas II of Opava]], a [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]] married to Przemysław's daughter.
duchy-of-raciborz.r: The [[e:opava|Opava]] [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslids]] ruled [[e:raciborz|Racibórz]] as part of a combined duchy of Opava and Racibórz, later separate. The duchy was a fertile land of grain and fish ponds, with a Polish-speaking population and German [[e:burghers|burghers]]. It was a Bohemian fief, and its dukes took part in the Hussite wars and the struggles between Bohemian and Hungarian kings.
duchy-of-raciborz.e: After the last [[e:premyslid-dynasty|Přemyslid]] duke died in 1521, [[e:raciborz|Racibórz]] passed to [[e:john-ii-the-good|John II the Good]] of [[e:opole|Opole]]. When he died in 1532, it fell to the Bohemian crown, held by the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and pledged to [[e:brandenburg-ansbach|Brandenburg-Ansbach]]. It passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742 and to [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

dominican-republic.t: The present Dominican Republic since 1966, which moved from the authoritarian rule of Joaquín Balaguer to democracy and fast tourism-led growth.
dominican-republic.o: After the civil war and US intervention of 1965 ended the [[s:third-dominican-republic|Third Dominican Republic]], an interim government organised elections in June 1966. [[e:joaquin-balaguer|Joaquín Balaguer]], a former aide of [[e:rafael-trujillo|Trujillo]], defeated [[e:juan-bosch|Juan Bosch]] and introduced a new constitution in November 1966.
dominican-republic.r: [[e:joaquin-balaguer|Balaguer]] ruled for twelve years with repression of the left, public works and [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] exports. The 1978 election brought a peaceful transfer to [[e:antonio-guzman-fernandez|Antonio Guzmán]], but [[e:balaguer|Balaguer]] returned from 1986 to 1996. [[e:leonel-fernandez|Leonel Fernández]] and Danilo [[e:medina|Medina]] of the [[e:dominican-liberation-party|Dominican Liberation Party]] then governed for most of the next two decades. Tourism, free trade zones, mining and remittances from Dominicans in the [[s:united-states|United States]] transformed the economy, making it one of the fastest growing in [[e:latin-america|Latin America]].
dominican-republic.e: [[e:luis-abinader|Luis Abinader]] of the [[e:modern-revolutionary-party|Modern Revolutionary Party]] won the presidency in 2020 and was re-elected in 2024. Relations with neighbouring [[s:republic-of-haiti|Haiti]], migration and inequality remain the central issues of the republic.

dutch-tobago.t: Contested Dutch colony on Tobago, named New Walcheren by Zeeland settlers and fought over by the Dutch, Courlanders, English and French.
dutch-tobago.o: Merchants of [[e:vlissingen|Vlissingen]] in [[s:county-of-zeeland|Zeeland]], led by Jan de Moor, sent settlers to [[e:tobago|Tobago]] in 1628 under a patent from the [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] and called the island New [[e:walcheren|Walcheren]]. The first colony was destroyed by the Spanish and [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]] from [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]] in 1637, but the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] returned in the 1650s under the Lampsins brothers, displacing the rival colony of the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland]].
dutch-tobago.r: The colony centred on Lampsinsburg and a cluster of forts and plantations growing tobacco, [[e:cotton|cotton]], [[e:indigo|indigo]] and [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] with the labour of enslaved Africans. In 1662 [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] made [[e:cornelis-lampsins|Cornelis Lampsins]] Baron of [[e:tobago|Tobago]], a rare French title over a Dutch-run island. The settlers were mostly [[e:dutch|Dutch]] Reformed Protestants, with French, Jewish and other incomers.
dutch-tobago.e: [[e:tobago|Tobago]] changed hands repeatedly during the Anglo-[[e:dutch|Dutch]] and Franco-Dutch wars. In 1677 a French fleet under [[e:jean-ii-destrees|Jean d'Estrées]] attacked, and a magazine explosion destroyed the Dutch fort and its defenders. The French razed the colony, and Dutch rule ended; the island stayed thinly settled until the British [[s:colony-of-tobago|Colony of Tobago]] of 1763.

cr.a: Thomas Bowen; derivative work by MagentaGreen

dominion-of-newfoundland.t: Britain's oldest colony, a self-governing dominion from 1907 that gave up self-government during the Depression and joined Canada in 1949.
dominion-of-newfoundland.o: The [[s:colony-of-newfoundland|Colony of Newfoundland]], self-governing since 1855, had declined to join [[s:canada|Canada]] in 1869. At the [[e:imperial-conference|Imperial Conference]] of 1907 it was granted the status of a dominion, equal in title to [[e:canada|Canada]], [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Australia]] and [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]], under Prime Minister [[e:robert-bond|Robert Bond]], who had sought a separate trade deal with the [[s:united-states|United States]].
dominion-of-newfoundland.r: The economy depended on the salt cod fishery, with newer pulp, paper and iron mining. In the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] the [[e:royal-newfoundland-regiment|Newfoundland Regiment]] was almost destroyed at [[e:beaumont-hamel|Beaumont-Hamel]] on 1 July 1916, and war debt, including a costly railway, weighed on the dominion. In 1927 the [[e:judicial-committee-of-the-privy-council|Privy Council]] awarded it the interior of [[e:labrador|Labrador]]. The [[e:great-depression|Depression]] brought near-bankruptcy and riots against Prime Minister [[e:richard-squires|Richard Squires]] in 1932.
dominion-of-newfoundland.e: In 1934 [[e:newfoundland|Newfoundland]] gave up self-government to a British-appointed [[e:commission-of-government|Commission of Government]]. American and Canadian bases brought prosperity in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]]. After two referendums in 1948, led by [[e:joey-smallwood|Joey Smallwood's]] campaign, it joined [[s:canada|Canada]] as its tenth province on 31 March 1949.

dar-masalit.t: A sultanate of the Masalit people in western Darfur that defeated a French column in 1910 and joined Sudan by agreement in 1922.
dar-masalit.o: The [[e:masalit-people|Masalit]] lived on the western fringe of the [[s:darfur-sultanate|Darfur Sultanate]]. In the 1870s, as [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]] fell to [[s:zubayrs-bahr-al-ghazal|Zubayr's Bahr al-Ghazal]] and the [[s:khedivate-of-egypt|Khedivate of Egypt]], a Masalit holy man, [[e:ismail-abd-al-nabi|Ismail Abd al-Nabi]], built up authority among them, and his family founded an independent sultanate around 1874.
dar-masalit.r: The sultans ruled a farming people from fortified centres, balancing between the [[s:mahdist-state|Mahdist State]], the [[s:wadai-empire|Wadai Empire]] and the restored [[s:darfur-sultanate|Darfur Sultanate]] of [[e:ali-dinar|Ali Dinar]]. In 1910 [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Taj al-Din defeated a French column at [[e:battle-of-dorothe|Dorothe]], though he died in the fighting. His successor [[e:muhammad-bahr-al-din|Muhammad Bahr al-Din]], known as Andoka, made [[e:el-geneina|Geneina]] his capital.
dar-masalit.e: After [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]] in 1916 and the Anglo-French border was fixed in 1919, the sultan accepted [[e:indirect-rule|indirect rule]]. Dar [[e:masalit-people|Masalit]] was formally joined to [[s:anglo-egyptian-sudan|Anglo-Egyptian Sudan]] in 1922, keeping its sultan as a traditional ruler.

duchy-of-krakow.t: The senior duchy of fragmented Poland, whose throne at Krakow carried overlordship of the other Piast dukes.
duchy-of-krakow.o: In his testament of 1138 [[e:boleslaw-iii-wrymouth|Boleslaw III Wrymouth]] divided [[e:poland|Poland]] among his sons, creating a senior province around [[e:krakow|Krakow]] to be held by the eldest [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] with authority over the others. The first senior duke, [[e:wladyslaw-ii-the-exile|Wladyslaw II the Exile]], tried to rule alone and was driven out by his brothers in 1146.
duchy-of-krakow.r: [[e:krakow|Krakow]] passed in turn to [[e:boleslaw-iv-the-curly|Boleslaw IV]], [[e:mieszko-iii-the-old|Mieszko III]] and [[e:casimir-ii-the-just|Casimir II the Just]], and the seniority principle broke down as rival dukes fought for the city. [[e:lesser-poland|Lesser Poland's]] nobles and [[e:bishop|bishops]] gained great influence. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] devastated the duchy in 1241, but under [[e:boleslaw-v-the-chaste|Boleslaw V the Chaste]] Krakow received town rights in 1257 and the salt mines of [[e:wieliczka|Wieliczka]] and [[e:bochnia|Bochnia]] brought wealth.
duchy-of-krakow.e: After the Silesian [[e:henry-iv-probus|Henry IV Probus]] and the Bohemian king [[e:wenceslaus-ii-of-bohemia|Wenceslaus II]], who ruled from 1291, [[e:wladyslaw-i-lokietek|Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high]] took [[e:krakow|Krakow]] in 1306. He was crowned there in 1320, and the duchy became the core of the reunited [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385).

duchy-of-bouillon.t: The Ardennes duchy whose castle Godfrey of Bouillon pawned for the First Crusade, later a small sovereign state of the La Marck and La Tour d'Auvergne families.
duchy-of-bouillon.o: [[e:godfrey-of-bouillon|Godfrey of Bouillon]] pledged his castle and lands to the [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]] in 1096 to fund the First Crusade, and the bishops held Bouillon for centuries. From the mid-15th century the [[e:house-of-la-marck|La Marck family]] gained control of it, and by the 1480s they ruled it in practice as an independent duchy.
duchy-of-bouillon.r: Bouillon was a forested, sparsely populated land around a great castle on the [[e:semois|Semois]]. [[e:robert-ii-de-la-marck|Robert II de la Marck]] and his heirs, also princes of [[s:principality-of-sedan|Sedan]], styled themselves dukes. Possession was contested between the [[e:house-of-la-marck|La Marcks]], their [[e:house-of-la-tour-dauvergne|La Tour d'Auvergne]] heirs and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]].
