In 1678 [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] took Bouillon and gave it to [[e:godefroy-maurice-de-la-tour-dauvergne|Godefroy-Maurice de La Tour d'Auvergne]] under French protection.
duchy-of-bouillon.e: French troops annexed the duchy in 1795. After the [[e:napoleonic-wars|Napoleonic Wars]] it went to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-luxembourg|Grand Duchy of Luxembourg]] in 1815 and to the [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Kingdom of Belgium]] in 1839.

dutch-delagoa-bay.t: A short-lived Dutch East India Company trading post on Delagoa Bay, founded to seek gold and ivory and abandoned after a decade.
dutch-delagoa-bay.o: In 1721 the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) sent an expedition from the Cape to [[e:delagoa-bay|Delagoa Bay]], hoping to tap the gold of the interior and the [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] of the bay. The settlers built Fort Lijdzaamheid on the site of modern [[e:maputo|Maputo]].
dutch-delagoa-bay.r: The post traded cloth, [[e:bead|beads]] and metal for [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves with the local [[e:tsonga-people|Tsonga]] rulers, including those of the [[s:tembe-kingdom|Tembe Kingdom]]. It suffered terribly from malaria, losing much of its garrison, and was attacked and briefly captured by [[e:piracy|pirates]] in 1722. Expeditions inland failed to find the hoped-for goldfields.
dutch-delagoa-bay.e: Unprofitable and deadly, the post was abandoned in 1730. The Portuguese reasserted their claim to the bay, which was later contested by [[e:austria|Austria]] and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] before the 1875 arbitration confirmed Portuguese possession.

dewas-senior.t: The senior of the two Maratha Puar states that shared the town of Dewas in Malwa, remembered through E. M. Forster's The Hill of Devi.
dewas-senior.o: The brothers [[e:tukoji-rao-i-puar|Tukoji Rao]] and [[e:jivaji-rao-puar|Jivaji Rao Puar]] came to [[e:malwa|Malwa]] with the [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]] [[e:baji-rao-i|Baji Rao I]] and received [[e:dewas|Dewas]] around 1728. Their shared holding developed into two states, the Senior Branch descending from Tukoji Rao and the Junior from Jivaji Rao, which divided land and revenues but kept the same capital.
dewas-senior.r: [[e:dewas|Dewas]] Senior was a [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] state of the [[e:central-india-agency|Central India Agency]], centred on the hill shrine of the goddess [[e:chamunda|Chamunda]] above the town. Each branch had its own palace, administration and quarter of Dewas. [[e:e-m-forster|E. M. Forster]] served as secretary to [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:tukoji-rao-iii-of-dewas-senior|Tukoji Rao III]] in 1921, an experience he described in [[e:the-hill-of-devi|The Hill of Devi]].
dewas-senior.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]], [[e:dewas|Dewas]] Senior merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948, which became part of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956.

duchy-of-pomerelia.t: The duchy of Gdansk Pomerania under the Samborides, whose end in 1294 led to centuries of conflict between Poland and the Teutonic Knights.
duchy-of-pomerelia.o: Eastern [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]], around Gdansk on the [[e:vistula|Vistula]] delta, was conquered by [[e:boleslaw-iii-wrymouth|Boleslaw III]] of [[e:poland|Poland]] in the early 12th century and governed for him by local nobles. In the mid 12th century these governors, the [[e:samborides|Samborides]], began to rule on their own account, and [[e:sambor-i|Sambor I]] founded the Cistercian abbey of [[e:oliwa-cathedral|Oliwa]] in 1186.
duchy-of-pomerelia.r: [[e:pomerelia|Pomerelia]] controlled the mouth of the [[e:vistula|Vistula]], and Gdansk grew into a busy port with German, Slavic and Danish merchants. [[e:swietopelk-ii-duke-of-pomerania|Swietopelk II the Great]], who ruled from the 1220s to 1266, threw off Polish overlordship, took the ducal title and fought long wars against the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]].
duchy-of-pomerelia.e: His son [[e:mestwin-ii|Mestwin II]], who died without sons, left the duchy to [[e:przemysl-ii|Przemysl II]] of [[s:duchy-of-greater-poland|Greater Poland]] under the [[e:treaty-of-kepno|Treaty of Kepno]] of 1282. After Mestwin's death in 1294, the land was contested, and in 1308 the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Knights]] seized Gdansk and held [[e:pomerelia|Pomerelia]] until it became part of [[s:royal-prussia|Royal Prussia]] in 1466.

duchy-of-opole.t: Upper Silesian Piast duchy whose duke Władysław Opolczyk brought the Black Madonna to Częstochowa and whose last prince died in 1532.
duchy-of-opole.o: In 1281 the [[s:duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz|Duchy of Opole and Racibórz]] was divided among the sons of [[e:wladyslaw-of-opole|Władysław of Opole]], and Bolko I received [[e:opole|Opole]] on the [[e:oder-river|Oder]]. He accepted Bohemian overlordship in 1327 along with other Upper Silesian dukes, while his descendants continued to rule.
duchy-of-opole.r: [[e:wladyslaw-ii-of-opole|Władysław II of Opole]] served as palatine of [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and in 1382 founded the Pauline monastery of [[e:jasna-gora-monastery|Jasna Góra]] at [[e:czestochowa|Częstochowa]], bringing the [[e:black-madonna-of-czestochowa|Black Madonna]] icon. The [[e:opole|Opole]] dukes later gathered much of [[e:upper-silesia|Upper Silesia]], and [[e:john-ii-the-good|John II the Good]] issued a charter of privileges for the region and allowed the mining town of [[e:tarnowskie-gory|Tarnowskie Góry]] to develop. The population was largely Polish-speaking.
duchy-of-opole.e: With [[e:john-ii-the-good|John II]]'s death in 1532 the Upper Silesian [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]] died out, and [[e:opole|Opole]] passed to the Bohemian crown under the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]], pledged at times to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] and the [[e:house-of-vasa|Polish Vasas]]. It went to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742 and to [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

dumnonii.t: Iron Age people of Devon and Cornwall, whose tin and remote farming settlements kept them apart from the coin-using kingdoms of the south-east.
dumnonii.o: The Dumnonii emerged from the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] communities of the south-western peninsula, a land of hillforts, defended farmsteads known as rounds, and coastal promontory forts. Greek writers from [[e:pytheas|Pytheas]] onwards describe the [[e:tin|tin]] trade of the far south-west, and harbours such as [[e:mount-batten|Mount Batten]] on [[e:plymouth-sound|Plymouth Sound]] linked the region with [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]] and the wider Atlantic world.
dumnonii.r: No kings or coins of the Dumnonii are known, which suggests a looser society of local lineages rather than a single dynasty. Most people lived in small enclosed farms raising [[e:cattle|cattle]] and grain, while [[e:tin|tin]] streaming in [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]] and [[e:dartmoor|Dartmoor]] gave the region its main export. Courtyard houses and underground passages called fogous are distinctive of the far west.
dumnonii.e: Roman forces reached the south-west after 43, and around 55 the legio [[e:legio-ii-augusta|II Augusta]] built a fortress at [[e:exeter|Exeter]]. When the army moved on, the town became Isca Dumnoniorum, capital of a self-governing civitas, though the countryside stayed little Romanised. The name survived in the post-[[s:roman-kingdom|Roman Kingdom]] of [[s:kingdom-of-dumnonia|Dumnonia]] and in the county name [[e:devon|Devon]].

dominion-of-india.t: Independent India's first constitutional form, a Commonwealth dominion that integrated the princely states and drafted the constitution of the republic.
dominion-of-india.o: Under the [[e:indian-independence-act-1947|Indian Independence Act]] of 1947, the [[s:british-raj|British Raj]] was partitioned, and on 15 August 1947 the [[e:dominion|Dominion]] of [[e:india|India]] was created with [[e:jawaharlal-nehru|Jawaharlal Nehru]] as prime minister. [[e:louis-mountbatten|Lord Mountbatten]] stayed on as Governor-General until 1948, succeeded by [[e:c-rajagopalachari|C. Rajagopalachari]], the only Indian to hold the post.
dominion-of-india.r: The dominion confronted partition violence and refugee resettlement, and fought the first war with the [[s:dominion-of-pakistan|Dominion of Pakistan]] over [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]]. [[e:vallabhbhai-patel|Vallabhbhai Patel]] and [[e:v-p-menon|V. P. Menon]] integrated more than five hundred [[e:princely-state|princely states]], using force against Hyderabad in 1948. [[e:mahatma-gandhi|Mahatma Gandhi]] was assassinated in January 1948. A Constituent Assembly chaired in drafting by [[e:b-r-ambedkar|B. R. Ambedkar]] wrote the new constitution.
dominion-of-india.e: The [[e:constitution-of-india|Constitution of India]] came into force on 26 January 1950, making [[e:india|India]] a sovereign republic within the Commonwealth and ending the British monarch's role as head of state. The dominion was succeeded by the [[s:republic-of-india|Republic of India]].

dali-kingdom.t: The Buddhist kingdom of the Duan family in Yunnan, which ruled the south-west for over three centuries until the Mongol conquest of 1253.
dali-kingdom.o: In 937 [[e:duan-siping|Duan Siping]], a commander of Bai descent from the Tonghai region, overthrew [[s:da-yining|Da Yining]] with the help of tribal allies from eastern [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]] and founded the Dali Kingdom, with its capital at [[e:yangjumie|Yangjumie]] near [[e:lake-erhai|Lake Erhai]].
dali-kingdom.r: Dali was a devoutly Buddhist state; esoteric Acharya [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] was strong, and many kings abdicated to become monks. From the late 11th century the [[e:gao|Gao]] family held hereditary office as chief ministers, and [[e:gao-shengtai|Gao Shengtai]] briefly took the throne in 1094 before the Duan were restored in 1096. Dali sold horses to the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]] and dominated routes to [[s:myanmar|Burma]].
dali-kingdom.e: In 1253 a Mongol army under [[e:kublai-khan|Kublai]] took the capital; the last king, [[e:duan-xingzhi|Duan Xingzhi]], fled but was captured in 1254 and submitted. The Duan family continued as hereditary governors under the [[s:yuan-dynasty|Yuan Dynasty]] until the [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]] conquered [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]] in 1382.

dutch-east-india-company-territories.t: The Asian empire of the Dutch East India Company, a trading firm that ruled ports and provinces from Batavia and controlled the world spice trade.
dutch-east-india-company-territories.o: The [[e:dutch-east-india-company|Dutch East India Company]] (VOC), chartered in 1602, appointed its first Governor-General, [[e:pieter-both|Pieter Both]], in 1610. In 1619 [[e:jan-pieterszoon-coen|Jan Pieterszoon Coen]] seized [[e:jakarta|Jayakarta]] and founded [[e:batavia|Batavia]] as its headquarters. The Company then conquered the [[e:banda-islands|Banda Islands]] in 1621, took [[e:malacca|Malacca]] from the Portuguese in 1641 and forced [[s:gowa-sultanate|Makassar]] into the [[e:treaty-of-bongaya|Treaty of Bongaya]] in 1667.
dutch-east-india-company-territories.r: [[e:batavia|Batavia]] was governed by the Governor-General and the [[e:council-of-the-indies|Council of the Indies]], answering to the [[e:heeren-xvii|Heeren XVII]] in [[e:amsterdam|Amsterdam]]. The Company enforced monopolies on [[e:nutmeg|nutmeg]], [[e:cloves|cloves]] and [[e:pepper|pepper]], used slave labour and forced deliveries, and intervened in the succession wars of the [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram Sultanate]], gaining much of [[e:java|Java]]. Batavia was a multi-ethnic city where Chinese settlers were massacred in 1740.
dutch-east-india-company-territories.e: Corruption, war and falling profits left the Company deeply indebted. It was nationalised by the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]] in 1796 and its charter expired on 31 December 1799, when its possessions passed to the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] state and became the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]].

dutch-malacca.t: Dutch-ruled Malacca, taken from Portugal in 1641, which guarded the Strait of Malacca for the Dutch East India Company for nearly two centuries.
dutch-malacca.o: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]], allied with the [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor Sultanate]], besieged [[s:portuguese-malacca|Portuguese Malacca]] for five months and captured it in January 1641. The Company wanted to secure the strait and divert trade to [[e:batavia|Batavia]] rather than revive [[e:malacca|Malacca]] as a great emporium, so the port was ruled as a fortified outpost.
dutch-malacca.r: A governor and council ran the city from the [[e:stadthuys|Stadthuys]], completed around 1660. [[e:malacca|Malacca]] checked shipping in the strait, bought [[e:tin|tin]] from [[s:perak-sultanate|Perak]] and other Malay states, and sold Indian cloth. Its population mixed [[e:dutch|Dutch]] officials, Portuguese Eurasians, Chinese, [[e:malays|Malays]] and Indians. [[e:jan-van-riebeeck|Jan van Riebeeck]], founder of [[e:cape-town|Cape Town]], governed it from 1662 to 1665.
dutch-malacca.e: British forces occupied [[e:malacca|Malacca]] in 1795 during the [[e:french-revolutionary-wars|French Revolutionary Wars]] and returned it in 1818. The [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824|Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824]] exchanged it for [[s:bencoolen|Bencoolen]], and after the handover in 1825 it became part of the [[s:straits-settlements|Straits Settlements]]. [[e:dutch|Dutch]] buildings still dominate its historic centre.

duchy-of-sorrento.t: Minor Byzantine-era duchy on the Sorrento peninsula, independent of Naples from the 9th century until the Normans took it in 1137.
duchy-of-sorrento.o: [[e:sorrento|Sorrento]], an old Roman town on the peninsula south of the [[e:bay-of-naples|Bay of Naples]], was part of the [[e:duchy-of-naples|Byzantine Duchy of Naples]]. In the 9th century, amid the conflicts with [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] [[e:benevento|Benevento]] and Arab raiders, it gained self-government under its own dukes, like neighbouring [[s:republic-of-amalfi|Amalfi]].
duchy-of-sorrento.r: Little is known of the duchy, which was small and overshadowed by [[e:naples|Naples]] and [[s:republic-of-amalfi|Amalfi]]. It ruled the western part of the peninsula and nearby islands, and its economy rested on fishing, farming and coastal trade. In 1039 [[e:guaimar-iv-of-salerno|Guaimar IV of Salerno]] seized it and gave it to his brother Guy, and it later passed among [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] and Norman lords.
duchy-of-sorrento.e: [[e:sorrento|Sorrento]] submitted to [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]] and was absorbed into the Norman [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]] by 1137, after which it was ruled as part of the kingdom's mainland territories.

duchy-of-rawa.t: A Masovian duchy in central Poland, one of the last Piast lands, incorporated into the Polish Crown in 1462.
duchy-of-rawa.o: After [[e:boleslaw-ii-of-masovia|Boleslaw II of Masovia]] died in 1313, his lands were divided among his sons, and [[e:siemowit-ii-of-masovia|Siemowit II]] received the southern part around Rawa. Over the next 150 years Rawa was repeatedly joined to and separated from the other Masovian duchies as the family's branches divided their inheritance.
duchy-of-rawa.r: Rawa was a modest farming land with a brick castle built under [[e:casimir-iii-the-great|Casimir III]]'s influence in the 14th century. Its dukes were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Polish Crown from 1351. [[e:siemowit-iii-of-masovia|Siemowit III]] reunited most of [[e:masovia|Masovia]] in the 1370s and issued laws for it, but it was divided again among his heirs, and Rawa was ruled by the Siemowit and Wladyslaw lines of [[s:duchy-of-plock|Plock]].
duchy-of-rawa.e: When Siemowit VI and [[e:wladyslaw-ii-of-plock|Wladyslaw II]], the last dukes of the line, died in 1462, [[e:casimir-iv-jagiellon|King Casimir IV]] took Rawa and [[e:gostynin|Gostynin]] into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569). The land became the [[e:rawa-voivodeship|Rawa Voivodeship]].

duchy-of-anhalt.t: Duchy that reunited the Anhalt lands in 1863 and became an industrial region on the Elbe and Saale.
duchy-of-anhalt.o: After the extinction of [[s:principality-of-anhalt-kothen|Anhalt-Köthen]] in 1847 and [[s:principality-of-anhalt-bernburg|Anhalt-Bernburg]] in 1863, Duke [[e:leopold-iv-duke-of-anhalt|Leopold IV Frederick]] of [[s:principality-of-anhalt-dessau|Anhalt-Dessau]] ruled all the [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]] territories. In 1863 they were formally combined as the Duchy of Anhalt, with [[e:dessau|Dessau]] as capital.
duchy-of-anhalt.r: [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]] was small but economically active, with [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] beet, lignite, potash and salt, and later chemical and engineering works. [[e:hugo-junkers|Hugo Junkers]] founded his first works at [[e:dessau|Dessau]] in 1895, later the base of the [[e:junkers|Junkers]] aircraft factory. A constitution of 1859, extended to the whole duchy, provided a diet. Anhalt joined the [[s:north-german-confederation|North German Confederation]] in 1867 and the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871.
duchy-of-anhalt.e: Duke [[e:joachim-ernst-duke-of-anhalt|Joachim Ernst]], a minor, abdicated through his regent in November 1918, and the duchy became the [[s:free-state-of-anhalt|Free State of Anhalt]]. After 1945 its territory was merged into [[e:saxony-anhalt|Saxony-Anhalt]], which still takes its name in part from the old duchy.

dikwa-emirate.t: A Kanuri emirate south of Lake Chad, carved out of the old Bornu lands that fell to German Kamerun, which joined Nigeria after the 1961 plebiscite.
dikwa-emirate.o: [[e:dikwa|Dikwa]] had been the capital of [[s:rabih-az-zubayrs-state|Rabih az-Zubayr]], the Sudanese warlord who conquered [[e:bornu|Bornu]] in 1893. After the French killed [[e:rabih-az-zubayr|Rabih]] in 1900, the European powers restored the al-Kanemi dynasty, but the old lands of the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]] were split by the borders of [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]], [[s:kamerun|Kamerun]] and [[e:chad|Chad]]. The part around Dikwa fell to [[e:germany|Germany]], where a separate shehu was installed.
dikwa-emirate.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] kept the Kanuri institutions of [[e:bornu|Bornu]]: a shehu with titled officials, district heads and Islamic courts. Under the Germans, and after 1916 under British rule in the [[e:northern-cameroons|Northern Cameroons]], it was administered through the shehu, with little development. Most people were Kanuri, [[e:shuwa-arabs|Shuwa Arab]] and other farmers and herders.
dikwa-emirate.e: In the 1961 plebiscite the [[e:northern-cameroons|Northern Cameroons]] voted to join [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]], and [[e:dikwa|Dikwa]] became part of [[e:northern-region-nigeria|Nigeria's Northern Region]], joining its Kanuri kin in the [[s:borno-emirate|Borno Emirate]]. The [[e:emirate|emirate]] survives as a traditional institution in [[e:borno-state|Borno State]].

danishmendids.t: A Turkish dynasty of central and north-eastern Anatolia that rivalled the Seljuks of Rum and inspired the epic of Danishmend Gazi.
danishmendids.o: After the Seljuk victory at [[e:battle-of-manzikert|Manzikert]] in 1071, a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] leader known as [[e:danishmend-gazi|Danishmend Gazi]], whose origins are obscure, conquered [[e:sivas|Sivas]], [[e:tokat|Tokat]], [[e:niksar|Niksar]], [[e:amasya|Amasya]] and later [[s:melid|Malatya]], founding one of the first Turkish principalities in [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].
danishmendids.r: The Danishmendids ruled a largely Christian population of [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and [[e:armenians|Armenians]] through [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] warriors and a growing urban Muslim elite. In 1100 [[e:danishmend-gazi|Danishmend Gazi]] captured [[e:bohemond-i-of-antioch|Bohemond of Antioch]], and his son [[e:gumustekin-gazi|Gazi Gumushtigin]] was for a time the strongest ruler in [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], receiving the title malik from the [[e:caliphate|caliph]]. They built mosques and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]] in [[e:tokat|Tokat]], [[e:niksar|Niksar]] and [[e:kayseri|Kayseri]]. Their deeds were later celebrated in the [[e:danishmendname|Danishmendname]], a Turkish epic of holy war.
danishmendids.e: After the death of [[e:yagibasan|Yagibasan]] in 1164 the family split and weakened. [[e:kilij-arslan-ii|Kilij Arslan II]] of the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]] annexed [[e:sivas|Sivas]] around 1174 and the [[s:melid|Malatya]] branch in 1178, ending the dynasty.

duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.t: The Farnese duchy in Emilia, later held by Bourbons and by Napoleon's widow Marie Louise, which lasted until Italian unification.
duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.o: In 1545 [[e:pope-paul-iii|Pope Paul III]] detached [[s:commune-of-parma|Parma]] and [[s:commune-of-piacenza|Piacenza]] from the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] and gave them to his son [[e:pier-luigi-farnese|Pier Luigi Farnese]], already Duke of [[s:duchy-of-castro|Castro]]. Pier Luigi was murdered in 1547 by nobles backed by the imperial governor of [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]].
duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.r: The Farnese built a court at [[s:commune-of-parma|Parma]], with the [[e:palazzo-della-pilotta|Pilotta]] palace and the wooden [[e:teatro-farnese|Teatro Farnese]] of 1618. [[e:alessandro-farnese-duke-of-parma|Alessandro Farnese]], [[e:spain|Spain's]] general in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]], was its most famous duke. When the Farnese died out in 1731, [[e:elisabeth-farnese|Elisabeth Farnese]], queen of Spain, passed the duchy to her son [[e:charles-iii-of-spain|Charles of Bourbon]]. After Austrian rule from 1735, [[e:philip-duke-of-parma|Philip of Bourbon]] founded the [[e:house-of-bourbon-parma|Bourbon-Parma]] line in 1748, with reforming minister [[e:guillaume-du-tillot|Guillaume du Tillot]].
duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.e: [[e:france|France]] annexed the duchy in 1802. In 1814 it went to [[e:marie-louise-duchess-of-parma|Marie Louise]], [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] widow, who ruled until 1847, then back to the [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbons]]. In 1859 it joined the [[s:united-provinces-of-central-italy|United Provinces of Central Italy]] and was annexed to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] in 1860.

duchy-of-bytom.t: Upper Silesian Piast duchy whose first duke became the first Silesian prince to pay homage to the King of Bohemia, in 1289.
duchy-of-bytom.o: When [[e:wladyslaw-of-opole|Władysław of Opole]] died in 1281, his lands were divided among his sons. Casimir received [[e:bytom|Bytom]], an old market town in eastern [[e:upper-silesia|Upper Silesia]], together with lands around [[e:gliwice|Gliwice]] and [[e:kozle|Koźle]]. In 1289 he paid homage to [[e:wenceslaus-ii-of-bohemia|Wenceslaus II of Bohemia]], the first Silesian duke to accept Bohemian overlordship.
duchy-of-bytom.r: The duchy was small, with farmland, forests and early [[e:silver|silver]] and lead mining around [[e:bytom|Bytom]]. Casimir's son Władysław ruled it in the early 14th century, and later dukes divided it into smaller shares. The population was largely Polish-speaking, with German settlers in the towns.
duchy-of-bytom.e: After the [[e:bytom|Bytom]] line died out in 1355, the duchy was divided between the dukes of [[e:olesnica|Oleśnica]] and [[e:cieszyn|Cieszyn]] and later fragmented further, with parts passing among Silesian princes until the end of the 15th century. It eventually came under the Bohemian crown, and Bytom is now in [[e:poland|Poland]].

duchy-of-styria.t: Alpine duchy of Graz and the Erzberg iron mountain, a Habsburg land for over six centuries and the shield of Inner Austria against the Ottomans.
duchy-of-styria.o: The March of [[e:styria|Styria]] grew from a Carolingian border zone ruled from the 11th century by the [[e:otakars|Otakar]] counts of [[e:steyr|Steyr]]. In 1180 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Emperor Frederick Barbarossa]] raised it to a duchy for [[e:ottokar-iv-of-styria|Ottokar IV]]. By the [[e:georgenberg-pact|Georgenberg Pact]] of 1186 it passed to the [[e:house-of-babenberg|Babenbergs]] of the [[s:duchy-of-austria|Duchy of Austria]] in 1192, and after [[e:ottokar-ii-of-bohemia|Ottokar II of Bohemia]] it came to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in 1282.
duchy-of-styria.r: [[e:styria|Styria]] was governed by its dukes with strong estates meeting in the [[e:landhaus-graz|Landhaus]] at [[e:graz|Graz]]. Iron from the [[e:erzberg|Erzberg]] made it an industrial heartland. From 1564 Graz was capital of [[s:inner-austria|Inner Austria]] under Archduke [[e:charles-ii-archduke-of-austria|Charles II]], who invited the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]]; his son [[e:ferdinand-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Ferdinand II]] expelled Protestants. Repeated Ottoman raids made defence a constant concern. German was spoken in the north and Slovene in [[e:lower-styria|Lower Styria]].
duchy-of-styria.e: [[e:styria|Styria]] remained a crown land of the [[s:habsburg-monarchy|Habsburg Monarchy]] and [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] until 1918. It was then divided: [[e:lower-styria|Lower Styria]] with [[e:maribor|Maribor]] went to the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes]] and is now in [[e:slovenia|Slovenia]], while the rest became the Austrian state of Styria.
