duchy-of-zagan.t: Silesian duchy that passed from the Piasts to the Wettins, Wallenstein and the Lobkowicz, and where Johannes Kepler worked for a time.
duchy-of-zagan.o: [[e:zagan|Żagań]], in north-western [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], became the seat of a separate duchy in the division of the [[e:glogow|Głogów]] lands after 1274. It was ruled by branches of the [[e:piast-dynasty|Głogów Piasts]], who accepted Bohemian overlordship in the 1320s and 1330s, and Żagań grew as a market town with a large Augustinian abbey.
duchy-of-zagan.r: The [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] dukes ruled until the turbulent [[e:jan-ii-the-mad|Jan II the Mad]] sold [[e:zagan|Żagań]] to the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettins of Saxony]] in 1472. It later returned to the Bohemian crown and in 1628 was granted to the general [[e:albrecht-von-wallenstein|Albrecht von Wallenstein]], who brought [[e:johannes-kepler|Johannes Kepler]] there. From 1646 the [[e:house-of-lobkowicz|Lobkowicz family]] held it, building a baroque palace.
duchy-of-zagan.e: In 1742 [[e:zagan|Żagań]] passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], and in 1786 the [[e:house-of-lobkowicz|Lobkowicz]] sold it to [[e:peter-von-biron|Peter von Biron]], Duke of [[e:courland|Courland]]. His daughter [[e:dorothea-von-biron|Dorothea]] later held it as Duchess of Sagan. The town has been Polish since 1945.

duchy-of-romagna.t: Cesare Borgia's brief state in Romagna, carved out with papal backing and studied by Machiavelli as a model of ruthless princely power.
duchy-of-romagna.o: Between 1499 and 1501 [[e:cesare-borgia|Cesare Borgia]], son of [[e:pope-alexander-vi|Pope Alexander VI]], conquered the small lordships of [[e:romagna|Romagna]] and the [[e:marche|Marche]], including [[e:imola|Imola]], Forlì, [[s:lordship-of-pesaro|Pesaro]], [[s:lordship-of-rimini|Rimini]] and [[s:lordship-of-faenza|Faenza]], with French and papal troops. In 1501 his father named him Duke of Romagna, with [[e:cesena|Cesena]] as the seat of government.
duchy-of-romagna.r: [[e:cesare-borgia|Cesare]] imposed order on a region torn by petty lords, setting up a central court of justice, the Rota, at [[e:cesena|Cesena]]. He sent his harsh governor [[e:ramiro-de-lorqua|Ramiro de Lorca]] to pacify the region, then had him executed in the square of Cesena in December 1502 to win popularity. At [[e:sena-gallica|Senigallia]] that month he trapped and killed rebellious captains. [[e:niccolo-machiavelli|Niccolò Machiavelli]], a Florentine envoy, observed him closely and later praised his methods in [[e:the-prince|The Prince]].
duchy-of-romagna.e: [[e:pope-alexander-vi|Alexander VI]] died in August 1503 while [[e:cesare-borgia|Cesare]] was gravely ill. [[e:pope-julius-ii|Pope Julius II]], a [[e:house-of-borgia|Borgia]] enemy, reclaimed the towns for the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], while [[e:venice|Venice]] seized [[s:lordship-of-rimini|Rimini]] and [[s:lordship-of-faenza|Faenza]].

duchy-of-urbino.t: The Montefeltro and della Rovere state in the Marche, whose ducal palace and court made Urbino a model of Renaissance civility.
duchy-of-urbino.o: The [[e:house-of-montefeltro|Montefeltro]] family, lords of a mountainous area on the borders of [[e:romagna|Romagna]] and the [[e:marche|Marche]], received Urbino as counts in the early 13th century; the register dates the county from 1213. They ruled as papal vicars and condottieri.
duchy-of-urbino.r: [[e:federico-da-montefeltro|Federico da Montefeltro]], a famous [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] captain, was made duke in 1474 and built the Ducal Palace and a celebrated library. His son [[e:guidobaldo-da-montefeltro|Guidobaldo]]'s court inspired Baldassare Castiglione's [[e:the-book-of-the-courtier|Book of the Courtier]], and [[e:raphael|Raphael]] was born in the city in 1483. In 1508 the duchy passed to [[e:francesco-maria-i-della-rovere|Francesco Maria I della Rovere]], nephew of [[e:pope-julius-ii|Pope Julius II]], and from 1523 [[s:lordship-of-pesaro|Pesaro]] became the main residence. The duchy was also known for maiolica.
duchy-of-urbino.e: [[e:francesco-maria-ii-della-rovere|Francesco Maria II della Rovere]] died without a male heir in 1631, and the duchy, already promised by agreement, devolved to the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], which ruled it until 1860.

dilaiyya.t: A Sufi lodge in the Middle Atlas that grew into a Berber state, ruling much of northern Morocco during the collapse of the Saadis.
dilaiyya.o: Around 1566 [[e:abu-bakr-ibn-muhammad|Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad]] al-Majati founded a zawiya at Dila in the [[e:middle-atlas|Middle Atlas]], among [[e:sanhaja|Sanhaja Berber]] tribes. It became a renowned centre of [[e:sufism|Sufi]] teaching and scholarship, attracting students and gifts, and grew wealthy and influential as the [[s:saadi-sultanate|Saadi Sultanate]] weakened after 1603.
dilaiyya.r: Under Muhammad al-[[e:hajj|Hajj]], from 1636, the zawiya became a political power. Its [[e:berbers|Berber]] forces defeated the [[s:marabout-state-of-al-ayyashi|Marabout state of al-Ayyashi]] in 1641, took [[e:fez|Fez]] and [[e:meknes|Meknes]] and controlled the [[s:republic-of-sale|Republic of Salé]]. The Dila'iyya combined religious prestige, tribal alliances and trade, and their lodge was famous for its library and teachers.
dilaiyya.e: The rising [[s:alaouite-sultanate|Alaouite Sultanate]] under [[e:al-rashid-of-morocco|Moulay al-Rashid]] defeated the Dila'iyya in 1668 and destroyed the zawiya, dispersing its family to [[e:fez|Fez]] and [[e:tlemcen|Tlemcen]]. Moroccan unity was restored under the [[e:alaouite-dynasty|Alaouites]].

duchy-of-friuli.t: The first Lombard duchy in Italy, a frontier march at Cividale guarding the north-eastern passes against Avars and Slavs.
duchy-of-friuli.o: When the [[e:lombards|Lombards]] entered [[e:italy|Italy]] in 568, [[e:alboin|King Alboin]] left his nephew [[e:gisulf-i-of-friuli|Gisulf]] at [[e:cividale-del-friuli|Forum Iulii]] (Cividale del [[e:friuli|Friuli]]) with chosen warrior families to hold the passes from the Julian [[e:alps|Alps]]. It became the first [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] duchy, and the name Friuli comes from Forum Iulii.
duchy-of-friuli.r: The dukes of [[e:friuli|Friuli]] were warrior frontier lords, often fighting the [[e:avars|Avars]] and [[e:slavs|Slavs]] to the east. In 610 the Avars sacked [[e:cividale-del-friuli|Cividale]] and killed Duke [[e:gisulf-ii-of-friuli|Gisulf II]]. The historian [[e:paul-the-deacon|Paul the Deacon]] came from a Friulian family. Duke [[e:ratchis|Ratchis]] became king in 744; the altar he commissioned and the [[e:tempietto-longobardo|Tempietto Longobardo]] in Cividale are masterpieces of [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] art. The patriarchs of [[e:aquileia|Aquileia]] also resided at Cividale.
duchy-of-friuli.e: After [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] conquered the [[s:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard Kingdom]], Duke [[e:hrodgaud|Hrodgaud of Friuli]] rebelled in 776 and was killed. Charlemagne replaced him with Frankish counts, and the territory became the [[s:march-of-friuli|March of Friuli]].

delphi.t: Sanctuary-state of Apollo on Mount Parnassus, whose oracle was consulted for centuries by Greek cities and foreign kings.
delphi.o: Delphi lies on the slopes of [[e:mount-parnassus|Mount Parnassus]] above the [[e:pleistos|Pleistos]] valley. A cult of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] was established there by the 8th century BCE, and the oracle quickly gained renown, sanctioning colonies across the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]]. The small town of Delphi grew up to serve the sanctuary.
delphi.r: The Delphians ran the shrine and the [[e:pythia|Pythia]], [[e:apollo|Apollo's]] priestess, who gave the oracles. The Amphictyony, a council of neighbouring peoples, protected the sanctuary, and in the [[e:first-sacred-war|First Sacred War]] c. 595 BCE it destroyed [[e:kirrha|Kirrha]]. The Pythian Games were reorganised in 586 BCE. Cities built treasuries along the Sacred Way, and the [[e:alcmaeonidae|Alcmaeonids]] rebuilt the temple after 548 BCE.
delphi.e: The [[s:phocian-league|Phocian League]] seized Delphi in the [[e:third-sacred-war|Third Sacred War]] of 356 to 346 BCE, and the [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]] later dominated it. [[e:rome|Rome]] freed Delphi in 191 BCE, and it lost independence by 146 BCE. The oracle declined under Roman rule and closed in the late 4th century CE.

duchy-of-guelders.t: A river principality on the Rhine, Maas and IJssel whose dukes resisted Burgundian and Habsburg rule until 1543.
duchy-of-guelders.o: Around 1096 [[e:gerard-i-of-guelders|Gerard of Wassenberg]] was first styled count of Guelders, after a castle near [[e:geldern|Geldern]]. His family added [[s:county-of-zutphen|Zutphen]] through marriage around 1138 and moved their centre north to the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] and [[e:veluwe|Veluwe]]. [[e:nijmegen|Nijmegen]], [[e:roermond|Roermond]], [[e:arnhem|Arnhem]] and Zutphen became the four quarters of the territory.
duchy-of-guelders.r: The counts expanded steadily, though [[e:reginald-i-count-of-guelders|Reinald I]] lost the battle of [[e:battle-of-worringen|Worringen]] in 1288. [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Louis IV]] made [[e:reginald-ii-duke-of-guelders|Reinald II]] a duke in 1339. Guelders was a land of river tolls, farming and Hanseatic towns. After the house of Egmond took power, [[e:charles-the-bold|Charles the Bold]] bought the duchy in 1473, but [[e:charles-ii-duke-of-guelders|Charles of Egmond]] won it back and fought the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] for decades.
duchy-of-guelders.e: Duke [[e:william-duke-of-julich-cleves-berg|William of Cleves]] lost the duchy to [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] and ceded it by the [[e:treaty-of-venlo|Treaty of Venlo]] in 1543, joining it to the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]]. In the [[e:dutch-revolt|Dutch Revolt]] it split: the northern quarters joined the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]], while [[e:upper-guelders|Upper Guelders]] around [[e:roermond|Roermond]] stayed Spanish.

duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz.t: Piast duchy of Upper Silesia that emerged from the division of Silesia and held off the Mongols in 1241 before splitting into four.
duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz.o: After the partition of the Polish realm, [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] was held by the sons of [[e:wladyslaw-ii-the-exile|Władysław II the Exile]]. In 1172 his son [[e:mieszko-iv-tanglefoot|Mieszko IV Tanglefoot]] received a separate share around [[e:raciborz|Racibórz]], the core of [[e:upper-silesia|Upper Silesia]]. In 1202 he added the [[e:opole|Opole]] district, creating a duchy independent of the Lower Silesian Duchy of Silesia.
duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz.r: The Upper Silesian [[e:piast-dynasty|Piasts]] ruled a largely Polish-speaking land of forests, farmland and river towns on the upper [[e:oder-river|Oder]]. [[e:casimir-i-of-opole|Kazimierz I]] and his successors brought in German settlers and granted town charters under German law, founding or refounding places such as [[e:opole|Opole]] and [[e:raciborz|Racibórz]]. During the Mongol invasion of 1241, [[e:mieszko-ii-the-fat|Mieszko II the Fat]] fought the raiders near Racibórz and Opole.
duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz.e: When Duke Władysław died in 1281, his four sons divided the duchy into the Duchies of [[e:opole|Opole]], [[e:raciborz|Racibórz]], [[e:bytom|Bytom]] and [[e:cieszyn|Cieszyn]]. These Upper Silesian duchies drifted towards the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]] and accepted Bohemian overlordship in 1327.

dongou.t: A small Yue kingdom in southern Zhejiang, ruled by a descendant of Goujian, whose people asked to be resettled in China after a Minyue attack in 138 BCE.
dongou.o: [[e:zou-yao|Zou Yao]], like the rulers of [[s:minyue|Minyue]] a descendant of [[e:goujian|King Goujian]] of the [[s:state-of-yue|State of Yue]], helped the Han against [[e:xiang-yu|Xiang Yu]]. In 192 BCE Emperor Hui of Han made him King of Donghai, known from its capital as Dong'ou, near modern [[e:wenzhou|Wenzhou]] in southern [[e:zhejiang|Zhejiang]].
dongou.r: Dong'ou was a small coastal kingdom of Yue fishermen and farmers that relied on Han patronage. It took part in the Rebellion of the Seven States in 154 BCE but then killed the rebel king of Wu at Han urging. Little else is recorded of its government.
dongou.e: When [[s:minyue|Minyue]] besieged Dong'ou in 138 BCE, a Han fleet came to its aid. Fearing further attacks, Dong'ou asked to move into Han territory, and some 40,000 people were resettled between the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] and the Huai, ending the kingdom.

duchy-of-alsace.t: Frankish frontier duchy between the Vosges and the Rhine, ruled by the Etichonid family whose saint, Odile, is the patron of Alsace.
duchy-of-alsace.o: In the mid 7th century the Merovingian kings of [[s:austrasia|Austrasia]] set up a duchy in [[e:alsace|Alsace]] to control the border with the [[s:alemanni|Alemanni]]. The first known duke was Gundoin, and from around 662 power passed to [[e:adalrich-duke-of-alsace|Adalric]], also called Eticho, founder of the [[e:etichonids|Etichonid]] dynasty.
duchy-of-alsace.r: The dukes governed from their estates around [[s:free-imperial-city-of-obernai|Obernai]] and founded many monasteries. [[e:adalrich-duke-of-alsace|Adalric]]'s daughter [[e:saint-odile|Odile]] founded the convent of Hohenburg on the mountain now called [[e:mont-sainte-odile|Mont Sainte-Odile]], and his descendants endowed abbeys such as Honau and Murbach.
duchy-of-alsace.e: Around 740, after the death of Duke Liutfrid, the Carolingian mayors abolished the duchy, which had grown too independent, and divided [[e:alsace|Alsace]] into two counties, the [[e:nordgau|Nordgau]] and the [[e:sundgau|Sundgau]]. The [[e:etichonids|Etichonid]] family remained powerful and gave rise to several later noble houses.

duchy-of-mecklenburg-strelitz.t: The smaller of the two Mecklenburg states, a quiet grand duchy whose princesses became queens of Britain and Prussia.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-strelitz.o: The Treaty of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-hamburg|Hamburg]] in 1701 ended a succession dispute by creating Mecklenburg-[[e:strelitz|Strelitz]] for [[e:adolf-frederick-ii-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Adolf Frederick II]] from the eastern [[e:lordship-of-stargard|Stargard]] lands and the detached [[s:principality-of-ratzeburg|Principality of Ratzeburg]]. After Strelitz palace burned in 1712, [[e:adolphus-frederick-iii-duke-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Adolf Frederick III]] founded the planned town of [[e:neustrelitz|Neustrelitz]] in 1733 as the new residence.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-strelitz.r: The duchy shared Mecklenburg's estates and its feudal constitution of 1755, so the knights retained great power and no modern constitution was adopted. It was rural, poor and Lutheran. [[e:charlotte-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz]] married [[e:george-iii|George III]] of [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Great Britain]] in 1761, and her niece [[e:louise-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Louise]] became Queen of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and a national heroine. The state became a grand duchy in 1815.
duchy-of-mecklenburg-strelitz.e: Mecklenburg-[[e:strelitz|Strelitz]] joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871. [[e:adolphus-frederick-vi-grand-duke-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Grand Duke Adolf Frederick VI]] died by suicide in February 1918, leaving no clear successor, and after the November revolution it became the [[s:free-state-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Free State of Mecklenburg-Strelitz]].

duchy-of-silesia.t: The Piast duchy of Silesia, created by the partition of Poland in 1138, which opened the region to German settlement and split into many small duchies.
duchy-of-silesia.o: By the testament of [[e:boleslaw-iii-wrymouth|Bolesław III Wrymouth]] in 1138, [[e:poland|Poland]] was divided among his sons, and Silesia, with its capital at [[e:wroclaw|Wrocław]], went to the eldest, [[e:wladyslaw-ii-the-exile|Władysław II the Exile]]. Expelled in 1146, he fled to the Empire; his sons returned in 1163 with the support of [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] and ruled Silesia as a separate duchy.
duchy-of-silesia.r: [[e:henry-the-bearded|Henry I the Bearded]] and his wife [[e:hedwig-of-silesia|Saint Hedwig]] invited German settlers, founded towns under German law and monasteries such as [[e:trzebnica|Trzebnica]]. Henry I and [[e:henry-ii-the-pious|Henry II the Pious]] tried to reunite [[e:poland|Poland]]. Henry II was killed fighting the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] at the [[e:battle-of-legnica|Battle of Legnica]] in 1241, a disaster for the duchy.
duchy-of-silesia.e: After [[e:henry-ii-the-pious|Henry II]]'s death his sons divided Silesia in 1248, the start of its fragmentation into numerous small [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] duchies. In the 14th century these accepted the overlordship of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]], and Silesia passed later to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and, in 1742, to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].

duan-xianbei.t: A Xianbei tribal state in the Liaoxi region that allied with the Jin against the Xiongnu and was ground down by Later Zhao and the Murong.
duan-xianbei.o: The Duan traced their rise to Riluzhuan, a man sold as a slave to the [[s:wuhuan|Wuhuan]] who gathered a band of followers in the Liaoxi region. By the late 3rd century his descendants led a powerful [[s:xianbei|Xianbei confederation]] based at Lingzhi, near modern [[e:qianan|Qian'an]] in [[e:hebei|Hebei]], on the north-eastern frontier of the [[s:western-jin|Western Jin]].
duan-xianbei.r: The Duan were cavalry herders under hereditary chiefs who married into the family of the Jin governor [[e:wang-jun-pengzu|Wang Jun]] and fought for him against [[s:han-zhao|Han Zhao]]. Their power depended on alliances and plunder. In 318 the chief [[e:duan-pidi|Duan Pidi]] killed the loyalist Jin general [[e:liu-kun|Liu Kun]], an act widely condemned.
duan-xianbei.e: [[s:later-zhao|Later Zhao]], allied with the [[e:murong-xianbei|Murong]] of [[s:former-yan|Former Yan]], crushed the Duan at Lingzhi in 338. A remnant under [[e:duan-kan|Duan Kan]] ruled the area around Guanggu in [[e:shandong|Shandong]] until [[e:former-yan|Former Yan]] conquered it in 356 to 357, after which the Duan merged with other [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] groups.

duchy-of-saxe-jena.t: Brief Ernestine duchy centred on the university town of Jena, carved out for a younger Weimar prince and gone within two decades.
duchy-of-saxe-jena.o: Duke [[e:william-duke-of-saxe-weimar|William of Saxe-Weimar]] died in 1662 and his lands were divided among his sons. In 1672, after a further rearrangement following the extinction of Saxe-[[e:altenburg|Altenburg]], Bernhard received [[e:jena|Jena]] and its surroundings as the Duchy of Saxe-Jena.
duchy-of-saxe-jena.r: Bernhard ruled from [[e:jena|Jena]], rebuilding the castle there and maintaining a modest Lutheran court. The [[e:university-of-jena|University of Jena]], founded in 1558, was shared among the Ernestine dukes and remained the town's main institution. The duchy was too small to pursue an independent policy and relied on its larger Ernestine relatives.
duchy-of-saxe-jena.e: Bernhard died in 1678 and his only son John William died as a child in 1690. The duchy was then divided between the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-eisenach|Duchy of Saxe-Eisenach]] and Saxe-[[e:weimar|Weimar]], with [[e:jena|Jena]] itself eventually going to Weimar.

dai-sixteen-kingdoms.t: The Tuoba Xianbei principality on the Inner Mongolian frontier that the Former Qin destroyed in 376 and that was reborn ten years later as the Northern Wei.
dai-sixteen-kingdoms.o: The [[e:tuoba|Tuoba]] were a [[s:xianbei|Xianbei confederation]] who moved into the area of modern [[e:hohhot|Hohhot]]. Their chief [[e:tuoba-yilu|Tuoba Yilu]] helped the Jin general [[e:liu-kun|Liu Kun]] against [[s:han-zhao|Han Zhao]], and in return the [[s:western-jin|Western Jin]] made him Duke of Dai in 310 and Prince of Dai in 315. His centre was [[e:shengle|Shengle]], near modern [[e:horinger|Horinger]] in [[e:inner-mongolia|Inner Mongolia]].
dai-sixteen-kingdoms.r: Dai remained a tribal confederation of herders, although Chinese advisers and captives brought farming and writing. [[e:tuoba-shiyijian|Tuoba Shiyijian]], who had spent years as a hostage at the [[s:later-zhao|Later Zhao]] court, created officials, written laws and a more settled capital during his long reign from 338.
dai-sixteen-kingdoms.e: In 376 the [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]] ruler [[e:fu-jian-337-385|Fu Jian]] invaded, Shiyijian died amid family violence, and Dai was divided. After Former [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] collapsed, his grandson [[e:emperor-daowu-of-northern-wei|Tuoba Gui]] restored Dai in 386 and soon renamed it the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]], which reunified northern [[e:china|China]].

darini.t: People of north-east Ireland recorded by Ptolemy, sometimes linked with the Dáirine of early Irish genealogies.
darini.o: [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 lists the Darini in north-east Ireland, inland or on the coast between the [[s:robogdii|Robogdii]] and the [[s:voluntii|Voluntii]], in what is now [[e:county-antrim|County Antrim]] or north Down. Like his other Irish names, this information came from earlier seafarers' reports and is hard to locate precisely.
darini.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or society from classical sources. Some scholars connect the name with the Dáirine, descendants of a legendary ancestor Dáire, a grouping that in Irish tradition includes the ruling families of the [[s:iverni|Érainn]] and of [[s:dal-fiatach|Dal Fiatach]] in [[s:northern-ireland|Ulster]], though the link is uncertain.
darini.e: The Darini disappear from the written record after Ptolemy. Their region later lay within the territories of the [[s:kingdom-of-ulaid|Kingdom of Ulaid]] and the [[s:dal-naraidi|Dal nAraidi]].

duchy-of-surabaya.t: The leading Muslim coastal state of East Java in the 16th and early 17th centuries, which resisted Sultan Agung of Mataram until 1625.
duchy-of-surabaya.o: Surabaya, at the mouth of the [[e:brantas-river|Brantas River]], grew as a Muslim port in the late 15th century as [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]] declined. Its rulers, styled adipati or duke, were allied with [[s:demak-sultanate|Demak]] and after Demak's fall became the leaders of a league of East Javanese coastal states.
duchy-of-surabaya.r: Surabaya controlled the trade of the [[e:brantas-river|Brantas]] valley and the eastern [[e:java-sea|Java Sea]], with links to [[e:banjarmasin|Banjarmasin]], Sukadana and the spice islands. Its rulers claimed descent from [[e:sunan-ampel|Sunan Ampel]]. At its height in the early 17th century it held influence over [[e:gresik|Gresik]], Sedayu and parts of [[e:borneo|Borneo]].
duchy-of-surabaya.e: [[e:sultan-agung|Sultan Agung of Mataram]] conquered the coastal allies one by one and besieged Surabaya for years, finally damming the [[e:brantas-river|Brantas]] to cut off its water. In 1625 Duke Jayalengkara surrendered. His son [[e:pangeran-pekik|Pangeran Pekik]] later served [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]] and married Agung's sister.

despotate-of-epirus.t: Byzantine Greek successor state in north-western Greece founded after 1204, a rival of Nicaea that passed through Greek, Italian and Serbian dynasties.
despotate-of-epirus.o: After the [[e:fourth-crusade|Fourth Crusade]], [[e:michael-i-komnenos-doukas|Michael Komnenos Doukas]], a relative of the [[e:angelos-dynasty|Angelos]] emperors, took control of [[e:epirus|Epirus]] around 1205, ruling from Arta. His half-brother Theodore expanded the state, taking [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]] in 1224 and creating the [[s:empire-of-thessalonica|Empire of Thessalonica]], until his defeat by the [[e:bulgarians|Bulgarians]] at [[e:battle-of-klokotnitsa|Klokotnitsa]] in 1230. The title despot was given to later rulers.
despotate-of-epirus.r: The rulers kept Byzantine administration and [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] church structures and claimed the imperial heritage against the [[s:empire-of-nicaea|Empire of Nicaea]]. Arta flourished, with churches such as the [[e:panagia-parigoritissa|Panagia Parigoritissa]]. [[e:michael-ii-komnenos-doukas|Michael II]] allied with the [[e:latins|Latins]] against [[e:nicaea|Nicaea]] but was defeated at [[e:battle-of-pelagonia|Pelagonia]] in 1259. The Orsini of [[e:kefalonia|Cephalonia]] took over in 1318.
despotate-of-epirus.e: [[s:serbia|Serbia]] under [[e:stefan-dusan|Stefan Dushan]] annexed [[e:epirus|Epirus]] in 1348. [[e:carlo-i-tocco|Carlo I Tocco]] reunited [[e:ioannina|Ioannina]] and Arta from 1411, but the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] took Ioannina in 1430, Arta in 1449 and the last fortresses in 1479.

donghu.t: The Eastern Hu nomads of Inner Mongolia and Manchuria, crushed by the Xiongnu leader Modu around 206 BCE; their survivors became the Wuhuan and Xianbei.
donghu.o: Chinese sources use Donghu, the Eastern Hu, for pastoral peoples living east of the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] in eastern [[e:inner-mongolia|Inner Mongolia]] and western [[e:liaoning|Liaoning]] from about the 7th century BCE. Archaeologists often link them with the Upper Xiajiadian culture, though the connection is debated.
donghu.r: They were a confederation of herding tribes with cavalry strong enough to raid the [[s:state-of-yan|State of Yan]], until the Yan general [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] Kai drove them back around 300 BCE and Yan built walls against them. Nothing is known of their language or rulers' names.
donghu.e: According to the [[e:records-of-the-grand-historian|Records of the Grand Historian]], the Donghu demanded [[e:modu-chanyu|Modu's]] best horse, then one of his wives, then land; Modu granted the first two and answered the third by destroying them. The survivors fled to the [[s:wuhuan|Wuhuan]] and [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] mountains and gave their names to the Wuhuan and the [[e:xianbei|Xianbei]].

der.t: A frontier city between Mesopotamia and Elam, guarding the road to the Iranian highlands and sacred to the god Ishtaran.
der.o: Der, modern Tell Aqar near [[e:badra-iraq|Badra]], lay at the foot of the [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]] on the main route from the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] to [[e:susa|Susa]]. It was a city from the third millennium BCE and a province of the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]]. After Ur collapsed around 2000 BCE, local rulers governed it independently.
der.r: Der was a small buffer state whose position made it valuable to [[e:elam|Elam]], [[s:eshnunna|Eshnunna]] and the cities of the south. Its patron god [[e:ishtaran|Ishtaran]], a judge deity represented by a serpent, was worshipped in the temple E-dimgalkalama. A local king, [[e:anum-muttabbil|Anum-muttabbil]], claimed in an inscription to have smitten Elam, [[s:kingdom-of-anshan|Anshan]] and [[s:shimashki-dynasty|Shimashki]], the clearest sign of the city's independent ambitions. Otherwise its rulers are poorly known.
der.e: Der lost its independence in the 18th century BCE, falling to [[s:eshnunna|Eshnunna]] and then to [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi's]] [[s:babylonian-empire|Babylonian Empire]]. It remained an important border fortress: in 720 BCE the [[e:battle-of-der|Battle of Der]] was fought there between [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] and the [[e:elamites|Elamites]].

denianke-kingdom.t: Fulani kingdom of the Senegal valley founded by the warlord Koli Tenguella, known to the Portuguese as the Great Fulo.
denianke-kingdom.o: Around 1490 the [[e:fula|Fulani]] leader [[e:koli-tenguella|Koli Tenguella]] led a mass migration of herders and warriors from the south-eastern highlands toward the [[e:senegal|Senegal]] river. After campaigns against the declining [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] and its neighbours, he conquered [[s:imamate-of-futa-toro|Futa Toro]], the old land of the [[s:kingdom-of-takrur|Kingdom of Takrur]], and founded a dynasty whose rulers bore the title Satigi.
denianke-kingdom.r: The Denianke kings were warrior rulers whose power rested on cavalry and [[e:fula|Fulani]] clan support. Their [[e:islam|Islam]] was considered lax by the Muslim scholars of [[s:imamate-of-futa-toro|Futa Toro]], the [[e:toroodbe|Torodbe]], who resented heavy taxes and the rulers' failure to protect villagers from enslavement. In the 18th century Moroccan and Moorish forces intervened repeatedly in succession disputes.
denianke-kingdom.e: In 1776 a clerical revolution led by [[e:sulayman-bal|Sulayman Bal]] and [[e:abdul-kader-kan|Abdul Kader Kan]] overthrew the Denianke and founded the [[s:imamate-of-futa-toro|Imamate of Futa Toro]], one of [[e:west-africa|West Africa's]] first Islamic reform states. Epic songs about [[e:samba-gelaajo-jeegi|Samba Gelaajo Jeegi]], a Denianke prince, remain popular in [[e:pulaar|Pulaar]] oral literature.

duchy-of-berg.t: A Rhineland duchy east of the Rhine with its capital at Düsseldorf, which became part of the Jülich lands and later a Napoleonic grand duchy.
duchy-of-berg.o: Count Adolf of Berg appears in 1101 with a castle on the Dhün river; the family later built [[e:schloss-burg|Burg Castle]] on the [[e:wupper|Wupper]]. [[e:engelbert-ii-of-berg|Engelbert I of Berg]], Archbishop of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]], was murdered in 1225. In 1288 Count Adolf V helped defeat the archbishop at [[e:battle-of-worringen|Worringen]] and granted [[e:dusseldorf|Düsseldorf]] town rights.
duchy-of-berg.r: Berg was raised to a duchy in 1380. In 1423 it was united with the [[s:duchy-of-julich|Duchy of Jülich]] and in 1521 with [[e:kleve|Cleves]]. Its industry developed early in the [[e:wupper|Wupper]] valley and around [[e:solingen|Solingen]], known for blades. Elector [[e:john-william-elector-palatine|Johann Wilhelm]] of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] ruled from [[e:dusseldorf|Düsseldorf]] in the early 18th century, building it into a court city.
duchy-of-berg.e: After 1614 Berg and Jülich belonged to [[s:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]] and later [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. In 1806 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] made Berg a grand duchy for his brother-in-law [[e:joachim-murat|Joachim Murat]]. In 1815 it passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], and [[e:dusseldorf|Düsseldorf]] is now capital of [[e:north-rhine-westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]].

duchy-of-camerino.t: An Apennine lordship of the Varano family in the Marche, raised to a duchy in 1515 before the popes reclaimed it.
duchy-of-camerino.o: The [[e:house-of-varano|Varano]] family took control of [[e:camerino|Camerino]], a hill town in the central [[e:apennines|Apennines]], in the second half of the 13th century; [[e:gentile-da-varano|Gentile da Varano]] is recorded as its leader from 1262. They ruled as papal vicars within the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].
duchy-of-camerino.r: The [[e:house-of-varano|Varano]] governed a hilly region of the [[e:marche|Marche]] with income from wool, paper and the papal service of their condottieri. [[e:giulio-cesare-da-varano|Giulio Cesare da Varano]] rebuilt the ducal palace in the 15th century. In 1502 [[e:cesare-borgia|Cesare Borgia]] seized [[e:camerino|Camerino]] and had Giulio Cesare and several sons killed. A surviving son, [[e:giovanni-maria-da-varano|Giovanni Maria]], regained the city, and Pope Leo X made him duke in 1515.
duchy-of-camerino.e: [[e:giovanni-maria-da-varano|Giovanni Maria]]'s heiress [[e:giulia-da-varano|Giulia da Varano]] married [[e:guidobaldo-ii-della-rovere|Guidobaldo II della Rovere]] of [[s:duchy-of-urbino|Urbino]], but [[e:pope-paul-iii|Pope Paul III]] took [[e:camerino|Camerino]] in 1539, and in 1545 it returned to direct government of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].

duchy-of-lower-bavaria.t: Wittelsbach duchy ruled from Landshut after the 1255 partition of Bavaria, whose duke Otto III was briefly King of Hungary.
duchy-of-lower-bavaria.o: In the partition of the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria|Duchy of Bavaria]] in 1255, [[e:henry-xiii-duke-of-bavaria|Henry XIII]] received [[e:lower-bavaria|Lower Bavaria]], the lands along the lower [[e:isar|Isar]], the [[e:danube|Danube]] and the [[e:inn-river|Inn]], with [[e:landshut|Landshut]] as residence. His brother [[e:louis-ii-duke-of-bavaria|Louis II the Strict]] took the [[s:duchy-of-upper-bavaria|Duchy of Upper Bavaria]]. The two lines were often hostile.
duchy-of-lower-bavaria.r: The dukes ruled from [[e:trausnitz-castle|Burg Trausnitz]] above [[e:landshut|Landshut]], relying on the estates, whose charter of 1311, the [[e:ottonian-handfeste|Ottonian Handfeste]], gave them taxation rights. [[e:henry-xiii-duke-of-bavaria|Henry XIII]]'s son [[e:otto-iii-duke-of-bavaria|Otto III]] was elected King of [[e:hungary|Hungary]] in 1305 but could not hold the throne. The duchy was repeatedly divided among co-rulers, and [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Louis IV]] of [[e:upper-bavaria|Upper Bavaria]] acted as guardian of its young dukes, defeating the Austrians at [[e:battle-of-gammelsdorf|Gammelsdorf]] in 1313.
duchy-of-lower-bavaria.e: When the last Lower Bavarian duke, John I the Child, died in 1340, [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Louis IV]] inherited the duchy and reunited [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. [[e:lower-bavaria|Lower Bavaria]] later re-emerged as [[e:bavaria-landshut|Bavaria-Landshut]] and is now a district of Bavaria.

dedan-state.t: A minor Kathi chiefship of southern Kathiawar, held by co-sharers of a local family.
dedan-state.o: [[s:kingdom-of-dedan|Dedan]] was a small estate in southern [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] held by a Kathi family from around 1700. Its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
dedan-state.r: Like many Kathi holdings, it was shared among members of the ruling family and supervised after 1807 by the [[e:kathiawar-agency|British Kathiawar Agency]]. Little else is recorded.
dedan-state.e: [[s:kingdom-of-dedan|Dedan]] merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in Amreli district.

duchy-of-mecklenburg.t: The Baltic duchy of the Obotrite-descended Niklotings, raised to ducal rank in 1348, whose partitions shaped north-east Germany until 1701.
duchy-of-mecklenburg.o: The [[e:house-of-mecklenburg|Niklotings]], descendants of the Obotrite prince [[e:niklot|Niklot]], had ruled the [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Lordship of Mecklenburg]] since the 12th century. In 1348 [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]] raised [[e:albert-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg|Albert II]] and his brother John to dukes of the empire. Albert's son Albert became King of [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in 1364, and the duchy later absorbed the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-stargard|Duchy of Mecklenburg-Stargard]] and the [[s:county-of-schwerin|County of Schwerin]].
duchy-of-mecklenburg.r: The dukes shared power with strong estates of knights and towns, including the Hanseatic ports of [[s:lordship-of-rostock|Rostock]] and [[s:swedish-wismar|Wismar]], and [[e:university-of-rostock|Rostock University]] was founded in 1419. The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] was formally adopted in 1549. The economy rested on grain grown on noble estates by increasingly bound peasants, and repeated partitions, notably the creation of the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-gustrow|Duchy of Mecklenburg-Güstrow]] in 1621, weakened the dukes.
duchy-of-mecklenburg.e: During the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]] [[e:albrecht-von-wallenstein|Wallenstein]] held [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] from 1628 to 1631. When the [[e:gustrow|Güstrow]] line died out in 1695, a succession dispute followed, settled by the [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-hamburg|Hamburg]] Compromise of 1701, which divided the land into the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-schwerin|Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin]] and the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-strelitz|Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz]].

delian-league.t: Athenian-led alliance formed against Persia in 478 BCE that turned into an Athenian empire funding the Parthenon and Athens' war with Sparta.
delian-league.o: After the defeat of [[e:xerxes-i|Xerxes]], the Ionian and [[e:aegean|Aegean]] [[e:greeks|Greeks]] wanted to continue the war against [[e:persia|Persia]] and resented the Spartan commander [[e:pausanias-general|Pausanias]]. In 478-477 BCE they swore an alliance with [[s:athens|Athens]] on the sacred island of [[s:delos|Delos]]. The Athenian [[e:aristides|Aristides]] assessed each member's contribution of ships or money, set at 460 [[e:talent|talents]] a year.
delian-league.r: Delegates first met on [[s:delos|Delos]], where the treasury was kept, but [[s:athens|Athens]] controlled the fleet and the treasurers. Over time most members paid tribute rather than providing ships, and revolts by [[s:naxos|Naxos]] (c. 470 BCE), [[s:thasos|Thasos]] (465 BCE) and [[s:samos|Samos]] (440 BCE) were crushed. The treasury moved to [[e:athens|Athens]] in 454 BCE, and [[e:pericles|Pericles]] used its funds for the buildings of the Acropolis. Athens imposed its coinage, courts and settlers on allies.
delian-league.e: [[e:cimon|Cimon's]] victory at the [[e:battle-of-the-eurymedon|Eurymedon]] (c. 466 BCE) secured the [[e:aegean|Aegean]]. Rivalry with [[s:sparta|Sparta]] led to the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]], in which many allies revolted after the Sicilian disaster of 413 BCE. [[e:athens|Athens]]' surrender in 404 BCE dissolved the league.

decapolis.t: A defensive league of ten Alsatian imperial cities, founded in 1354, that guarded their freedoms until Louis XIV absorbed them into France.
decapolis.o: In 1354 [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]] approved an alliance of ten imperial cities in [[e:alsace|Alsace]]: [[s:free-imperial-city-of-haguenau|Haguenau]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-colmar|Colmar]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-wissembourg|Wissembourg]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-selestat|Sélestat]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-obernai|Obernai]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-kaysersberg|Kaysersberg]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-rosheim|Rosheim]], [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-turckheim|Turckheim]] and [[s:republic-of-mulhouse|Mulhouse]]. They promised one another aid against the nobility and the [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-strasbourg|Strasbourg]], under the protection of the imperial bailiff (Landvogt) at Haguenau.
decapolis.r: The league had no central government; delegates met in assemblies to settle disputes, share military costs and defend each member's rights. Membership changed: [[s:republic-of-mulhouse|Mulhouse]] left in 1515 to ally with the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Old Swiss Confederacy]], and the [[s:free-imperial-city-of-landau|Free Imperial City of Landau]] took its place in 1521. The members divided over the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], with [[s:free-imperial-city-of-colmar|Colmar]] and [[e:landau|Landau]] becoming Protestant while others stayed Catholic.
decapolis.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 transferred the imperial bailiwick to [[e:france|France]], whose kings treated it as [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]]. [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] forced the cities to submit and had their walls razed in 1673, and the [[e:treaties-of-nijmegen|Treaty of Nijmegen]] of 1679 confirmed their annexation to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

duchy-of-olomouc.t: The main Moravian appanage duchy of the Přemyslid dynasty, seat of a bishopric and base for princes who contested the Bohemian throne.
duchy-of-olomouc.o: After [[e:bretislaus-i-duke-of-bohemia|Bretislaus I]] died in 1055, [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] was divided among his sons. [[e:olomouc|Olomouc]] in central [[e:moravia|Moravia]] went to [[e:vratislaus-ii-of-bohemia|Vratislaus]], then in 1061 to Otto I the Fair, whose line held it through the 12th century. The bishopric of Olomouc was restored in 1063, making the town Moravia's religious centre.
duchy-of-olomouc.r: [[e:olomouc|Olomouc]] princes such as Svatopluk, who seized [[e:prague|Prague]] in 1107, and Otto III were influential figures in the dynasty's power struggles. The town grew around the castle, which included a [[e:romanesque-architecture|Romanesque]] [[e:bishop|bishop]]'s palace built by Bishop [[e:jindrich-zdik|Jindřich Zdík]] in the 1140s.
duchy-of-olomouc.e: Late in the 12th century the Moravian [[e:appanage|appanages]] lost their separate status. [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] became a margraviate under imperial recognition, and around 1197 [[e:vladislaus-iii-duke-of-bohemia|Vladislaus Henry]] united it. [[e:olomouc|Olomouc]] remained [[e:moravia|Moravia's]] ecclesiastical capital; its bishopric became an archbishopric in 1777.

dutch-suratte.t: The Dutch East India Company's trading establishment at Surat, the Mughal Empire's greatest port.
dutch-suratte.o: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) opened a factory at [[e:surat|Surat]] around 1616, shortly after the English, gaining access to the trade of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]]. Surat became the headquarters of the directorate of Suratte, which also oversaw posts at [[e:ahmedabad|Ahmedabad]], [[e:agra|Agra]] and [[e:khambhat|Cambay]].
dutch-suratte.r: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] bought [[e:indigo|indigo]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth and saltpetre for export to [[e:europe|Europe]] and [[e:asia|Asia]] and sold [[e:spice-trade|spices]] from [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]], competing closely with the [[e:east-india-company|English East India Company]]. The factory was a commercial establishment, not a territorial state, operating under Mughal permission and local governors. It declined with [[e:surat|Surat]] after the [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] sacks of 1664 and 1670.
dutch-suratte.e: [[e:surat|Surat's]] trade shifted to [[e:mumbai|Bombay]] in the 18th century, and the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] presence dwindled. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] held the post during the [[e:napoleonic-wars|Napoleonic Wars]] and, under the [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824|Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824]], it was formally ceded in 1825.

duchy-of-nassau.t: Rhineland duchy with spas at Wiesbaden and Bad Ems, the first German state to grant a constitution after Napoleon.
duchy-of-nassau.o: In 1806 the principalities of [[s:principality-of-nassau-usingen|Nassau-Usingen]] and [[s:county-of-nassau-weilburg|Nassau-Weilburg]] united as the Duchy of [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] and joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]]. After 1815, the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] added former [[e:house-of-orange-nassau|Orange-Nassau]] lands, consolidating a state between the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], Main and [[e:lahn|Lahn]], with [[e:wiesbaden|Wiesbaden]] as capital.
duchy-of-nassau.r: [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] adopted a constitution in 1814, the first of the German states. The duchy was mixed Catholic and Protestant, and in 1817 it created one of the first united Lutheran-Reformed churches. Spa towns such as [[e:wiesbaden|Wiesbaden]], [[e:bad-ems|Bad Ems]] and Schlangenbad attracted international visitors, and the [[e:rheingau|Rheingau's]] vineyards and the [[e:lahn|Lahn's]] iron mines supported the economy.
duchy-of-nassau.e: Duke [[e:adolphe-grand-duke-of-luxembourg|Adolphe]] sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866, and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] annexed [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] into the [[e:province-of-hesse-nassau|Province of Hesse-Nassau]]. Adolphe later became Grand Duke of [[s:grand-duchy-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]] in 1890, where his descendants still reign.

delmatae.t: Illyrian people of the Dalmatian hinterland who fought Rome for two centuries and gave their name to the province of Dalmatia.
delmatae.o: The Delmatae lived in the karst uplands behind the Adriatic coast, around [[e:delminium|Delminium]] (near modern [[e:tomislavgrad|Tomislavgrad]]). Around 180 BCE they broke away from the Illyrian king [[e:gentius|Gentius]] and built their own league, extending their power over neighbouring peoples and the coastal towns.
delmatae.r: Their league joined communities of herders and farmers living in hillforts. They raided the [[s:daorsi|Daorsi]] and the Greek cities of Issa's mainland colonies. [[e:rome|Rome]] fought them in 156–155 BCE, when [[e:publius-cornelius-scipio-nasica-corculum|Scipio Nasica]] destroyed [[e:delminium|Delminium]], and again in 119 and 78–76 BCE. In the winter of 48–47 BCE they defeated a Roman army under [[e:aulus-gabinius|Aulus Gabinius]].
delmatae.e: Octavian's campaign of 34–33 BCE took their strongholds such as [[e:promona|Promona]]. They rose again in the [[e:great-illyrian-revolt|Great Illyrian Revolt]] of 6–9 CE, and their last fortress, [[e:andetrium|Andetrium]], fell to [[e:tiberius|Tiberius]] in 9 CE. Their name lived on in the Roman province of [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]].

dang-states.t: A group of small Bhil chiefships in the forested Dangs of southern Gujarat, whose rajas leased their forests to the British.
dang-states.o: [[e:dang-district|The Dangs]], a hilly teak forest between [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and [[e:khandesh|Khandesh]], were held by a number of [[e:bhils|Bhil]] chiefs, Rajas and Naiks, who raided the plains in the 18th century. After the British took Khandesh in 1818, they made agreements with these chiefs, recognising them as petty rulers.
dang-states.r: From the 1840s the British leased the [[e:dang-district|Dang]] forests from the chiefs for [[e:timber|timber]] in return for annual payments, and administered the area through the collector of [[e:khandesh|Khandesh]]. The population was almost entirely Adivasi, [[e:bhils|Bhil]], [[e:kokna-people|Kokna]] and [[e:warli|Varli]], living from shifting cultivation and forest produce. The chiefs gathered each year at the [[e:dang-darbar|Dang Darbar]].
dang-states.e: [[e:dang-district|The Dangs]] were merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and became a district of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. The former chiefs' families still receive political pensions, presented at the annual [[e:dang-darbar|Dang Darbar]] at [[e:ahwa|Ahwa]].

duchy-of-pomerania-stolp.t: The eastern Pomeranian duchy ruled from Stolp, whose prince Eric of Pomerania became king of the Kalmar Union.
duchy-of-pomerania-stolp.o: In 1368 a new partition of [[e:pomerania-wolgast|Pomerania-Wolgast]] gave the lands of [[e:further-pomerania|Further Pomerania]], east of the [[e:swina|Świna]] and Oder, to Duke Bogislaw V, who ruled from [[e:slupsk|Stolp]] (Słupsk). His dynasty kept close ties with [[e:poland|Poland]], and his daughter [[e:elizabeth-of-pomerania|Elizabeth]] married [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]].
duchy-of-pomerania-stolp.r: The duchy covered [[e:further-pomerania|Further Pomerania]], a land of farms, forests and small towns such as [[e:slupsk|Stolp]] and [[e:darlowo|Rügenwalde]]. Its dukes balanced between the [[s:state-of-the-teutonic-order|State of the Teutonic Order]], [[e:poland|Poland]] and [[e:denmark|Denmark]]. [[e:eric-of-pomerania|Eric of Pomerania]], grandson of Bogislaw V, was elected king of the [[s:kalmar-union|Kalmar Union]] in 1397.
duchy-of-pomerania-stolp.e: Deposed from his Scandinavian thrones, Eric retired first to [[s:gotland|Gotland]] and from 1449 to [[e:darlowo|Rügenwalde]] (Darłowo), where he ruled part of the duchy until his death in 1459. [[e:slupsk|Stolp]] then passed to [[e:eric-ii-duke-of-pomerania|Eric II of Pomerania-Wolgast]], and all the Pomeranian lands were later reunited by [[e:bogislaw-x|Bogislaw X]].

duchy-of-mirandola.t: The small Emilian state of the Pico family, birthplace of the philosopher Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, which lasted four centuries.
duchy-of-mirandola.o: The [[e:house-of-pico|Pico]] family held lands around [[e:mirandola|Mirandola]], north of [[e:modena|Modena]], and in 1311 [[e:francesco-pico|Francesco Pico]] was named imperial vicar there by [[e:henry-vii-holy-roman-emperor|Henry VII]]. The family ruled as lords and imperial [[e:vassal|vassals]], and the state was raised to a principality in 1596 and a duchy in 1617.
duchy-of-mirandola.r: The [[e:house-of-pico|Pico]] governed a fortified town and the countryside of [[e:mirandola|Mirandola]] and Concordia, often allied with [[e:france|France]]. The humanist [[e:giovanni-pico-della-mirandola|Giovanni Pico della Mirandola]], author of the [[e:oration-on-the-dignity-of-man|Oration on the Dignity of Man]], was a younger son of the family. In 1511 [[e:pope-julius-ii|Pope Julius II]] personally led the siege of the fortress. Family quarrels and murders were frequent.
duchy-of-mirandola.e: Duke [[e:francesco-maria-pico|Francesco Maria Pico]] sided with [[e:france|France]] in the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]] and was deposed by the emperor in 1708. In 1710 [[e:mirandola|Mirandola]] was sold to [[e:rinaldo-d-este-duke-of-modena|Rinaldo d'Este]], joining the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]].

duchy-of-saxony.t: The stem duchy of northern Germany whose dukes became kings and emperors, later the power base of Henry the Lion before its break-up in 1180.
duchy-of-saxony.o: After [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] conquest, [[e:saxony|Saxony]] was ruled by Frankish counts. In the mid 9th century the [[e:ottonian-dynasty|Liudolfing]] family, descended from Count [[e:liudolf-duke-of-saxony|Liudolf]], emerged as dukes; Liudolf founded [[s:imperial-abbey-of-gandersheim|Gandersheim Abbey]] in 852. His grandson [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler]] was elected king of [[s:east-francia|East Francia]] in 919, and Otto I passed the duchy to the [[e:house-of-billung|Billung]] family.
duchy-of-saxony.r: The duchy covered [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]], [[e:angria|Engern]] and [[e:eastphalia|Eastphalia]] between the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] and the [[e:elbe|Elbe]], with Slavic marches to the east. [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] of the [[e:house-of-welf|Welf]] family, duke from 1142, made it a near-royal power, founding [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] and [[e:munich|Munich]] and ruling from [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]], where he built [[e:dankwarderode-castle|Dankwarderode Castle]] and set up the bronze lion.
duchy-of-saxony.e: In 1180 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] deposed [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]]. The western part became the [[s:duchy-of-westphalia|Duchy of Westphalia]] under the [[s:electorate-of-cologne|Electorate of Cologne]], and the name [[e:saxony|Saxony]] passed with a smaller duchy to the [[e:bernhard-duke-of-saxony|Ascanian Bernhard]]. In 1296 this split into Saxe-Lauenburg and Saxe-[[e:wittenberg|Wittenberg]], whose electoral title later moved the name Saxony up the [[e:elbe|Elbe]].

drougoubitai.t: Slavic tribe west of Thessalonica that besieged the city in the 7th century and later gave its name to a Byzantine bishopric.
drougoubitai.o: The Drougoubitai settled in the plain west and north-west of [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]], towards the [[e:vardar|Vardar]] and [[e:pelagonia|Pelagonia]], in the early 7th century. They appear in the [[e:miracles-of-saint-demetrius|Miracles of Saint Demetrius]] among the tribes that attacked Thessalonica.
drougoubitai.r: Known only from Byzantine sources, they lived under their own chiefs and alternated between hostility and alliance with [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]], at times supplying the city with grain. In the 680s they were involved in the affair of [[e:kuver|Kuver's]] [[e:bulgars|Bulgars]], who settled near them.
drougoubitai.e: By the 9th century the southern Drougoubitai were within Byzantine rule, with a bishopric of Drougoubiteia, while northern lands fell to the [[s:first-bulgarian-empire|First Bulgarian Empire]]. The tribe then disappears as a distinct group.

duchy-of-ahtum.t: Realm in the Banat ruled from Morisena by Ahtum (Ajtony), a powerful Orthodox lord defeated by Stephen I of Hungary.
duchy-of-ahtum.o: [[e:ahtum|Ahtum]] is known from the [[e:legend-of-saint-gerard|Legend of Saint Gerard]]. Around 1000 he held the land between the [[e:mures-river|Mureș]], the [[e:tisza|Tisza]] and the [[e:danube|Danube]], ruling from [[e:cenad|Morisena]] (Cenad). He had been baptised by the [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] rite at [[e:vidin|Vidin]], and the [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta Hungarorum]] makes him a descendant of [[e:glad|Glad]] of the [[s:duchy-of-glad|Duchy of Glad]].
duchy-of-ahtum.r: [[e:ahtum|Ahtum]] was rich in horses and [[e:cattle|cattle]] and taxed the salt carried down the [[e:mures-river|Mureș]] to the king of [[e:hungary|Hungary]], which provoked conflict. He founded a Greek monastery at [[e:cenad|Morisena]], staffed by Byzantine monks, and recognised Byzantine authority.
duchy-of-ahtum.e: Stephen I sent his commander [[e:csanad-commander|Csanád]], who defeated and killed [[e:ahtum|Ahtum]]. Historians date this either to around 1003 or to around 1028. Csanád became count of the region, renamed Csanád, and Gerard founded a [[e:latin|Latin]] bishopric there, part of the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1000-1301|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1000-1301).

duchy-of-merania.t: A title duchy of the Andechs counts on the Adriatic coast, whose family married into the royal houses of France, Hungary and Poland before dying out in 1248.
duchy-of-merania.o: In 1152 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] gave Count [[e:conrad-ii-count-of-dachau|Conrad of Dachau]] the title Duke of Merania, a coastal area on the [[e:kvarner-gulf|Kvarner Gulf]] of [[e:croatia|Croatia]] and [[s:histria|Istria]]. After the Dachau line died out, the [[e:house-of-andechs|Andechs]] counts of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] took the title in 1180, holding lands in Bavaria, [[e:franconia|Franconia]], [[e:tyrol|Tyrol]], Istria and [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]].
duchy-of-merania.r: The duchy was more a title than a territory, but the [[e:house-of-andechs|Andechs-Merania]] dukes were among the leading princes of the Empire. [[e:berthold-iv-duke-of-merania|Berthold IV]]'s daughters married widely: [[e:agnes-of-merania|Agnes]] became Queen of [[e:france|France]], [[e:gertrude-of-merania|Gertrude]] Queen of [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and mother of [[e:elizabeth-of-hungary|Saint Elizabeth]], and [[e:hedwig-of-silesia|Hedwig]] Duchess of [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], later Saint Hedwig.
duchy-of-merania.e: The family lost lands after allegedly being involved in the murder of King [[e:philip-of-swabia|Philip of Swabia]] in 1208. The last duke, [[e:otto-ii-duke-of-merania|Otto II]], died in 1248, and the lands were divided among the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbachs]], the counts of [[e:tyrol|Tyrol]] and others. [[e:house-of-andechs|Andechs]] became a monastery.

duchy-of-oswiecim.t: A Silesian Piast duchy on the Vistula, under Bohemian overlordship until the Polish king bought it in 1457.
duchy-of-oswiecim.o: [[e:oswiecim|Oswiecim]], west of [[e:krakow|Krakow]], belonged to the Silesian [[s:duchy-of-cieszyn|Duchy of Cieszyn]]. In 1315 it was split off for Wladyslaw, a son of the duke of [[e:cieszyn|Cieszyn]], who became the first duke of Oswiecim. In 1327 his successor did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|John of Bohemia]], making the duchy a fief of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-oswiecim.r: The duchy was a small land on the upper [[e:vistula|Vistula]], with salt and trade routes between [[e:krakow|Krakow]], [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] and [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]]. Its [[e:piast-dynasty|Piast]] dukes were minor rulers balancing between [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and [[e:poland|Poland]]. In 1445 its lands were divided, and the [[s:duchy-of-zator|Duchy of Zator]] was created for one branch of the family.
duchy-of-oswiecim.e: In 1457 Duke [[e:jan-iv-of-oswiecim|Jan IV]] sold [[e:oswiecim|Oswiecim]] to [[e:casimir-iv-jagiellon|Casimir IV of Poland]] for 50,000 marks, and it was fully incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569) in 1564. The town's German name, Auschwitz, was later given to the Nazi concentration and extermination camp built nearby.

dharmasraya.t: The Malayu kingdom of the upper Batang Hari in Sumatra, successor to Srivijaya's power in the 12th and 13th centuries and partner of Javanese Singhasari.
dharmasraya.o: As [[e:srivijaya|Srivijaya]] weakened, power in [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]] shifted to the [[s:melayu-kingdom|Malayu]] kingdom on the upper [[e:batang-hari-river|Batang Hari River]]. The Grahi inscription of 1183, found in southern [[s:thailand|Thailand]], names Srimat Trailokyaraja Maulibhusana Warmadewa as its overlord, showing its reach beyond Sumatra. Its centre, Dharmasraya, lay in today's [[e:west-sumatra|West Sumatra]].
dharmasraya.r: Dharmasraya controlled the gold of the [[e:minangkabau-people|Minangkabau]] highlands and the river route to the [[e:strait-of-malacca|Strait of Malacca]]. In 1275 [[e:kertanegara|Kertanegara of Singhasari]] sent the Pamalayu expedition, and in 1286 a statue of [[e:amoghapasa|Amoghapasa]] was sent from [[e:java|Java]] to King [[e:tribhuwanaraja-mauli-warmadewa|Tribhuwanaraja Mauli Warmadewa]], as the [[e:padang-roco-inscription|Padang Roco inscription]] records. [[e:vajrayana|Tantric Buddhism]] flourished at the court.
dharmasraya.e: In 1347 [[e:adityawarman|Adityawarman]], a prince with [[s:melayu-kingdom|Malayu]] and Javanese ancestry who had served [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]], inscribed the back of the [[e:amoghapasa|Amoghapasa]] statue and declared himself king. He moved the court inland, founding the [[s:pagaruyung-kingdom|Pagaruyung Kingdom]].

duchy-of-holstein.t: A German duchy ruled by the kings of Denmark for four centuries, whose bond with Schleswig sparked two 19th-century wars.
duchy-of-holstein.o: In 1460 the estates of the [[s:duchy-of-schleswig|Duchy of Schleswig]] and the [[s:county-of-holstein|County of Holstein]] elected [[e:christian-i-of-denmark|King Christian I of Denmark]] as their ruler, promising that the lands would remain 'forever undivided'. In 1474 [[e:frederick-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Frederick III]] raised Holstein, a fief of the empire, to a duchy.
duchy-of-holstein.r: [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] was governed together with [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]], but while Schleswig was a Danish fief, Holstein belonged to the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] and later the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]]. From 1544 it was split between the royal line and the [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Duchy of Holstein-Gottorp]], with their lands intermingled. [[e:gluckstadt|Glückstadt]], founded by [[e:christian-iv-of-denmark|Christian IV]] in 1617, became the seat of royal government. [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] took hold in the 16th century.
duchy-of-holstein.e: Danish attempts to tie [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] more closely to the kingdom led to war in 1848 to 1851 and again in 1864, when [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:austria|Austria]] defeated [[e:denmark|Denmark]]. [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] came under Austrian administration in 1865 and was annexed by Prussia in 1866, becoming part of the province of [[s:provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein|Schleswig-Holstein]].

duchy-of-gascony.t: Duchy between the Garonne and the Pyrenees, set up by the Franks to contain the Basques, which became the core of Gascon identity.
duchy-of-gascony.o: Around 602 the Frankish kings created a Duchy of Vasconia under a duke named Genial to control the [[e:basques|Basques]], who had pushed north of the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] into the old Roman [[e:novempopulania|Novempopulana]]. The region soon slipped from Frankish control and was often allied with the dukes of the [[s:early-duchy-of-aquitaine|Early Duchy of Aquitaine]].
duchy-of-gascony.r: The [[e:basques|Basques]] were notoriously hard to govern: in 778 they ambushed [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] rearguard at [[e:battle-of-roncevaux-pass|Roncevaux]]. From the late 9th century a native dynasty, traditionally descended from the semi-legendary Sancho Mitarra, ruled largely independently. Duke [[e:william-sanchez-of-gascony|William Sánchez]] defeated [[e:vikings|Viking]] raiders and founded the abbey of [[e:saint-sever|Saint-Sever]], and [[e:bordeaux|Bordeaux]] became the ducal seat.
duchy-of-gascony.e: The male line ended with [[e:sancho-vi-william-of-gascony|Sancho VI William]] in 1032. After a succession struggle, [[e:william-viii-duke-of-aquitaine|Guy-Geoffrey]], count of [[s:county-of-poitou|Poitou]], secured [[e:gascony|Gascony]] in the 1050s and united it with the [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Duchy of Aquitaine]]. Gascony passed with Aquitaine to the English kings and kept its own Occitan dialect.

duchy-of-menumorut.t: Realm in the Crișana region around Biharea attributed by the Gesta Hungarorum to Menumorut, who resisted and then made peace with the Hungarians.
duchy-of-menumorut.o: [[e:menumorut|Menumorut]] is known only from the [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta Hungarorum]], written around 1200. It places his duchy between the [[e:tisza|Tisza]], the [[e:somes|Someș]] and the Igfon forest, with its fortress at [[e:biharea|Bihar]] (Biharea), inhabited by [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]] and other peoples, around the time of the Hungarian conquest of the 890s.
duchy-of-menumorut.r: The [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta]] says [[e:menumorut|Menumorut]] refused to cede land to [[e:arpad|Árpád]], claiming the Byzantine emperor as his lord. Hungarian forces besieged [[e:biharea|Bihar]], and he agreed to marry his daughter to Árpád's son [[e:zolta|Zoltán]]. Excavations at Biharea show a fortified site of the period, but no contemporary written source confirms the ruler.
duchy-of-menumorut.e: According to the [[e:gesta-hungarorum|Gesta]], [[e:menumorut|Menumorut]] died around 904 and his lands passed to [[e:zolta|Zoltán]], joining the [[s:principality-of-hungary|Principality of Hungary]]. Romanian and Hungarian historians still debate whether the duchy existed as described.

duchy-of-pomerania-wolgast.t: The western of the two Pomeranian duchies created by the Griffin partition of 1295, ruled from the castle of Wolgast near the Baltic coast.
duchy-of-pomerania-wolgast.o: In 1295 the [[e:house-of-griffins|Griffin]] brothers [[e:bogislaw-iv-duke-of-pomerania|Bogislaw IV]] and Otto I divided the [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Duchy of Pomerania]]. Bogislaw took the coastal lands north of the [[e:peene|Peene]] and ruled from [[e:wolgast|Wolgast]]. In 1325 his line gained the [[s:principality-of-rugen|Principality of Rügen]], and later partitions split off further branches, including the [[s:duchy-of-pomerania-stolp|Duchy of Pomerania-Stolp]] in 1368.
duchy-of-pomerania-wolgast.r: The [[e:house-of-griffins|Griffins]] were a Slavic dynasty that had become thoroughly German in culture. Power was shared with the estates and with Hanseatic towns such as [[e:stralsund|Stralsund]], [[e:greifswald|Greifswald]] and [[e:anklam|Anklam]], which grew rich on Baltic trade, and [[e:university-of-greifswald|Greifswald University]] was founded in 1456. [[e:johannes-bugenhagen|Johannes Bugenhagen]], a Pomeranian, helped bring the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]], adopted at the [[e:diet-of-treptow|Diet of Treptow]] in 1534.
duchy-of-pomerania-wolgast.e: The duchy was reunited with [[e:szczecin|Stettin]] under [[e:bogislaw-x|Bogislaw X]] from 1478 and split off again in 1532. When Duke [[e:philip-julius-duke-of-pomerania-wolgast|Philip Julius]] died childless in 1625, [[e:bogislaw-xiv|Bogislaw XIV]] of [[e:pomerania-stettin|Pomerania-Stettin]] inherited it, uniting [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]] for the last time shortly before [[e:sweden|Sweden]] occupied it in 1630; most of it later became [[s:swedish-pomerania|Swedish Pomerania]].

duchy-of-ferrara.t: The Este state on the Po whose court made Ferrara a capital of Renaissance poetry, painting and town planning.
duchy-of-ferrara.o: In 1264 the citizens of the [[s:commune-of-ferrara|Commune of Ferrara]] proclaimed [[e:obizzo-ii-deste|Obizzo II d'Este]] their perpetual lord. The [[e:house-of-este|Este]], a feudal family with lands near [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]], held [[e:ferrara|Ferrara]] as papal vicars and added [[e:modena|Modena]] and [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]]. [[e:pope-paul-ii|Pope Paul II]] made [[e:borso-deste|Borso d'Este]] duke of Ferrara in 1471.
duchy-of-ferrara.r: The [[e:house-of-este|Este]] ran a brilliant court. [[e:ercole-i-d-este|Ercole I]]'s planned extension of the city, the [[e:addizione-erculea|Addizione Erculea]], was one of the first modern urban plans. [[e:ferrara|Ferrara]] supported the poets [[e:matteo-maria-boiardo|Boiardo]], [[e:ludovico-ariosto|Ariosto]] and [[e:torquato-tasso|Tasso]] and the painters of the [[e:palazzo-schifanoia|Schifanoia]] frescoes. Alfonso I, husband of [[e:lucrezia-borgia|Lucrezia Borgia]], was famous for his artillery. The duchy was a papal fief, while [[e:modena|Modena]] was held from the emperor.
duchy-of-ferrara.e: [[e:alfonso-ii-deste|Alfonso II]] died without a legitimate heir in 1597. [[e:pope-clement-viii|Pope Clement VIII]] refused to recognise his cousin [[e:cesare-d-este-duke-of-modena|Cesare]], and in 1598 [[e:ferrara|Ferrara]] passed to the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]]. The [[e:house-of-este|Este]] moved their court to the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]].

decantae.t: People of Easter Ross in northern Scotland recorded by Ptolemy, whose name resembles that of the Deceangli of Wales.
decantae.o: [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 places the Decantae on the east coast of the northern Highlands, usually located in [[e:easter-ross|Easter Ross]] and the [[e:black-isle|Black Isle]] around the [[e:cromarty-firth|Cromarty]] and [[e:dornoch-firth|Dornoch Firths]]. Their name resembles that of the [[s:deceangli|Deceangli]] of north-east [[e:wales|Wales]], possibly reflecting a shared Celtic element rather than any direct link.
decantae.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers or society. The fertile coastlands of [[e:easter-ross|Easter Ross]] supported farming communities, and the area has numerous hillforts, including vitrified forts such as [[e:knockfarrel|Knockfarrel]], whose stone walls were fused by intense fire.
decantae.e: The Decantae do not appear after Ptolemy. [[e:easter-ross|Easter Ross]] later became an important district of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Kingdom of the Picts]], with major monastic and sculptural sites such as [[e:portmahomack|Portmahomack]], [[e:nigg-stone|Nigg]] and [[e:shandwick-stone|Shandwick]].

dominion-of-new-england.t: James II's attempt to merge the colonies from Maine to New Jersey into one royal government without assemblies, overthrown by a Boston revolt in 1689.
dominion-of-new-england.o: After the charter of the [[s:massachusetts-bay-colony|Massachusetts Bay Colony]] was revoked in 1684, [[e:james-ii-of-england|James II]] decided to combine the [[e:new-england|New England]] colonies under direct royal rule. [[e:joseph-dudley|Joseph Dudley]] headed an interim government from 1686, and [[e:edmund-andros|Sir Edmund Andros]] arrived in [[e:boston|Boston]] as governor in December 1686. The [[s:province-of-new-york|Province of New York]] and East and [[s:west-jersey|West Jersey]] were added in 1688.
dominion-of-new-england.r: [[s:andros|Andros]] ruled with an appointed council and no elected assembly, levied taxes without consent, restricted town meetings and questioned land titles granted under the old charters. He enforced the [[e:navigation-acts|Navigation Acts]] and held Anglican services in a [[e:boston|Boston]] meeting house, angering [[e:puritans|Puritans]]. Protests such as that of the [[e:ipswich-massachusetts|Ipswich]] minister [[e:john-wise|John Wise]] were punished. Andros governed [[e:new-york|New York]] through his lieutenant [[e:francis-nicholson|Francis Nicholson]].
dominion-of-new-england.e: News of the [[e:glorious-revolution|Glorious Revolution]] reached [[e:boston|Boston]], and on 18 April 1689 a crowd rose, jailing [[s:andros|Andros]]. The colonies restored their old governments, and [[s:province-of-massachusetts-bay|Massachusetts]] gained a new charter in 1691 as the Province of [[s:massachusetts-bay-colony|Massachusetts Bay]].

dmt.t: The earliest known kingdom of the northern Ethiopian highlands, centred on the temple town of Yeha and closely tied to South Arabian Saba.
dmt.o: D'mt emerged in the early first millennium BCE on the plateau of today's [[s:tigray|Tigray]] and highland [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]]. Its name appears in a handful of royal inscriptions, written in a [[e:south-arabia|South Arabian]] script, whose rulers took the title of mukarrib. Close contacts across the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] with the [[s:kingdom-of-saba|Sabaeans]] shaped its writing, architecture and religion, though most scholars now stress local roots as well.
dmt.r: The kingdom is known mainly from monuments and inscriptions. The [[e:great-temple-of-yeha|Great Temple of Yeha]], built of finely dressed stone around the 7th century BCE, honoured the Sabaean moon god [[e:almaqah|Almaqah]]. Farmers grew cereals, probably with ox-drawn ploughs, and used iron tools, while sites such as [[e:grat-beal-gebri|Grat Beal Gebri]] show palace-like buildings. Its rulers and borders remain obscure.
dmt.e: D'mt seems to have broken up into smaller polities around the 5th century BCE, and little is known of the centuries that followed. Its legacy of monumental building, writing and highland state-making passed to the [[e:aksumite-empire|Kingdom of Aksum]], which rose in the same region from the 1st century CE.

danish-osel.t: Danish-ruled island of Saaremaa, bought in the Livonian War in 1559 and held by Denmark until it was lost to Sweden in 1645.
danish-osel.o: In 1559 [[e:johann-von-munchhausen|Bishop Johann von Münchhausen]] sold the [[s:bishopric-of-osel-wiek|Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek]] to [[e:frederick-ii-of-denmark|Frederick II of Denmark]], who gave it to his brother [[e:magnus-duke-of-holstein|Magnus of Holstein]]. Magnus landed on [[s:saaremaa|Saaremaa]] in 1560, but his ambitions soon took him to the mainland as [[e:ivan-iv-of-russia|Ivan IV's]] [[e:vassal|vassal]] king of the [[s:kingdom-of-livonia|Kingdom of Livonia]].
danish-osel.r: After [[e:magnus-duke-of-holstein|Magnus]] died in 1583, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] ruled Ösel directly through governors at [[e:kuressaare|Arensburg]] (Kuressaare). The island's German nobility kept their estates and privileges, and Estonian peasants remained serfs. Denmark valued the island as an outpost in the eastern Baltic and as a bargaining counter against [[e:sweden|Sweden]].
danish-osel.e: [[e:denmark|Denmark]] lost the [[e:torstenson-war|Torstenson War]] against [[e:sweden|Sweden]], and by the [[e:treaty-of-bromsebro-1645|Treaty of Brömsebro]] in 1645 it ceded Ösel to Sweden, together with [[s:gotland|Gotland]], [[s:jamtland|Jämtland]] and [[e:harjedalen|Härjedalen]]. The island joined [[s:swedish-livonia|Swedish Livonia]], and after 1721 it passed to [[e:russia|Russia]].

duchy-of-strzelce.t: A minor Upper Silesian appanage duchy around Strzelce, created in the Opole partition of 1313 and later reabsorbed by its parent duchy.
duchy-of-strzelce.o: When [[e:bolko-i-of-opole|Bolko I of Opole]] died in 1313, his son Albert received [[e:strzelce-opolskie|Strzelce]] (Strehlitz), east of [[e:opole|Opole]], as his share of the [[s:duchy-of-opole|Duchy of Opole]]. Albert did homage to [[e:john-of-bohemia|King John of Bohemia]] in 1327, placing the small duchy under the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]].
duchy-of-strzelce.r: The duchy comprised the castle town of [[e:strzelce-opolskie|Strzelce]] and its surrounding farmland. Its later history is poorly documented: after Albert's death it was held by members of the Opole dynasty, sometimes as a dower or [[e:appanage|appanage]] rather than as a fully separate state.
duchy-of-strzelce.e: By the mid-15th century [[e:strzelce-opolskie|Strzelce]] had been reabsorbed into the [[s:duchy-of-opole|Duchy of Opole]], which itself fell to the Bohemian crown in 1532. The town followed [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742 and to [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945, as Strzelce Opolskie.
